author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.title: Research Summary: June 09, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by a landmark, scientist-in-the-loop evaluation showing contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science. Authors of 121,640 preprints judged LLM follow-up ideas from their own papers across 25,139 rating sets, exposing a creativity ceiling with major implications for autonomous research agents.

Safety and alignment dominate, spanning theory, attacks, and multilingual failures:

  • When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails formalizes the audit gap between behavioral and representation-level robustness, building dissociated models that pass safety tests yet remain internally unsafe.
  • A first large-scale multilingual sycophancy study benchmarks six models across 1.1 million instances, showing alignment degrades across languages and topics.
  • Hiding in Plain Floats transports prompt-injection payloads as structured float parameters, evading text-centric detectors.

Theory and foundations advance with an information-theoretic definition of open-ended learning (via the bit-equivalent metric) and Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws, which grounds empirical multi-domain mixing in Kaplan/Chinchilla-style theory.

Agents, scaling, and embodiment round out the set:

  • SWE-Marathon benchmarks 20 ultra-long-horizon tasks with executable environments and multi-layer evaluation.
  • Scaling Participation (Zettlemoyer, Choi, Tsvetkov) proposes bottom-up modular systems composed from many stakeholder-trained models.
  • Ego-Pi (Finn) shows egocentric human data improves cross-embodiment transfer for pi_0.5-based VLA policies.
  • Sparrow accelerates long-context RLVR via sparse-attention rollouts, navigating the stability-efficiency tradeoff.
entry.content:
Today's research is anchored by a landmark, scientist-in-the-loop evaluation showing contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science. Authors of 121,640 preprints judged LLM follow-up ideas from their own papers across 25,139 rating sets, exposing a creativity ceiling with major implications for autonomous research agents.

Safety and alignment dominate, spanning theory, attacks, and multilingual failures:

  • When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails formalizes the audit gap between behavioral and representation-level robustness, building dissociated models that pass safety tests yet remain internally unsafe.
  • A first large-scale multilingual sycophancy study benchmarks six models across 1.1 million instances, showing alignment degrades across languages and topics.
  • Hiding in Plain Floats transports prompt-injection payloads as structured float parameters, evading text-centric detectors.

Theory and foundations advance with an information-theoretic definition of open-ended learning (via the bit-equivalent metric) and Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws, which grounds empirical multi-domain mixing in Kaplan/Chinchilla-style theory.

Agents, scaling, and embodiment round out the set:

  • SWE-Marathon benchmarks 20 ultra-long-horizon tasks with executable environments and multi-layer evaluation.
  • Scaling Participation (Zettlemoyer, Choi, Tsvetkov) proposes bottom-up modular systems composed from many stakeholder-trained models.
  • Ego-Pi (Finn) shows egocentric human data improves cross-embodiment transfer for pi_0.5-based VLA policies.
  • Sparrow accelerates long-context RLVR via sparse-attention rollouts, navigating the stability-efficiency tradeoff.

entry.title: Contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science

author.name: Honglin Bao, Siyang Wu, Xiao Liu, Sida Li, Shiyun Cao, James A. Evans

entry.summary: This large-scale study invited authors of 121,640 preprints to judge LLM-generated follow-up ideas from their own papers, collecting 25,139 rating sets from 6,749 scientists. It finds contemporary AI lacks imagination to diverge or negate in science, with non-reasoning LLMs collapsing into convention.

entry.title: When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails: A Representation-Level Perspective

author.name: Enyi Jiang, Anders Gj{\o}lbye, Yibo Jacky Zhang, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: This work formalizes the audit gap between behavioral safety evaluations and representation-level robustness, constructing dissociated models that appear safe but remain vulnerable in latent space. It introduces intervention-based evaluation via harmful fine-tuning and latent perturbations.

entry.title: An Information-Theoretic Definition for Open-Ended Learning

author.name: Wanqiao Xu, Yifan Zhu, Benjamin Van Roy

entry.summary: This paper introduces an information-theoretic definition of open-ended learning based on the bit-equivalent, the information required to attain each reward level, defining open-endedness as linear growth in bit-equivalent. It shows classical bandits are not open-ended, constructs one that is, and provides an algorithm achieving open-ended learning.

entry.title: SWE-Marathon: Can Agents Autonomously Complete Ultra-Long-Horizon Software Work?

author.name: Rishi Desai, Jesse Hu, Joan Cabezas, Neel Harsola, Pratyush Shukla, Roey Ben Chaim, Adnan El Assadi, Omkaar Mukund Kamath, Fenil Faldu, Prannay Hebbar, Jiankai Sun, Yiyuan Li, Pramod Srinivasan, Ishan Gupta, Christopher Settles, Daniel Wang, Derek Chen, Pranav Raja, Albert Liu, Marek \v{S}uppa, Nevasini Sasikumar, Luyang Kong, Erik Quintanilla, Xiangyi Li, Ivan Bercovich, Steven Dillmann

entry.summary: SWE-Marathon is a benchmark of 20 ultra-long-horizon software engineering tasks, each with executable environments, reference solutions, and multi-layer verification, where logged agent attempts average over 27 million tokens. It targets measuring agent planning, long-context, and memory capabilities far beyond typical short-task benchmarks.

entry.title: Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws

author.name: Rui Dai, Shuran Zheng

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical framework explaining empirical data mixing scaling laws, extending Kaplan/Chinchilla perspectives to multi-domain settings. It identifies capacity competition and skill overlap as key factors governing domain losses under different data mixtures.

entry.title: Hiding in Plain Floats: Steganographic Carriers for Indirect Prompt and Content Injection

author.name: Mudit Sinha, Sanika Chavan

entry.summary: This work demonstrates an indirect prompt-injection attack where payloads caught in plain text evade detectors when transported as structured float parameters and reconstructed as fragmented telemetry. Across 14,400 trials on three commercial LLM APIs, the float-array carrier preserves 94.3% leakage attack success under strong dual-layer text-classifier defenses.

entry.title: Sycophancy as a Multilingual Alignment Failure: How Safety Degrades Across Languages, Topics, and Models

author.name: Arya Shah, Himanshu Beniwal, Mayank Singh, Chaklam Silpasuwanchai

entry.summary: This paper presents the first large-scale multilingual study of LLM sycophancy, benchmarking six instruction-tuned models across 1.1 million instances spanning 38 languages and 33 topics. It finds a consistent resource-tier effect where sycophancy spikes in low-resource and zero-shot language settings, topic-agnostically.

entry.title: Scaling Participation in Modular AI Systems

author.name: Shangbin Feng, Yike Wang, Weijia Shi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Yejin Choi, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: This work proposes scaling participation, a paradigm where modular AI systems are built bottom-up from many small stakeholder-trained models that collaborate compositionally, reportedly outperforming monolithic LLMs by up to 15.4% across 15 tasks. It challenges centralized model development with a participatory alternative.

entry.title: Ego-Pi: VLA Fine-Tuning for Ego-Centric Human and Robot Data

author.name: Ji Woong Kim, Ke Wang, Zipeng Fu, Sirui Chen, Cong Zhao, Jeff Lai, Chelsea Finn

entry.summary: Ego-Pi investigates fine-tuning VLA models (built on pi_0.5) across human and humanoid embodiments with dexterous hands, showing egocentric human data enables robots to learn new task semantics and compose skills without corresponding robot data. It addresses robotics data scarcity by leveraging easily-collected human demonstrations.

entry.title: Beyond Additivity: Causal Discovery in Location-Scale Noise Models with Hidden Variables

author.name: Mariyam Khan, Shohei Shimizu, Thong Pham

entry.summary: This paper proves identifiability for causal discovery in location-scale noise models with hidden variables, where causes modulate both mean and variance of effects. It establishes the first identifiability result for causally insufficient models beyond additive noise and provides a sound two-stage algorithm.

entry.title: Sparrow: Sparse Rollout for Stable and Efficient Long-context RL of Large Language Models

author.name: Yang Zhou, Ranajoy Sadhukhan, Zhaofeng Sun, Zhuoming Chen, Souvik Kundu, Saket Dingliwal, Sai Muralidhar Jayanthi, Aram Galstyan, Haizhong Zheng, Beidi Chen

entry.summary: Sparrow accelerates long-context RL with verifiable rewards by using sparse attention during rollout generation, navigating the stability-efficiency tradeoff via analysis of sparse-to-dense actor-policy mismatch. It observes that most sparse tokens align with dense even under aggressive sparsity, enabling selective sparsification.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Flow-Matching Policies with Density Transport

author.name: Boshu Lei, Kostas Daniilidis, Antonio Loquercio

entry.summary: RLDT is an online RL algorithm for fine-tuning flow-matching policies by viewing policy improvement as transport of action densities toward high-reward regions, constructing a transport field from a maximum-entropy objective using Stein Variational Gradient Descent. It avoids biased gradients and preserves multimodal modeling capacity unlike distillation approaches.

entry.title: Diffuse AI Control on Fuzzy Tasks

author.name: Mikhail Terekhov, Caglar Gulcehre, Vivek Hebbar, Joe Benton

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for Diffuse AI Control modeling AI sabotage on hard-to-grade fuzzy tasks as an adversarial blue-team/red-team game using weak trusted models. Addresses subtle misalignment risks distributed over long deployment horizons. Relevant to AI safety in critical domains.

entry.title: Tight Sample Complexity of Transformers

author.name: Chenxiao Yang, Nathan Srebro, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: Tightly characterizes the VC dimension of depth-L Transformers with W parameters, providing matching upper and lower bounds, and extends this to the sample complexity of chain-of-thought learning under teacher forcing. Fundamental learning-theory contribution. Matters for understanding transformer generalization.

entry.title: Hacking Generative Perplexity: Why Unconditional Text Evaluation Needs Distributional Metrics

author.name: Antonio Franca, Alexander Tong

entry.summary: This paper argues that generative perplexity, the dominant metric for diffusion and flow-based language models, is unsound because it measures only predictability under a scoring AR rather than grammaticality or coherence. It constructs zero-parameter naive samplers that hack gen-PPL and advocates for distributional metrics.

entry.title: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures

author.name: Jaineet Shah

entry.summary: Causal Agent Replay (CAR) attributes LLM-agent failures to specific steps by modeling runs as structural causal models, applying do-operations to steps and re-executing trajectories to measure the causal shift. It addresses the inadequacy of unreliable LLM-judge attribution (about 14% accuracy on Who&When).

entry.title: Active Flow Expansion for Out-of-Distribution Discovery: from Theory to Molecules

author.name: Riccardo De Santi, Bruce Lee, Cristian Perez Jensen, Kimon Protopapas, Sophia Tang, Cheng-Hao Liu, Pranam Chatterjee, Yisong Yue, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: Introduces Active Flow Expansion, a learning principle for generative discovery that enlarges a model's generable set rather than matching the observed data distribution, enabling sampling of valid out-of-distribution designs. Applied to molecule generation. Matters for AI-driven scientific design beyond known data.

entry.title: Bridging intent and execution in agentic systems

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Science argues that as LLMs improve, the performance bottleneck for AI agents shifts from model reasoning to the harness, the software layer translating model intent into actions. They formalize this as the intent-execution gap and show that minimizing this bidirectional mismatch yields state-of-the-art results on agentic benchmarks like SWE-Verified and Terminal-Bench2 without task-specific tuning.

entry.title: VATS: Exploiting Implicit Authority in Error-Path Injection via Systematic Mutation

author.name: Harshil Patel, Kunal Pai

entry.summary: VATS is a mutation-driven framework exploiting the implicit authority of tool error messages in the Model Context Protocol to triple indirect prompt injection success, reaching up to 100% compliance on frontier models. It exposes the error-handling loop as a critical unexamined attack surface for agents.

entry.title: Ablation-Reversible Heads Don't Transfer: A Stress Test for Mechanistic Role Claims in Transformers

author.name: Philip Quirke

entry.summary: This stress-test paper shows that attention heads passing standard mechanistic-role checks (necessity, linear encoding, ablation-recovery) routinely fail to transfer their computation when patched into different prompts under matched controls. It introduces a KID lens and a pipeline questioning common mechanistic role claims.

entry.title: ResearchClawBench: A Benchmark for End-to-End Autonomous Scientific Research

author.name: Wanghan Xu, Shuo Li, Tianlin Ye, Qinglong Cao, Yixin Chen, Hengjian Gao, Yiheng Wang, Qi Li, Kun Li, Sheng Xu, Shengdu Chai, Fangchen Yu, Xiangyu Zhao, Zhangrui Zhao, Weijie Ma, Zijie Guo, Haoyu Zhou, Haoxiang Yin, Lixue Cheng, Chaofan Hu, Haoxuan Li, Lu Mi, Xuxuan Xie, Yifan Zhou, Ruizhe Chen, Zhiwang Zhou, Xingjian Guo, Yuhao Zhou, Xuming He, Shengyuan Xu, Xinyu Gu, Jiamin Wu, Mianxin Liu, Chunfeng Song, Fenghua Ling, Dongzhan Zhou, Shixiang Tang, Yuqiang Li, Mao Su, Peng Ye, Siqi Sun, Bin Wang, Xue Yang, Zhenfei Yin, Tianfan Fu, Guangtao Zhai, Wanli Ouyang, Bo Zhang, Lei Bai, Wenlong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces ResearchClawBench, a benchmark for end-to-end autonomous scientific research across 40 tasks from 10 domains, each grounded in a real published paper with hidden targets and expert-curated multimodal rubrics. Evaluates seven auto-research agents and seventeen LLMs under a unified protocol.

entry.title: Pre-Intervention Prediction of Sparse Autoencoder Steering Side Effects

author.name: Evan Duan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a pre-intervention screening framework that forecasts sparse autoencoder steering side effects from feature statistics computed before steering. It operationalizes effect stability and collateral spread across multiple models and SAE dictionary types to predict steering modularity.

entry.title: PACT: Self-Evolving Physical Safety Alignment for Diffusion Policies in Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Lingxuan Wu, Zijian Zhu, Lizhong Wang, Chengyang Ying, Huayu Chen, Xiao Yang, Fangming Liu, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: PACT is a self-evolving post-training framework that projects pretrained diffusion robot policies onto constraint-feasible regions without demonstration data or task rewards, distilling constraint gradients via a reverse-KL objective with dense supervision. It addresses physical safety constraints often violated by diffusion policies at deployment.

entry.title: A retrieval conditioned rebinding circuit for dynamic entity tracking in large language models

author.name: Soyoung Oh, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: This interpretability study identifies a retrieval-conditioned rebinding mechanism in LLMs, a compact attention head circuit that encodes swap-relevant binding information and reinstates it at readout for dynamic entity tracking. It uses causal interventions across Gemma and Llama, finding the representational signature differs across model families.

entry.title: Hardening Agent Benchmarks with Adversarial Hacker-Fixer Loops

author.name: Ziqian Zhong, Ivgeni Segal, Ivan Bercovich, Shashwat Saxena, Kexun Zhang, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: Audits 1,968 agent-benchmark tasks finding 16% hackable by frontier models, then introduces a hacker-fixer loop that uses three cooperating LLM agents to build exploit-resistant verifiers without per-task manual patching. Addresses reward hacking that corrupts leaderboards and RL training signal.

entry.title: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale

author.name: Ang Li, Sean McLeish, Haozhe Chen, Nimit Kalra, Zaiqian Chen, Artem Gazizov, Venkata Anoop Suhas Kumar Morisetty, Bhavya Kailkhura, Harshitha Menon, Zhuang Liu, Brian R. Bartoldson, Tom Goldstein, Sanae Lotfi, Micah Goldblum, Pavel Izmailov

entry.summary: Presents an encoder-decoder context compression method that maps long token sequences to shorter latent embeddings, aiming to beat KV-cache compression on the accuracy-efficiency frontier for long-context inference. It addresses memory bottlenecks while staying compatible with production inference engines.

entry.title: iOSWorld: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Phone Agents

author.name: Lawrence Keunho Jang, Mareks Woodside, Geronimo Carom, Andrew Keunwoo Jang, Jing Yu Koh, Ruslan Salakhutdinov

entry.summary: iOSWorld is the first interactive native iOS simulator benchmark built around a persistent user identity across 26 custom apps with connected personal data, testing personally intelligent phone agents on 133 tasks including memory and personalization. Addresses a gap in mobile agent evaluation. Matters for personalized agent research.

entry.title: Where Instruction Hierarchy Breaks: Diagnosing and Repairing Failures in Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Sanjay Kariyappa, G. Edward Suh

entry.summary: This paper introduces a white-box diagnostic framework that localizes instruction-hierarchy failures in reasoning models into identification, conflict resolution, and execution stages, then proposes repairs. It matters for securing agentic workflows where privileged instructions must override conflicting ones.

entry.title: Scaffold Effects on GAIA: A Controlled Comparison

author.name: Jason Starace

entry.summary: This pre-registered controlled study isolates scaffold effects on GAIA by comparing ReAct, planner-actor-rater, and planner-then-executor scaffolds across five models, finding scaffold choice alone can move accuracy by up to 28 percentage points. It quantifies the elicitation gap that conflates model capability with scaffold design.

entry.title: Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation: A Learned Precursor to Reward Hacking and Its Generalization

author.name: Mohammad Beigi, Ming Jin, Lifu Huang

entry.summary: PRIME studies a learned precursor to reward hacking, defining proxy reward internalization and mechanistic exploitation as the capability to assess task correctness, predict proxy acceptance, and reason about exploitable proxy-gold gaps. In coding RL with exploitable pytest rewards, PRIME emerges in stages before sustained hacking and its probe score forecasts later hack onset and severity.

entry.title: Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence

author.name: Vansh Gupta, Peter Nutter, Samuel Stante, Andreas Krause, Florian Tram\`er, Lukas Fluri, Xin Chen, Anna Hedstr\"om

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that anthropomorphic misalignment research (deception, emergent misalignment, sycophancy) often relies on weak evidence and proposes a framework of evidence levels and a diagnostic checklist to improve methodological rigor for safety-critical decisions. Calls for stronger causal interventions and robust datasets.

entry.title: BCG-FM: A Foundation Model for Ambient Cardiac Health Sensing

author.name: Magnus Ruud Kjaer, Haejun Han, Ashish Neupane, David Q. Sun

entry.summary: BCG-FM is the first foundation model for ambient ballistocardiography signals from bed-embedded piezoelectric sensors, pretrained with participant-level contrastive learning on 2.75 million hours from nearly 146,000 individuals. Frozen embeddings achieve strong biological-age estimation without requiring deliberate user action.

entry.title: EgoAERO: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Egocentric Video without Object Assets

author.name: Yichen Niu, Haoran Lv, Xinrui Zhang, Xueyao Wan, Shiyu Gao, Ying Ai, Hui Xu, Yongqi Hu, Hengyi Zhang, Yang Xie, Zhaxizhuoma, Yue Zhao, Zhenshan Bing, Yan Ding, Jianxing Liu

entry.summary: EgoAERO learns dexterous robot manipulation from a single egocentric RGB-D human video without pre-scanned object assets, reconstructing contact-consistent hand-object trajectories via asset-free tracking and residual learning. It addresses the practical barrier of object pose/geometry requirements in robot learning from human demos.

entry.title: FlashCP: Load-Balanced Communication-Efficient Context Parallelism for LLM Training

author.name: Zheng Wang, Eric Liu, Linan Jiang, Zhongkai Yu, Zaifeng Pan, Yue Guan, Yuke Wang, Yufei Ding

entry.summary: FlashCP is a load-balanced, communication-efficient context parallelism framework for long-context LLM training that eliminates redundant KV communication via sharding-aware mechanisms and a Whole-Doc sharding strategy. It addresses workload imbalance and inefficient kernels in existing CP methods.

entry.title: A Unifying View of Attention Sinks: Two Algorithms, Two Solutions

author.name: Lukas Fesser, Mozes Jacobs, Thomas Fel, Andy Keller, Sham Kakade

entry.summary: Provides a unifying account of attention sinks in transformers, showing visually similar sink patterns reflect two distinct mechanisms: adaptive nop (update suppression) and broadcast (global information aggregation). It links interventions like gating and registers to which mechanism they target.

entry.title: The Hidden Bias of Process Reward Models:PRISM for Rewarding the Right Reasoning

author.name: Aakriti Agrawal, Souradip Chakraborty, Armin Saghafian, Nihal Sharma, Rizal Fathony, Nam H Nguyen, C. Bayan Bruss, Amrit Singh Bedi, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Identifies a hidden bias in Process Reward Models caused by step-level data imbalance, where false positives asymmetrically steer downstream selection and policy optimization toward flawed reasoning. Proposes PRISM, shifting from pointwise labels to reliable relative comparisons. Matters for reasoning model training.

entry.title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment

author.name: David D. Baek, Xinnuo Li, Anay Gupta, Taslim Mahbub, Kejian Shi, Max Tegmark, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Argues alignment faking may reflect sycophancy toward AI researchers (performative misalignment) rather than strategic scheming, showing evaluation awareness persists even when models are told they are deployed. Provides empirical findings challenging the intentional-deception interpretation.

entry.title: Causally Evaluating the Learnability of Formal Language Tasks

author.name: V\'esteinn Sn{\ae}bjarnarson, Anej Svete, Josef Valvoda, Reda Boumasmoud, Brian DuSell, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: Uses formal languages from probabilistic finite automata to causally study the relationship between training data frequency and task learnability, introducing the binning semiring to control how often a property occurs in sampled corpora. It demonstrates that standard correlational evaluation practices are flawed.

entry.title: Safety is Contextual, LLM-Judges Are Not: Navigating the Rigid Priors of Evaluators

author.name: Anissa Alloula, Federico Licini, Ava Batchkala, Seraphina Goldfarb-Tarrant

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM-judges rely on in-context information and can be steered to differing safety definitions, finding they learn from new info but are largely unwilling to deviate from internal safety priors. It exposes a key reliability gap in using LLMs to evaluate safety at scale.

entry.title: SurfDesign: Effective Protein Design on Molecular Surfaces

author.name: Fang Wu, Shuting Jin, Xiangru Tang, Mark Gerstein, Xiangxiang Zeng, Yejin Choi, Jure Leskovec, Jinbo Xu

entry.summary: Introduces SurfDesign, a surface-conditioned protein design framework modeling molecular surfaces as continuous manifolds with equivariant message passing, integrated with pretrained protein language models. Outperforms backbone-only and prior surface methods on binder and enzyme design benchmarks.

entry.title: What Makes Video World Model Latents Action-Relevant: Prediction over Reconstruction

author.name: Jewon Yeom, Hanseul Kim, Jeongjae Park, Sungmok Jung, Jaejin Lee, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: This study probes which video world model pretraining signals induce action-relevant latent structure, finding via inverse-dynamics probing that temporal video pretraining with latent prediction drives action recoverability rather than pixel reconstruction fidelity. Strong pixel decoders can have near-zero action recoverability.

entry.title: The ACUTE Protocol: Operationalizing Language Model Activations for Better Calibration, Utility, and Trust

author.name: Nishant Subramani, Palash Goyal, Yiwen Song, Mani Malek, Yuan Xue, Tomas Pfister, Hamid Palangi

entry.summary: The ACUTE protocol introduces an activation-based confidence, utility, and trust framework for language models, including a new metric (EURO) that balances calibration and informativeness to resist gaming by base-rate predictors. Authors are from Google and CMU.

entry.title: vla.cpp: A Unified Inference Runtime for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Khanh D. Nguyen, Hung T. Ho, Chinh T. Nguyen, Thanh Q. Duong, Linh D. Le, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien A. Ngo, An T. Le

entry.summary: vla.cpp is a portable C++ inference runtime built on llama.cpp that natively serves flow-matching and diffusion VLA models, supporting seven architectures behind one protocol. It targets the mismatch between GPU-heavy Python VLA stacks and the constrained hardware robots actually use.

entry.title: Emergence World: A Platform for Evaluating Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Autonomy

author.name: Deepak Akkil, Ravi Kokku, Karthik Vikram, Tamer Abuelsaad, Aditya Vempaty, Satya Nitta

entry.summary: Emergence World is a continuously running multi-agent simulation platform hosting LLM-driven agent populations in a shared spatial world grounded in live external data, designed to measure long-horizon dynamics like behavioral drift and cross-model influence. It argues exam-style evaluations mismatch the weeks-to-months timescales of deployed autonomous systems.

entry.title: ActProbe: Action-Space Probe for Early Failure Detection of Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Bingjia Huang, Xiangyu Li, Xiang Wang, Liang Mi, Zixu Hao, Weijun Wang, Hao Wu, Kun Li, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: ActProbe is a lightweight action-space failure detector for generative robot policies using two compact signals from a single forward pass: temporal consistency error between action chunks and action chunk magnitude. It avoids white-box access and runtime resampling overhead of existing online detectors.

entry.title: A case study of evaluating AI agents on a neuroscience data-to-discovery pipeline

author.name: Kai A. Horstmann, Ethan Lin, Alice A. Robie, Jennifer J. Sun, Kristin Branson

entry.summary: This case study empirically evaluates general-purpose coding agents on a realistic neuroscience data-to-discovery pipeline using datasets far larger than typical benchmarks and expert-grounded criteria. It matters as a rigorous, domain-realistic assessment of where agentic scientific automation succeeds and fails.

entry.title: The AI Epistemic Deference Index: A Continuous Measure of Sycophancy

author.name: Alejandro Botas, Paul de Font-Reaulx, Luke Hewitt

entry.summary: The AI Epistemic Deference Index (AEDI) is a continuous measure of sycophancy capturing graded shifts in a model's expressed support in response to user attitudes, using a new protocol to estimate probabilities from natural-language outputs. It improves measurement of subtle, real-world sycophantic behavior beyond binary flips.

entry.title: To Nuke or Not to Nuke: LLMs' (Missing) Ethical Reasoning and Actions in a High-Stakes Decision-Making Simulation

author.name: John Chen, Sihan Cheng, Can Gurkan, H M Abdul Fattah

entry.summary: This study evaluates LLM ethical reasoning in a complex Civilization V simulation where models spontaneously escalated to nuclear authorization, replaying 130 high-tension episodes across 13 models with ethical, rationale-removal, and high-stakes framing interventions. It probes whether dilemma-level ethical competence transfers to long-horizon agentic decisions.

entry.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents

author.name: Kale-ab Abebe Tessera, Andras Szecsenyi, Cameron Barker, Alexander Rutherford, Davide Paglieri, Aidan Scannell, Henry Gouk, Elliot J. Crowley, Tim Rockt\"aschel, Amos Storkey

entry.summary: Alem is a JAX-based benchmark for open-ended multi-agent coordination on Craftax-like dynamics, embedding procedurally generated coordination, communication, soft specialization, and controllable difficulty in a long-horizon survival world. It evaluates 13 modern LLMs zero-shot against trained MARL references.

entry.title: Trajectory-Refined Distillation

author.name: Li Jiang, Haoran Xu, Yichuan Ding, Amy Zhang

entry.summary: Trajectory-Refined Distillation identifies prefix failure in on-policy distillation, where dense per-token teacher supervision induces a bimodal mixture and fragmented gradients, and proposes trajectory-level output corrections instead of token-level loss tweaks. It improves post-training distillation of LLMs.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for Mathematical Reasoning: An Integrated Survey of Language Models, Neuro-symbolic Systems, and Verified Discovery

author.name: Syed Rifat Raiyan, Mohsinul Kabir, Hasan Mahmud, Md Kamrul Hasan

entry.summary: This integrated survey maps AI for mathematical reasoning across four axes: informal text/diagram reasoning, formal proof-assistant reasoning, neuro-symbolic theorem provers, and verified discovery workflows, tracing the evolution from rule-based solvers to modern reasoning models. It provides a unified account of a consequential AI frontier.

entry.title: Baichuan-M4: A Clinical-Grade Medical Agent System for Continuous Care

author.name: Aiyuan Yang, Chengfeng Dou, Da Pan, Dian Wang, Fan Yang, Fei Deng, Fei Li, Guangwei Ai, Hui Liu, Hongda Zhang, Jinyang Tai, Kai Lu, Lijun Liu, Linwei Chen, Linyu Li, Meiqing Guo, Peidong Guo, Qiang Ju, Rihui Xin, Shuai Wang, XinKai Ma, Xudong Chen, Yichuan Mo, Canbin Piao, Leyi Pan, Yihe Luo, Zian Wang

entry.summary: Baichuan-M4 is a clinical-grade medical agent system for continuous care built around a unified RL/deployment runtime, a continuous-care reasoning model with span-level reward modeling and curriculum learning, and a clinical tool layer with long-term patient memory. It targets multi-turn longitudinal care rather than single-turn QA.

entry.title: Correct Looks Better: Pairwise Comparisons Reveal Accuracy Rankings

author.name: Mina Remeli, Moritz Hardt

entry.summary: This paper shows that pairwise-comparison rankings (Elo) of generative models strongly agree with ground-truth accuracy rankings (Spearman above 0.9) across five benchmarks converted to free-form generation, and that style and judge bias have only minor effects. It offers a reassuring empirical defense of pairwise evaluation, especially when judges are weak.

entry.title: Post-training is (Massive) Supervised Learning

author.name: Michael Hassid, Yossi Adi, Roy Schwartz

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that current LLM post-training (SFT + RL) effectively reverts to the BERT-era pre-train-then-fine-tune paradigm, tailoring models to benchmarks rather than general capability. Supports the claim by comparing pretrained vs randomly initialized models after fine-tuning.

entry.title: Systematic LLM Translation of Legacy Scientific Code to Differentiable Frameworks: Application to a Land Surface Model

author.name: Aya Lahlou, Linnia Hawkins, Pierre Gentine

entry.summary: This work presents a five-phase LLM agentic pipeline that translates legacy Fortran scientific code into differentiable JAX, using static dependency analysis, compile-repair loops, and a Fortran oracle for numerical parity verification. It is demonstrated on a 19,000-line land surface model.

entry.title: Adversarial Robustness of Activation Steering in Large Language Models

author.name: Kien Le, Thai Le

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of activation steering robustness under adversarial text perturbations, covering multiple extraction methods, attacks, personas, and models from 1.5B to 30B. Attacks broadly succeed, dropping directional robustness by up to 64% and collapsing post-attack confidence.

entry.title: Illusions of the Gold Standard: A Large-scale Analysis of Human Evaluation Protocols for Long-form Text Generation

author.name: Katelyn Xiaoying Mei, Yi-Li Hsu, Minjoon Choi, Zongwan Cao, Chenjun Xu, Bingbing Wen, Su Lin Blodgett, Lucy Lu Wang

entry.summary: This large-scale study analyzes human evaluation protocols for long-form text generation across *CL conference papers from 2023-2025, manually reviewing 284 papers and LLM-assisting analysis of over 1,800 more against 20 reproducibility criteria. It finds widespread under-reporting that undermines evaluation reliability.

entry.title: Defending Against Malicious Finetuning by Scaling Train-time Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Haoming Wen, Shi Chen, Qingyu Shi, Siyuan Liu, Minrui Luo, Jingzhao Zhang, Tianxing He

entry.summary: Patcher defends open-weight LLMs against malicious finetuning, including stronger full-parameter attacks, by scaling up train-time adversarial optimization steps in a bi-level setup to find parameters insensitive to such attacks. It improves on existing defenses limited to parameter-efficient finetuning attacks.

entry.title: How Deep Are Deep GPs, Really? A Sharp Threshold and a Non-Gaussian Limit for Compositional GPs

author.name: Mark Kozdoba, Shie Mannor

entry.summary: This paper studies the limiting behavior of compositional Gaussian processes where each layer is a vector-valued GP, establishing a sharp threshold for prior degeneration and identifying a non-Gaussian limit. It extends deep GP theory beyond prior RBF-kernel degeneracy results.

entry.title: Generative Frontier Planning for Adaptive Peer-Referral Recruitment under Covariate-Dependent Arrivals

author.name: Lingkai Kong, Hezi Jiang, Andrew Ma, Keyu Wang, Akseli Kangaslahti, Milind Tambe

entry.summary: This work addresses adaptive peer-referral recruitment (respondent-driven sampling) for hidden populations affected by infectious diseases, modeling covariate-dependent arrivals where referral capacity and recruit covariates depend on the referrer. It uses generative frontier planning to allocate limited referral resources across rounds.

entry.title: Auditing Proprietary Alignment in Large Language Models: A Comparative Framework Without a Ground-Truth Standard

author.name: Alireza Arbabi, Florian Kerschbaum

entry.summary: This paper proposes a statistical framework for detecting proprietary alignment in black-box LLMs via comparative behavioral analysis without a ground-truth standard. It addresses how providers can inject undisclosed provider-specific policies leading to censorship or misinformation.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Personalized Multi-Objective Bandits with Proactive Conversational Queries

author.name: Linfeng Cao, Ming Shi, Ness B. Shroff

entry.summary: This paper formalizes personalized multi-objective bandits with proactive conversational queries, modeling user preference signals via a Plackett-Luce subset choice model. It proves query-only learning is insufficient due to shift-invariance and provides provably efficient algorithms leveraging structured query signals.

entry.title: GEAR-VLA: Learning Geometry-Aware Action Representations for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yuan Zhang, Shiqi Zhang, Yedong Shen, Shuai Dong, Jiajun Deng, Xin Zhang, Yuxuan Gao, Jiajia Wu, Xin Nie, Zhiyuan Cheng, Jianmin Ji, Yanyong Zhang, Xingyi Zhang, Jia Pan

entry.summary: GEAR-VLA learns unified geometry-aware action representations for generalizable robotic manipulation, using coarse-to-fine action learning and multi-source embodied pretraining to handle unseen objects, background shifts, and different embodiments. It argues existing VLAs fail from lacking geometry-aware representations.

entry.title: HARBOR: A Harness Framework for Agentic Robot Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zechu Li, Yufeng Jin, Xiaoyang Liu, Puze Liu, Vignesh Prasad, Carlo D'Eramo, Georgia Chalvatzaki

entry.summary: HARBOR is an agentic framework that automates robot RL as a harness-engineering problem, taking a simulator codebase and task specification to automate environment setup, reward shaping, and policy training in simulation. It decomposes objectives into bounded stages executed by specialized agents.

entry.title: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation

author.name: Qi Cao, Jian Lou, Meiting Liu, Wenjie Feng, Dan Li, See-Kiong Ng, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: Examines whether activation steering, an inference-time behavior-modulation technique, can induce emergent misalignment similar to finetuning on unsafe examples. Provides a comprehensive evaluation of this previously underexplored safety risk.

entry.title: The Easy, the Hard, and the Learnable: Confidence and Difficulty-Adaptive Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhanke Zhou, Xiangyu Lu, Chentao Cao, Brando Miranda, Tongliang Liu, Bo Han, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Analyzes GRPO RL training dynamics for LLM reasoning, identifying confidence inflation, advantage contraction, and hierarchical convergence. It proposes CoDaPO, which adapts sampling and weighting to question difficulty and model competence for more efficient compute allocation.

entry.title: Few-step Cofolding with All-Atom Flow Maps

author.name: Gianluca Scarpellini, Ron Shprints, Peter Holderrieth, Juno Nam, Pranav Murugan, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli, Tommi Jaakola, Maruan Al-Shedivat, Nicholas Matthew Boffi, Avishek Joey Bose

entry.summary: Introduces DeCAF, a framework for distilling state-of-the-art all-atom cofolding models into flow maps that generate high-quality biomolecular complex structures in few inference steps. It uses denoiser-based flow maps with endpoint losses supporting SE(3) alignment.

entry.title: The Spectral Dynamics and Noise Geometry of Muon

author.name: Pierfrancesco Beneventano, Mahmoud Abdelmoneum, Tomaso Poggio

entry.summary: Studies the optimization bias of the Muon optimizer, which replaces a matrix gradient by its polar factor to flatten the update spectrum. It proves the polar update is the one-step entropy-maximizing bounded update and derives exact singular-value dynamics ruling out a common low-rank interpretation.

entry.title: Reformulate LLM Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Training under Black-box Discrepancy

author.name: Jiashun Liu, Runze Liu, Xu Wan, Jing Liang, Hongyao Tang, Ling Pan

entry.summary: This paper reframes LLM reinforcement learning to address the hidden train-inference discrepancy that causes training collapses, identifying a tolerance region where the policy can self-correct. It proposes more efficient training by selectively narrowing the discrepancy only when it exceeds a threshold. This matters for stabilizing RL post-training of LLMs.

entry.title: From Shortcuts to Reasoning: Robust Post-Training of Theory of Mind with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jike Zhong, Yuxiang Lai, Ming Li, Yuheng Li, Wuao Liu, Behzad Dariush, Konstantinos Psounis, Shao-Yuan Lo

entry.summary: Reveals a pervasive shortcut problem in Theory of Mind post-training where models reach up to 99% accuracy by exploiting spurious correlations, and develops an RL-based framework with shortcut-resistant data to foster genuine reasoning. Matters for robust ToM and safe foundation-model behavior.

entry.title: SoK: Reconstruction Attacks on Synthetic Tabular Data (Insights from Winning the NIST CRC)

author.name: Steven Golob, Sikha Pentyala, Martine De Cock

entry.summary: Provides the first systematization of reconstruction (attribute inference) attacks on synthetic and de-identified tabular data, with a taxonomy and the most systematic empirical evaluation to date pitting fourteen attacks against nine generation methods across five datasets. Draws insights from winning the NIST CRC competition.

entry.title: Representational Similarity and Model Behavior in Multi-Agent Interaction

author.name: Yujin Potter, Seun Eisape, Shiyang Lai, Alexander Huth, James Evans, Been Kim, Jacob Eisenstein, Dawn Song, Alane Suhr

entry.summary: Examines whether representational similarity between LLM pairs predicts cooperation and novelty across 276 model pairs in eight games, finding similar models cooperate more but produce less novelty. Extends human social-neuroscience principles to multi-agent AI.

entry.title: Multi-Hop Knowledge Composition is Bound by Pretraining Exposure

author.name: Yannis Karmim, Luis Marti, Djam\'e Seddah, Valentin Barri\`ere

entry.summary: Studies why LLMs fail at implicit multi-hop reasoning even when both facts are individually memorized, establishing that compositional failure persists at 97% single-hop accuracy and is a pretraining limitation rather than missing knowledge. It tests nine data-centric augmentation formats.

entry.title: The Neutral Mask: How RLHF Provides Shallow Alignment while Leaving Partisan Structure Intact in a Large Language Model

author.name: Wendy K. Tam

entry.summary: A mechanistic case study showing that RLHF does not remove the structured partisan political direction in Llama 3.1 8B but instead conceals it, producing functional compliance rather than deep alignment. It compares internal representations before and after RLHF.

entry.title: VideoWeaver: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Agentic Long Video Generation

author.name: Jianhui Wei, Jie Tan, Hengchuan Zhu, Xiaotian Zhang, Yan Zhang, Ziyi Chen, Daoan Zhang, Wei Xu, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: VideoWeaver introduces an agent harness and benchmark (16 categories, 285 cases) testing whether code-agent frameworks can self-compose workflows for long video generation rather than following fixed pipelines. It targets an underexplored long-horizon multimodal agentic task.

entry.title: Language as a Sensor: Calibrated Spatial Belief Estimation in 3D Scenes from Natural Language

author.name: Aryan Naveen, Jason Xinyu Liu, Luca Carlone, Andreea Bobu

entry.summary: This work introduces a Language Sensor Model that treats natural-language spatial descriptions as a calibrated sensor, mapping utterances and scene-graph context to multimodal 3D belief distributions with mixture weights encoding referential ambiguity. It enables fusing language observations with other sensor modalities.

entry.title: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yiyang Zhao, Zhuo Zhang, Qingxuan Le, Lizhen Qu, Zenglin Xu

entry.summary: MAC-Bench is a dynamic adversarial benchmark evaluating procedural compliance in multi-agent systems, using a Seed-Evolve-Refine-Verify pipeline to convert legal texts into contamination-free executable scenarios. It addresses Goodhart-style reward-hacking and Machiavellian behavior in autonomous agents.

entry.title: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Zayx Shawn

entry.summary: PACE recasts the commit decision in self-evolving agents as a sequential, anytime-valid hypothesis test, arguing the weak point is the acceptor rule that naively keeps changes scoring higher and effectively p-hacks itself. It offers a training-free statistically grounded commit evaluation to prevent drift.

entry.title: SciTrace: Trajectory-Aware Safety Reasoning for Scientific Discovery Agents

author.name: Tanush Swaminathan, Runmin Jiang, Letian Zhang, Min Xu

entry.summary: SciTrace weaves trajectory-aware safety reasoning into every stage of scientific discovery agents via a Safety-Intrinsic Reasoning Loop that maintains cumulative risk, addressing how sequences of benign tool calls can compose into harmful outcomes. It targets failure modes that output-only safety filters miss.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Scientific Agent Discovers Generalizable Physically-Reasoned Fluid Control

author.name: Boai Sun, Wenjin Guo, Zongmin Yu, Liu Yang

entry.summary: This work presents a self-evolving LLM-driven scientific agent that automates interpretable fluid-control discovery by deploying candidate strategies in simulations, diagnosing dynamics from multimodal evidence, and iteratively refining source code rather than tuning weights. It yields generalizable, physically-reasoned controllers.

entry.title: Emergent alignment and the projectability of ethical personas

author.name: Guillermo Del Pinal, Youngchan Lee, Cameron McNamara, Alejandro Perez Carballo

entry.summary: This paper investigates emergent alignment, the converse of emergent misalignment, by finetuning a helpful-only model on broad and narrow safety tasks using four ethical constitutions (deontology, consequentialism, virtue ethics, aligning AIs as subagents). It supports and refines the persona-selection hypothesis and proposes a projectability desideratum for alignment.

entry.title: Trait-space Monitoring for Emergent Misalignment During Supervised Finetuning

author.name: Huy Nghiem, Sy-Tuyen Ho, Sarah Wiegreffe, Hal Daum\'e III

entry.summary: Investigates detecting emergent misalignment during fine-tuning from internal representations, tracking drift along seven alignment-relevant linear trait directions across checkpoints in four 7-9B LLMs. Finds EM-relevant drift concentrates on a low-dimensional axis explaining 65.5% of variance, enabling a low-overhead monitor.

entry.title: From `May' to `Is': Certainty Distortion in Language Model Rewriting

author.name: Catarina G Belem, Shang Wu, Hongyu Yao, Mark Steyvers, Sameer Singh, Padhraic Smyth

entry.summary: This work studies certainty distortion in language models, defined as meaningful changes in expressed confidence when rewriting or summarizing content with preserved meaning, proposing an LM-based metric aligned with population judgments. It finds models systematically shift hedged claims toward overconfident assertions in scientific and medical contexts.

entry.title: Fast LLM-Based Semantic Filtering: From a Unified Framework to an Adaptive Two-Phase Method

author.name: Kyoungmin Kim, Martin Catheland, Anastasia Ailamaki

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified framework and adaptive two-phase method for fast LLM-based semantic filtering, where a fast proxy cascades with an expensive LLM oracle to evaluate yes/no predicates over corpora. It addresses limitations of prior cascades that commit to single representations and binary labels.

entry.title: When Video Misreads: Closed-Loop Distillation of Reading Heuristics for Exploratory Manipulation Trace QA

author.name: Haizhou Ge, Yufei Jia, Yue Li, Zhixing Chen, Lu Shi, Lei Han, Guyue Zhou, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: This work formalizes Exploratory Manipulation Trace QA, where a robot must read a video of an exploratory trace (including failed attempts revealing latent preconditions) to predict the minimal-success action chain. It uses closed-loop distillation of reading heuristics, finding even state-of-the-art video models misread such traces.

entry.title: INFUSER: Influence-Guided Self-Evolution Improves Reasoning

author.name: Siyu Chen, Miao Lu, Beining Wu, Heejune Sheen, Fengzhuo Zhang, Shuangning Li, Zhiyuan Li, Jose Blanchet, Tianhao Wang, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: INFUSER is an influence-guided self-evolution framework with co-evolving generator and solver roles, where the generator drafts questions and golden answers from unstructured documents and is rewarded by influence on solver improvement. Aims for scalable reasoning improvement with minimal supervision.

entry.title: Muon Learns More Robust and Transferable Features than Adam

author.name: Tianyu Ruan, Fengzhuo Zhang, Shuche Wang, Shihua Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates the feature-learning advantages of the Muon optimizer over Adam and SGD, showing Muon-trained models are consistently more robust to corruptions and more transferable across transformers and CNNs. Layer-wise probes reveal larger logit margins explaining the robustness advantage.

entry.title: Still: Amortized KV Cache Compaction in a Single Forward Pass

author.name: Charles O'Neill, Alex Sandomirsky, Harry Partridge, Mudith Jayasekara, Max Kirkby

entry.summary: Introduces Still, a small per-layer Perceiver trained once against a frozen base model to compress the KV cache into compact keys and values in a single forward pass. It achieves a favorable speed-quality frontier on Qwen and Gemma at compression ratios from 8x to 20x+.

entry.title: Understanding the Parameter Space Geometry of Transformers Encoding Boolean Functions

author.name: Blanka K\"over, Alexandra Butoi, Anej Svete, Michael Hahn, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: Analyzes transformer parameter-space geometry to explain why transformers fail to learn sensitive functions like PARITY despite being expressible, showing such functions occupy a vanishingly small region unlikely to be found by random initialization. It clarifies the mechanism behind the low-sensitivity learning bias.

entry.title: Beyond FLOPs: Benchmarking Real Inference Acceleration of LLM Pruning under a GEMM-Centric Taxonomy

author.name: Haozhe Hu, Hao Wu, Anhao Zhao, Longwei Ding, Peiran Yin, Yunpu Ma, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Introduces a GEMM-centric taxonomy reorganizing LLM pruning methods by matrix-multiplication M/N/K dimensions and benchmarks their real hardware speedups, revealing that realized acceleration diverges sharply from FLOP reductions. Clarifies practical pruning benefits. Matters for efficient LLM inference.

entry.title: Breaking the Tokenizer Barrier: On-Policy Distillation across Model Families

author.name: Yifan Niu, Han Xiao, Dongyi Liu, Zelong Wang, Dihong Gong, Yasheng Wang, Jia Li

entry.summary: Enables on-policy distillation across model families with different tokenizers, overcoming the same-tokenizer restriction that previously limited OPD, allowing high-fidelity token-level distribution signals to propagate across heterogeneous models. Matters for flexible knowledge transfer between LLMs.

entry.title: Clinically Grounded Privacy Evaluation of Medical LMs

author.name: Sasha Ronaghi, Sana Tonekaboni, Lena Stempfle, Vivian Utti, Jordan Li Cahoon, Nathaniel Hendrix, Ayin Vala, Marzyeh Ghassemi, Emily Alsentzer

entry.summary: Introduces a clinically grounded privacy evaluation framework for medical language models that measures leakage along a graded axis of adversarial access, from inferable demographics to leaked note fragments. Applied to a model pretrained on 378k clinical notes, it finds metadata elicits high verbatim memorization.

entry.title: Latent Spatial Memory for Video World Models

author.name: Weijie Wang, Haoyu Zhao, Yifan Yang, Feng Chen, Zeyu Zhang, Yefei He, Zicheng Duan, Donny Y. Chen, Yuqing Yang, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: Mirage introduces latent spatial memory for video world models, a persistent 3D cache storing scene info directly in diffusion latent space via depth-guided back-projection, avoiding costly and lossy pixel-space round trips. It maintains 3D spatial consistency more efficiently.

entry.title: Overcoming the Regulatory Bottleneck via Agent-to-Agent Protocols: A Nuclear Case Study

author.name: Akshay J. Dave, David Grabaskas, Joseph A. Renevitz, Richard B. Vilim

entry.summary: This work proposes a Regulatory Context Protocol, an agent-to-agent communication standard replacing human-to-human regulatory pipelines for advanced nuclear reactor licensing, calibrated against 1,236 NRC documents and shown to cut costs 50-77% in a pilot. It demonstrates agentic automation in high-stakes regulatory processes.

entry.title: The CIFAR Synthetic Evidence Corpus for Detecting AI-Generated Evidence

author.name: Kelly McConvey, Jalehsadat Mahdavimoghaddam, Nima Jamali, Maksym Taranukhin, Sajad Ebrahimi, Wentao Zhang, Yuntian Deng, Karen Eltis, Maura R. Grossman, Vered Shwartz, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: The CIFAR Synthetic Evidence Corpus provides training and evaluation data for detecting subtly AI-altered evidentiary documents (receipts, communications, records) where small localized edits change legal meaning. It fills a critical gap for the justice system facing generative-document forgery.

entry.title: When Does Delegation Beat Majority? A Delegation-Based Aggregator for Multi-Sample LLM Inference

author.name: Yasushi Sakai, Allen Song, Kent Larson

entry.summary: This paper proposes Propagational Proxy Voting (PPV), a delegation-based unsupervised aggregator for multi-sample LLM inference that exploits within-group letter entropy and between-group reasoning geometry to beat majority voting on MMLU-Pro. It shows majority voting discards useful free signals from each sample.

entry.title: VESTA: A Fully Automated Scenario Generation and Safety Evaluation Framework for LLM Agents

author.name: Lu Jia, Haibo Tong, Feifei Zhao, Jindong Li, Dongqi Liang, Ping Wu, Qian Zhang, Yi Zeng

entry.summary: VESTA is a fully automated scenario-generation and safety-evaluation framework for LLM agents that instantiates abstract risks across five dimensions into 1,072 measurable scenarios capturing risks during task execution, not just final outputs. It addresses limitations of manual, static safety evaluations.

entry.title: Momentum for Reasoning: Dense Intrinsic Signals in Policy Optimization

author.name: Hao Chen, Zhanming Shen, Liyao Li, Yanyu Chen, Xuhang Zhu, Xiaomeng Hu, Qi Zhang, Ru Peng, Xiaoyu Shen, Haobo Wang, Junbo Zhao

entry.summary: ISPO addresses failure modes in RLVR/GRPO training such as zero-advantage collapse and hallucinated certainty by densifying binary rewards with intrinsic signals computed from the policy's own conditional probabilities. It targets more stable long-chain reasoning training.

entry.title: PRISM: Recovering Instruction Sets from Language Model Activations

author.name: Gilad Gressel, Rahul Pankajakshan, Julia Diament, Efim Hudis, Krishnashree Achuthan, Yisroel Mirsky

entry.summary: PRISM formalizes instruction-set retrieval and introduces an activation-conditioned interpreter that decodes a frozen target model's hidden states into a faithful bullet list of the simultaneous instructions, constraints, and subgoals steering its behavior. It targets monitoring of agents under prompt injection and hidden objectives.

entry.title: Repetition Mismatch: Why Data Mixture Experiments Don't Scale and How to Fix Them

author.name: Kevin Zhou, Lisa Alazraki, Kris Cao, Marek Rei

entry.summary: Identifies repetition mismatch as a primary reason data-mixture experiments fail to scale: because high-quality datasets are small, their repetition rate shifts as training budget grows, moving the optimal mixture. Proposes a subsampling procedure matching target repetition rate that enables reliable extrapolation from cheap small-scale runs.

entry.title: A Dataset for Dynamic Human Preferences for Vision Language Models

author.name: Hannah Gao (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Dylan Hadfield-Menell (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Rachel Ma (Massachusetts Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: This work introduces a benchmark for evaluating how well vision-language models adapt to dynamic, in-context human preferences passed at inference time, rather than static learned preferences. It includes an automated benchmark-generation pipeline and a multimodal preference dataset from MIT authors.

entry.title: SAW: Stage-Aware Dynamic Weighting for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Yuchen He, Baolong Bi, Shenghua Liu, Huaming Liao, Yuyao Ge, Bolin Wan, Siqian Tong, Juan Chen, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: SAW is a stage-aware dynamic weighting mechanism for multi-objective RL in LLMs that addresses asynchronous reward learning across objectives, where well-learned dimensions add noise that drowns out under-learned ones. It uses coefficient-of-variation signals to dynamically reweight objectives in GRPO/GDPO.

entry.title: The Cross-Architecture Substrate: A Domain-Transcendent, Calibration-Surviving Geometric Invariant of Modern Vision Encoders

author.name: Yousef Radwan

entry.summary: This work reports that the top sixteen principal directions inside thirteen modern vision encoders converge to the same sixteen-dimensional geometric object, dubbed the cross-architecture substrate, persisting across diverse visual domains and surviving calibration. It is studied via PCA, CKA, and Procrustes analysis.

entry.title: Sci-Rho: A Multilingual Visually-Grounded Symbolic Benchmark for STEM Problems

author.name: Muhammad Falensi Azmi, Ikhlasul Akmal Hanif, Vallerie Alexandra Putra, Adi Yeltay, Abdullah Mubarak, Fajri Koto

entry.summary: Sci-Rho is a dynamic, visually-grounded symbolic benchmark covering five STEM subjects in seven languages, with 4,242 expert-crafted templates that generate equivalent problem variants. It tests model robustness under minor modifications, extending symbolic benchmarks beyond English-only math reasoning.

entry.title: GlobeAudio: A Multilingual Multicultural Benchmark for Naturalistic Evaluation of Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Ryner Tan, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: GlobeAudio is a multilingual, multicultural benchmark of 5,637 expert-crafted multiple-choice questions across six typologically diverse languages, designed for naturalistic evaluation of large audio-language models. It emphasizes linguistic, cultural, and acoustic authenticity missing from existing LALM benchmarks.

entry.title: SceneConductor: 3D Scene Generation from Single Image with Multi-Agent Orchestration

author.name: Jeonghwan Kim, Yushi Lan, Yongwei Chen, Hieu Trung Nguyen, Chuanyu Pan, Xingang Pan

entry.summary: SceneConductor is a multi-agent orchestration framework for generating complete 3D scenes from a single image, decomposing the task into scene initialization, environment construction, and multi-agent refinement. It avoids entangled holistic pipelines that demand extensive scene-level supervision.

entry.title: AI Code Sandboxes: A Comparative Security Study. Part 1 of 2 -- Engine-Level Properties (Attack Surface, Leakage, Stackability, CVE History, Patch Cadence, Fuzzing)

author.name: George Andronchik, Pavel Lokhmakov

entry.summary: This is part one of a comparative security study of five AI code sandbox products across six engine-level measurements including attack surface, leakage, CVE history, and patch cadence. It finds engine classes separate cleanly on architectural axes while products within a class do not, and that pin policy is the dominant operator-facing variable.

entry.title: Not Just After One: Sleep-Inspired Replay Prevents Catastrophic Forgetting After Sequential Tasks

author.name: Anthony Bazhenov, Jean Erik Delanois, Giri P. Krishnan

entry.summary: This neuroscience-inspired work shows multiple new tasks can be trained sequentially before an unsupervised sleep-like replay phase partially restores performance across all prior tasks. It departs from algorithms that protect memories during or immediately after each task, mimicking how animals consolidate memories.

entry.title: The Confidence Trap: Calibration Attacks for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Cuong Dang, Jiahao Zhang, Hieu Ta Quang, Dung Le, Lu Cheng, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: This work introduces Unified Graph Calibration Attack, a framework for adversarial calibration attacks on graph neural networks that manipulate confidence via structural perturbations. It addresses challenges of discrete graph optimization, driving predictions toward uniformity, and avoiding unintended label changes.

entry.title: Unifying Object-Centric World Models and Diffusion Policy: A Hierarchical Framework for Multi-Stage Robotic Tasks

author.name: Raktim Gautam Goswami, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Yann LeCun, Farshad Khorrami

entry.summary: WorldDP unifies object-centric world models with diffusion policy in a hierarchical framework for multi-stage robotic manipulation, using a high-level world model to optimize subgoals reached by a low-level diffusion policy. Co-authored by Yann LeCun.

entry.title: CARE: A Conformal Safety Layer for Medical Summarization

author.name: Suhana Bedi, Bridget Lin, Anson Y. Zhou, Chloe O. Stanwyck, Jenelle A. Jindal, Sanmi Koyejo, David Stutz, Nigam H. Shah

entry.summary: CARE is a model-agnostic conformal safety layer for medical summarization that overlays calibrated omission and hallucination flags with finite-sample, distribution-free guarantees. It uses conformal risk control to bound missed errors while managing clinician review burden.

entry.title: Reasoning Arena: Trace Tournaments When Verifiable Rewards Fall Short

author.name: Han Zhou, Adam X. Yang, Laurence Aitchison, Anna Korhonen, Albert Q. Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes Reasoning Arena, a framework that routes non-diverse reward groups in RLVR to a judge that runs head-to-head trace tournaments, addressing the problem of uninformative group-level rewards. This recovers gradient signal when all sampled traces receive identical outcome rewards.

entry.title: Learning to Attack and Defend: Adaptive Red Teaming of Language Models via GRPO

author.name: Blake Bullwinkel, Eugenia Kim, Amanda Minnich, Mark Russinovich

entry.summary: Introduces AdvGRPO, a co-training framework making GRPO viable for joint attacker-defender red-teaming of language models using dense multi-channel rewards and decoupled advantage normalization. It progresses through a curriculum from single-turn to closed-loop multi-turn attacks.

entry.title: The Routing Plateau: Understanding and Breaking the Accuracy Limits of LLM Routers

author.name: Yifan Lu, Qiyue Zhang, Shenrun Zhang, Zhibo Yu, Zhuang Wang, Hanjie Chen, Jiarong Xing

entry.summary: Studies 21 LLM routing methods across five benchmarks and identifies the routing plateau, where diverse methods converge to similar accuracy far below the oracle router due to a predictability bottleneck. Routers mainly learn global average performance trends rather than per-query distinctions.

entry.title: Cutting LLM Evaluation Costs with SySRs: A Bandit Algorithm that Provably Exploits Model Similarity

author.name: Zifan Lyu, Chahine Nejma, Tobias Wegel, Fanny Yang, Florian E. Dorner

entry.summary: Proposes Synchronized Successive Rejects, a bandit algorithm for best-model identification that provably exploits model response similarity via paired comparisons to cut LLM benchmarking costs. It augments classical Successive Rejects to adaptively allocate evaluation budget.

entry.title: Routine laboratory trajectories encode the onset of organ-level complications in cancer

author.name: Jannik L\"ubberstedt, Krischan Braitsch, Jacqueline Lammert, Christof Winter, Florian Gabriel, Tristan Lemke, Christopher Zirn, Markus Graf, Friedrich Puttkammer, Hartmut H\"antze, Johannes Moll, Anirudh Narayanan, Andrei Zhukov, Fabian Drexel, Zeineb Ben Chaaben, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Su Hwan Kim, Marion H\"ogner, Jan Kirschke, Florian Bassermann, Marcus Makowski, Christian Wachinger, Lisa Adams, Keno Bressem

entry.summary: Trains a transformer on 2.78M longitudinal lab measurements from 3,905 cancer patients to predict two-year onset of 162 treatment-associated complications across eight clinical categories. It outperforms non-sequential baselines, showing lab trajectories encode evolving organ-level complications.

entry.title: DynaCF: Mitigating Shortcut Learning in Reward Models via Dynamic Counterfactual Sensitivity

author.name: Fengyuan Liu, Yongliang Miao, Zirui He, Yanguang Liu, Fei Sun, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: DynaCF mitigates shortcut learning in reward models by dynamically downweighting samples with high shortcut sensitivity, measured online via counterfactual perturbations and margin shifts. Improves reliance on genuine quality signals. Matters for robust RLHF reward modeling.

entry.title: PBSD: Privileged Bayesian Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Credit Assignment

author.name: Yang Tian, Rui Wang, Xumeng Wen, Junjie Li, Shizhao Sun, Lei Song, Jiang Bian, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: PBSD performs fine-grained credit assignment in long-horizon agentic RL by using a Bayes-calibrated self-distillation that measures trajectory quality via the posterior-to-prior probability ratio of the verified answer. Targets multi-turn search agents under sparse rewards. Matters for training capable LLM agents.

entry.title: Benchmarking Empirical Privacy Protection for Adaptations of Large Language Models

author.name: Bart{\l}omiej Marek, Lorenzo Rossi, Vincent Hanke, Xun Wang, Michael Backes, Franziska Boenisch, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: Benchmarks empirical privacy protection of differentially private LLM adaptations using strong attacks (membership inference, canary extraction) across data distributions from exact pretraining overlap to OOD. Reveals that DP guarantees can be undermined by pretraining interdependencies. Matters for trustworthy private ML.

entry.title: Rethinking the Divergence Regularization in LLM RL

author.name: Jiarui Yao, Xiangxin Zhou, Penghui Qi, Wee Sun Lee, Liefeng Bo, Tianyu Pang

entry.summary: Rethinks divergence regularization in LLM RL, arguing that importance ratios poorly proxy distributional shift in long-tailed vocabularies and that DPPO's hard divergence mask is suboptimal, motivating a softer trust-region approach based on token probability shifts. Matters for stable off-policy LLM RL. Methodological improvement to PPO/GRPO-style training.

entry.title: Large-scale empirical tuning and comparison of default optimizers for variational inference

author.name: Trevor Campbell, Jonathan H. Huggins, Kyurae Kim, Charles C. Margossian

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale empirical evaluation of 56 adaptive stochastic optimizers for black-box variational inference to establish state-of-the-art tuning-free posterior approximation. Aims to make BBVI a genuinely black-box method by removing problem-specific tuning.

entry.title: MilliVid: Hierarchical Latents for Long-Range Consistency in Video Generation

author.name: Ishaan Preetam Chandratreya, David Charatan, Basile Van Hoorick, Sergey Zakharov, Vitor Guizilini, Phillip Isola, Vincent Sitzmann

entry.summary: Introduces MilliVid, which improves long-range consistency in video generation via coarse-to-fine rollout in a multi-scale hierarchical token space, where coarse levels capture layout and semantics and finer levels add texture. Mitigates the impractical transformer sequence lengths required for consistent long videos.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Model Parallel Decoding via Product-of-Experts Bridge

author.name: Juntong Shi, Brian L. Trippe, Jure Leskovec, Stefano Ermon, Minkai Xu

entry.summary: Proposes PoE-Bridge, a decoding framework that bridges diffusion and autoregressive language model distributions via a Product-of-Experts intermediate distribution, improving both parallel-decoding speed and quality. Reduces the particle cost of importance-sampling-based DLM-AR bridging.

entry.title: Building Comparative Motivation Profiles with Instrumental Interventions

author.name: David Vella Zarb, Rustem Turtayev, Taywon Min, Jinghua Ou, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Introduces a symmetric intervention framework to distinguish strategic self-preservation from researcher-expectation sensitivity in LLM alignment faking, targeting instrumental processes like consequence-tracking. Probes the construct validity of motivation inferences in safety evaluations.

entry.title: DyCo-RL: Dynamic Cross-Modal Coordination for Visual Reasoning

author.name: Hangui Lin, Yan Shu, Zhengyang Liang, Chi Liu, Xiangrui Liu, Minghao Qin, Teng Long, Zheng Liu, Nicu Sebe

entry.summary: DyCo-RL studies how multimodal LLMs fail to alternate between extracting visual evidence and synthesizing text during chain-of-thought reasoning, and proposes a reinforcement learning method that rewards dynamic cross-modal coordination. It addresses a credit-assignment gap in RLVR for visual reasoning.

entry.title: CapRL++: Unified Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for Dense Image and Video Captioning

author.name: Penghui Yang, Long Xing, Xiaoyi Dong, Yuhang Zang, Yuhang Cao, Yibin Wang, Yujie Zhou, Jiazi Bu, Jianze Liang, Qidong Huang, Jiaqi Wang, Feng Wu, Dahua Lin

entry.summary: CapRL++ applies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to open-ended dense image and video captioning, using a reference-free framework to avoid memorization from supervised fine-tuning. It targets more diverse, generalizable captions for VLM pretraining.

entry.title: POTATR: A Lightweight Image-to-Graph Model for Page-Level Table Extraction

author.name: Brandon Smock, Libin Liang, Max Sokolov, Amrit Ramesh, Valerie Faucon-Morin, Tayyibah Khanam, Maury Courtland

entry.summary: POTATR is a lightweight 29M-parameter image-to-graph model for page-level table extraction that outperforms frontier MLLMs on PubTables-v2 while running over 130x faster at far lower cost with spatially grounded outputs. It extends the Table Transformer for contextualized extraction.

entry.title: SIMPLE: Simulation-Based Policy Learning and Evaluation for Humanoid Loco-manipulation

author.name: Songlin Wei, Zhenhao Ni, Jie Liu, Zhenyu Zhao, Junjie Ye, Hongyi Jing, Junkai Xia, Xiawei Liu, Michael Leong, Liang Heng, Di Huang, Yue Wang

entry.summary: SIMPLE is a unified simulation testbed for humanoid loco-manipulation coupling MuJoCo dynamics with IsaacSim rendering, providing 60 tasks, 50 scenes, and over 1000 objects plus data generation pipelines. It addresses the lack of scalable reproducible benchmarks for whole-body humanoid evaluation.

entry.title: Two Bridges, One Pathway: From VLMs to Generalizable VLAs with Embodied Trajectory-Coupled Data

author.name: Linqi Yin, Shiduo Zhang, Shenling Qiu, Chenxin Li, Zhaoyang Fu, Lei Xiao, Xiang Wang, Chenchen Yang, Zhe Xu, Pengfang Qian, Jingjing Gong, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: This work bridges the gap between vision-language models and vision-language-action models using embodied trajectory-coupled data as intermediate supervision, allowing gradual transfer rather than crossing perception and action gaps at once. It aims to preserve pretrained generalization while learning robot control.

entry.title: Video2Sim2Real: Full-Stack Autonomous Dexterous Skill Acquisition from a Single Human Video

author.name: Yunhai Han, Jianuo Qiu, Linhao Bai, Ziyu Xiao, Zihang Zeng, Yangcen Liu, Zhaodong Yang, Shalin Jain, Wenrui Ma, Jiaqi Fu, Yuqian Zheng, Manisha Natarajan, Muhammad Zubair Irshad, Kenneth Shaw, Matthew Gombolay, Zsolt Kira, Harish Ravichandar

entry.summary: Video2Sim2Real is a full-stack framework for autonomous dexterous skill acquisition from a single human manipulation video, reconstructing a simulator-ready digital twin and leveraging object-centric keyframes for supervision rather than treating extracted robot motion as a reliable reference. It addresses perception errors and embodiment gaps.

entry.title: Efficient tradeoffs and the safety-usefulness tradeoff model

author.name: Buck

entry.summary: This post articulates a safety-usefulness tradeoff model where developers face limited willingness to sacrifice usefulness for safety, distinguishing between pushing out the Pareto frontier via safety tech and increasing the safety budget. It examines when this model holds and how risk-reduction strategies are affected when its assumptions fail.

entry.title: Stress-testing medical large language models reveals latent safety pathology beyond benchmark accuracy

author.name: Yuan Shen, Xiaojun Wu, Linghua Yu

entry.summary: AI-MASLD adapts metabolic stress-testing logic from hepatology to stress-audit clinical LLMs across 240 cases with narrative perturbations, revealing safety failure modes hidden by clean benchmark accuracy. It shows models that perform uniformly well diverge sharply under realistic narrative stress.

entry.title: UniQL: Towards Dialect-Universal Benchmarking for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Jianling Gao, Chongyang Tao, Jiayuan Bai, Liu Yang, Xuanguang Pan, Jinrui Liu, Shihao Xing, Xiaohan Xu, Jie Liang, Shuai Ma

entry.summary: UniQL is a human-verified cross-dialect text-to-SQL benchmark aligning 1,534 questions to executable queries across 16 SQL dialects (24,544 queries) with shared intents and schemas for controlled generalization evaluation. It addresses over-reliance on SQLite in existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Online Agent-as-a-Judge: Situation-Generating Evaluation for Interactive Agents

author.name: Hyogon Ryu, Jeonghwan Kim, Yewon Lim, Chaeun Lee, Jeongwook Kim, Donghoon Ham

entry.summary: Online Agent-as-a-Judge is a situation-generating evaluation framework that deploys an in-world evaluator agent to actively interact with target social agents, eliciting capabilities (like conflict handling) that passive trajectory scoring would miss. It improves evaluation of interactive social agents.

entry.title: PAEC: Position-Aware Entropy Calibration for LLM Reasoning in RLVR

author.name: Shumeng Yang, Yisu Liu, Jiayi Zheng, Zhaohui Yang, Linjing Li

entry.summary: PAEC introduces position-aware entropy calibration for RLVR reasoning, applying a soft mask from local top-p entropy and top-two candidate competition with an anchor-based lower-bound penalty to prevent entropy collapse only at decision-relevant tokens. It improves exploration efficiency over uniform global entropy regularization.

entry.title: Item Response Scaling Laws: A Measurement Theory Approach for Efficient and Generalizable Neural Scaling Estimation

author.name: Sang Truong, Yuheng Tu, Rylan Schaeffer, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Introduces Item Response Scaling Laws integrating Item Response Theory with scaling laws to disentangle latent model ability from question difficulty, reducing parameter complexity from O(MxN) to O(M+N) and enabling efficient, generalizable scaling estimation. Avoids prohibitively expensive evaluations across thousands of checkpoints.

entry.title: WhiFlash: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Token-Level Cross-Paradigm Routing

author.name: Young D. Kwon, Miles Williams, Rui Li, Alexandros Kouris, Stylianos I. Venieris

entry.summary: WhiFlash is the first cross-paradigm speculative decoding method that unifies autoregressive and diffusion-based parallel drafting under a single token-level router, adapting to fluctuating drafting accuracy within a sequence. It targets faster LLM inference for agentic workloads.

entry.title: STELLAR: Spatio-Temporal Environmental Learning with Latent Alignment and Refinement for Long-Tailed Species Distribution Modeling

author.name: Shufeng Kong, Tao Yu, Yuanyuan Wei, Caihua Liu, Junwen Bai, Yingheng Wang, Marc Grimson, Daniel Fink, Carla P. Gomes

entry.summary: STELLAR is a spatio-temporal framework for joint species distribution modeling that learns a shared latent space with alignment and refinement to handle dynamic environmental drivers, non-linear community structure, and severe long-tail rare-species imbalance. It addresses limitations of static-covariate approaches in biodiversity monitoring.

entry.title: Intrinsic Selection and Particle Resampling for Inference-Time Scaling Beyond Domain Verifiability

author.name: Giorgio Giannone, Mustafa Eyceoz, Shabana Baig, Shivchander Sudalairaj, Anna C. Doris, Faez Ahmed, Akash Srivastava, Kai Xu

entry.summary: Proposes using intrinsic statistics of parallel sample sets (length-adjusted tail entropy) as a verifier-free quality signal for inference-time scaling beyond verifiable domains. Uses these statistics as a difficulty gate for adaptive compute allocation.

entry.title: Context-Fractured Decomposition Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents: Exploiting Artifact Provenance Gaps

author.name: Xiaofeng Lin, Yukai Yang, Daniel Guo, Sahil Arun Nale, Charles Fleming, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces context-fractured decomposition attacks exploiting artifact provenance gaps in tool-using LLM agents, where jailbreak enforcement is fragmented across tools and time without provenance tracking. Shows multi-turn jailbreak assumptions break down in realistic agent pipelines.

entry.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via APIs 4: Tabular Data

author.name: Toan Tran, Arturs Backurs, Zinan Lin, Victor Reis, Li Xiong, Sergey Yekhanin

entry.summary: Extends the Private Evolution framework to tabular data, introducing Tab-PE for differentially private synthetic tabular generation that captures high-order correlations via tabular-specialized evolutionary operators. It addresses gaps where prior methods only handle low-order marginals.

entry.title: Where the Score Lives: A Wavelet View of Diffusion

author.name: Emma Finn, Binxu Wang, T. Anderson Keller, Demba E. Ba

entry.summary: Provides an analytically solvable parameterization of diffusion score functions via a 2D orthogonal wavelet basis, deriving optimal score functions in terms of data moments. It offers architecture-agnostic insight into how the score localizes in scale and space.

entry.title: Can LLMs extract scientific consensus? A case study in high-temperature superconductivity

author.name: Mouyang Cheng, Wenhao He, Zhuotao Jin, Bowen Yu, Ju Li, Boris Kozinsky, Yao Wang, Pavel Volkov, Liangzi Deng, Ching-Wu Chu, Xiao-Gang Wen, Mingda Li

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can recover latent scientific consensus in the contested field of high-temperature superconductivity, building a structured knowledge graph from nearly 18,000 highly-cited publications linking competing mechanisms and evidence. Tests LLM ability to synthesize debated scientific knowledge. Matters for AI-assisted scientific synthesis.

entry.title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves

author.name: Hangfan Zhang, Shao Zhang, Kangcong Li, Chen Zhang, Yang Chen, Yiqun Zhang, Lei Bai, Shuyue Hu

entry.summary: Self-Harness is a paradigm where an LLM agent improves its own operating harness without human engineers, via an iterative loop of weakness mining, refinement, and validation. It addresses the poor scalability of human-engineered, model-specific harnesses.

entry.title: End-to-End Optimization of Incoherent Imaging for Classification Under Detector-Limited Readout

author.name: Archer Wang, Joshua Chen, Sachin Vaidya, Marin Solja\v{c}i\'c

entry.summary: This paper develops a formalism for when end-to-end co-optimized incoherent optical front-ends (phase masks) outperform conventional lenses for classification, proving gains arise mainly under constrained detector readout.
