entry.summary: GD-MIL is a grade-disentangled multiple instance learning approach for predicting prostate cancer biochemical recurrence from whole slide images plus clinical data. The paper notably establishes a rigorous out-of-fold benchmark to avoid inflated concordance from checkpoint selection.

entry.title: Adversarial Attack and Disturbance Detection by Hadamard-Coded Output Representations for Object Detection and Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Lucas G\"ornhardt, Timo Bartels, Niklas Schwarz, Tim Fingscheidt

entry.summary: This work extends Hadamard-coded output representations to object detection and semantic segmentation for adversarial attack and disturbance detection, introducing a novel decoding procedure exploiting codeword redundancy. It improves calibration and detection over one-hot encodings.

entry.title: Cooperative Long Rope Skipping via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zihao Wang, Shijie Peng, Kerui Wu, Yu Huang, Ruiqi Xue, Dong Liu, Tian Xu, Lei Yuan, Yang Yu

entry.summary: Marope uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to enable humanoid robots to cooperatively perform long rope skipping, requiring two rope turners to coordinate with a jumper. It explores precise multi-participant coordination, an underexplored area in humanoid sports.

entry.title: Learning from Human Driving: A Human-in-the-Loop Online Behavior Cloning Framework for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuhong Shi, Jianyi Liu, Lihang Sun, Li Li, Xudong Dong

entry.summary: HiL-OBC is a human-in-the-loop online behavior cloning framework for autonomous driving that integrates large foundation model perception with human expert intervention to handle long-tail and complex interaction scenarios. It aims to overcome distribution shift and causal confusion.

entry.title: Real-Time and Accurate Collision-Free Teleoperation via Differentiable Constraint-Based Trajectory Planning

author.name: Max Grobbel, Tristan Schneider, Daniel Fl\"ogel, S\"oren Hohmann

entry.summary: This paper presents a real-time collision-free teleoperation method using differentiable constraint-based trajectory planning with exact convex-set collision-avoidance constraints, avoiding sphere approximations. It enhances operator end-effector control while preventing self-collisions and obstacle collisions.

entry.title: How valuable are weak AI safety regulations?

author.name: MichaelDickens

entry.summary: This post analyzes how weak or light-touch AI safety regulations might reduce extinction risk, examining direct effects like GPU export restrictions and mandatory testing, downsides, and specific regulation categories as stepping stones toward stronger international agreements. It weighs marginal benefits of incremental policy.

entry.title: Real-world grounding in agentic AI

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Amazon Science post describes the shift from knowledge-focused foundation models to agentic AI acting in the physical world, introducing Project Eluna for fulfillment center operations and emphasizing real-world grounding to overcome hallucination in physical environments. It frames 2026 as the year of physical AI agents.

entry.title: From Human Guidance to Autonomy: Agent Skill System for End-to-End LLM Deployment on Spatial NPUs

author.name: Jiajie Li, Erwei Wang, Zhiru Zhang, Samuel Bayliss

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage methodology for deploying LLMs end-to-end on spatial NPUs, progressing from human-guided agent development to agent autonomy, instantiated on AMD XDNA 2 with notable prefill and decode speedups. Targets energy-efficient edge LLM inference.

entry.title: Sample-Efficient Post-Training for LEGO Spatial-Physics Reasoning

author.name: Yuhuan Yuan, Zhouliang Yu, Minghao Liu, Weiyang Liu, Ge Lin Kan

entry.summary: Identifies PhysHack, a failure mode where LLM-generated LEGO assemblies satisfy physical validity yet are geometrically or semantically wrong, and proposes a model-based data selection plus PVPO, a sample-efficient RL method coupling physical feasibility with voxel-space geometric rewards. Shows physical validity alone is insufficient for grounded assembly.

entry.title: DOME: Learning Transferable Domain Variables from Sparse Supervision for Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Xiaoran Xu, Yifan Xu, Yupeng Wu, Xiaoshan Yang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: Proposes DOME, a domain encoder for test-time adaptation that explicitly models each sample's domain in a zero-shot manner using vision-language pretraining, parameterizing domains as distributional variables with a momentum-updated sparse domain bank. Injects explicit domain cues so even basic entropy minimization adapts robustly.

entry.title: Chiaroscuro Attention: Spending Compute in the Dark

author.name: Prateek Kumar Sikdar

entry.summary: CHIAR-Former routes each token to one of three operators (DCT spectral mixing, RBF kernel mixing, or full self-attention) based on per-token spectral entropy. The work discovers routing collapse where the router rejects RBF, finding spectral mixing and attention complementary and sufficient.

entry.title: SpaceVLN: A Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation Agent with Online Spatial Cognitive Memory and Reasoning

author.name: Yucheng Deng, Pingrui Lai, Xinhai Li, Chenjia Bai, Xiaoheng Deng, Chengnuo Sun, Xuelong Li, Hua Yang

entry.summary: SpaceVLN is a zero-shot vision-and-language navigation agent using spatial cognitive memory and task-guided spatial reasoning in a stagewise closed-loop framework. It moves beyond local visual cues and linear history reasoning to capture spatial structure of explored regions.

entry.title: ATM: Action-Consistency Transfer Matrix for Diagnosing and Improving Latent World Models

author.name: Jiaheng Chen

entry.summary: ATM, an Action-Consistency Transfer Matrix, diagnoses whether latent world models preserve planning-relevant action semantics using lightweight post-hoc probes instead of slow planner-coupled evaluation. It produces an interpretable matrix revealing representational quality.

entry.title: CT-VAM: A Cerebello-Thalamic-Inspired Vision-Action Model for Efficient Visuomotor Control

author.name: Jiacheng Li, Yize Guo, Jiabin Guo, Qingchen Liu, Jiahu Qin

entry.summary: Proposes CT-VAM, a cerebello-thalamic-inspired vision-action model for efficient task-conditioned visuomotor control that predicts action chunks from dual-view observations and a lightweight task condition. It separates high-level semantic reasoning from fast local execution, enabling a cloud-edge paradigm.

entry.title: An 84-Format Numeric Catalog with Bit-Exact Conformance Vectors: A Vendor-Neutral Reference for FP8, BF16, MXFP4, and Microscaling Formats

author.name: Dmitrii Vasilev

entry.summary: Provides a vendor-neutral catalog of 84 numeric formats across 13 families with six bit-exact conformance packs for FP8, BF16, MXFP4, and microscaling formats, plus an IEEE P3109 cross-walk. It aims to help engineers diagnose silent divergences when porting models across accelerators.

entry.title: Temporal Coverage over Density: Parsimonious Training-Set Design for ML Climate Downscaling

author.name: Karandeep Singh, Stefan Rahimi, Chad W. Thackeray, Stephen Cropper, Alex Hall

entry.summary: Compares training-year selection strategies for ML climate downscaling under fixed data budgets using the CESM2 ensemble over the western US. It finds temporal coverage across the climate trajectory matters more than data density for capturing forced response and variability.

entry.title: Physically Consistent Null Space Alignment for Detection of Low-Magnitude False Data Injection Attacks

author.name: Xin Li, Chenhan Xiao, Jonathan Cohen, Aviad Elyashar, Yang Weng, Rami Puzis

entry.summary: Proposes Physically Consistent Null Space Alignment (PCNSA) to detect stealthy low-magnitude false data injection attacks in power-system state estimation that hide in the pseudo-null space. It preserves geometric correspondence between physical and measurement-derived null spaces.

entry.title: Disentanglement with Holographic Reduced Representations

author.name: Jhonny J. Velasquez Olivera, Christo K. Thomas, Walid Saad

entry.summary: Proposes treating disentangled representations as symbolic structures using Holographic Reduced Representations, enabling compositional symbolic disentanglement while maintaining differentiability without complex architectures. Alternative to VAE/GAN-based continuous disentanglement. Contribution to representation learning.

entry.title: Barycentric Projections of Optimal Transport Plans on Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Kisung You

entry.summary: Develops a framework for barycentric projections of optimal transport couplings on Riemannian manifolds, converting probabilistic couplings into deterministic maps via conditional Frechet means. Establishes optimality under squared geodesic loss and a variance measure for map-induced couplings.

entry.title: A Comparison of SSL-Based Feature Extractors and Back-End Classifiers for Spoofing Detection: A Multi-Corpus Training and Cross-Linguistic Analysis

author.name: Anh-Tuan Dao, Driss Matrouf, Mickael Rouvier, Nicholas Evans

entry.summary: Benchmarks four self-supervised feature extractors paired with four back-end classifiers for voice spoofing detection across multi-corpus training and cross-linguistic evaluation. Exposes a domain bias in ASVspoof 5 where naive data scaling degrades performance.

entry.title: SNN-MLIR: An MLIR Dialect for Compiling Neuromorphic SNNs from NIR to Bare-Metal C

author.name: Alejandro Garc\'ia Gener, Alvaro Roll\'on de Pinedo

entry.summary: Presents snn-mlir, an out-of-tree MLIR dialect for spiking neural networks plus a NIR-to-MLIR-to-C compilation bridge that provides a shared, transformable compiler representation for deploying trained SNNs to bare-metal C. Fills the gap left by the Neuromorphic Intermediate Representation, which describes networks but offers no deployment path.

entry.title: From Holistic Evaluation to Structured Criteria: Rubrics Across the Evolving LLM Landscape

author.name: Hao Chen, Ziyu Han, Yukun Yan, Qingfu Zhu, Maosong Sun, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Introduces rubrics as a unifying framework spanning LLM evaluation, reinforcement learning, and safety alignment, characterizing their recurrence as a response to paradigm shifts. Systematically organizes rubric construction and optimization across these threads.

entry.title: Civil Court Simulation with Large Language Models

author.name: Yifan Chen, Haitao Li, Kaiyuan Zhang, Yueyue Wu, Qingyao Ai, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent court simulation framework for Chinese civil cases organized around a five-stage trial procedure with memory and statute retrieval. It extends LLM court simulation beyond the commonly studied criminal cases to harder civil litigation.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Masking for Robust Silent Speech Synthesis Using sEMG and Lipreading

author.name: Eder del Blanco, David Gimeno-G\'omez, Eva Navas, Carlos-D. Mart\'inez-Hinarejos, Inma Hern\'aez

entry.summary: Proposes a masked multimodal speech synthesis framework combining surface electromyography and lipreading for silent speech interfaces, using modality masking during training for robustness to sensor failure or degradation. It targets assistive speech restoration for impaired laryngeal voice.

entry.title: Do VLMs See What Sensors Feel? A Scalable Expert-Guided Design for Wheelchair Accessibility Assessment from Street View

author.name: Dongdong Wang, Alina Hagen, Isabelle Gatmaitan, Hao Zhou, Yiwen Dong, Shabboo Valipoor, Vivian W. H. Wong, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: Examines whether VLMs can identify wheelchair accessibility barriers from Google Street View imagery, proposing an expert-guided retrieval-augmented framework combining images, ADA guidance, and rubrics. It uses a campus-scale dataset linking GSV locations with GPS-derived wheelchair dwell behavior.

entry.title: Leveraging Morphology for Historical Script Metrological Analysis

author.name: Malamatenia Vlachou Efstathiou, Rapha\"el Baena, Dominique Stutzmann, Mathieu Aubry

entry.summary: This work uses morphological script analysis with a transformer detector and prototype-based line reconstruction to learn character prototypes from historical manuscripts, enabling scalable paleographic measurements. It bridges handwritten text recognition and interpretable visual metrology.

entry.title: Impedance MPC for Physical Human-Robot Interaction: Predictive Disturbance Rejection with Joint-Limit Safety

author.name: Yongyan Cao, Jinshan Tang

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-layer Impedance MPC for physical human-robot interaction that analytically cancels dynamics in one layer and solves a fast convex QP in the other to provide compliant safety with joint-limit constraints. It resolves steady-state position errors in classical impedance control.

entry.title: Autonomous Obstacle Removal for Excavators through Policy Learning with Particle Simulation

author.name: Yuki Kadokawa, Sandro M. Alcantara Tacora, Taro Abe, Daisuke Endo, Genki Yamauchi, Takeshi Hashimoto, Takamitsu Matsubara

entry.summary: This work develops policy learning with particle simulation for autonomous obstacle removal by excavators, exploiting the observation that obstacle burial depth governs both task difficulty and simulation cost to manage computational expense. It enables state-dependent excavation across changing soil-obstacle conditions.

entry.title: Beyond Pass Rate: A Multilingual, Execution-Grounded Evaluation of Open Code LLMs

author.name: Sayed Erfan Arefin

entry.summary: This work presents a large-scale execution-grounded evaluation of 9 open coding LLMs across 12 languages and 2,707 LeetCode problems, totaling over 325k jobs. It finds even the best open model reaches only 23.6% correctness versus a 57.2% human reference, exposing language and failure-mode variation.

entry.title: TRL-Bench: Standardizing Cross-Paradigm Representation-Level Evaluation of Tabular Encoders

author.name: Wei Pang, Xiangru Jian, Hehan Li, Zhixuan Yu, Alex Xue, Jinyang Li, Zhengyuan Dong, Xinjian Zhao, Hao Xu, Chao Zhang, Reynold Cheng, M. Tamer \"Ozsu, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: TRL-Bench is a multi-granular benchmark standardizing cross-paradigm representation-level evaluation of tabular encoders, exporting row/column/table embeddings probed by shared lightweight heads across three suites. It enables direct comparison of encoders from different training paradigms.

entry.title: From 0-to-1 to 1-to-N: Reproducible Engineering Evidence for MetaAI Recursive Self-Design

author.name: Dun Li, Jiatao Li, Hongzhi Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes an operational evidence framework with four criteria (inspectable target system, meta-level modifier, feedback-directed selection, recursive continuation) to assess recursive self-design in AI, mapping systems like Darwin Goedel Machine, STOP, and ShinkaEvolve against them. It treats MetaAI as a human-seeded, AI-expanded development pattern.

entry.title: ABLE: Representing and Mapping LLMs via Attribution-Based Large-model Embedding

author.name: Zirui Wang, Yusen Hou, Shaofeng Liang, Bowen Tian, Yanlin Zhang, Wenshuo Chen, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Proposes ABLE, an attribution-based embedding framework for representing and comparing LLMs across heterogeneous architectures and tokenizers, useful for provenance auditing and model selection. Tackles the challenge of comparing models with different internals or similar behaviors.

entry.title: DIYHealth Suite: Dataset, Model, and Benchmark for Health Management at Home

author.name: Changshuo Liu, Junran Wu, Zhongle Xie, Wenqiao Zhang, Kaiping Zheng, Jiaqi Zhu, Qingpeng Cai, Ooi Gene Anne, Marcus Chun Jin Tan, Jianwei Yin, James Wei Luen Yip, Beng Chin Ooi

entry.summary: Presents DIYHealth Suite, a dataset, model, and benchmark for home-based generative-AI health management using portable devices, addressing heterogeneous data and lack of standardized evaluation. Targets accessible care outside clinical settings.

entry.title: MetaEvo: A Meta-Optimization Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution

author.name: Bowen Ren, Heyan Huang, Yinghao Li, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes MetaEvo, a two-stage meta-optimization framework for continual agent evolution that improves how an LLM learns from task experience via preference-based principle abstraction and experience reuse, rather than only what it stores. Aims to overcome early performance plateaus of static agents.

entry.title: SENTRY: Statistical Reliability Analysis of Vision Transformers Under Soft Errors

author.name: Pramit Kumar Bhaduri, Mahdi Taheri, Samira Nazari, Maksim Jenihhin, Christian Herglotz, Michael Hubner

entry.summary: Presents SENTRY, a statistical fault-injection framework for vision transformers using finite-population sampling theory to bound failure rates within 1% at 99% confidence using only thousands of samples. Achieves up to 10,700x reduction in experimental cost versus exhaustive campaigns.

entry.title: MemoVAD: Resource-Efficient Video Anomaly Detection via Dynamic Semantic Memory in Edge Computing Scenarios

author.name: Guo Li, Jiandian Zeng, Yang Li, Zihao Peng, Ke Chen, Tian Wang

entry.summary: MemoVAD is an edge-cloud collaborative framework for video anomaly detection that runs a lightweight detector on-device and selectively invokes VLM semantics via an uncertainty-aware gating policy. It targets resource-efficient deployment for real-world surveillance.

entry.title: Agentic multi-fidelity learning of quasiparticle and excitonic properties

author.name: Arnab Neogi, Aaron Forde, Christopher A. Lane, Sergei Tretiak, Jian-Xin Zhu

entry.summary: This work introduces an agent-guided multi-fidelity framework that detects and corrects numerical instabilities in GW-Bethe-Salpeter calculations of quasiparticle and excitonic properties in strained MoS2-WS2 bilayers. It identifies spike-like excursions and near-zero-gap collapse across stacking and strain configurations.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution for LLM-Agent Workflows: An Integrated Five-Dimension Method

author.name: Faisal Fareed

entry.summary: This paper presents a cost-aware speculative execution method for LLM-agent workflows that launches downstream operations on predicted upstream inputs, pricing each speculation in real dollars and using an expected-value rule with a single latency-versus-cost dial. It targets reclaiming idle time in chained agent operations.

entry.title: SafeECGMatch: Calibration-Aware Joint Frequency and Time Space Semi-Supervised Learning for Open-Set ECG Classification

author.name: Hongkyu Koh, Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: SafeECGMatch is a calibration-aware semi-supervised learning framework for open-set ECG classification, handling out-of-distribution anomalies in unlabeled clinical data via a dual-branch time-frequency architecture. It addresses overconfident pseudo-labeling under label distribution mismatch.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for CBCT-Based Detection of Temporomandibular Joint Osteoarthritis

author.name: Shradhdha Trivedi, Vrundan Sojitra, Mariela Padilla

entry.summary: This study evaluates how DINO-family self-supervised vision transformers (including radiology-pretrained RAD-DINO) transfer to CBCT-based detection of temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis. A slice-based pipeline with attention-based multiple instance learning aggregates frozen or partially adapted ViT features for patient-level classification.

entry.title: Latent Diffusion Policy: Shaping Latent Spaces for Diffusion-Based Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhexuan Zhou, Yichen Lai, Jinhao Zhang, Huizhe Li, Youmin Gong, Jie Mei

entry.summary: Latent Diffusion Policy decouples scene understanding from trajectory generation in diffusion-based robot manipulation by performing flow matching in a shaped latent space via a conditional VAE encoder. This simplifies learning for tasks requiring precise multi-arm temporal coordination.

entry.title: PACT: Learning Diverse Diagnostic Strategies via Privileged Synthesis and Branch Consensus

author.name: Gen Li, Yuanze Hu, Zhichao Yang, Qingchen Yu, Jianwei Lv, Yue Guo, Yujing Liu, Faguo Wu, Hongwei Zheng, Xiandong Li, Bo Yuan, Yifan Sun, Zhaoxin Fan

entry.summary: PACT trains LLM medical agents to flexibly use multiple diagnostic reasoning paradigms via supervised multi-paradigm dialogue synthesis and consensus-based branch training. A doctor-patient-supervisor pipeline produces validated dialogues under information constraints.

entry.title: TLDR: Compressing Audio Tokens for Efficient Autoregressive Text-to-Speech

author.name: Yejin Lee, Junwon Moon, Hyoeun Kim, Hyunjin Choi, Heeseung Kim, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: TLDR accelerates codec-based autoregressive TTS by grouping consecutive audio tokens into compact latent patches, shifting causal modeling from token-level to patch-level sequences. This reduces the long-sequence and KV-cache bottleneck of speech token modeling.

entry.title: See More, Think Deeper: Query-Expanded Visual Evidence and Answer-Clue Guided Reflection for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Shuning Wang, Zhiheng Wu, YiNuo Lu, Naiming Liu, Chen Jia, Bowen Liu, Shuo Nie, Weijie Zhu, Yumeng Zhang

entry.summary: CoVER improves long-video understanding by dynamically gathering query-expanded visual evidence (See More) and verifying draft answers with answer-specific visual feedback (Think Deeper). It shifts long-video QA from answer-centric generation to evidence-grounded reflection.

entry.title: Brain-Prompt Injection: A Route-Safety Audit for BCI-LLM Agents

author.name: Jianwei Tai

entry.summary: Defines brain-prompt injection, a new attack surface where BCI-to-agent pipelines can be manipulated via signal-side perturbations and context injections while monitors remain blind. Proposes a Route-Safety Audit Contract with formal separation theorems for auditing such systems.

entry.title: Scaling Neural Network Verification with Tensor Parallelism and Fully Sharded Data Parallelism

author.name: Sergei Vorobyov, Eugene Ilyushin

entry.summary: Adapts tensor parallelism and fully sharded data parallelism from large-scale training to formal neural network verification frameworks (auto_LiRPA, alpha-beta-CROWN), achieving roughly 2x peak-memory reduction. It addresses the GPU memory bottleneck in bound-propagation verification.

entry.title: Safe-RULE: Safe Reinforcement UnLEarning

author.name: Shixiong Jiang, Taozheng Zhu, Fanxin Kong

entry.summary: Proposes Safe-RULE, a safe reinforcement unlearning framework that removes the influence of poisoned data in offline safe RL without retraining from scratch. It accounts for both task performance and safety constraints when unlearning malicious samples.

entry.title: MeCo: One-Step MeanFlow-based Corrector for Multi-Channel Speech Separation

author.name: Dohwan Kim, Jung-Woo Choi

entry.summary: Proposes MeCo, a one-step MeanFlow-based generative corrector that maps discriminative multi-channel speech separation outputs onto the clean speech manifold in a single step. Introduces Data-Space Optimization with displacement-penalizing and endpoint SI-SDR losses to improve human listening quality.

entry.title: Observability for Delegated Execution in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Abhinav Mishra, Kumar Sharad

entry.summary: Argues delegation-scoped execution in agentic AI is not identifiable from standard audit logs and traces, which can be identical under incompatible delegation assignments. Proposes observability semantics to reconstruct what actions occurred under a given delegation across heterogeneous systems.

entry.title: Decoding Naturalistic Emotion Dynamics from the Brain: An LLM-Enhanced Regression Framework

author.name: Lemei Zhang, Peng Liu, Hans Dahle Kvadsheim, August S{\ae}tre Aasv{\ae}r, Shuer Ye, Reza Bonyadi, Maryam Ziaei, Jon Atle Gulla

entry.summary: Reframes emotion decoding from fMRI as continuous multi-target regression rather than discrete classification, using LLM-extracted sentiment profiles from a naturalistic narrative as proxies for subjective affect. It tracks overlapping emotional dimensions over time.

entry.title: GPT-Micro: A large language paradigm for accelerated, inexpensive, and thermodynamics-consistent discovery of constitutive models in manufacturing

author.name: Soumik Dutta, Kiarash Naghavi Khanghah, Sania Shree, Logan McNeil, Thomas Feldhausen, Hongyi Xu, Rajiv Malhotra

entry.summary: Introduces GPT-Micro, an LLM-driven paradigm for autonomous, data-sparse, thermodynamics-consistent discovery of constitutive models in manufacturing. It aims to enforce physical laws while reducing data and human-expertise dependence.

entry.title: GeoGNN: Time Series Geo-Localization using Two-Tower Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Toan Tran, Waqwoya Abebe, Abhishek Potnis, Supriya Chinthavali, Cyrus Shahabi, Li Xiong, Dalton Lunga

entry.summary: Formalizes time-series geolocalization (inferring geographic origin of raw time series) and proposes GeoGNN, a two-tower architecture matching temporal representations against geographic cell embeddings learned over an adjacency graph. It enables location-aware downstream applications.

entry.title: Inferring hidden forcing in a biological oscillator using Kolmogorov-Arnold networks

author.name: Julian Szereszewski, Facundo Fainstein, Leandro E. Fernandez, Gabriel B. Mindlin

entry.summary: Uses interpretable Kolmogorov-Arnold networks to reconstruct hidden muscular forcing in avian respiratory dynamics from air-sac pressure alone, recovering governing equations and a nontrivial relaxation-like oscillation. It demonstrates inferring hidden drivers from partial biological observations.

entry.title: Convolutional Sparse Coding via the Locally Competitive Algorithm on Loihi 2

author.name: Geoffrey Kasenbacher, Daniel Ruepp, Gerrit A. Ecke

entry.summary: Presents a Loihi 2 neuromorphic implementation of convolutional sparse coding via the Locally Competitive Algorithm, extending prior non-convolutional work to handle spatial structure, weight sharing, and overlapping receptive fields. It demonstrates practical sparse inference on neuromorphic hardware.

entry.title: Online Learning with Recency: Algorithms for Sliding-window Streaming Multi-armed Bandits

author.name: Vladimir Braverman, Chen Wang, Liudeng Wang, Samson Zhou

entry.summary: Studies sliding-window streaming multi-armed bandits where only the most recent W arms are valid, providing algorithms and analysis for pure exploration and regret minimization with limited memory. Captures recency effects in online learning. Theoretical contribution to bandits.

entry.title: Structural Grid Descriptors Predict Within-Task Solver Success on ARC-AGI

author.name: Ayan Pendharkar

entry.summary: Investigates whether structural grid descriptors at intermediate solver states predict success of symbolic ARC-AGI solvers, finding significant within-task predictive signal along a grid-complexity axis across two solver architectures. Large-scale empirical study. Relevant to abstract reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Beyond Convolution: Advancing Hypergraph Neural Networks with Hypergraph U-Nets

author.name: Fuli Wang, Wei Qian, Daniel L. Lau, Gonzalo R. Arce

entry.summary: Pioneers U-Net architectures for hypergraph data by designing pooling and unpooling operators derived from hierarchical clustering dendrograms, retaining structural information. Extends hypergraph neural networks beyond convolution. Architectural contribution to higher-order graph learning.

entry.title: Disturbance-Aware Aerial Robotics for Ethical Wildlife Monitoring

author.name: Mahmut Osmanovic, Isac Paulsson, Teddy Lazebnik

entry.summary: Introduces a disturbance-aware reinforcement learning framework for ethical, behaviorally-aware aerial wildlife monitoring that adapts drone behavior to minimize animal disturbance across species and platforms. Avoids reliance on costly, ethically difficult real-world training data.

entry.title: IR-SIM: A Lightweight Skill-Native Simulator for Navigation, Learning, and Benchmarking

author.name: Ruihua Han, Shuai Wang, Chengyang Li, Rui Gao, Xinyi Wang, Zhe Liu, Guoliang Li, Yupu Lu, Qi Hao, Jia Pan, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Presents IR-SIM, a lightweight skill-native navigation simulator where scenarios are fully defined by YAML configuration files specifying kinematics, collision checking, LiDAR sensing, and behavior modules. Designed for rapid prototyping, reproducible benchmarking, and LLM-supported automated robotics research.

entry.title: Aperon Technical Report: Hierarchical No-Pointer Tangent-Local Search for High-Dimensional Approximate Nearest Neighbors

author.name: Yong Fu

entry.summary: Presents HNTL, a pointerless approximate-nearest-neighbor indexing framework that partitions high-dimensional space into local grains, represents vectors as low-dimensional tangent-space coordinates, and scans them in a cache-friendly Structure-of-Arrays layout. Avoids the memory overhead and irregular access patterns of proximity graphs like HNSW.

entry.title: From A to B to A: Palindromic Zero-Shot Voice Conversion with Non-Parallel Data

author.name: Moshe Mandel, Shlomo E. Chazan

entry.summary: Presents a zero-shot voice conversion framework using KNN retrieval over WavLM representations to align non-parallel source and target speech into synthetic training pairs, supporting multilingual data without parallel corpora. Adds a speaker-verification-based loss to maintain consistent target-speaker identity.

entry.title: Dense Force Estimation with an Event-based Optical Tactile Sensor

author.name: Agis Politis, Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Valentina Cavinato

entry.summary: Introduces the first framework for dense 3D force-field reconstruction from event-based optical tactile sensors using inverse FEM on event-derived surface displacements. Enables high-temporal-resolution tactile sensing for dexterous robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Customer-Agent: Overcoming Context Limitations in Ultra-Long Shopping Trajectories via Tool-Augmented Agents and RLVR

author.name: Hongye Liu, Rongmei Lin, Anurag Kashyap, Hejie Cui, Ricardo Henao, Besnik Fetahu, Bing Yin

entry.summary: Introduces ShopTrajQA, a long-context benchmark for ultra-long shopping trajectories, and uses tool-augmented agents with RLVR to overcome LLM context limitations. Addresses multi-year customer behavior understanding with privacy-safe simulated data.

entry.title: TLRD: Teaching LLMs to Reason over Tabular Data with Tri-Level Rationale Distillation

author.name: Tianyuan Liang, Xuwei Tan, Lei Shi, Junsheng Zhong, Ziyu Hu, Tian Xie, Zhiqun Zuo, Xiaodong Yu, Xueru Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TLRD, a Tri-Level Rationale Distillation framework that converts label-only tabular data into multi-level rationales to teach LLMs to reason over and explain tabular predictions. Avoids catastrophic forgetting from label-only fine-tuning.

entry.title: PaperMentor: A Human-Centered Multi-Agent Writing Tutor for AI Research Papers on Overleaf

author.name: Jiarui Liu, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Ryan Faulkner, X. Angelo Huang, Vil\'em Zouhar, Dominik Glandorf, Isabel Dahlgren, Van Q. Truong, Rishit Dagli, Yuen Chen, Felix Leeb, Punya Syon Pandey, Yves Bicker, Suvajit Majumder, Wenyuan Jiang, Zeju Qiu, Sankalan Pal Chowdhury, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Mona Diab, Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: Presents PaperMentor, a human-centered multi-agent writing tutor delivering actionable Overleaf-native inline comments on AI research drafts while leaving writing to humans. Integrates an expert skill library curated from experienced researchers.

entry.title: PerspectiveGap: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent Orchestration Prompting

author.name: Youran Sun, Xingyu Ren, Kejia Zhang, Xinpeng Liu, Jiaxuan Guo

entry.summary: Introduces PerspectiveGap, a benchmark of 110 scenarios across 10 topologies evaluating LLMs' ability to compose orchestration prompts that convey what each sub-agent needs to know. Frames the task via a Prompt Economy principle for multi-agent systems.

entry.title: N\"ushuVoice: Reviving the Voice of Endangered N\"ushu with Pitch-Aware Text-to-Speech

author.name: Hongkun Yang, Xinhui Yi, Xiyan Zhao, Yibo Meng, Lionel Z. Wang, Lixu Wang, Yaqi Zhang, Ruiqi Chen, Xuanyue Zhao, Lanxin Zhang, Yu Zeng, Weijia Chu, Yiming Ma, Chenyu Liu, Jianghao Lin, Xin Xu

entry.summary: NushuVoice is the first text-to-speech benchmark for Nushu, an endangered phonetic script historically used by women in Hunan, China, building a sentence-level dataset and pitch-aware TTS despite extremely limited recordings. It tackles acoustic reconstruction for a critically under-resourced language.

entry.title: In-Context Learning for the Imputation of Public Opinion Data with Large Language Models

author.name: Tobias Holtdirk, Georg Ahnert, Joseph W Sakshaug, Anna-Carolina Haensch

entry.summary: Proposes using in-context learning with LLMs to impute missing survey data, evaluating across missingness mechanisms on 150 opinion variables from the American Trends Panel. It compares ICL against established statistical imputation methods like MICE PMM.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Community Perspectives on Machine Translation

author.name: Yujun Wang, Ehud Reiter, Shimei Pan, Steffen Eger, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale analysis of what four stakeholder communities (AI developers, professional translators, language learners, language service providers) post about machine translation, surfacing concerns about ethics, trust, reliability, and cost. It argues research should align with real user needs beyond benchmark accuracy.

entry.title: Can LLMs understand LilyPond? A benchmark for symbolic music generation and understanding

author.name: Matteo Spanio, Mohammad Torabi, Andrea Poltronieri, Antonio Rod\`a

entry.summary: LilyBench is a LilyPond-based benchmark that jointly evaluates symbolic music generation and understanding on open-weight LLMs, with a 200-prompt generation suite and ten understanding tasks. It uses compile rate, descriptor distributions, and a LilyBERT-based Frechet Music Distance.

entry.title: IMAGINE: Adaptive Schema-Imagery Enhanced Composition for Composed Video Retrieval

author.name: Jiale Huang, Zixu Li, Zhiwei Chen, Zhiheng Fu, Chunxiao Wang, Yupeng Hu

entry.summary: IMAGINE handles composed video retrieval where modification text describes implicit concepts not directly visible, using schema-imagery enhancement to materialize latent associations. It moves beyond explicit feature matching.

entry.title: A practical probabilistic framework for deformable image registration uncertainty in radiotherapy dose propagation

author.name: Stefan Heldmann, Sven Kuckertz, Nasim Givehchi, Thomas Coradi, Mikel Byrne, Ben Archibald-Heeren, Nils Papenberg

entry.summary: This work presents a probabilistic framework for propagating deformable image registration uncertainty into voxel-wise dose statistics and dose-volume histograms in radiotherapy. It yields interpretable confidence bounds for clinically relevant dose estimates.

entry.title: See More, Match Better: Multi-Source Feature Fusion for Two-View Correspondence Learning

author.name: Xiaojie Li, Xin Jiang, Luanyuan Dai, Jinnan Yang, Yongdong Zhang, Zechao Li

entry.summary: TriMatch is a multi-source feature fusion framework for two-view correspondence learning that jointly uses geometric, texture-semantic, and structural-semantic features to better filter outliers. It targets challenging scenes with repetitive structures and textureless regions.

entry.title: Efficient Minimal Solvers for Visual-Inertial Relative Pose Estimation in Multi-Camera Systems

author.name: Tao Li, Zhenbao Yu, Banglei Guan, Jianli Han, Weimin Lv

entry.summary: This paper proposes two efficient minimal solvers for visual-inertial relative pose estimation in multi-camera systems using IMU priors (vertical direction and rotation axis) and only four point correspondences. It reduces computational complexity for autonomous platforms.

entry.title: Optical Music Recognition for Real-World Manuscripts with Synthetic Data

author.name: Ji\v{r}\'i Mayer, Martina Dvo\v{r}\'akov\'a, Vojt\v{e}ch Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Mark\'eta Herz\'anov\'a Vlkov\'a, Filip B\'im, Pavel Pecina, Samuel \v{S}omorjai, Petr \v{Z}abi\v{c}ka, Jan Haji\v{c} jr

entry.summary: This work provides a baseline for optical music recognition on real-world handwritten piano manuscripts using synthetic data, addressing the domain gap from born-digital training datasets in resource-constrained heritage settings. It tackles complex notation under data scarcity.

entry.title: A VideoMAE-v2 Approach to Zero-Shot Traffic Accident Anticipation

author.name: Siyuan Li, Xiaoyang Bi, Mengshi Qi

entry.summary: This paper tackles zero-shot traffic accident anticipation by pairing a VideoMAE-v2 backbone with a per-frame prediction head trained only on a binary-labelled accident dataset under a sliding-window scheme. It bridges frame-level risk estimation with coarsely labelled data.

entry.title: TUDSR: Twice Upsampling-Diffusion for Higher Super-Resolution

author.name: Zhiqiang Wu, Yitong Dong, Xian Wei

entry.summary: TUDSR enables higher super-resolution beyond a diffusion model's native ratio using a twice upsampling-diffusion approach without training large native-high-resolution architectures. It addresses poor quality when upscaling ratios exceed model support.

entry.title: SemDINO: A DINOv3-Driven Network for Cross-Temporal Semantic Alignment in Change Detection

author.name: Xinyu Tong, Meihua Zhou, Jinxiao Sun, Yingjie Tang, Lei Wang

entry.summary: SemDINO is a semantic change detection network integrating frozen DINOv3 features with a CNN backbone via gated pyramid fusion, plus multi-scale temporal interaction and semantic purification. It improves cross-temporal alignment and robustness to pseudo-changes.

entry.title: OpenOpt: An Open-Source SRAM Optimizer Based on Equivalent Circuit Model

author.name: Yikai Wang, Yiheng Wu, Can Wang, Bohao Liu, Junhao Ma, Zhuohua Liu, Qinxin Mei, Shan Shen

entry.summary: OpenOpt is an open-source SRAM optimizer that jointly optimizes architecture and transistor sizing using equivalent circuit models, achieving up to 61.4x simulation speedup with high fidelity. It integrates seven optimization algorithms, with MOEA/D performing best.

entry.title: Quantitative Performance Analysis of Stopping Criteria for CMA-ES

author.name: Ryoji Tanabe

entry.summary: This paper quantitatively analyzes the behavior of 11 stopping criteria in CMA-ES on the noiseless BBOB benchmark, evaluating their effectiveness based on optimal stopping. It addresses the poorly understood role of stopping criteria, particularly under restart strategies.

entry.title: MuJoCo-Drones-Gym: A GPU-Accelerated Multi-Drone Simulator for Control and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Manan Tayal

entry.summary: MuJoCo-Drones-Gym is an open-source GPU-accelerated multi-drone simulator built on MuJoCo with Gymnasium compatibility for RL and control research. It targets the trade-off between physical fidelity, multi-agent support, and training throughput.

entry.title: Propeller-Assisted Robust 3D Hopping Robot with Hierarchical Force Allocation

author.name: Chuhan Zhang, Hongbo Zhang, Yanlin Chen, Yunxi Tang, Yun-Hui Liu, Mingyi Liu, Xiangyu Chu

entry.summary: Pro-OMEGA2 is a propeller-assisted 3D monopedal hopping robot using a hierarchical force allocation scheme to coordinate leg contact forces and propeller thrust across stance and flight phases. It improves flight-phase control authority for underactuated hopping.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Intention Prediction for Human-to-Robot Assembly Teleoperation

author.name: Fnu Heman, Yixuan Wang, Kolin Xu, Conner Wallace, John Dang, Akhil Joshi, Jun Sheng, Pinhas Ben-Tzvi, Mingyu Cai

entry.summary: This work proposes an uncertainty-aware framework for predicting human intentions in robot assembly teleoperation, using hierarchical transfer learning where a model pretrained on human hand demonstrations is fine-tuned on limited robot data. It enables timely robotic assistance during long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Can we stabilize an inverted pendulum with feedback from a time-of-flight camera?

author.name: Anthony Czubarow, Antonio Terpin, Raffaello D'Andrea

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that an inexpensive low-resolution time-of-flight camera provides sufficient feedback to reliably balance an inverted pendulum, challenging the belief that depth noise and low resolution preclude precise feedback control. It uses a canonical fast unstable dynamics benchmark.

entry.title: Dual Quaternion-Based Unscented Kalman Filter with Visual Inertial Odometry for Navigation in GPS-Denied Environments

author.name: Mohamed Khalifa, Hashim A. Hashim

entry.summary: This work presents a dual-quaternion-based unscented Kalman filter integrated with visual-inertial odometry for navigation in GPS-denied environments, using error-state formulation with unit dual quaternions and twistor parameterization for sigma points. It enables accurate pose estimation for robotics and aerospace.

entry.title: Bun's Migration from Zig to Rust as a Potential Case Study for Gradual Disempowerment

author.name: Sayhan Yalvaçer

entry.summary: This post discusses Bun's migration from Zig to memory-safe but harder-to-read Rust, performed almost entirely by Claude Code, framing it as an early case study of human control over major software becoming increasingly indirect. It connects LLM-driven code generation to gradual disempowerment concerns.

entry.title: An Effective Router for Vision-Language Model Selection

author.name: Can Wang, Shengwei Wang, Bolin Zhang, Zhiying Tu, Dianhui Chu

entry.summary: ARMS is a router for selecting among vision-language models given a query, supported by a new multimodal dataset of seven VLMs' outputs on 32,626 image-text queries. It tackles data scarcity, feature representation, and adaptation challenges for VLM selection.

entry.title: LATTEArena: An Evaluation Framework for LLM-powered Tabular Feature Engineering (Extended Version)

author.name: Ankai Hao, Ke Chen, Huan Li, Lidan Shou

entry.summary: LATTEArena is a competitive evaluation framework for LLM-powered automated tabular feature engineering that enables fair, cost-aware comparisons and isolates the contributions of individual technique components. It addresses the lack of standardized platforms in this emerging area.

entry.title: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour

author.name: Radeen Mostafa, Sawradip Saha

entry.summary: SuperBrowser is an autonomous web-navigation agent designed on the hypothesis that agents should browse like humans, using a vision-first bounding-box perception pipeline and a three-role brain (orchestrator, planner, executor). It operationalizes a perception-cognition-action triad.

entry.title: Bayesian Selective Latent Inference for Wastewater-First Influenza Monitoring

author.name: Yixuan Zhang (Section of Health Data Science and AI, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark), Yang Song (Section of Health Data Science and AI, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark), Hao Wang (Rutgers University, New Brunswick, NJ, USA), Samir Bhatt (Section of Health Data Science and AI, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark, MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis, Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology, School of Public Health, Faculty of Medicine, Imperial College London, London, United Kingdom), Hengguan Huang (Section of Health Data Science and AI, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark, MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis, Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology, School of Public Health, Faculty of Medicine, Imperial College London, London, United Kingdom)

entry.summary: BSLI casts wastewater-first influenza monitoring as a selective decision problem, using Bayesian inference to decide whether wastewater evidence suffices, which delayed official stream to query next, or when to abstain under source ambiguity. It moves beyond fixed-evidence wastewater models.

entry.title: Beware of GeeksBearing Gifts: Building True EU Frontier AI Sovereignty

author.name: Nick Mo\"es, Toni Lorente, Amin Oueslati, Jonathan Smith, Robin Staes-Polet, Radina Kraeva

entry.summary: A policy paper proposing a unified framework for EU frontier AI sovereignty across five pillars, highlighting Europe's structural dependence on US and Chinese models and compute. Addresses strategic autonomy across the AI value chain.

entry.title: Subtitle-Aligned Fine-Tuning of Whisper for Swiss German ASR: Benchmark Contamination, Convention Mismatch, and an Honest Baseline at 25.6% WER (13.8% cWER)

author.name: Felix Akeret

entry.summary: Presents a careful study of fine-tuning Whisper large-v3 for Swiss German ASR using 1,367 hours of subtitle-paired broadcast speech, achieving an honest 25.6% WER on disjoint data while exposing benchmark contamination and subtitle convention mismatch. Emphasizes transparent evaluation separating genuine errors from stylistic variation.

entry.title: Active Learning with Foundation Model Priors: Efficient Learning under Class Imbalance

author.name: Jiancheng Zhang, Meiqing Li, Qi Zhang, Yinglun Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes an active learning framework using foundation model priors to handle class imbalance and noisy labels, enabling imbalance-aware co-decisions between a foundation model and a small model to select informative, balanced samples. Studies efficient learning under skewed distributions across image and text.

entry.title: Instrumented data for causal scientific machine learning

author.name: Daniel N. Wilke

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues for instrumented data in scientific machine learning, where each datum carries its generating mechanistic model, explicit uncertainty, and executable counterfactuals, exemplified by verification-and-validation image-to-simulation pipelines. It positions this as a third option between observational and template synthetic data.

entry.title: LCAM: A Framework for Diagnosing Interactional Alignment Failures in Con-versational AI

author.name: Manuele Reani, Hongyu Tian

entry.summary: LCAM is a conceptual framework for diagnosing interactional alignment failures in conversational AI, defining alignment as calibrated fit among system behavior, user goals, task demands, and norms. It focuses on harms arising through interaction like authority framing and simulated empathy rather than output correctness.

entry.title: NutriMLLM: Multimodal Large Language Models for Dietary Micronutrient Analysis

author.name: Runze Yan, Minxiao Wang, Jiaying Lu, Darren Liu, Xiao Hu, Hanqi Luo

entry.summary: NutriMLLM shows leading MLLMs are unreliable for dietary micronutrient estimation from food images and repurposes population-scale dietary recall data via text-to-image synthesis to build training data. Aims to improve clinical nutrition micronutrient analysis without costly expert annotation.

entry.title: Stage-1 Controls the Entropy Regime, Not the Outcome

author.name: Jianxiong Shen

entry.summary: Investigates two-stage post-training for VLMs, finding that Stage-1 warm-start controls the entropy regime rather than the in-domain outcome, with all warm-starts reaching a narrow validation band. Early-stopped SFT improves out-of-domain generalization while over-training hurts.

entry.title: Resource-aware Computation-Communication Overlap for multi-GPU ML Workloads

author.name: Minyu Cui, Miquel Pericas

entry.summary: Explores concurrent execution of computation and collective communication in multi-GPU ML workloads using shared-memory occupancy shaping for compute kernels and elevated scheduling priority for communication kernels. Addresses communication overhead as a dominant bottleneck in distributed training.

entry.title: Model Poisoning Against Federated Model Adaptation with Chain of Bit-Flips

author.name: Bastien Vuillod, Kevin Hector, Pierre-Alain Moellic, Jean-Max Dutertre, Olivier Potin

entry.summary: Introduces a backdoor attack against federated model adaptation that relies on hardware-fault attacks (chained bit-flips like Rowhammer) rather than algorithmic data poisoning. It presents a task-agnostic backdoor leveraging the expanded hardware-level attack surface.

entry.title: Transition-Based Digital Twin Modelling for Alzheimer's Disease under Sparse Longitudinal Data

author.name: Yinyu Huang, Yilin Zhang, Sofia Michopoulou, Christopher Kipps, Rahman Attar

entry.summary: Presents a personalized digital twin framework for Alzheimer's disease progression prediction under sparse, irregular longitudinal data, integrating transition modeling with temporal dependencies for subject-specific, uncertainty-aware reasoning. It supports scenario-based analysis beyond static cohort-level risk.

entry.title: Bandits for Efficient Experimentation: Adapting to Control Group, Preferences, and Context Drifts

author.name: Udvas Das, Waris Radji, Debabrota Basu, Odalric-Ambrym Maillard

entry.summary: Studies linear contextual bandits with personalized user preferences and drifting context distributions, reducing the setting to linear bandits with heteroskedastic non-stationary noise. Introduces Dri-MED, a MED-inspired algorithm enforcing baseline-exceeding mean rewards at each step.

entry.title: Fourier fractal dimension to predict the generalization of deep neural networks

author.name: Joao B. Florindo, Davi Wanderley Misturini

entry.summary: Proposes a generalization predictor for deep nets based on the Fourier fractal dimension of weight variations, derived from analyzing Levy-driven SGD dynamics in the frequency domain. It estimates generalization without hold-out validation data.

entry.title: Quantum Global Variational Learning for Quantum Error Correction

author.name: Shun Ryuzaki, Hideo Mukai

entry.summary: Proposes a globally structured quantum neural network for quantum error correction that reduces required unitary matrices, achieving 97% less training time, higher completion rates, and improved error-correction fidelity including under internal network noise. It surpasses prior reported QEC performance in their setup.

entry.title: Declarative Outcome-Conformant Synthesis: Exact, Closed-Form Specification Satisfaction and a Conformance Benchmark

author.name: Muhammed Rasin

entry.summary: Studies exact, closed-form satisfaction of declared analytical outcomes (e.g., revenue curves, churn rates) in synthetic tabular data without source data, contrasting with fidelity-focused imitation methods. It provides a conformance benchmark for outcome-conformant synthesis.

entry.title: Learning Dynamics Reveal a Hierarchy of Weight-Induced Layerwise Gram Metrics

author.name: Claudio Nordio

entry.summary: Reformulates gradient descent in ReLU networks as a collective dynamics over training-set-space fields, eliminating weight variables for single hidden layers and revealing a hierarchy of weight-induced Gram operators for deeper networks. Theoretical contribution to learning dynamics. Niche but foundational.

entry.title: Identifiability and Estimation for Unlabeled Finite Mixtures under Marginal Independence

author.name: Takafumi Kanamori, Yushi Hirose, Shohei Yamamoto

entry.summary: Studies identifiability and estimation for unlabeled finite mixtures sharing latent components but with unknown mixing weights, using marginal independence as the identifying signal. Proves structural recovery results under linear independence and full-rank conditions without labels or clean samples.

entry.title: AI-Native Closed-Loop Security for 6G-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems: From Edge Detection to Network-Wide Mitigation

author.name: Bilal Hussain, Muhammad Bilal, Tan Li, Haris Pervaiz, Xiao Tang, Qinghe Du, Fawad Ahmad, Muhammad Azhar, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Surveys and reframes 6G cyber-physical-system security as an AI-native closed-loop pipeline spanning edge detection to network-wide mitigation, using call-detail records for baseline learning and sub-millisecond RAN telemetry for latency-critical decisions. Argues traditional perimeter security cannot meet millisecond breach-to-harm budgets in 6G.

entry.title: MS-COOT: Comparing Morse-Smale Complexes with Co-Optimal Transport

author.name: Guangyu Meng, Mingzhe Li, Erin Wolf Chambers

entry.summary: Introduces MS-COOT, a co-optimal transport distance for comparing Morse-Smale complexes represented as hypergraphs, jointly computing correspondences between critical points and regions. Preserves region-level structure that prior graph-based scalar-field comparison methods discard.

entry.title: Beyond Individual Personas: Aligning Synthetic Dialogue to Population-Level Behavior Distributions

author.name: Xinyi Liu, Rinat Khaziev, Hooshang Nayyeri, Emine Yilmaz, Charith Peris, Hari Thadakamalla

entry.summary: Presents GroupPersona, which aligns synthetic dialogue corpora to population-level behavior distributions rather than optimizing individual conversations. Separates each dialogue's behavioral signature from side effects to condition generation on reference population patterns.

entry.title: SSR: Can Simulated Patients Learn to Stigmatize Themselves? Modeling Self-Stigma through Internal Monologue

author.name: Kunyao Lan, Bingrui Jin, Zichen Zhu, Mengyue Wu

entry.summary: Introduces a simulation framework grounded in the 3A1H model of self-stigmatization, creating the SSR dataset augmenting mental health dialogues with stigma-aware internal monologues. Enables more realistic patient simulation exhibiting context-sensitive resistance for clinical training.

entry.title: Cross-Source Reasoning-based Correction for Author Name Disambiguation

author.name: Fanjin Zhang, Yunhe Pang, Bo Chen, Zhiyu Shen, Yanghui Rao, Evgeny Kharlamov, Jie Tang

entry.summary: Proposes CrossND, a full-stack framework for author name disambiguation that exploits inconsistent paper-author assignments across sources via chain-of-refinement, cross-source reasoning, and test-time scaling. Reduces cumulative errors without expensive expert annotation.

entry.title: Building Customer Support AI Agents at 100M-User Scale: An Evaluation-Driven Framework

author.name: Aman Gupta, Kevin Rossell, Edesio Alcoba\c{c}a, Jose Chrystian Lima Pacheco, Carolina Baptista de Lima, Shao Tang, Luiz Paulo Rabachini, Luis Moneda, Herbert Fei, Daniel Silva, Rohan Ramanath

entry.summary: Presents a unified evaluation-driven framework for building production customer-support AI agents at Nubank's 100M+ user scale, bridging offline development with online impact through context engineering, training, and measurement. Addresses blind spots from developing these pillars in isolation.

entry.title: Guide Me Out: A Framework to Benchmark VLM Operators Communication in Crisis Scenarios

author.name: Giacomo Gonella, Stefano Menini, Marco Guerini

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmarking framework for evaluating vision-language models guiding civilian agents through simulated crisis evacuations, testing communication strategies, environment representations, and threat behaviors. It addresses the gap of dynamic embodied crisis communication.

entry.title: MUDIDI: A Two-Stage Framework for Multilingual Dictionary Digitization with Language Models

author.name: David Setiawan, Temuulen Khishigsuren, Milind Agarwal, Pagnarith Pit, Aso Mahmudi, Ekaterina Vylomova

entry.summary: MUDIDI is a two-stage framework for digitizing multilingual dictionaries for low-resource languages using vision-language models, evaluating character recognition, markup preservation, and entry segmentation. It tackles complex multi-column layouts and language-specific scripts.

entry.title: Overcoming Decoder Inconsistencies in Whisper for Dravidian and Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Chowdam Venkata Kumar, Kumud Tripathi, Pankaj Wasnik

entry.summary: Diagnoses why Whisper has higher word error rates for Dravidian languages, attributing it to longer words, vocabulary diversity, and decoder imbalance between self-attention and cross-attention. It introduces weighted-attention decoder enhancements to mitigate these issues.

entry.title: PereStruct: Multimodal Semantic Assembly for Robust Historical Document Parsing

author.name: Maksim Shandybo, Ivan Bespalov, Daniil Yefimov, Marina Kosheleva, Alexander Loukianov

entry.summary: PereStruct is an automated pipeline for parsing historical newspapers with complex multi-column layouts and severe degradation, combining a fine-tuned YOLO for layout analysis with a semantic assembly module that reconstructs articles. It addresses out-of-distribution challenges in archival digitization.

entry.title: Echo-DM: Ultrasound Marker Removal via Conditional Latent Diffusion and Region-Aware Fusion

author.name: Zhiwei Wang, Tao Huang, Wentao Jiang, Muyi Li, Jianxin Liu, Jian Chen, Jie Zou, Yong Luo, Bo Du, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: Echo-DM removes calipers and text markers from ultrasound images using conditional latent diffusion with region-aware fusion, avoiding mask dependence and over-smoothing. It aims to reduce shortcut bias in downstream automated analysis.

entry.title: Detecting Aimbot Cheaters in MOGs

author.name: Salman Shaikh, Tao Ni, Marc Dacier

entry.summary: This paper introduces PATCH, a proactive adversarial defense against visual aimbot cheats in multiplayer games that exploit client screen captures and evade kernel-level anti-cheat. It targets a CV-model-based threat undetectable by conventional methods.

entry.title: Trajectory Optimization in Single and Dual-UAV Bearing-Only Target Localization

author.name: Zhijian Xiao, Huayu Huang, Bin Li, Yang Shang, Banglei Guan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a trajectory optimization method for single and dual UAVs in bearing-only target localization using a spectrally-weighted Fisher Information Matrix objective for better gradient dynamics. It dynamically integrates geometry and maneuverability to improve localization accuracy.

entry.title: Efficient Minimal Solvers for Relative Pose Estimation in Autonomous Driving Applications

author.name: Tao Li, Liang Liu, Jianli Han, Weimin Lv

entry.summary: This paper introduces efficient minimal solvers for relative pose estimation in multi-camera autonomous driving systems using a novel translation parameterization and first-order rotation approximation. It reduces computation and feature-match requirements for time-sensitive scenarios.

entry.title: LAEI: Layered Autonomous Edge Intelligence Framework for Robust UAV Swarm Operations

author.name: Changmin Park, Wooyong Jung, Hwangnam Kim

entry.summary: LAEI is a layered autonomous edge intelligence framework for UAV swarms combining onboard learned policies with lightweight mission-level supervision for adaptive goal reassignment and fault-aware recovery. It balances centralized coordination consistency with decentralized robustness.

entry.title: Curation of a Cardiology Interface Terminology for Highlighting Electronic Health Records using Machine Learning

author.name: Mahshad Koohi Habibi Dehkordi, Shuxin Zhou, Yehoshua Perl, Fadi P. Deek, James Geller, Gai Elhanan, Andrew J. Einstein, Luke Lindemann, Vipina K. Keloth

entry.summary: This study designs a Cardiology Interface Terminology using a novel machine-learning technique to automatically highlight all clinically relevant details in dense cardiology EHR notes, reducing manual training-data preparation. It aims to help clinicians avoid missing crucial information.

entry.title: Bridging Expert Knowledge and Automated Feature Engineering via Self-Evolution

author.name: Varun Khurana, Vijval Ekbote, Vashu Chauhan, Yaman Kumar Singla, Rajiv Ratn Shah, Balaji Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: FEST proposes a self-evolving tree-based system for automated feature engineering that produces interpretable, expert-aligned features from unstructured content in high-stakes domains like clinical care and content moderation. It aims to operationalize qualitative expert criteria into precise discriminative features.

entry.title: FAME: Forecastability-Aware Mixture of Experts for Heterogeneous Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Qianyang Li, Xingjun Zhang, Shaoxun Wang, Tao Peng, Jia Wei

entry.summary: FAME is a sparse mixture-of-experts framework for heterogeneous time series forecasting that represents each series with a forecastability fingerprint and learns cost-aware expert routing from validation performance. It targets large-scale retail/industrial forecasting with diverse regimes.

entry.title: Graph2Idea:Retrieval-Augmented Scientific Idea Generation with Graph-Structured Contexts

author.name: Xu Li, Hanzhe Tu, Xun Han

entry.summary: Graph2Idea is a knowledge-graph-guided retrieval-augmented framework for scientific idea generation that transforms retrieved papers into structured graphs capturing cross-paper relations among problems, methods, and findings. It aims to overcome redundancy in flat-text retrieval contexts.

entry.title: Implicit Causal Graph Construction in Text via Chain Discovery

author.name: Liesbeth Allein, Marie-Francine Moens

entry.summary: Studies implicit causal graph construction from text by treating cause-effect pairs as endpoints of latent graphs and using LLMs to infer intermediate events via chain discovery. Includes wisdom-of-the-crowd extensions aggregating multiple LLMs.

entry.title: DiffoR: A Unified Continuous Generative Framework for Universal Ordinal Regression

author.name: Hongxu Ma, Lin Wang, Chenghou Jin, Han Zhou, Jie Zhang, Xiaoyu Yang, Chunjie Chen, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Reformulates ordinal regression as a continuous generative task with DiffOR, using diffusion/rectified-flow style modeling to overcome quantization artifacts and capture global ordinal topology. Targets non-stationary semantic transitions in ordinal data.

entry.title: No Free Lunch for Synthetic Images under Data Scarcity Conditions

author.name: Borja Arroyo Galende, Alejandro Almod\'ovar, Patricia A. Apell\'aniz, Juan Parras, Silvia Uribe, Santiago Zazo

entry.summary: Investigates fidelity-privacy-utility trade-offs in synthetic image generation under data scarcity, evaluating VAE, GAN, and DDPM with differential privacy on MNIST, OCTMNIST, and OrganAMNIST. Finds GAN and DDPM more robust to DP noise while VAE degrades faster.

entry.title: Liquid Neural Networks as a Drop-in Continuous-Time Deformation Field for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Mingzhao Li, Arghya Pal, Guan Yuan Tan

entry.summary: This work replaces the MLP deformation field in dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting with closed-form continuous-time Liquid Neural Network cells, providing genuine temporal coupling instead of discrete per-frame offsets. It claims improved temporal smoothness as a drop-in modification.

entry.title: Pharmacogenomic Knowledge Graph Augmentation for Graph Neural Network-Based Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction

author.name: Juergen Dietrich

entry.summary: This study augments GNN-based drug-drug interaction prediction with pharmacogenomic prior knowledge (CYP enzyme substrate/inhibitor/inducer annotations) to surpass an information ceiling that purely structural models cannot exceed. The added metabolic pathway context is complementary to molecular structure.

entry.title: Jas: AI-Paired Engineering as a Revival of N-Version Programming

author.name: Jason Hickey

entry.summary: Jas presents a case study of AI-paired software engineering producing five working ports of a vector illustration app across Rust, Swift, OCaml, Python, and browser platforms in roughly 120 hours, framed as a revival of N-version programming. It uses an executable YAML specification and parallel implementations as differential testing safeguards.

entry.title: Decoupling Semantics and Logic: A Training-Free Coarse-to-Fine Pipeline for Video Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Jiaxin Dai, Zehang Wei, Jiamin Yan, Xiang Xiang

entry.summary: This system description presents a training-free two-stage cascaded video RAG pipeline that decouples semantic retrieval from logical reasoning through modality-aware division of labor for cross-lingual long-video comprehension. It isolates noisy modalities like OCR and ASR during high-recall pre-fetching.

entry.title: Human-Centered Benchmarking of Driver Monitoring Models

author.name: Ruben Dario Florez-Zela

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Human-Centered Benchmarking Framework for driver monitoring models, evaluating across accuracy, explainability, efficiency, and robustness rather than accuracy alone. Applied to four lightweight architectures on eye-state classification, it shows each model leads on a different dimension.

entry.title: Lost in the Flow with Code Talkers: Unveiling the Instruction-Tuning Tax of Large Language Models in Code Tasks

author.name: Shi Ying Chang, Chiok Yew Ho, Yichen Li, Yintong Huo

entry.summary: Investigates the instruction-tuning tax for LLMs in code tasks across Flow (infill/completion) and Command (instruction-following) cognitive modes. It examines whether instruction tuning degrades code-completion capabilities developers need in IDEs.

entry.title: Hybridizing Equilibrium Propagation with Ising Machines for Efficient Energy-Based Learning

author.name: Chen-Rui Fan, Bo Lu, Xing-Yu Wu, Tie-Jun Wang, Chuan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces an Ising-dynamics-inspired equilibrium-propagation framework replacing dissipative Hopfield relaxation with extended phase-space dynamics using conjugate variables to avoid local-minima convergence. Targets energy-efficient physical learning hardware.

entry.title: From USD Scenes to Knowledge Graphs: Zero-Shot Ontology Grounding with LLMs

author.name: Jiangtao Shuai, Zongxiong Chen, Manfred Hauswirth, Sonja Schimmler

entry.summary: Investigates zero-shot LLM grounding of USD 3D scene objects to formal ontology classes for robot knowledge graphs, achieving 90-96% accuracy with descriptive names versus brittle dictionaries. Offers a training-free alternative to manual grounding.

entry.title: SAILS: Surrogate-based Analysis of Interactions via Local Effect Smooths

author.name: Timo Hei{\ss}, Julia Herbinger, Bernd Bischl, Giuseppe Casalicchio

entry.summary: Introduces SAILS, a model-agnostic framework that analyzes pairwise feature interactions via interpretable GAM surrogates fitted to local effects, revealing functional forms rather than just detecting interactions. It enables interaction detection through significance tests on smooth terms.

entry.title: A Finetuned SpeechLLM for Joint Multi-Granular L2 Assessment and Natural-Language Rationales

author.name: Aditya Kamlesh Parikh, Cristian Tejedor-Garcia, Catia Cucchiarini, Helmer Strik

entry.summary: Presents a rubric-guided SpeechLLM fine-tuned for multi-aspect, multi-granular L2 speech assessment that jointly predicts ordinal proficiency labels and generates natural-language rationales. Uses supervised fine-tuning plus Bounded Direct Preference Optimization and analyzes rationale reliability.

entry.title: ArtiFact: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal Cultural Heritage Dataset

author.name: Luciano Duarte, Olga Ovcharenko, Sebastian Schelter

entry.summary: Releases ArtiFact, a large multimodal cultural heritage dataset of 651K museum records combining tables, text, and images from three major museums. Demonstrates utility through cross-modal error detection with a curated taxonomy of seven error categories.

entry.title: SPIN: Decentralized Swarm Control via Tensorized Policy Coordination

author.name: Zhaowen Fan

entry.summary: Introduces SPIN, a decentralized swarm control framework that models swarm topologies as compressed tensor networks, factorizing joint policy tensors into Matrix Product State chains to reduce complexity from exponential to linear. It targets resource-constrained edge platforms for multi-agent coordination.

entry.title: KITE: A Tri-Modal Transformer Integrating Text, Images, and Knowledge Graphs for Fake News Detection

author.name: Kevin Patel, Shashi Bhushan Jha

entry.summary: Introduces KITE, a tri-modal transformer fusing text, images, and Wikidata knowledge graphs via RoBERTa, CLIP, and a graph attention network for fake news detection. It jointly models semantic inconsistencies across modalities rather than treating knowledge as post-processing.

entry.title: Mesh Graph Neural Network Framework for Accelerating Finite Element Simulation for Arbitrary Geometries

author.name: Josiah D. Kunz, Kamal Choudhary

entry.summary: Presents a mesh graph network surrogate predicting von Mises stress fields for 2D components with arbitrary hole geometries, using node-type and relative-edge features instead of absolute coordinates for generalization. It accelerates finite element analysis across geometries.

entry.title: Backward Coherence and Hidden-State Stability in Recurrent Neural Networks: A Quasi-Reverse-Martingale Theory

author.name: Yuan-chin Ivan Chang

entry.summary: Develops a quasi-reverse-martingale theory for RNN hidden-state stability via backward coherence, where states can be reconstructed from future states. Provides convergence guarantees and a regularization scheme that improves stability empirically. Theoretical contribution to RNN understanding.

entry.title: Heterophily-Aware Adaptive Knowledge Distillation for Hypergraph Neural Networks

author.name: Joohee Cho, David Yoon Suk Kang, Yunyong Ko

entry.summary: Proposes HADES, a heterophily-aware adaptive knowledge distillation method for hypergraph neural networks that modulates teacher knowledge transfer based on node heterophily as a reliability estimate. Improves student model quality. Relevant to efficient hypergraph learning.

entry.title: Machine-Learning Emulation of Satellite Greenhouse Gas Retrievals: Stability over Time

author.name: Nugzar Gognadze, Motonobu Kanagawa, Yu Someya, Hisashi Yashiro

entry.summary: Studies temporal stability of ML emulators of satellite greenhouse gas retrievals using GOSAT data, showing prediction accuracy degrades when test periods move away from training periods. Highlights distribution-shift challenges in environmental emulation. Relevant to climate monitoring ML.

entry.title: Information-Geometric Optimization on Spheres

author.name: Vladimir Ja\' cimovi\'c

entry.summary: Designs two information-geometric optimization flows for black-box optimization on spheres using hyperbolic geometry of Poincare and Bergman balls, showing ensembles of generalized Kuramoto oscillators compute natural search gradients. Connects to quantum decision making. Theoretical optimization contribution with physics links.

entry.title: Hardware-aware Low-latency Quantum Compilation with Data-driven Lightweight Error Detection for Early Fault-Tolerant Systems

author.name: Sumit Chongder (Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur)

entry.summary: Presents an integrated hardware-aware quantum compilation and lightweight error-detection framework that jointly optimizes qubit mapping, SWAP insertion, and syndrome scheduling under latency constraints. Targets the early fault-tolerant regime where full error correction is too costly.

entry.title: RACT: Retrieval Augmented Column-Table Learning and Prediction for Multi-Table Schema Matching

author.name: Leonard Traeger, Enas Khwaileh, Andreas Behrend, George Karabatis

entry.summary: Proposes RACT, a self-supervised retrieval-augmented framework for multi-table schema matching that uses referential context to probabilistically retrieve candidate tables, constraining relevant column matches. Outperforms similarity-based baselines on holistic schema matching.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Modeling of Multiple-Choice Questions Improves Automatic Difficulty Estimation

author.name: Gabriel Ortega, Abelino Jim\'enez, S\'everin Lions, Pablo Dartnell

entry.summary: Studies automatic difficulty estimation for multiple-choice questions, hypothesizing that explicitly modeling distractors as separate structural components improves prediction over treating them as appended text. Shows structure-aware modeling of distractors consistently improves difficulty estimation over baselines that omit them.

entry.title: Report the Floor: A Training-Free Conformal Interval Is a Mandatory Baseline for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Valery Manokhin

entry.summary: Argues that a training-free split-conformal interval around a last-value forecast is a strong yet routinely omitted baseline for probabilistic time-series forecasting, beating many learned methods across 2,217 real series. A methodological critique calling for honest baselines.

entry.title: Arabic Sentence Segmentation Across Genres and Punctuation Conditions

author.name: Mohammed Elkholy, Khalid N. Elmadani, Nizar Habash, Bashar Alhafni

entry.summary: Introduces AraSEG, a genre-diverse Arabic sentence segmentation corpus spanning eight genres and varied punctuation conditions, finding lightweight encoders and dependency parsers outperform LLMs in hard settings. Addresses robustness gaps in realistic Arabic text.

entry.title: Cross Paraphrastic Invariance Learning for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Shanshan Lin, Dongsheng Hong, Sibo Ju, Chao Chen, Sihong Xie, Xiangwen Liao

entry.summary: Proposes CPIL, a two-stage Siamese framework for hallucination detection that enforces paraphrastic invariance via positive views and mines same-document opposite-label hard negatives. Maximizes utility of limited labeled data without costly LLM evaluators.

entry.title: Multilingual Sentiment Aware Text Summarization A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Consistency Maintenance

author.name: Mikhail Krasitskii, Alexander Gelbukh, Olga Kolesnikova, Grigori Sidorov

entry.summary: Studies sentiment drift in RLHF-based multilingual summarization, showing a systematic shift toward neutral sentiment that strengthens with KL regularization across eight languages. Proposes a reinforcement learning approach for sentiment consistency, revealing an alignment-vs-affective-fidelity tradeoff.

entry.title: Explicit Representation Alignment for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Baode Wang, Ziming Wang, Huacan Wang, Ronghao Chen, Biao Wu

entry.summary: This paper identifies representation misalignment between independently pretrained modality encoders as a key bottleneck in multimodal sentiment analysis, arguing that alignment before fusion matters more than fusion complexity. It proposes using vision-language models to convert visual content into structured text for explicit alignment.

entry.title: Introducing multiplex semantic networks as multifaceted representations of creative associative knowledge across multilingual samples

author.name: Edith Haim, Kurt Haim, Roger E. Beaty, Cynthia S. Q. Siew, Massimo Stella

entry.summary: Introduces multiplex semantic networks built from six cognitive tasks across 518 individuals in four countries as a multifaceted representation of creative associative knowledge, comparing with AI persona-based responses. It models creativity more comprehensively than single-task measures.

entry.title: Learning a Semantic Calibration Network for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Yang Sun, Tao Wang, Anastasia Ioannou, Ge Xu

entry.summary: The Semantic Calibration Network refines mask classification for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation by explicitly modeling semantic correlations between classes rather than just feature aggregation or fine-tuning. It aims to enhance discriminative power for novel concepts.

entry.title: MAGIS: Evidence-Based Multi-Agent Reasoning for Interpretable Strabismus Clinical Decision-Making

author.name: Xikai Tang, Yifan Wang, Jiafan Zhuang, Li Luo, Jinming Guo, Xiaoling Xie, Jiacheng Liu, Peiwei Wei, Lihao Zhong, Xiaoli Kang, Jie Cen, Guangqiang Yin, Kunliang Qiu, Ce Zheng, Zhun Fan

entry.summary: MAGIS is a multi-agent reasoning framework for interpretable strabismus diagnosis that replaces black-box predictions with structured hypothesis generation and evidence-constrained reasoning to reduce hallucination. It targets a rule-driven medical imaging task requiring transparency.

entry.title: IB-HFN: Information Bottleneck-Driven SAR-Optical Fusion Network for High-Fidelity Cloud Removal

author.name: Haojun Guo, Fan Feng, Ziquan Wang

entry.summary: IB-HFN uses an information bottleneck to fuse SAR and optical imagery for cloud removal, employing a dual-stream backbone to preserve modality-specific features and avoid propagating SAR speckle noise. It targets high-fidelity surface reconstruction in remote sensing.

entry.title: Cranio-Diff: Diffusion-based Cross-domain Craniofacial Reconstruction with 2D X-ray Skull Guidance and Structural Identity Constraints

author.name: Ravi Shankar Prasad, Naresh Gurjar, Shashank Baghel, Chirag, Dinesh Singh

entry.summary: Cranio-Diff performs cross-domain craniofacial reconstruction from 2D X-ray skull images using a diffusion framework with ControlNet skull-conditioned structural guidance and biometric text conditioning. It addresses structural identity misalignment in skull-to-face translation.

entry.title: Assessing model calibration with boosting trees

author.name: Selim Gatti

entry.summary: This paper shows that boosting trees can test necessary conditions for model calibration and auto-calibration, where conditional mean estimates match true conditional means, important for applications like insurance pricing to avoid cross-subsidization. It connects gradient boosting to calibration assessment.

entry.title: How to build a cancer vaccine, and whether they will work this time

author.name: Abhishaike Mahajan

entry.summary: This essay explains the science of therapeutic cancer vaccines, distinguishing them from preventive vaccines against oncogenic viruses, and reviews why the field has largely failed over forty years and whether new approaches may finally succeed. It offers an accessible technical overview of cancer immunotherapy.

entry.title: Standpoint Logics with Defeasible Beliefs

author.name: Nicholas Leisegang, Thomas Meyer, Sebastian Rudolph

entry.summary: This paper integrates KLM defeasible logic with standpoint logic to formally represent multiple, possibly contradicting viewpoints that hold defeasible beliefs, providing a representation result and lifting entailment relations to the standpoint-enhanced setting. It advances formal knowledge representation for multi-perspective reasoning.

entry.title: ZIPP:Zero-shot Image Personalization from Personas

author.name: Harini SI, Somesh Singh, Yaman Kumar Singla, David Doermann, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.summary: ZIPP enables zero-shot personalization of text-to-image generation by conditioning on natural-language personas describing a user's aesthetic identity, avoiding per-user fine-tuning or dense interaction histories. It targets cold-start and pluralistic preference settings.

entry.title: MASS: Deep Research for Social Sciences with Memory-Augmented Social Simulation

author.name: Yongrui Liu, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: MASS is a deep-research paradigm for social sciences that augments LLM idea generation with realistic, research-oriented social simulations to improve creativity and empirical grounding. It integrates goal-path planning under social norms with a multi-disciplinary simulation backbone.
