entry.title: Can activation verbalizers surface an internal chain of thought?

author.name: oakhu

entry.summary: Introduces an evaluation for activation verbalizers—interpretability tools mapping residual-stream activations to natural language—testing whether they can surface a model's single-forward-pass reasoning while solving math problems, finding it possible but unreliable for open-weight natural-language autoencoders. Probes monitoring of opaque internal reasoning.

entry.title: Learn to Match: Two-Sided Matching with Temporally Extended Feedback

author.name: Haijing Zong, Yancheng Liang, Boyang Zhou, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework for two-sided matching with temporally extended feedback, formulating it as a partially observable Markov game with costly pre-match screening, noisy observations, and evolving latent profiles. Learn2Match is a multi-agent RL benchmark for dynamic matching markets.

entry.title: From Sampled Outcomes to Capability Distributions: Rethinking Supervision for LLM Routing

author.name: Guannan Lai, Haoran Hu, Long Chen, Zhenguo Li, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: DARS rethinks LLM routing supervision by constructing capability labels from a distributional view of stochastic model behavior rather than single noisy responses. It captures both input-side and output-side uncertainty to improve routing reliability.

entry.title: SlimSearcher: Training Efficiency-Aware Web Agents via Adaptive Reward Gating

author.name: Zequn Xie, Junjie Wang, Dan Yang, Jie Feng, Yue Shen, Jian Wang and Jinjie Gu

entry.summary: SlimSearcher is a framework that pushes the accuracy-cost Pareto frontier for deep research web agents across SFT and RL, using Pareto-efficient filtration and adaptive reward gating to reduce redundant tool calls and token consumption. It addresses the efficiency trap of brute-force agent strategies.

entry.title: The Masked Advantage: Uncovering Local-Language Access to Cultural Knowledge in LLMs

author.name: Yang Zhang, Xiao Fei, Amr Mohamed, Sarah Almeida Carneiro, Mersin Konomi, Mingmeng Geng, Ahmed Asaad, Guokan Shang, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: Using a controlled framework with item-response-theory ability estimation, the paper studies whether LLMs access local cultural knowledge better in English or the local language, separating language proficiency from language-conditioned knowledge access. Finds nuanced advantages for local-language querying of culture-specific knowledge.

entry.title: What an Autonomous Agent Discovers About Molecular Transformer Design: Does It Transfer?

author.name: Edward Wijaya

entry.summary: An autonomous agent runs over 3,000 architecture-search experiments across molecular (SMILES), protein, and English text sequences to test whether transformers designed for language transfer to molecular data. It finds architecture search is counterproductive for SMILES (tuning learning rates matters more) yet drives most gains for natural language, while discovered innovations transfer across all domains.

entry.title: Human Adults and LLMs as Scientists: Who Benefits from Active Exploration?

author.name: Mandana Samiei, Eunice Yiu, Anthony GX-Chen, Dongyan Lin, Jocelyn Shen, Blake A. Richards, Alison Gopnik, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Compares human adults and LLMs as active scientists in a blicket-detector causal learning task, finding active exploration improves adults' conjunctive causal reasoning that passive observation typically hinders. Investigates who benefits from agency in causal discovery.

entry.title: UnpredictaBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Distributional Randomness in LLMs

author.name: Amirhossein Abaskohi, Amirhossein Dabiriaghdam, Liang Luo, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Lele Wang, Giuseppe Carenini, Peter West

entry.summary: Introduces UnpredictaBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can sample outcomes calibrated to true target distributions rather than collapsing to single plausible answers, covering statistical distributions, stochastic programs, and natural distributions. Motivated by LLMs being used as substitutes for humans in simulations.

entry.title: AEGIS: A Backup Reflex for Physical AI

author.name: Josef Chen

entry.summary: AEGIS uses a lightweight probe on a weak policy's frozen activations to detect high-risk steps in robot manipulation and selectively escalate control to a stronger policy only when needed. On LIBERO-Spatial it recovers more than double the failed trajectories of budget-matched baselines.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Imputation with Graph-Informed Flow Matching

author.name: Zepeng Zhang, Aref Einizade, Jhony H. Giraldo, Olga Fink

entry.summary: GiFlow is a graph-informed flow matching framework for spatiotemporal imputation that replaces the Gaussian prior with a prior built via spatiotemporal filtering of observable signals. This improves efficiency and accuracy over diffusion-based methods for applications like air quality and traffic monitoring.

entry.title: RECAP: Regression Evaluation for Continual Adaptation of Prompts

author.name: Harsh Deshpande, Kushal Chawla, Sangwoo Cho, William Campbell

entry.summary: RECAP is a benchmark measuring continual-learning phenomena (forgetting, regression, forward transfer) for prompt optimization in agentic systems under a strictly proactive adapt-then-test protocol. It targets production scenarios where agents must comply with evolving constraints from the next interaction.

entry.title: PromptPrint: Behavioral Biometrics Through Natural Language Prompting in LLMs

author.name: Shaiv Patel, Kartik Narayan, Vishal Patel

entry.summary: PromptPrint studies whether brief task-driven LLM prompts contain stable author-identifiable signals, using 20,680 real prompts from 1,034 users. It finds lexical representations outperform semantic encoders, supporting a lexical stability hypothesis for prompt-based behavioral biometrics.

entry.title: A Four-Condition Diagnostic Protocol for Evidence Utilization in Long-Context and Retrieval-Augmented Language Models

author.name: Haizhou Xia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a matched four-condition protocol (no evidence, full context, retrieved evidence, oracle reference) to diagnose whether long-context and RAG models actually use provided evidence rather than parametric memory. It introduces ONCU as a protocol-bound estimator of recovered oracle-reference evidence advantage.

entry.title: VideoSEG-O3: A Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Ming Dai, Sen Yang, Boqiang Duan, Boyuan Tong, Jiedong Zhuang, Wankou Yang, and Jingdong Wang

entry.summary: VideoSEG-O3 is a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework for reasoning video object segmentation that emulates coarse-to-fine cognition via temporal-spatial chain-of-thought. It actively acquires visual evidence to resolve complex references in long videos.

entry.title: The Dark Regulome: Disentangling Predictability from Regulation in Genomic Foundation Models

author.name: Chahat Baranwal, Aadtya Baranwal and Lakshya Nitin Tandon

entry.summary: This work introduces a residualization-and-permutation diagnostic to disentangle sequence predictability from genuine regulatory signal in genomic foundation models for glioma research. It tests three architectures across thousands of dark genome elements.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Learning for Long-Horizon Task Planning Under Complex Logical Constraints

author.name: Qiwei Du, Zitong Zhan, Shaoshu Su, Bowen Li, Yi Du, Zhipeng Zhao, Taimeng Fu, Sebastian Scherer, Jiaoyang Li, Chen Wang

entry.summary: This paper formulates object-importance learning for long-horizon robot task planning as an imperative bilevel optimization to address exposure bias from fixed offline supervision. It improves neuro-symbolic planning efficiency under complex logical constraints.

entry.title: ARAPDiffusion: ARAP Regularization for Diffusion-Based Deformable Shape Space Learning

author.name: Haibo Liu, Jinghan Ke, Haitao Yang, Xiangru Huang, Georgios Pavlakos, Qixing Huang

entry.summary: ARAPDiffusion injects as-rigid-as-possible deformation regularization into latent diffusion to learn continuous deformable shape spaces with limited 3D training data. It improves both the encoder/decoder and the diffusion model alternately.

entry.title: DRIFT: From Robustness Gaps to Invariance Manifolds for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Abhishek Ameta, Sayan Banerjee, Shreyas Pandith, Harshit, Ankita Chatterjee, Akshay Janardan Bankar, Amit Satish Unde

entry.summary: DRIFT formulates AI-generated image detection as learning a structured invariance manifold of real images under one-class supervision, with projection heads decomposing representations into robust and fragile subspaces. It improves over training-free robustness-gap approaches for unseen generators.

entry.title: The Fine-Tuning Trap: Evaluating Negative Transfer and the Role of PEFT in Sub-1B Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Rahul Nair, Chun Tao

entry.summary: This study benchmarks five sub-1B models on math reasoning and finds that full fine-tuning actively harms models under 300M parameters (negative transfer), dropping below zero-shot baselines, making PEFT a stability requirement. LoRA and DoRA perform comparably with task-dependent strengths.

entry.title: Exploring Agentic Tool-Calling Decisions via Uncertainty-Aligned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yijin Zhou, Linqian Zeng, Xiaoya Lu, Wenyuan Xie, Dongrui Liu, Junchi Yan, Jing Shao

entry.summary: TRUST incorporates uncertainty quantification into reward design for LLM agents to improve tool-calling decisions, treating uncertainty as a repulsive force to maintain separation between correct and incorrect actions. It addresses overconfident mistakes in agentic tool use.

entry.title: DaX: Learning General Pathology Representations Across Scales

author.name: Bokai Zhao, Yiyang Zhang, Long Bai, Tai Ma, Hanqing Chao, Minfeng Xu

entry.summary: DaX is a pathology vision foundation model adapting DINOv3-style self-supervised learning to whole-slide histopathology, with continuous magnification training and acquisition-robust augmentations. It aims to produce representations robust across magnification, staining, and scanner variation.

entry.title: DataEvolver: Automatic Data Preparation for Large Language Models through Multi-Level Self-Evolving

author.name: Chao Deng, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: DataEvolver is a self-evolving data preparation system that automatically constructs pipelines to transform raw data into high-quality training data for LLMs, using a multi-level mechanism for operator selection and pipeline construction. It reduces reliance on costly manual curation.

entry.title: ForensicConcept: Transferable Forensic Concepts for AIGI Detection

author.name: Menyanshu Zhou, Ziyin Zhou, Ke Sun, Yunpeng Luo, Jiayi Ji, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: ForensicConcept extracts explicit, transferable forensic concepts from AI-generated image detectors via attribution and concept codebooks, enabling auditable evidence readouts and cross-backbone transfer. It addresses the black-box nature and poor cross-generator generalization of detectors.

entry.title: Beyond Rubrics: Exploration-Guided Evaluation Skills for Reward Modeling

author.name: Xing Yue, Linjuan Wu, Daoxin Zhang, Yongliang Shen, Weiming Lu

entry.summary: Eval-Skill synthesizes reusable domain-level evaluation skills for reward modeling through workflow and principle generation, reframing reward guidance as context evolution rather than per-query rubric generation. It uses only 100 cases per domain to reduce inference overhead.

entry.title: LARA: Latent Action Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mengya Liu, Baoxiong Jia, Jiangyong Huang, Jingze Zhang, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: LARA is a plug-and-play framework that jointly optimizes latent action models and vision-language-action models via representation alignment, addressing the disconnect when they are trained separately. It enables grounding latent actions during VLA training while leveraging unlabeled human videos.

entry.title: OffQ: Taming Structured Outliers in LLM Quantization by Offsetting

author.name: Haoqi Wang, Lorenz K. Mueller, Jiawei Zhuang, Mathieu Salzmann, Lukas Cavigelli

entry.summary: OffQ mitigates activation outliers in low-bit LLM quantization through an offsetting mechanism that identifies a low-dimensional outlier subspace via top-1 PCA, concentrates outliers into one channel via rotation, and absorbs it as a shared offset. This reduces activation standard deviation for better quantization.

entry.title: Learning Explicit Behavioral Models with Adaptive Questions and World-Model Probes

author.name: Hikaru Shindo, Yu Deng, Teng Cao, Quentin Delfosse, Christopher Tauchmann, Jannis Bl\"uml, Gopika Sudhakaran, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Explicit Symbolic Behavioral Model, a trainable model coupling task performance with evidence-grounded question answering and executable mechanism prediction using typed predicates, weighted rules, and mechanism memory. It addresses brittle agents that score well without representing why actions succeed.

entry.title: Explicit Evidence Grounding via Structured Inline Citation Generation

author.name: Anar Yeginbergen, Amelie W\"uhrl, Anna Rogers, Rodrigo Agerri

entry.summary: FullCite generates structured inline citations linking each claim to both its source document and supporting evidence span, using prompt-based generation, constrained decoding over a citation grammar, and posthoc span alignment. It is evaluated on ASQA, BioASQ, and ExpertQA for citation quality and faithfulness.

entry.title: From Correctness to Utility: Gain-Based Prefix Evaluation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Yixin Cao, Guangnan Ye

entry.summary: This work introduces the Prefix Utility Model (PUM), which evaluates LLM reasoning prefixes by their causal solve-rate improvement (prefix gain) rather than local step correctness, trained with pairwise ranking. PUM improves Best-of-N, beam search, and RL on mathematical reasoning. The outcome-grounded utility framing is a meaningful shift for process reward models.

entry.title: The Proxy Benders Decomposition

author.name: Changkun Guan, El Mehdi Er Raqabi, Mathieu Tanneau, Pascal Van Hentenryck

entry.summary: Proxy-BD replaces repeated exact Benders subproblem solves with certified optimization proxies via a self-supervised predict-project-and-complete mechanism producing dual-feasible solutions. Aims to accelerate large-scale mixed-integer optimization by exploiting subproblem repetitiveness.

entry.title: DisPOSE: Projected Polystochastic Diffusion for Self-Supervised Multi-View 3D Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Tony Danjun Wang, Tolga Birdal, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: DisPOSE casts the discrete multi-view person-assignment problem in multi-person 3D pose estimation as a generative diffusion over polystochastic tensors with differentiable Sinkhorn projections, regressing skeletons via hypergraph convolution from 2D priors. Self-supervised approach reducing reliance on synthetic 3D pose catalogues.

entry.title: Skill-3D: Evolving Scene-Aware Skills for Agentic 3D Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Haoyuan Li, Zhengdong Hu, Jun Wang, Hehe Fan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Skill-3D enables MLLM agents to perform 3D spatial reasoning via self-evolving scene-aware skills stored in a Scene Memory, where successful tool-use trajectories from similar scenes are distilled into reusable skills, addressing biased and uniform tool use. Improves agentic 3D reasoning over non-agentic baselines.

entry.title: Network Recovery from Cascade Data: A Debiased Jacobian-Based Machine Learning Approach

author.name: Lei Huang

entry.summary: CascadeNet recovers hidden influence networks from cascade data without assuming a diffusion model, characterizing the influence structure via the Jacobian of the one-step transition function and applying Neyman-orthogonal debiasing via the Riesz representer. Robust network recovery across diffusion mechanisms.

entry.title: How reliable are LLMs when it comes to playing dice?

author.name: Luca Avena, Gianmarco Bet, Bernardo Busoni

entry.summary: Benchmarks probabilistic reasoning in 8 LLMs on standard versus counterintuitive discrete probability problems, finding 0.96 accuracy on standard but only 0.59 on counterintuitive ones, with over 20% drops from disguised formulations (token bias) and up to 34% drops when misleading hints are embedded. Reveals fragility and heuristic susceptibility in LLM probabilistic reasoning.

entry.title: Theory of learning of high-dimensional controlled non-linear dynamical systems (I): models and methods

author.name: Pierfrancesco Urbani

entry.summary: Part one of a theory of learning for high-dimensional controlled nonlinear dynamical systems via neural ODEs, presenting models and methods that exploit the dual inference and training dynamics to study training and generalization. Offers a unifying theoretical framework spanning many learning settings.

entry.title: FAIR-Calib: Frontier-Aware Instability-Reweighted Calibration for Post-Training Quantization of Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Haoyu Huang, Linlin Yang, Sheng Xu, Boyu Liu, Guodong Guo, Zhongqian Fu, Hang Zhou, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FAIR-Calib, a two-stage post-training quantization framework for diffusion LLMs that protects fragile early token decisions at the write frontier by estimating a position prior and performing instability-reweighted layer-wise calibration. Addresses how quantization error flips and permanently locks in borderline decisions in dLLMs.

entry.title: HKJudge: A Legal Discourse-Annotated Corpus for Interpreting What Courts Find, How They Reason, and What They Rule

author.name: Xi Xuan, Wenxin Zhang, Yufei Zhou, King-kui Sin, Chunyu Kit

entry.summary: HKJudge is the first sentence-level expert-annotated legal discourse corpus for Hong Kong criminal judgments, with ~290k sentences labeled across 26 rhetorical roles and sentencing element spans. It supports interpreting what courts find, how they reason, and what they rule.

entry.title: Towards Serverless Semi-Decentralized Federated Learning with Heterogeneous Optimizers

author.name: Su Wang, Mung Chiang, H. Vincent Poor

entry.summary: SSD-FL proposes serverless semi-decentralized federated learning with heterogeneous optimizers, addressing cluster formation in fully decentralized settings without persistent server infrastructure. It uses a one-time device-to-device initialization phase coupling network structure, data heterogeneity, and optimizer diversity.

entry.title: STRIPS-WM: Learning Grounded Propositional STRIPS-style World Models from Images

author.name: Abhiroop Ajith and Constantinos Chamzas

entry.summary: STRIPS-WM learns grounded propositional STRIPS-style symbolic world models from raw image transitions for long-horizon robot manipulation planning. It bridges classical symbolic planning with learning from visual experience.

entry.title: Translate-R1: Cost-Aware Translation Tool Use via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pratik Jayarao, Chaitanya Dwivedi, Himanshu Gupta, Neeraj Varshney, Adithya M Devraj, Meet Vadera, Priyanka Nigam, Bing Yin

entry.summary: Translate-R1 learns a single RL policy that decides when to invoke translation to the model's dominant language, balancing cost against the multilingual performance gap. It avoids manual heuristics and routers by learning from reward alone.

entry.title: SpectCount: Spectrotemporal Counting via Synthetic Signals Improves Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Seonuk Kim, Yonghyeon Jun, Ju Yeon Kang, Jimin Hong, Yoonhyeong Lee, Nam Soo Kim

entry.summary: SpectCount improves large audio language models via data-efficient fine-tuning on fully synthetic on-the-fly audio signals targeting spectrotemporal perceptual weaknesses. It improves performance across sound, music, and speech benchmarks unseen during fine-tuning.

entry.title: T-GMP: Terrain-conditioned Generative Motion Priors for Versatile and Natural Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Junhong Guo, Hao Hu, Chen Chen, Haoxuan Han, Linao Gong, Xin Yang, Zhicheng He, Yao Su, Fenghua He

entry.summary: T-GMP learns terrain-conditioned generative motion priors via a conditional VAE from few expert state-terrain demonstrations for humanoid locomotion. Integrated into an adversarial RL pipeline with a Foothold Penalty, it enables natural and robust terrain-adaptive locomotion.

entry.title: Auditing Training Data in Domain-adapted LLMs: LoRA-MINT

author.name: Gonzalo Mancera, Daniel DeAlcala, Aythami Morales, Julian Fierrez, Ruben Tolosana, Francisco Jurado

entry.summary: LoRA-MINT is a membership inference test for LLMs fine-tuned with LoRA, using model perplexity to determine whether individual samples were in the adaptation training data. It achieves precision of 0.77 to 0.92 across four models and three datasets, providing a data-auditing tool.

entry.title: Don't Pause: Streaming Video-Language Synchrony for Online Video Understanding

author.name: Zhenyu Yang, Kairui Zhang, Shengsheng Qian, Weiming Dong, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: LyraV introduces Streaming Video-Language Synchrony for online video understanding, with a frame-driven transition controller that avoids pausing video perception while generating responses. It addresses real-time stutters in streaming video-LLM interaction.

entry.title: StainFlow: Entity-Stain Tracking and Evidence Linking for Process Rewards in GUI Agents

author.name: Haojie Hao, Longkun Hao, Yihang Lou, Yan Bai, Zhenyang Li, Zhichao Yang, Dongshuo Huang, Hongyu Lin, Lanqing Hong, Jiakai Wang, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: StainFlow introduces entity-stain tracking and evidence linking to provide process rewards for GUI agents, addressing sparse trajectory-level feedback in long-horizon RL. It aims to improve credit assignment by accommodating multiple valid execution paths and capturing long-range evidence.

entry.title: STREAM: Stochastic Riemannian Flow Matching with Anisotropic Decoder for Digital Histopathology Image Generation

author.name: Won June Cho, Daeky Jeong, Hyeongyeol Lim, Hongjun Yoon

entry.summary: STREAM is a stochastic Riemannian flow matching framework with an anisotropic decoder for histopathology image generation that uses pretrained pathology foundation models as the latent space itself to avoid conditioning collapse. It targets high-quality, diverse synthetic pathology images.

entry.title: Predictive Style Matching: Natural and Robust Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Simeon Nedelchev, Ekaterina Chaikovskaia, Egor Davydenko, Eduard Zaliaev, and Roman Gorbachev

entry.summary: Predictive Style Matching improves humanoid locomotion naturalness by using an offline predictor that maps lower-body state history and velocity commands to interpretable upper-body and gait targets that shape RL rewards. State-conditioned targets avoid the disturbance sensitivity of time-indexed motion imitation.

entry.title: Dreaming when Necessary: Advancing World Action Models with Adaptive Multi-Modal Reasoning

author.name: Yinzhou Tang, Jingbo Xu, Yu Shang, Zihao Song, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li

entry.summary: AdaWAM is a world action model with adaptive multimodal reasoning that uses a lightweight dynamic router to trigger textual reasoning during task transitions and visual reasoning during fine-grained manipulation. It addresses the limitations of video-prediction-only action priors on long-horizon embodied tasks.

entry.title: Native3D: End-to-End 3D Scene Generation via Unified Mesh-Texture Modeling and Semantic Alignment

author.name: Yibo Liu, Ziwei Zhang, Haozhou Pang, Menghao Li, Lanshan He, Gan Qi

entry.summary: Native3D is an end-to-end 3D scene generation framework that bypasses 2D intermediate representations using a unified mesh-texture joint representation with a transformer scene encoder and a 3D Representation Alignment Loss. It avoids domain adaptation issues like geometric distortion and texture degradation.

entry.title: QuadVerse: An Integrated Framework Aligning Visual-Physical Reality for Quadruped Simulation

author.name: Yuxiang Chen, Yuanhao Wang, Ziheng Zhang, Meng Zhang, Yu Liu, Yufei Jia, Tiancai Wang, Erjin Zhou, and Jin Xie

entry.summary: QuadVerse is an integrated quadruped simulation framework that uses reconstructed 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes as a calibration substrate to jointly align visual perception, physical interaction, and actuator dynamics. It addresses how visual and dynamic sim-to-real gaps accumulate together.

entry.title: Closed-Form Spectral Regularization for Multi-Task Model Merging

author.name: Yongxian Wei, Runxi Cheng, Xingxuan Zhang, Li Shen, Chun Yuan, Peng Cui, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: This paper explains why iterative gradient descent outperforms the exact closed-form pseudoinverse solution in multi-task model merging, showing the iterative solver acts as an implicit spectral regularizer for an ill-posed normal equation rather than as an optimizer. It then proposes a closed-form spectral regularization that captures this benefit. The mechanistic explanation plus efficient closed-form solution is a strong combination.

entry.title: SWE-Explore: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Explore Repositories

author.name: Shaoqiu Zhang, Yuhang Wang, Jialiang Liang, Yuling Shi, Wenhao Zeng, Maoquan Wang, Shilin He, Ningyuan Xu, Siyu Ye, Kai Cai, Xiaodong Gu

entry.summary: SWE-Explore is a benchmark isolating the repository-exploration capability of coding agents, asking explorers to return ranked relevant code regions under a fixed line budget across 848 issues, 10 languages, and 203 repositories with line-level ground truth. It complements holistic resolved/unresolved benchmarks like SWE-bench by evaluating fine-grained subskills. The decomposed evaluation is valuable for diagnosing agent capabilities.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Disentangling Performance Bottlenecks in Video Instance Segmentation

author.name: Danial Hamdi, Fardin Ayar, Mahdi Javanmardi

entry.summary: Introduces an ILP-based oracle diagnostic framework that disentangles classification, segmentation, and tracking error sources in video instance segmentation, applied across seven methods and multiple datasets. Reveals tracking instability as the dominant bottleneck for online methods under occlusion.

entry.title: Drifting Models for Surrogate Flow Modeling

author.name: Chris R. Jung, Markus D\"orr, Natalie J\"ungling, Jennifer Niessner, Adam T. M\"uller, Nicolaj C. Stache

entry.summary: Adapts a generative drifting framework to fluid mechanics, performing conditional drifting in a learned VAE latent space with label-aware masking to align outputs with boundary conditions, matching iterative diffusion accuracy at roughly 100x faster single-pass CFD surrogate generation. Enables rapid indoor-flow design exploration.

entry.title: Sparse Subspace-to-Expert Sharing for Task-Agnostic Continual Learning

author.name: Fatema Siddika, Md Anwar Hossen, Tanwi Mallick, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: SETA addresses the plasticity-stability dilemma in continual learning for LLMs via adaptive sparse subspace decomposition into task-specific and shared experts, isolating task knowledge to prevent catastrophic forgetting while sharing common capabilities. Targets task-agnostic continual learning.

entry.title: P-Cast Precision in FP8 Attention: Sink-Induced Collapse and the Optimality of S=2^8

author.name: Reed Lau

entry.summary: Analyzes FP8 precision challenges in attention computation, showing forward KV iteration causes P-collapse where probability values underflow under the attention sink phenomenon, while reverse iteration plus an optimal scaling factor of 256 eliminates it. Provides theoretical guarantees for zero-underflow FP8 attention.

entry.title: Synthetic Benchmarks Overstate Forward-Forward Scaling: Real-Data Limits of Layer-Local Training

author.name: Yucheng Chen

entry.summary: Develops DTG-FF (dynamic temperature goodness, decoupled normalization, multi-layer fusion) to set Forward-Forward learning state-of-the-art across nine real benchmarks, then uses it to audit how far layer-local training actually scales. Finds backprop baselines still beat FF and that synthetic benchmarks overstate FF scaling.

entry.title: Elmes*: Automated Construction of Fine-Grained Evaluation Rubrics for Large Language Models in Long-Tail Educational Scenarios

author.name: Tao Liu, Ye Lu, Ruohua Zhang, Siyu Song, Wentao Liu, Aimin Zhou, Hao Hao

entry.summary: Introduces Elmes, an end-to-end framework for automatically constructing fine-grained scenario-specific evaluation rubrics for educational LLMs, using a multi-agent teacher-student-judge engine and a self-evolving SceneGen module. Builds Edu-330 covering 330 scenarios with over 1,000 indicators to measure how models teach.

entry.title: RigPAPR: Rig-Based Animation of Static Neural Point Clouds from a Fixed-Viewpoint Video

author.name: Shichong Peng, Yanshu Zhang, Ke Li

entry.summary: RigPAPR animates static neural point cloud reconstructions to follow fixed-viewpoint driving videos and recovers rigged, re-posable 3D assets. It traces joint-boundary artifacts to per-splat canonical tiling under rigid skinning and proposes a representation that bends correctly under articulation.

entry.title: RPC-GS: Gaussian Splatting with native RPC Rendering for Satellite Imagery

author.name: Valentin Wagner, Sebastian Bullinger, Christoph Bodensteiner, Michael Arens

entry.summary: RPC-GS is the first Gaussian Splatting framework for satellite imagery operating natively with Rational Polynomial Camera models, avoiding the geometric errors of perspective or affine approximations used by prior methods. It projects Gaussian means and covariances directly through the RPC model.

entry.title: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents

author.name: Shubham Gaur, Ian Lane

entry.summary: Signal-Driven Observation decouples observation frequency from action frequency in long-horizon web agents, using a dedicated sub-call to extract only task-relevant DOM elements re-invoked when a lightweight signal detector fires. This combats context degradation from ingesting tens of thousands of tokens per step.

entry.title: Evidence Graph Consistency in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Model-Dependent Analysis of Hallucination Detection

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: EGC constructs a local evidence graph per RAG response and computes structural consistency measures as hallucination indicators, evaluated on RAGTruth across six LLMs. It reveals a model-family split where graph consistency direction reverses between Llama-2 and GPT/Mistral models.

entry.title: Explain Like I'm 5 or Whatever I Choose: Evaluating the Interactive Potential of Language Model Responses

author.name: Indu Panigrahi, Tal August

entry.summary: This paper proposes an evaluation framework, grounded in a 16-participant formative study, testing whether models can generate multiple responses to one query that vary along an interpretable language-complexity axis inspired by direct manipulation interfaces. It evaluates GPT-5.1, GPT-5 mini, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and DeepSeek-V3.1 for interactive potential.

entry.title: Three-dimensional hydro-cluttered locomotion by an undulatory robot

author.name: Tianyu Wang, Matthew Fernandez, Galen Tunnicliffe, Nikolas Cornell, Justin Duong, Donoven Dortilus, Zhaochen J. Xu, Patricia Meza, Sean Lublinsky, Darsh Parikh, Jianfeng Lin, Emily Grace, Daniel I. Goldman

entry.summary: This robotics paper develops principles for 3D aquatic locomotion in hydro-cluttered environments using AquaMILR, an undulatory limbless robot with cable-driven actuation and programmable compliance. It tackles the difficult contact-rich regime that is hard to model or simulate.

entry.title: MotionEnhancer: Leveraging Video Diffusion for Motion-Enhanced Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yifan Xu, Chao Zhang, Ruifei Ma, Fei Gao, Zhifei Yang, Jiaxing Qi, Zhipeng Chen

entry.summary: MotionEnhancer distills motion priors from video diffusion models into vision-language models via attention alignment to improve fine-grained motion understanding. It addresses VLMs' focus on static semantics over dynamic motion.

entry.title: GlucoFM-Bench: Benchmarking Time-Series Foundation Models for Blood Glucose Forecasting

author.name: Baiying Lu, Zhaohui Liang, Ryan Pontius, Shengpu Tang, Temiloluwa Prioleau

entry.summary: GlucoFM-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark evaluating time-series foundation models against supervised deep learning for blood glucose forecasting across heterogeneous diabetes populations. It assesses eight representative models in an understudied medical forecasting setting.

entry.title: TALAN: Task-Aligned Latent Adaptation Networks for Targeted Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Chengkai Zhang, Ziteng Liu, Junpu Wang, Zeyi Tao, Yang Wang, Sagar Chordia, Qin Huang

entry.summary: TALAN is a sequence-conditioned latent side path inserted into the residual stream and co-trained with a low-rank adapter for targeted LLM post-training. It aims to improve reasoning, math, and code without degrading existing strengths.

entry.title: EASE-TTT: Evidence-Aligned Selective Test-Time Training for Long-Context Question Answering

author.name: Xiaopeng Yuan, Zebin Wang, Suwen Wang, Zongxin Yang, Haohan Wang, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: EASE-TTT is an evidence-aligned selective test-time training method for long-context QA that adapts query-side attention parameters toward localized answer-bearing evidence. It combines within-context retrieval with targeted test-time adaptation.

entry.title: polyDAG: Polynomial Acyclicity Constraints for Efficient Continuous Causal Discovery in Visual Semantic Graphs

author.name: Wenhao Zhang, Ramin Ramezani, Tao Han, Kai Hwang, Minyi Guo

entry.summary: polyDAG replaces the matrix-exponential acyclicity constraint with a finite polynomial trace constraint for continuous causal discovery in visual semantic graphs, proving it is zero exactly for acyclic graphs. A geometric-series implementation avoids explicit summation.

entry.title: Teaching the Way, Not the Answer: Privileged Tutoring Distillation for Multimodal Policy Optimization

author.name: Shizhe Xiang, Ke An, Wenlong Yu, Yue Liu, Jian Luan, Pei Fu, Qilong Wang

entry.summary: PTD-PO is a privileged tutoring distillation framework for RLVR in vision-language models that provides dense token-level guidance for failed rollouts without exposing answer information. It addresses sparse reward inefficiency in multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: The Sim-to-Real Gap of Foundation Model Agents: A Unified MDP Perspective

author.name: Xiaoou Liu, Tiejin Chen, Weibo Li, Xiyang Hu, Hua Wei

entry.summary: This position paper reframes the sim-to-real gap of foundation model agents through a unified MDP perspective, mapping discrepancies onto observation, action, transition, and reward, and advocates adopting established techniques like domain randomization. It sets a research agenda connecting classical control robustness to foundation model agents.

entry.title: CF-JEPA: Mask-free forward prediction with asymmetric encoder utilization for time-series representation learning

author.name: Jaehoon Lee, Sunghyun Sim

entry.summary: CF-JEPA is a mask-free joint-embedding predictive architecture for time-series representation learning that replaces masking with multi-horizon forward prediction using random crops as context. It avoids disrupting temporal continuity inherent in masking-based methods.

entry.title: SigmaScale: LLM Compression with SVD-based Low-Rank Decomposition and Learned Scaling Matrices

author.name: Ernests Lavrinovics, Marco Letizia, Roy Janco, Shai Segal, Johannes Bjerva, Maurizio Pierini

entry.summary: SigmaScale learns auxiliary diagonal scaling matrices to aid truncated SVD-based LLM compression under an activation-aware loss, lowering the effective intrinsic rank of weight matrices. It is competitive with state-of-the-art SVD compression on Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen3-8B.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Bounds for Sparse Covariance Estimation in the Vertical-Split Distributed Model

author.name: Jing Yee Tan, Guangyue Han

entry.summary: This paper derives information-theoretic minimax bounds for sparse covariance estimation in the vertical-split distributed model where agents observe different feature coordinates with limited communication. It proves that sparsity reduces communication and sample complexity for cross-covariance estimation, in contrast to the horizontal-split setting.

entry.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning

author.name: Christian Bianchi, Siamak Yousefi, Alessio Sampieri, Andrea Roberti, Luca Rigazio, Fabio Galasso, Luca Franco

entry.summary: WIZARD is a weight-space meta-learning framework that generates task-specific LoRA parameters for a frozen Vision-Language-Action policy from only a language instruction and a short demonstration video, in a single forward pass without action labels or test-time optimization. It sidesteps costly per-task fine-tuning for robotic manipulation. The hypernetwork-style fast adaptation for VLAs is a notable efficiency advance.

entry.title: MMAE: A Massive Multitask Audio Editing Benchmark

author.name: Ziyang Ma, Ruiqi Yan, Ruiyang Xu, Jie Fang, Zhikang Niu, Yi-Wen Chao, Wenming Tu, Tianrui Wang, Auden, Qi Chen, Wenxi Chen, Jiaying Chi, Yanru Huo, Zixuan Jiang, Xiquan Li, Yalin Li, Junxi Liu, Minghao Liu, Binghao Qiang, Yijia Shan, Zheshu Song, Tian Tan, Zixiang Wang, Zeyu Xie, Zhifei Xie, Xiaoyu Xing, Qixiang Xu, Chen Yang, Guanrou Yang, Shan Yang, Yifan Yang, Steve Yves, Haotian Zhang, Haina Zhu, Kai Yu, Liefeng Bo, Eng-Siong Chng, Xie Chen

entry.summary: MMAE is the first comprehensive benchmark for general-purpose instruction-based audio editing, spanning 7 audio modalities (sound, speech, music, mixtures) and a taxonomy of editing operations. It addresses fragmented evaluation infrastructure as audio editing expands from visual domains. The large multi-author benchmark establishes a foundational evaluation testbed.

entry.title: Dash2Sim: Closed-Loop Driving Simulation from in-the-wild Dashcam Videos

author.name: Anurag Ghosh, Francesco Pittaluga, Khiem Vuong, Angela Chen, Juan Alvarez-Padilla, Manmohan Chandraker and Srinivasa Narasimhan

entry.summary: Dash2Sim turns in-the-wild monocular dashcam videos into metric, geo-referenced 4D driving logs compatible with existing simulators, verifying each against an independently maintained map without annotations, and uses it to create the ROADWork4D work-zone benchmark. It expands closed-loop driving simulation to broad, long-tailed real-world scenarios. The annotation-free 4D reconstruction from monocular dashcams is a notable advance.

entry.title: RhinoVLA Technical Report

author.name: Huixi Intelligence: Chen Zhang, Chenyang Zhou, Guanglei Ding, Guanghui He, Haibin Gao, Jiajia Chen, Jianyong Zhang, Lianyi Yu, Ningyi Xu, Ping Xu, Qingchen Li, Yingjun Hu, Yijia Zhang, Yuxi Liu

entry.summary: RhinoVLA is a deployment-oriented vision-language-action model co-designed with an edge SoC, using a token-efficient Qwen3-VL backbone and continuous Action Expert to cut visual/context token latency for real-time robotic manipulation. Targets practical edge deployment of VLA models.

entry.title: The Lipreading Gap: Do VSR Models Perceive Visual Speech Like Human Lipreaders?

author.name: Rishabh Jain and Naomi Harte

entry.summary: Compares three visual speech recognition systems to human lipreaders on word-level data, finding that despite higher overall accuracy, models succeed and fail on different words, rely heavily on training word frequency, and do not perceive visual speech like humans. Questions whether benchmark gains imply human-like perception.

entry.title: Time series Foundation Models based on Physics-Informed Synthetic Histories for Cold-Start Photovoltaic Forecasting

author.name: Lorenzo Longarini, Alessandro Rongoni, Simone Silenzi, Emanuele Frontoni and Riccardo Rosati

entry.summary: Addresses cold-start photovoltaic forecasting by generating physics-informed synthetic production histories from plant metadata and weather, enabling time-series foundation models to forecast zero-shot via inference-time conditioning across 440 sites. Covariate-aware TSFMs outperform baselines by roughly 1.7-2x.

entry.title: CoMetaPNS: Continually Meta-learning Personalized Neural Surrogates for Cardiac Electrophysiology Simulations

author.name: Ryan Missel, Xiajun Jiang, Linwei Wang

entry.summary: CoMetaPNS continually meta-learns personalized neural surrogates for cardiac electrophysiology, avoiding costly retraining and catastrophic forgetting when new subject data arrives, without requiring known task identifiers. Combines few-shot personalization with continual learning for virtual heart simulation.

entry.title: Affordance-Based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Quadruped Pedipulation

author.name: Tuba Girgin, Jose Castelblanco, Gabriel Rodriguez, Emre Girgin, Cagri Kilic

entry.summary: Proposes a three-level hierarchical RL framework for quadruped pedipulation that uses pose and interaction-point affordances to guide navigation, locomotion, and manipulation policies, removing the need for expert-designed high-level trajectories. Enables autonomous object-centric manipulation by legged robots.

entry.title: Secret Loyalties Likely Raise Remote-Influenceability

author.name: Kaustubh Kislay

entry.summary: Argues that among capable reward-seeking models a secret installed loyalty likely increases propensity for remote-influenceability (responsiveness to a distant party that can advance reward), and that post-hoc removal may not eliminate this raised propensity, recommending representation-level verification. A conceptual AI safety threat-model analysis.

entry.title: Secure Code Generation at Scale with Reflexion

author.name: Arup Datta, Ahmed Aljohani, Hyunsook Do

entry.summary: Evaluates secure code generation across five instruction-tuned code LLMs using a cleaned prompt protocol and three-round reflexion prompting, measuring repair, regression, and net security gains by language and vulnerability family. Finds 25-33% of programs insecure at baseline, with reflexion improving some categories.

entry.title: Deployed trusted-node quantum key distribution over 300 km with a multi-core fiber access link

author.name: Martin Clason, Joakim Argillander, Didrik Bergstr\"om, Daniel Spegel-Lexne, Giulio Foletto, Ashraf El Hassan, Mohamed Bourennane, Onur G\"unl\"u, Katia Gallo, Rui Lin, Guilherme B. Xavier

entry.summary: Demonstrates deployed trusted-node quantum key distribution over 303 km of real fiber infrastructure including a multi-core fiber access link, using commercial QKD systems with superconducting single-photon detectors. Shows practical QKD coexistence with realistic heterogeneous networks.

entry.title: Capturing non-Markovian dynamics in non-equilibrium stochastic systems using flow matching

author.name: Bhargav Sriram Siddani, John B. Bell, Alejandro L. Garcia, Ishan Srivastava

entry.summary: The authors develop a generative flow matching method to model probability distributions of fluxes in stochastic particle systems, capturing non-Markovian and non-Gaussian effects missed by coarse-grained SPDE models. They demonstrate it on the Kramers first passage time problem for Brownian particles.

entry.title: Optimal Control Approach for Non-prehensile Ball Juggling Using a 7-DoF Manipulator

author.name: Joel Ramadani (1), Vasilije Rak\v{c}evi\'c (1), Riddhiman Laha (1), Arne Sachtler (1 and 3), Valentin Le Mesle (1), Achim J. Lilienthal (1), Sami Haddadin (2) ((1) Technical University of Munich, (2) MBZUAI Abu Dhabi, (3) DLR Oberpfaffenhofen)

entry.summary: This paper develops an optimal control approach for non-prehensile ball juggling using a 7-DoF manipulator, achieving dynamic stabilization of an underactuated object whose stability depends entirely on applied forces. It addresses the highly timing-sensitive hybrid dynamics of high-speed manipulation.

entry.title: Modular Monolingual Adaptation using Pretrained Language Models

author.name: Nalin Kumar, Ond\v{r}ej Du\v{s}ek

entry.summary: This paper proposes a modular approach to adapting pretrained language models for low-resource languages by replacing tokens, freezing the corresponding embeddings, and tuning the rest of the model. Experiments on Scottish Gaelic, Irish, and very low-resource Quechua suggest full model tuning is often unnecessary.

entry.title: MADRAG: Multi-Agent Debate with Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Training-Free Analytic Essay Scoring

author.name: Ali Keramati, Shiyuan Zhou, Sharad Mehrotra, Mark Warschauer

entry.summary: MADRAG is a training-free multi-agent debate framework for analytic essay scoring where an Advocate, Skeptic, and Judge interact, with the Judge augmented by rubric-aligned exemplar retrieval for calibration. It outperforms prompt-based baselines and approaches supervised systems without task-specific training.

entry.title: Progress-SQL: Improving Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-SQL via Progressive Rewards

author.name: Shihao Zhang, Xiaoman Wang, Yuan Liu, Yunshi Lan, Weining Qian

entry.summary: Progress-SQL is a multi-turn RL framework for Text-to-SQL using progressive rewards derived from an Oracle-guided Diagnostic Tree that gives clause-level diagnostic feedback. It provides dense reward signals for iterative SQL refinement.

entry.title: Think Like a Pilot: Fine-Grained Long-Horizon UAV Navigation

author.name: Xiangyi Zheng, Xiangyu Wang, Qinan Liao, Zimu Tang, Yue Liao, Dongyue Lyu, Guodong Wang, Junjie Liu, Si Liu

entry.summary: FLIGHT is a fine-grained long-horizon benchmark for instruction-guided UAV navigation combining multi-stage instructions with dense 6-DoF trajectory annotations. It targets the gap between coarse VLN tasks and short atomic UAV maneuvers.

entry.title: FreeAnimate: Training-Free Human Image Animation with Preview-Guided Denoising

author.name: Yuan Zeng, Yujia Shi, Zongqing Lu, QingMin Liao

entry.summary: FreeAnimate is a training-free human image animation framework that leverages image diffusion models with preview-guided denoising for temporal consistency and identity preservation. It introduces Inversion-Boosted and Reference-Anchored attention modules.

entry.title: Workflow-to-Skill: Skill Creation via Routing-Workflow-Semantics-Attachments Decomposition

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Xinyuan Han, Xudong Jiang and Run Wang

entry.summary: W2S (Workflow-to-Skill) automatically constructs reusable agent Skills from heterogeneous interaction traces using the RWSA intermediate representation decomposing workflow structure, semantics, and runtime attachments. It targets safety-critical and rare behaviors often lost in summarization.

entry.title: Beyond Skeletons: Learning Animation Directly from Driving Videos with Same2X Training Strategy

author.name: Yuan Zeng, Yujia Shi, Yuhao Yang, Dongxia Liu, Zongqing Lu, Wenming Yang, Qingmin Liao

entry.summary: DirectAnimator learns human image animation directly from raw driving videos, bypassing error-prone pose estimators, using a Driving Cue Triplet of pose, face, and location cues fused via a CueFusion DiT block. A Same2X training strategy handles identity mismatch between driving and reference.

entry.title: Quantum-Inspired Trace-Augmented Evidence Selection for Reasoning over Structured Hypothesis Spaces

author.name: Laura Wynter, Nirvik Sahoo, Paul Griffin

entry.summary: This work treats selection of chain-of-thought reasoning fragments as a quantum-inspired combinatorial optimization problem, allowing well-supported minority hypotheses to override noisy majority votes. It is evaluated on evidence-intensive legal reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: When is 3D Worth It? A Resource-Performance Frontier for CNNs and Transformers in Lung CT

author.name: Md Enamul Hoq, Sharafat Hossain, Imraul Emmaka, Linda Larson-Prior, Lawrence Tarbox, Jonathan Bona, Donald Johann Jr.and Fred Prior

entry.summary: This study maps a resource-performance frontier examining how input dimensionality (2D, 2.5D, 3D) affects CNNs and ViTs for lung CT under a fixed protocol. It finds 2.5D CNNs offer the best discrimination-stability trade-off while 3D CNNs show threshold instability and transformers degenerate.

entry.title: Principles of Concept Representation in Sentence Encoders

author.name: Isabelle Mohr, John Dujany, Jonathan Souquet, Andre Freitas

entry.summary: This paper investigates what makes sentence encoders produce good concept representations through a compositionality lens, training on millions of synonym and definition pairs and identifying four principles. It shows fine-tuning recalibrates latent geometry rather than expanding it, with semantic signal concentrating in the final layer.

entry.title: Towards Unified Song Generation and Singing Voice Conversion with Accompaniment Co-Generation

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Chunyu Qiang, Xiaopeng Wang, Yuxin Guo, Kang Yin, Wenjie Tian, Jingbin Hu, Tianlun Zuo, Zhao Guo, Teng Ma, Yuzhe Liang, Chen Zhang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: UniSinger is an end-to-end framework unifying speaker-cloning song generation and accompaniment co-generation singing voice conversion, built on a multimodal diffusion transformer with a unified speaker embedding space. It uses curriculum learning to mitigate multi-task conflicts.

entry.title: UrduMMLU: A Massive Multitask Benchmark for Urdu Language Understanding

author.name: Ahmer Tabassum, Sarfraz Ahmad, Hasan Iqbal, Owais Aijaz, Momina Ahsan and Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: UrduMMLU is a large MMLU-style benchmark of 26,431 native Urdu multiple-choice questions across 26 subjects, built from real educational sources rather than translations, and evaluates 30 LLMs. It fills a major gap for evaluating a language spoken by 230+ million people. The native-source and dual-annotation methodology strengthens multilingual evaluation.

entry.title: Adversarial Creation and Detection of AI-Generated Social Bot Content

author.name: Mykola Trokhymovych, Ricardo Baeza-Yates, Alessandro Flammini, Diego Saez-Trumper, Filippo Menczer

entry.summary: This paper presents an adversarial methodology to model malicious impersonation of real social media users, producing a multilingual cross-platform dataset of paired human and AI-generated messages. Training on this adversarial data yields detectors that outperform existing content-based bot detection on real-world out-of-distribution data. The ground-truth-paired approach addresses a key weakness in AI-text detection.

entry.title: Reversible Foundations: Training a 120B Sparse MoE through State-Preserving Scaling

author.name: Rohan Shravan

entry.summary: An experience report on training a 120B sparse MoE (with reversible recurrence backbone, grown in stages from a dense seed) on a single 8-GPU node, emphasizing reversibility, state-preserving scaling, and high sparsity (about 5% active params). Documents systems disciplines for memory-efficient large-model training.

entry.title: Watch, Remember, Reason: Human-View Video Understanding with MLLMs

author.name: Jiahao Meng, Yue Tan, Qi Xu, Kuan Gao, Weisong Liu, Yanwei Li, Jason Li, Lingdong Kong, Haochen Wang, Qianyu Zhou, Jiangning Zhang, Guangliang Cheng, Yunhai Tong, Lu Qi, Minghsuan Yang

entry.summary: Presents a human-view perspective on MLLM video understanding organized around watching, remembering, and reasoning, providing a unified formulation for how systems acquire evidence, preserve context, and produce grounded outputs in long, knowledge-intensive video. Offers a structuring framework rather than isolated benchmarks.

entry.title: Physiologically Constrained Musculoskeletal Neural Network for Multi-DoF Joint Kinematics Estimation from Partially Observed sEMG

author.name: Wending Heng, Mingming Zhang, Glen Cooper, Zhenhong Li

entry.summary: MSK-NN is a physiologically constrained musculoskeletal neural network estimating multi-DoF joint kinematics from partially observed sEMG while inferring activations of both measured and unmeasured muscles, using a differentiable forward-dynamics module without needing biomechanical labels. Enables kinematics estimation under sensor-limited conditions.

entry.title: Implicit Data Synthesis for Contrastive Unsupervised Data Augmentation

author.name: Patrick Kage, Trevor Hedges, N. Siddharth, Pavlos Andreadis

entry.summary: Proposes generating contrastive learning samples by perturbing network weights rather than data, preserving the underlying structure of scientific observations where data-space augmentations can distort meaning, demonstrated in a SimCLR-based pipeline. Targets unsupervised representation learning for scientific imagery.

entry.title: Gene dependency-informed inference of response to targeted cancer therapies

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications paper on gene dependency-informed inference of patient response to targeted cancer therapies (no abstract text provided). Applies ML to precision oncology using gene dependency information.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Embedding Drift Detection: A Lightweight Defense Against Prompt Injections in LLMs

author.name: Anirudh Sekar, Mrinal Agarwal, Rachel Sharma, Akitsugu Tanaka, Jasmine Zhang, Arjun Damerla, Kevin Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes ZEDD, a lightweight zero-shot defense against prompt injection that detects attacks by measuring semantic drift in embedding space between benign and suspect inputs. It works without model-specific patches for both direct and indirect injections.

entry.title: GOPAgen: Motion-Aware and Efficient Agentic Long-Video Understanding with Structural Memory and Hierarchical Reasoning

author.name: Haozhe Chi, Yang Jin, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: Proposes GOPAgen, an agentic long-video understanding system that integrates video codec Groups-of-Pictures into a motion agent plus a GOP-tree reasoning algorithm and structural memory for efficient motion comprehension. Targets detailed motion understanding with an efficient hierarchical memory architecture.

entry.title: JA-SIREN: Deterministic Initialization for Sinusoidal Networks via Spectral Matching

author.name: Mohammed Alsakabi, Kejia Hu, John M. Dolan, Ozan K. Tonguz

entry.summary: JA-SIREN provides deterministic initialization for sinusoidal implicit neural representations using the Discrete Sine Transform and Jacobi-Anger expansion to derive closed-form weights matching the target signal's spectrum. It addresses reproducibility problems from stochastic initialization that cause large performance variance.

entry.title: Compute-Optimal Network Design for Echocardiography Myocardial Segmentation and Perfusion Quantification using Neural Scaling Laws

author.name: Clara Rodrigo Gonz\'alez, Matthieu Toulemonde, Lasha Gvinianidze, Cameron A. B. Smith, Oscar Bates, Roxy Senior, Fu Siong Ng and Meng-Xing Tang

entry.summary: This work applies neural scaling laws, borrowed from LLM optimization, to predict compute-optimal network size for echocardiography myocardial segmentation and perfusion quantification under scarce in-domain data. It validates clinical utility by comparing derived perfusion parameters against references.

entry.title: Learning Fair Demand Models

author.name: Adam N. Elmachtoub, Hyemi Kim, Jonathan Y. Tan

entry.summary: This paper studies fairness in data-driven pricing by analyzing a two-stage demand-estimation-then-optimization pipeline under parity and Rawlsian fairness notions. It shows how incorporating fairness at different stages affects societal outcomes.

entry.title: CRAFT: A Unified Counterfactual Reasoning Framework for Tabular Question Answering and Fact Verification

author.name: Chenshuo Pan, Yu Zhao, Jie Zhang, Changzai Pan, Zhenhe Wu, Jiayi Liang, Yujie Mao, Shuangyong Song, Yongxiang Li, Zhongjiang He

entry.summary: CRAFT reformulates tabular QA and fact verification into a bidirectional counterfactual verification process, constructing declarative statements and counterfactual variants. Evidence from both reasoning paths is integrated via a weighted mechanism.

entry.title: Multi-FRuGaL: Multimodal Flexible Redundancy-aware Decomposed Gated Learning for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis

author.name: Sanket Kachole, Siddhesh Thakur, Shubham Innani, Sanyukta Adap, Suhang You, Carla Pitarch-Abaigar, Spyridon Bakas

entry.summary: Multi-FRuGaL is a redundancy-aware adaptive gated fusion framework for multimodal cancer diagnosis and prognosis that handles missing modalities. It separates redundant from complementary signals across radiology, pathology, text, and clinical data.

entry.title: Task Editing for Generalizable 3D Visuomotor Policy Learning

author.name: Jian-Jian Jiang, YiHan Yang, Lan Wei, Yuming Luo, Xiao-Ming Wu, Xuhang Chen, Bin Fan, Dandan Zhang, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: Task-Edit is a demonstration generation strategy for 3D visuomotor policy learning that synthesizes diverse scene-skill-object combinations beyond simple object-centric transformations. It aims to improve data efficiency for complex robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Never Seen Before: Benchmarking Genuine Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval with Consistent Video-Sourced Datasets

author.name: Zhenyu Yang, Zemin Du, Shengsheng Qian, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: ZeroSight is a new benchmark for genuine zero-shot composed image retrieval using consistent reference-target pairs sourced from videos, avoiding the contamination of public image datasets seen by CLIP. It addresses irrelevance and non-true-zero-shot issues in existing datasets.

entry.title: Residual-Controlled Multiplier Learning for Stochastic Constrained Decision-Making

author.name: Kang Liu, Jianchen Hu, Ziyu Qu

entry.summary: Residual-Controlled Multiplier Learning reformulates Lagrangian multiplier updates as projected-pressure feedback for stochastic constrained decision-making, decomposing the multiplier into a pressure signal and a memory residual to handle noisy mini-batch gradients. It improves robustness in safety/fairness-constrained optimization.

entry.title: 3DMorph: Single-Image-Guided Local 3D Shape Editing and Morphing

author.name: Tobias Preintner, Yunfei Deng, Phillip M\"uller, Sebastian Illing, Adrian K\"onig, Thomas B\"ack, Elena Raponi, Niki van Stein

entry.summary: 3DMorph is a training-free framework for single-image-guided local 3D shape editing and morphing that automatically localizes the relevant 3D region and transfers 2D modifications to 3D while preserving unmodified areas. It enables intuitive geometry editing of existing meshes.

entry.title: Generative Molecular Morphing for Flexible-Size Design via Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Malte Franke, Stefan P. Schmid, Zarko Ivkovic, Kjell Jorner, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: Morph is a flexible-size generative model for 3D molecular design based on geometric graphs and unbalanced optimal transport, dynamically adapting the number of atoms rather than fixing it as in current diffusion/flow models. This enables better integration of structural priors like scaffolds and improved property steering. The flexible-size morphing addresses a real limitation tying molecular size to properties.

entry.title: Where Rectified Flows Leak: Characterising Membership Signals Along the Interpolation Path

author.name: Thomas Sesmat, Gabriel Meseguer-Brocal and Geoffroy Peeters

entry.summary: This paper characterizes membership-inference signals in Rectified Flow generative models along the interpolation path, showing a bell-shaped train/test reconstruction gap over the interpolation parameter that accumulates during training while validation metrics stay stable, with the peak location derived in closed form. It has implications for copyright and privacy of deployed flow-based systems. The analysis exposes exploitable training-data traces beyond verbatim memorization.

entry.title: Making the Most of Limited Data: Score-Aware Training for Text-to-Music Generation

author.name: Yun-Chen Cheng, Tzu-Hung Huang, Chih-Pin Tan

entry.summary: Proposes score-aware training for text-to-music generation that repurposes low-alignment audio-caption segments via a CLAP-conditioned Beta noise schedule rather than discarding them, plus filtering and two-stage captioning. Aims to enable competitive generation under limited data and compute.

entry.title: Rapid co-design of Buoyancy-assisted robots for Challenging Locomotion using Gaussian Evolutionary Specialists

author.name: Ankit Sinha, Nitish Sontakke, Dennis Hong, Yusuke Tanaka and Sehoon Ha

entry.summary: Proposes Gaussian Evolutionary Specialists for rapid co-design of buoyancy-assisted legged robot morphology and control, addressing behavioral diversity collapse in universal policies and representation collapse in MoE co-design. Enables efficient joint morphology-control optimization for challenging locomotion.

entry.title: Unsupervised Continual Clustering via Forward-Backward Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Mohammadreza Sadeghi, Sareh Soleimani, Zihan Wang, and Narges Armanfard

entry.summary: FBCC introduces Unsupervised Continual Clustering, using forward-backward knowledge distillation with a continual teacher and clustering projector to mitigate catastrophic forgetting without labels or replay buffers. Fills a gap in clustering-specific objectives for unsupervised continual learning.

entry.title: Bradley-Terry Rankings for Recommender Systems Across Dataset Taxonomies

author.name: Ekaterina Grishina, Stepan Kuznetsov, Askar Tsyganov, Ilya Ivanov, Daria Korovaitceva, Margarita Rusanova, Uliana Parkina, Alexander Derevyagin, Evgeny Frolov, Sergey Samsonov, Anton Lysenko

entry.summary: Introduces a Bradley-Terry-based, data-driven methodology for ranking recommendation algorithms that accounts for dataset characteristics like sparsity, sequence structure, and scale, plus a ranking-consistency metric robust to incomplete data. Argues naive metric averaging yields misleading algorithm rankings.

entry.title: Architecture-Adaptive Uncertainty Fusion for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Ritesh Sharma, Mohammad Ghasemigol and Yuichi Motai

entry.summary: COF is an architecture-adaptive framework for deepfake detection that fuses five uncertainty sources by maximizing correlation between fused scores and prediction errors via simplex optimization. It achieves reliable uncertainty quantification in seconds versus tens of hours for deep ensembles.

entry.title: HybridCodec: Fast Dual-Stream, Semantically Enhanced Neural Audio Codec

author.name: Arjun Gangwar, S Umesh

entry.summary: HybridCodec is a neural audio codec unifying two semantic-acoustic disentanglement paradigms by employing separate semantic and acoustic branches while distilling SSL representations into the semantic stream. This achieves strong disentanglement without requiring an SSL model at inference.

entry.title: FS-DVS: A Frequency-Selective Dynamic Visual Sensing Paradigm for Enhancing Information Completeness

author.name: Feiyu Ji, Xiaokang Yang, Xiaoyun Yuan

entry.summary: FS-DVS is a frequency-selective dynamic vision sensing paradigm that inserts a learnable spatial filter before event triggering to mimic retinal ganglion cell aggregation. It aims to recover information lost to sub-threshold signals in conventional DVS.

entry.title: What Is My Robot Thinking? Design Considerations for Transparent and Trustworthy Shared Autonomy

author.name: Atharv Belsare, Zohre Karimi, Connor Mattson, Rushiil Nakka, and Daniel S. Brown

entry.summary: This user study (N=25) investigates how interface transparency choices, feedback modality, and information richness affect trust and coordination in vision-based shared-autonomy robots. It finds that making inferred goals legible improves intent alignment and reduces corrective intervention.

entry.title: Declarative Skills for AI Agents in Knowledge-Grounded Tool-Use Workflows

author.name: M. Danish Lim, I. Danial Bin Sharudin, Wen Han Chen, Cedric Lim, Laura Wynter

entry.summary: This paper argues that declarative agents equipped with natural-language skill files are an effective orchestration paradigm, comparing them against imperative state-machine agents and an unscaffolded baseline in customer-service workflows. It formalizes the three agents as policies over an unstructured knowledge base.

entry.title: SVHighlights: Towards Extremely Long Sport Video Highlight Detection

author.name: Donggyu Lee, Youngbin Ki, Jeonghun Kang, and Taehwan Kim

entry.summary: SVHighlights is the first benchmark for highlight detection in extremely long sports videos exceeding one hour, built from full-game and official-highlight pairs across multiple sports. It comprises 320 videos totaling over 640 hours via a scalable label-generation pipeline.

entry.title: SS-TPT: Stability and Suitability-Guided Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Adversarially Robust Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sunoh Kim, Daeho Um

entry.summary: SS-TPT is a stability-and-suitability-guided test-time prompt tuning method for adversarially robust VLMs that scores augmented views by prediction invariance and feature-space density. It improves robustness while addressing the slowdown of using many augmented views.

entry.title: MADE: Beyond Scoring via a Multilingual Agentic Diagnosing Engine for Fine-Grained Evaluation Insights

author.name: Yilun Liu, Miao Zhang, Shimin Tao, Minggui He, Chunguang Zhao, Chenxin Liu, Li Zhang, Chen Liu, Cheng Qian, Liqun Deng, Xiaojun Meng, Daimeng Wei

entry.summary: MADE is a multilingual agentic diagnosing engine that decomposes post-evaluation analysis into planning, aggregate analysis, case inspection, cultural reflection, and report synthesis. It targets actionable insights from metric-rich but insight-poor multilingual benchmark landscapes.

entry.title: Front-to-Attractors: Modifying the Front-to-Front Heuristic in Bidirectional Search

author.name: Alvin Zou, Muhammad Suhail Saleem, Maxim Likhachev

entry.summary: This paper introduces front-to-attractors, a new heuristic class for bidirectional search that preserves much of the informativeness of front-to-front heuristics while reducing the computational overhead of extensive pairwise evaluations. It modifies the classic F2F heuristic.

entry.title: TrioPose: Native Triple-Stream Diffusion Transformers for Pose-Guided Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Dian Gu, Zhengyi Yang

entry.summary: TrioPose is a native triple-stream diffusion transformer for pose-guided text-to-image generation built on SD3.5M, treating pose as an independent modality with layer-wise activation and zero-initialized residual injection. It addresses limb distortions and feature crosstalk in multi-person scenarios.

entry.title: GP-Adapter: Gaussian Process CLIP-Adapter for Few-Shot Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Taisei Saito, Koretaka Ogata, Takafumi Hiroi

entry.summary: GP-Adapter is a training-free framework augmenting CLIP with Gaussian process uncertainty modeling for few-shot classification and out-of-distribution detection, using modality-specific class-wise one-class GPs to produce variance-aware confidence scores. It requires no backbone fine-tuning.

entry.title: Style or Content? Evaluating Style Classifiers with Controlled Content Overlap

author.name: Zhuo Liu, Haozheng Du, Xiangxiang Xu, Hangfeng He

entry.summary: This paper studies whether style classifiers rely on content cues using a controlled content overlap setup on parallel Bible translations, defining an overlap parameter via mutual information residuals. It shows low-overlap models degrade when content is removed while high-overlap models transfer more robustly.

entry.title: Learning Perspectivist Social Meaning via Demographic-Conditioned Fusion Embeddings

author.name: Amanda Cercas Curry, Lucio La Cava, Luca Maria Aiello, Gianmarco De Francisci Morales

entry.summary: This work models social meaning along a perspectivist spectrum capturing how interpretations vary across demographic groups, using 28k human annotations and proposing demographic-conditioned fusion embeddings. The fusion models yield consistent significant improvements over text-only baselines.

entry.title: EvoGS: Constructing Continuous-Layered Gaussian Splatting with Evolution Tree for Scalable 3D Streaming

author.name: Yuang Shi, Simone Gasparini, G\'eraldine Morin, Wei Tsang Ooi

entry.summary: EvoGS introduces continuous-layering Gaussian Splatting organized as an evolution tree with wavelet-inspired parent-child refinement, replacing discrete level-of-detail layering for scalable 3D streaming. It reduces splat redundancy from over 65% to under 25% and corrects ancestral errors structurally. The continuous-layering design is a genuine advance for streamable 3D representations.

entry.title: Off-Policy Evaluation with Strategic Agents via Local Disclosure

author.name: Kiet Q. H. Vo, Abbavaram Gowtham Reddy, Julian Rodemann, Siu Lun Chau, Krikamol Muandet

entry.summary: This paper studies off-policy evaluation when strategic agents modify their covariates in response to a policy, inducing policy-dependent covariate shift that breaks standard OPE assumptions. It proposes using post-hoc explanations to disclose local information revealing agents' pre-strategic covariates in a one-shot setting with only partial knowledge of response behavior. The connection between explanations and strategic OPE is novel.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Evolution for Medical Decision Pipelines

author.name: Ivan Sviridov, Artem Oskin, Ivan Panin, Iaroslav Bespalov, Dmitry Dylov, Ivan Oseledets, Aleksandr Nesterov

entry.summary: This work studies LLM-guided MAP-Elites evolution as an inference-time alternative to fine-tuning for discovering medical decision pipelines, formulating triage, consultation, and image classification as evolutionary searches over executable artifacts. Evolved programs substantially improve over manual baselines, raising triage accuracy and emergency recall. The evolutionary inference-time pipeline discovery is a credible contribution with strong author backing.

entry.title: Discovering Multiscale Deep Formulas in Complex Systems via Neural-Guided Lambda Calculus

author.name: Hanqiao Yu, Shusen Yang, Xuebin Ren, and Cong Zhao

entry.summary: Builds a scalable simulation framework that auto-generates diverse reach-to-grasp demonstrations from a wrist-mounted virtual camera to train biosignals-free shared-autonomy control of prosthetic hands, avoiding costly real-world data collection. Targets natural, low-effort prosthetic grasping without EMG.

entry.title: PaperFlow: Profiling, Recommending, and Adapting Across Daily Paper Streams

author.name: Fuqiang Wang, Song Tan, Zheng Guo, Jiaohao Fu, Xinglong Xu, Bihui Yu, Jie Dong, Zheng Sun, Siyuan Li, Jingxuan Wei, Cheng Tan

entry.summary: PaperFlow reframes scientific paper recommendation as a longitudinal daily process with coupled Profiling, Recommending, and Adapting stages plus a user-day benchmark capturing interest drift and accumulating feedback. Moves beyond static ranking to realistic, evolving recommendation.

entry.title: ChronoForest: Closed-Loop Multi-Tree Diffusion Planning for Efficient Bridge Search and Route Composition

author.name: Jungmin Seo and Jaesik Park

entry.summary: Proposes ChronoForest, a closed-loop multi-tree diffusion planning method for long-horizon route composition from only short-horizon offline trajectories, addressing both segment-composition search-versus-quality trade-offs and waypoint ordering. Targets efficient goal-reaching routes that visit required waypoints.

entry.title: SCALE: Scalable Cross-Attention Learning with Extrapolation for Agentic Workflow Scheduling

author.name: Zhifei Xu, Jierui Lan, Zixuan Liang, Aiji Liang, Jinxi He

entry.summary: SCALE is a deep RL scheduler for agentic LLM workflow DAGs that uses a cross-attention pointer network to generalize across cluster sizes without retraining. It addresses distribution shift issues when extrapolating to unseen scales.

entry.title: EgoPressDiff: Multimodal Video Diffusion for Egocentric UV-Domain Hand-Pressure Estimation

author.name: Yuan Zeng, Zilue Gao, Yujia Shi, Zongqing Lu, Wenming Yang, QingMin Liao

entry.summary: EgoPressDiff is a conditional video diffusion framework that generates UV-domain hand-pressure maps from egocentric video using pose, mesh, and depth conditioning. It addresses temporal inconsistency and quantization errors in contact pressure estimation.

entry.title: A Cross-view Fusion Framework for Robust 6-DoF Grasp Pose Estimation

author.name: Kangjian Zhu, Haobo Jiang, Jianjun Qian, Jin Xie

entry.summary: This work proposes a cross-view fusion framework for robust 6-DoF grasp pose estimation that handles occlusion via an auxiliary view and self-supervised contrastive learning. It avoids costly multi-view reconstruction through post-fusion.

entry.title: LUCID: Learning Unified Control for Image Deflaring and Exposure Mastery in Nighttime Photography

author.name: Tingyu Yang, Yuan Cheng, and Xiaoyun Yuan

entry.summary: LUCID is a unified framework for nighttime photography restoration that treats flare removal and exposure correction as entangled, controllable processes. It combines a flare disentanglement module with a diffusion-driven generative reconstruction module.

entry.title: When CLIP Sees More, It Fights Back Harder: Multi-View Guided Adaptive Counterattacks for Test-Time Adversarial Robustness

author.name: Sunoh Kim, Daeho Um

entry.summary: MAC (Multi-view guided Adaptive Counterattack) improves CLIP's test-time adversarial robustness by using multiple augmented views with corruption-aware soft weighting instead of a single corrupted view and hard gating. It strengthens counterattacks under strong adversarial perturbations.

entry.title: CL-CLIP: CLIP-Based Continual Learning Framework with Cost-Volume Category Decoupling for Object Detection

author.name: Zihan Liu, Yuguang Yang, Shengjie Su, Jianing Pang, Linlin Yang, Chunyu Xie, Nikolai Yu. Zolotykh, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: CL-CLIP is a CLIP-based continual learning framework for object detection that uses cost-volume category decoupling to mitigate catastrophic forgetting while preserving zero-shot generalization. It bridges open-vocabulary and continual detection settings.

entry.title: DIFFRACT: Neuralized Utility Maximization for Wireless Networks by Differentiable Programming

author.name: Chee Wei Tan and Siya Chen

entry.summary: DIFFRACT is a neuralized utility maximization framework for wireless networks using differentiable programming, mapping iterative interference management algorithms into differentiable architectures via algorithm unrolling with a duality theory for interference functions. It enables distributed end-to-end gradient-based resource management.

entry.title: A Data-Free Symbolic Regression Approach for Solving Equations

author.name: Sergei Garmaev, Vinay Sharma, Olga Fink

entry.summary: The Symbolic Equation Solver (SES) formulates equation solving as optimization over differentiable symbolic models using only the governing equation and boundary conditions, eliminating the need for paired input-output training data. It returns explicit symbolic solutions for algebraic and differential equations. This data-free symbolic regression approach is a genuinely novel framing.

entry.title: Test-Time Trajectory Optimization for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yihong Xu, Eloi Zablocki, Yuan Yin, Elias Ramzi, Ellington Kirby, Alexandre Boulch, Matthieu Cord

entry.summary: TOAD treats an autonomous-driving planner's scorer as a learned reward and runs Cross-Entropy Method search at test time to find higher-scoring trajectories, requiring no retraining. It improves results across six base planners on NAVSIM and HUGSIM benchmarks. The plug-and-play test-time optimization is a clean, generalizable idea.

entry.title: A Held-Out Transition-Pair Falsifier for Long-Horizon Non-Abelian State Tracking

author.name: Jeonghoon Lee

entry.summary: This paper introduces a held-out transition-pair falsifier for finite non-Abelian group state tracking, forbidding selected ordered generator pairs in training to block local-transition memorization. A projected recurrent state model trained on length-8 sequences achieves error-free predictions up to over a million tokens, far outperforming GRU and bag baselines. The result probes genuine algorithmic length-generalization in sequence models.

entry.title: AnchorWorld: Embodied Egocentric World Simulation with View-based Evolution Customization

author.name: Yu Li, Menghan Xia, Gongye Liu, Xintao Wang, Conglang Zhang, Lei Ke, Yuxuan Lin, Ruihang Chu, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: AnchorWorld is a framework for embodied egocentric world simulation using 3D human motion as the primary interaction modality, with auxiliary exogenous-viewpoint supervision to complement truncated body parts in first-person views and enable flexible world customization. It improves spatial grounding of human-world interactions. The egocentric simulation with view-based evolution is a notable contribution to interactive world modeling.

entry.title: TabSwift: An Efficient Tabular Foundation Model with Row-Wise Attention

author.name: Si-Yang Liu, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: TabSwift revisits TabPFN and shows a lightweight row-wise attention-only backbone stays competitive with two simple enhancements: gated attention stabilization and learnable register tokens for global context, reducing inference cost versus increasingly complex tabular foundation models. It supports classification and regression via in-context learning. The efficiency-focused simplification is a useful corrective to architectural bloat.

entry.title: Impact of Synthetic Lesional MR Images in Automated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Detection in Low-Data Scenarios

author.name: Prabhjot Kaur, Hakim Ouaalam, Sedat Kandemirli, Sanjay P. Prabhu, Simon K. Warfield

entry.summary: Generates synthetic lesional MRI conditioned on FCD masks and shows the synthetic data improves automated focal cortical dysplasia detection in low-data settings, reducing the need for manual annotations. Neuroradiologists could not reliably distinguish synthetic from real scans.

entry.title: Amortized Neural Optimization for Pre-Layout Signal Integrity Design Space Exploration using Differentiable Surrogates

author.name: Julian With\"oft, Werner John, Emre Ecik, Ralf Br\"uning, J\"urgen G\"otze

entry.summary: Amortized neural optimization (ANO) eliminates iterative black-box search in pre-layout signal-integrity design by training a global optimization policy using analytical gradients extracted from differentiable surrogate models. Enables fast multi-corner design space exploration in EDA workflows.

entry.title: Graph Neural Network leveraging Higher-order Class Label Connectivity for Heterophilous Graphs

author.name: Takuto Takahashi, Itsuki Nakayama, Takahiro Mitani, Ryosuke Kikuchi, Yuya Sasaki, Makoto Onizuka

entry.summary: Proposes the Label Context Classifier (LCC) to capture higher-order class-label connectivity in directed heterophilous graphs, where neighboring nodes tend to have different labels, improving node classification beyond convolution-based GNNs. Targets a known weakness of standard GNNs.
