entry.summary: VentAgent uses LLMs for multi-objective arbitration in ARDS mechanical ventilation, balancing oxygenation, lung protection, and acid-base homeostasis while addressing imitation bias from inconsistent EHR demonstrations and the opacity of standard RL policies. It targets interpretable, robust ventilation decision support.

entry.title: Learning Empirically Admissible Neural Heuristics for Combinatorial Search

author.name: Siddharth Sahay

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for learning validation-calibrated admissible neural heuristics for combinatorial search puzzles, ensuring A* optimality by avoiding the overestimation that standard MSE training produces. It calibrates value networks to never overestimate cost-to-go.

entry.title: Deliberate Evolution: Agentic Reasoning for Sample-Efficient Symbolic Regression with LLMs

author.name: Xinyu Pang, Zhanke Zhou, Xuan Li, Fangrui Lv, Shanshan Wei, Sen Cui, Bo Han, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Deliberate Evolution is an agentic framework for symbolic regression that decouples candidate generation from search control, using adaptive operators, analytical diagnostic tools, and reflective memory to improve sample efficiency. It addresses the limitation of LLM-based SR methods relying only on scalar MSE feedback.

entry.title: Beyond Symmetric Alignment: Spectral Diagnostics of Modality Imbalance in Vision-Language Models in the Medical Domain

author.name: Alessandro Gambetti, Qiwei Han, Cl\'audia Soares, Hong Shen

entry.summary: This work introduces the Spectral Alignment Score, an asymmetric metric that projects vision and language modalities onto an anchor's principal eigenbasis to quantify directional modality information imbalance, diagnosing why VLMs fail on medical image-text data. It benchmarks 15 VLMs across natural and medical datasets.

entry.title: Beyond Objective Equivalence: Constraint Injection for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling on Vehicle Routing Problems

author.name: Xizi Luo, Changhong He, Dongdong Geng, Chenggong Shi, Yu Mei

entry.summary: This work proposes constraint injection for LLM-based optimization modeling, using feasible probes to expose spurious over-constraints and one-constraint-violating probes to reveal silent omissions, forming a dual verifier alongside differential testing. It addresses the weakness of objective-equivalence signals for constraint-dense operations research problems like vehicle routing.

entry.title: Localizing Prompt Ambiguity in Large Language Models with Probe-Targeted Attribution

author.name: Govind Ramesh, Yao Dou, Wei Xu

entry.summary: PRIG is a gradient attribution method that uses a trained linear probe distinguishing clear from ambiguous prompts to attribute latent prompt ambiguity to specific token positions. It addresses the difficulty that ambiguity is a latent prompt property, unlike observable outputs that existing attribution methods explain.

entry.title: TARPO: Token-Wise Latent-Explicit Reasoning via Action-Routing Policy Optimization

author.name: Liting Zhang, Shiwan Zhao, Xuyang Zhao, Zichen Xu, Jianye Wang, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: TARPO is a pure-RL framework that adaptively routes between discrete token generation and continuous latent reasoning at each step using a lightweight action head, restoring policy exploration that deterministic latent reasoning lacks. It blends explicit and latent reasoning.

entry.title: IA-RAG: Interval-Algebra-Driven Temporal Reasoning for Dynamic Knowledge Retrieval

author.name: Xiaoman Wang, Yaoze Zhang, Wenzhuo Fan, Hongwei Zhang, Ding Wang, Guohang Yan, Song Mao, Botian Shi, Yunshi Lan, Pinlong Cai

entry.summary: IA-RAG models knowledge as time intervals organized in a hierarchical Thematic Forest governed by Allen's Interval Algebra, enabling temporal reasoning over duration, overlap, and containment in retrieval. It addresses coarse timestamp handling in RAG.

entry.title: Membrane: A Self-Evolving Contrastive Safety Memory for LLM Agent Defense

author.name: Minseok Choi, Seungbin Yang, Dongjin Kim, Subin Kim, Jungmin Son, Yunseung Lee, Jaegul Choo, Youngjun Kwak

entry.summary: Membrane is a self-evolving guardrail with Contrastive Safety Memory pairing harmful-query blocking conditions with permitting superficially similar benign requests, evolving without retraining to resist new jailbreaks while reducing over-refusal. It distills contrastive cells indexed by attack strategy.

entry.title: Asuka-Bench: Benchmarking Code Agents on Underspecified User Intent and Multi-Round Refinement

author.name: Xin Wang, Liangtai Sun, Yaoming Zhu, Shuang Zhou, Jiaxing Liu, Fengjiao Chen, Lin Qiu, Xuezhi Cao, Xunliang Cai, Licheng Zhang, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: Asuka-Bench benchmarks code agents on underspecified user intent and multi-round refinement grounded in browser-rendered behavior, using a closed loop of Code Agent, UI Agent, and User LLM. It comprises 50 web tasks with 784 criteria and 2402 expected outcomes.

entry.title: LLM-Guided ANN Index Optimization for Human-Object Interaction Retrieval

author.name: Shahrzad Esmat, Chaunte W. Lacewell, Sameh Gobriel, Nilesh Jain, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: This paper proposes a phase-aware LLM agent for optimizing coupled approximate nearest neighbor index parameters in human-object interaction retrieval, overcoming the independence assumption limiting traditional hyperparameter optimization. The LLM conditions proposals on full optimization history across exploration and exploitation phases.

entry.title: Multi-Task Crack Foundation Model for Engineering-Reliable Crack Representation and Topology Preservation in Civil Infrastructure

author.name: Blessing Agyei Kyem, Joshua Kofi Asamoah, Eugene Denteh, Armstrong Aboah

entry.summary: CrackGeoFM is a multi-task crack foundation model combining a frozen visual backbone with crack-specific adaptation for mask prediction, skeleton reconstruction, and uncertainty estimation. It addresses topology preservation and calibrated uncertainty for reliable civil infrastructure crack assessment under domain shift.

entry.title: Unveiling the Unknown: Open Vocabulary Object Detection with Scene Graphs

author.name: Yi Chen, Yinghao Lu, Zhehao Li, Chenchen Yan, Jiafei Wu, Chong Wang, Jiangbo Qian

entry.summary: This work proposes a scene-guided relational modeling framework for open-vocabulary object detection, using scene graphs to capture structured semantic and spatial relationships between candidate regions. This addresses the oversight of image-specific object relationships in knowledge-distillation approaches.

entry.title: RQUL-UIE: Revitalizing Quality-Unstable Labels for Underwater Image Enhancement via In-Dataset Self-Supervision

author.name: Haochen Hu, Yanrui Bin, Chih-yung Wen, Bing Wang

entry.summary: RQUL-UIE proposes a diffusion-based in-dataset self-supervised strategy for underwater image enhancement that exploits the quality distribution of unstable training labels. It evaluates label quality via diffusion semantic embeddings and quantizes scores into noise levels for level-wise supervision, preventing low-quality labels from degrading the model.

entry.title: SC-MFJ: A Simple Haptic Quality Metric for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Souraj Adhikary, Negar Chabi, Andre Mastmeyer

entry.summary: SC-MFJ is a simple, inexpensive haptic quality metric for medical image segmentation that samples a segmented organ surface with virtual stylus walks and measures contact-force jerkiness. It evaluates surface suitability for haptic rendering in surgical simulation, revealing large differences (147x) between segmentation approaches that Dice/Hausdorff miss.

entry.title: GMBFormer: An NDVI-Guided Global Memory Bank Transformer for Urban Green-Space Extraction from Ultra-High-Resolution Imagery

author.name: Hao Lei, Xi Cheng, Chenlu Shu, Zhiheng Chen, Zhengjie Duan, Haoyu Wang, Zhanfeng Shen

entry.summary: GMBFormer is a SegFormer-based framework for urban green-space extraction from ultra-high-resolution imagery that replaces adjacency-driven feature propagation with similarity-driven prototype retrieval into a global memory bank. NDVI is decoupled as a physics-informed gate rather than mixed into the RGB backbone.

entry.title: OLIVE: Online Low-Rank Incremental Learning for Efficient Adaptive Exoskeletons

author.name: Dong Liu, Yanxuan Yu, Ben Lengerich, Tony Geng, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: OLIVE provides parameter-efficient online low-rank incremental adaptation for exoskeleton control, personalizing policies during deployment by decomposing updates into a low-rank residual. Reduces online update cost substantially.

entry.title: VOLT: Vision and Language Trajectory Segmentation for Faster-than-Demonstration Policies

author.name: Robert Ramirez Sanchez, Daniel J. Evans, Dylan P. Losey, Siddarth Jain

entry.summary: VOLT uses vision and language to segment demonstration trajectories and selectively downsample segments, learning robot policies that execute faster than human demonstrations while preserving precision where needed. Finds non-uniform downsampling outperforms uniform speedup.

entry.title: Wave Focusing in Metamaterials: Tactile Displays Beyond the Diffraction Limit

author.name: Gregory Reardon, Max Linnander, Dustin Goetz, Neeli Tummala, Yon Visell

entry.summary: Engineers distributed haptic displays that focus mechanical waves below the diffraction limit by augmenting a flexural plate with a locally resonant metamaterial lattice, creating independently addressable virtual tactile pixels. Overcomes wave diffraction limits at tactile frequencies.

entry.title: Effective Dimensionality as an Operator Invariant for Physics-Preserving Constraint Adaptation in Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Cornelius Otchere, Michael Shields

entry.summary: Analyzes task interference in physics-informed neural networks using the Fisher Information Matrix to define an effective dimensionality measuring parameter directions unconstrained by the differential operator. Shows d_eff converges exactly to the operator kernel dimension independent of network architecture.

entry.title: I Know What You Meme, Even If it Emerged Today: Understanding Evolving Memes through Open-World Knowledge Acquisition

author.name: Shanhong Liu, Rui Cao, Pai Chet Ng, De Wen Soh

entry.summary: Introduces Query-Retrieve-Conclude, a zero-shot framework that fetches open-web evidence to interpret emerging multimodal memes, plus a 2024-2026 meme benchmark with knowledge annotations. It matters for keeping multimodal understanding current with fast-evolving cultural content.

entry.title: Critic-Guided Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reasoning for Reliable Mathematical Problem Solving

author.name: Muhammad Talha Sharif, Abdul Rehman

entry.summary: Proposes a critic-guided heterogeneous multi-agent generator-validator framework where the validator both judges correctness and offers critiques to guide regeneration, improving reliability on complex math problems. It matters for reducing hallucinations in mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: Statistical Priors for Implicit Preferences: Decoupling Skill Selection as a Local Harness in Personal Agents

author.name: Zeyu Gan, Huayi Tang, Yong Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight local preference harness for personal agents that decouples statistical preference learning from semantic intent parsing to handle implicit user preferences over expanding skill sets under local-deployment constraints. It matters for personalizing locally deployed agents using remote models.

entry.title: RedditPersona: A Modular Framework for Community-Conditioned LLM Adaptation from Reddit

author.name: Amirhossein Ghaffari, Ali Goodarzi, Huong Nguyen, Simo Hosio, Lauri Lov\'en, Ekaterina Gilman

entry.summary: Presents RedditPersona, a modular framework standardizing community-conditioned LLM adaptation choices, profiling users under five grouping strategies, training QLoRA adapters per strategy, and evaluating with a shared metric suite across fluency, fidelity, alignment, and community identifiability. It matters for reproducible community-conditioned adaptation research.

entry.title: Personal AI Agent for Camera Roll VQA

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Krishna Kumar Singh, Donghyun Kim, Yong Jae Lee, Yuheng Li

entry.summary: Studies personal camera roll visual question answering, where a conversational assistant retrieves relevant photos from large personal collections to answer factual and open-ended queries. Collects and annotates real-world-style questions requiring long-horizon personalized visual understanding.

entry.title: Can AI Refute Economic Theory? Evidence from Beyond the Knowledge Cutoff

author.name: Alexis Akira Toda

entry.summary: Documents experiments asking AI models (Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, Refine) to check correctness of four published economic theory papers containing known errors. ChatGPT Pro performed best but no model found a true error without substantial human guidance, complicated by data contamination.

entry.title: Selective-Advantage Entropy-Adaptive Horizon GRPO: Asymmetric Token-Level Discounting for Efficient Reinforcement Learning of Language Models

author.name: Chirag Chawla, Rohan Charudatt Salvi, Madhav S. Baidya

entry.summary: Extends GRPO reinforcement learning for language models with entropy-based adaptive token-level discounting and selective application to negative-advantage rollouts. Aims to improve training efficiency by treating tokens and rollouts asymmetrically.

entry.title: When New Generators Arrive: Lifelong Machine-Generated Text Attribution via Ridge Feature Transfer

author.name: Zhen Sun, Yifan Liao, Zhicong Huang, Jiaheng Wei, Cheng Hong, Yutao Yue, Xinlei He

entry.summary: Proposes RidgeFT, a lightweight exemplar-free analytic update framework for lifelong machine-generated text attribution that incorporates new text generators while retaining recognition of previously seen ones. Addresses the stability-plasticity balance in continually identifying which LLM produced a given text.

entry.title: Beyond Waveform Robustness: Robust Feature-Vocoder Adversarial Attacks on Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Yifan Liao, Zongmin Zhang, Zhen Sun, Yuhui Sun, Xinhu Zheng, Xinlei He

entry.summary: Proposes a Clean-Referenced Feature-Vocoder adversarial attack on ASR systems that moves the adversarial search from raw waveforms to self-supervised learning representations, improving black-box transferability and evading input-space defenses. Targets robustness limitations of prior waveform attacks.

entry.title: Narrative Knowledge Weaver: Narrative-Centric Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Long-Form Text Understanding

author.name: Qiuyu Tian, Fengyi Chen, Yiding Li, Youyong Kong, Fan Guo, Yuyao Li, Jinjing Shen, Zhijing Xie, Yiyun Luo, Xin Zhang, Yingce Xia, Zequn Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Narrative Knowledge Weaver, a source-grounded retrieval-augmented framework that aligns textual evidence with atomic facts, graph structure, entity profiles, episodes, and storylines for long-form narrative QA. Encodes how evidence functions within a story rather than just relations or chunks.

entry.title: MARDoc: A Memory-Aware Refinement Agent Framework for Multimodal Long Document QA

author.name: Kaifeng Chen, Hongtao Liu, Qiyao Peng, Jian Yang, Yongqiang Liu, Xiaochen Zhang, Qing Yang

entry.summary: Proposes MARDoc, a memory-aware refinement agent framework that decouples multimodal long-document QA into Explorer, Refiner, and Reflector agents to distill interaction traces into structured evidence memories. Addresses scattered and diluted evidence in single growing-context iterative agents.

entry.title: Staying with the Uncertainty: Uncertainty-Scaffolding Strategies for Artificial Moral Advisors in LLM-to-LLM Simulated Conversations

author.name: Salvatore Greco, Hainiu Xu, Jacopo Domenicucci, Yulan He, Sylvie Delacroix

entry.summary: Studies how LLM-based Artificial Moral Advisors can help interlocutors stay with uncertainty, proposing three uncertainty modes (Perspective-Multiplying, Tension-Preserving, Process-Reflecting) compared against persuasive and sycophantic controls in LLM-to-LLM simulated ethical dialogues. Examines persona prompt formats and finds no single model dominates as simulator.

entry.title: Measuring the sensitivity of LLM-based structured extraction to prompt, model, and schema choices in clinical discharge summaries

author.name: Martin Murin

entry.summary: Proposes a query-adaptive audio-visual person retrieval framework that detects active modalities via cross-modal score consistency, avoiding noise injection from absent modalities in real-world broadcast archives. Achieves 89% modality-detection accuracy and improves retrieval over fixed multimodal fusion on the BBC Rewind corpus.

entry.title: A Finite Certificate for the Positive $n=9$ Vasc Inequality

author.name: Dakai Guo, Ruichen Qiu, Yichuan Cao, Ruyong Feng

entry.summary: Provides a finite certificate proving the positive n=9 case of the Vasc cyclic inequality, using a human-guided AI agent to generate and verify a certificate covering all 40320 sorted cones. It demonstrates AI-assisted formal mathematical proof at substantial combinatorial scale.

entry.title: EasyLens: A Training-Free Plug-and-Play Subtle-Lesion Representation Amplifier for Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Qiwei Zeng, Hao Wang, Jinghao Lin, Shuchang Ye, Yuezhe Yang, Yige Peng, Haoyuan Che, Jinman Kim, Lei Bi

entry.summary: EasyLens is a training-free, plug-and-play module that amplifies subtle-lesion representations in medical vision-language models, addressing how weak lesion cues get underrepresented when local tokens are aggregated into global representations. It improves lesion sensitivity without retraining vision encoders.

entry.title: Position: Deployed Reinforcement Learning should be Continual

author.name: Parnian Behdin, Kevin Roice, Golnaz Mesbahi

entry.summary: This position paper argues that deployed reinforcement learning should be continual, contending that any deployed agent receiving evaluative rewards but incapable of optimality is inherently facing a continual RL problem. It identifies four post-deployment sources of non-stationarity and analyzes real-world continual RL successes.

entry.title: LLM Compression with Jointly Optimizing Architectural and Quantization choices

author.name: Hoang-Loc La, Truong-Thanh Le, Amir Taherkordi, Phuong Hoai Ha

entry.summary: Introduces a differentiable neural architecture search framework that explores the full search space and jointly optimizes architectural configurations with mixed-precision quantization for LLM linear layers, aiming to compress pretrained LLMs for edge devices. It avoids decoupling architecture from quantization as in prior NAS.

entry.title: Stationarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Shiqiao Zhou, Holger Sch\"oner, Zipeng Wu, Edouard Fouch\'e, IAG Wilson, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: SARAF adapts retrieval-augmented generation ideas to time series forecasting by balancing relevance and diversity when retrieving historical segments, addressing the problem that similar past patterns don't guarantee similar futures under non-stationarity. It aims to make retrieval-based forecasting more robust to regime shifts.

entry.title: ADAPTOOD: Uncertainty-Aware Fine-Tuning for Out-of-Distribution ECG Time Series Models

author.name: Sotirios Vavaroutas, Yu Yvonne Wu, Ali Etemad, Cecilia Mascolo

entry.summary: ADAPTOOD proposes uncertainty-aware fine-tuning for out-of-distribution ECG time series, explicitly accounting for shift severity rather than treating all distribution shifts identically. It targets robust medical sensor models when only small annotated datasets are available.

entry.title: PE-MHL: Physics-Encoded Modular Hybrid Layers for Scalable Learning of Complex Systems

author.name: Ismail Hassaballa, Mircea Lazar

entry.summary: PE-MHL is a physics-encoded modular hybrid layer framework that incrementally refines a baseline physics model by adding sub-models, each preserving prior learned components, with a least-squares-initialization training guarantee. It targets scalable, interpretable learning of complex systems for control.

entry.title: Latent Anchor-Driven Test Generation for Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Bin Duan, Matthew B. Dwyer, Guowei Yang

entry.summary: Latte is a black-box DNN testing framework that generates semantically proximate, diverse, and fault-revealing test cases by leveraging latent-space anchors. It addresses trade-offs among exploration controllability, failure diversity, and semantic drift in safety-critical model testing.

entry.title: Contrastive Learning and Correlation Clustering for Sequences of Network Telescope Data

author.name: Jannik Presberger, Alexander M\"annel, Maynard Koch, Thomas C. Schmidt, Matthias W\"ahlisch, Bjoern Andres

entry.summary: This work uses contrastive learning (without pretraining or annotations) to embed sequences of network flow records from internet scanners, then formulates and solves a correlation clustering problem to estimate semantically meaningful relationships between scanner sources. It addresses the scarcity of semantic annotations in network telescope analysis.

entry.title: UniFair: A unified fair clustering approach based on separation and compactness

author.name: Antonia Karra, Vasiliki Papanikou, Georgios Vardakas, Evaggelia Pitoura, Aristidis Likas

entry.summary: Proposes UniFair, a fair clustering framework that jointly optimizes separation fairness (groups farther from decision boundaries) and social fairness (reduced within-cluster cost disparities). It uses gradient-based optimization to unify multiple fairness notions.

entry.title: DetectZoo: A Unified Toolkit for AI-Generated Content Detection Across Text, Audio, and Image Modalities

author.name: Sajad Ebrahimi, Nima Jamali, Bardia Shirsalimian, Kelly McConvey, Wentao Zhang, Jalehsadat Mahdavimoghaddam, Maksym Taranukhin, Maura Grossman, Vered Shwartz, Yuntian Deng, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: DetectZoo is a unified, extensible toolkit standardizing the empirical pipeline for AI-generated content detection across text, audio, and image modalities to enable fair comparison and reproducibility. It addresses fragmentation among existing detectors that use incompatible codebases and evaluation protocols.

entry.title: CRAFT: Cost-aware Refinement And Front-aware Tuning of Prompts

author.name: Shanu Kumar, Shubhanshu Khandelwal, Akhila Yesantarao Venkata, Parag Agrawal, Yova Kementchedjhieva, Manish Gupta

entry.summary: CRAFT is a Pareto-front prompt optimizer that jointly tunes prompts for accuracy and token cost, treating expensive target-LLM validation calls as a scarce resource allocated to candidates near the optimistic candidate front. It avoids scalarization collapse, where weighting objectives into a single sum recovers only a narrow front region.

entry.title: TIDE: Proactive Multi-Problem Discovery via Template-Guided Iteration

author.name: Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Minki Kang, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: TIDE is a template-guided iterative framework that proactively discovers multiple hidden problems from a user's broader context, rather than acting only on explicit requests, grounding each in evidence and pairing it with concrete actions. It addresses the limitation that single-pass prediction anchors only on the most salient cases.

entry.title: BiasGRPO: Stabilizing Bias Mitigation in High-Variance Reward Landscapes via Group-Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Saket Reddy, Ke Yang, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: BiasGRPO applies Group Relative Policy Optimization to stabilize social bias mitigation in LLMs, where bias lacks a single ground truth and creates a high-variance subjective reward landscape. It normalizes rewards across groups of sampled completions to avoid DPO's lack of exploration and PPO's instability.

entry.title: Rethinking LoRA Memory Through the Lens of KV Cache Compression

author.name: Chunsheng Zuo, Liaoyaqi Wang, William Jurayj, William Fleshman, Benjamin Van Durme

entry.summary: Studies how document-specific LoRA adapters (parametric retrieval) interact with KV cache context in document QA. Finds LoRA contributes little with intact KV cache but recovers 13-21 ROUGE-L points under aggressive cache compression.

entry.title: Beyond Alignment: Value Diversity as a Collective Property in Multicultural Agent Systems

author.name: Shaoyang Xu, Jingshen Zhang, Long P. Hoang, Jinyuan Li, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes value diversity as a system-level evaluation axis for multicultural multi-agent systems, measuring dissimilarity between culturally conditioned agents on the World Values Survey across 19 cultures and 18 models. It argues alignment is insufficient to capture cultural plurality.

entry.title: SkillComposer: Learning to Evolve Agent Skills for Specification and Generalization

author.name: Qi Zhang, Zhaopeng Feng, Xiaonan Shi, Xiaomeng Hu, Chu Liu, Pengjun Xie, Xiaobin Wang, Jieping Ye, Bryan Hooi, Haobo Wang, Junbo Zhao

entry.summary: SkillComposer decomposes agent skill construction into learnable create, improve, and merge operations trained via rejection sampling, addressing the tension between task-specific and overly-abstract skills. It enables skills that both specify and generalize.

entry.title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios

author.name: Giuseppe Attanasio, Beatrice Savoldi, Daniel Chechelnitsky, Matteo Negri, Marine Carpuat, Maarten Sap, Andr\'e F. T. Martins

entry.summary: Ouvia is a user-centered framework measuring perceived usability of speech translation in real one-to-one communication, collecting over 1,750 interactions in healthcare and everyday situations across dialects and genders. It shifts evaluation from decontextualized quality to communication needs.

entry.title: CollabSim: A CSCW-Grounded Methodology for Investigating Collaborative Competence of LLM Agents through Controlled Multi-Agent Experiments

author.name: Jiaju Chen, Bo Sun, Yuxuan Lu, Yun Wang, Dakuo Wang, Bingsheng Yao

entry.summary: CollabSim is a CSCW-grounded methodology for investigating collaborative competence of LLM agents through controlled multi-agent experiments, focusing on common ground, shared understanding, incentive balancing, and misalignment repair. It moves beyond task-outcome-only MAS evaluation.

entry.title: Recovering Physically Plausible Human-Object Interactions from Monocular Videos

author.name: Dingbang Huang, Etienne Vouga, Qixing Huang, Georgios Pavlakos

entry.summary: RePHO reconstructs physically plausible human-object interactions from monocular video by refining noisy kinematic estimates with RL in a physics simulator, using adaptive sampling and a dual self-updating mechanism to stabilize training. It removes interpenetration and floating artifacts.

entry.title: ORACLE-CT: Anatomy-Aware Support Pooling for CT Classification

author.name: Lavsen Dahal, Yubraj Bhandari, Geoffrey Rubin, Joseph Y. Lo

entry.summary: ORACLE-CT introduces anatomy-aware support pooling for abdominal CT disease classification, using multi-organ segmentation to restrict attention pooling to label-relevant anatomical regions. This addresses the mismatch between localized disease evidence and global feature aggregation.

entry.title: Robust Scene Transfer for PointGoal Navigation via Privileged Sensor Guided Contrastive Learning

author.name: Amirhossein Zhalehmehrabi, Tiziano Tezze, Alberto Castelini, Alessandro Farinelli

entry.summary: This paper proposes sensor-guided contrastive learning for PointGoal navigation, using privileged LiDAR during training to guide visual embeddings toward navigation-relevant structure. The frozen encoder then serves as a perceptual backbone for RL, decoupling representation from policy learning.

entry.title: Video-Rate Streaming Stylization on a Vision-Aware MLLM-Conditioned Edit Diffusion: Asymmetric Batched Inference on a Distilled UNet + MLLM Text Encoder

author.name: Yoshiyuki Ootani

entry.summary: This work presents a video-rate streaming stylization pipeline where, after aggressive U-Net distillation, the MLLM text encoder becomes the critical path. It introduces asymmetric CUDA pipelining, text-encoder amortization, and a compile-friendly ControlNet-LLLite reformulation for real-time edit diffusion.

entry.title: Quantifying Uncertainty In Wide Two-Layer Neural Networks: On The Law Of The Limiting Fluctuation Process

author.name: Arnaud Descours (LSAF), Arnaud Guillin (LMBP), Geoffrey Lacour (MaIAGE), Manon Michel (LMBP), Boris Nectoux (LMBP), Paul Stos (UCA, LMBP)

entry.summary: Studies the law of the limiting fluctuation process around the mean-field limit of wide two-layer networks trained by SGD, deriving PDE-based uncertainty quantification cheaper than deep ensembles. Builds on a trajectorial central limit theorem.

entry.title: Preserving Full 6-DOF Actuation Under Abrupt Total Rotor Failures: Passive Fault-Tolerant Flight Control Using a Biaxial-Tilt Hexacopter

author.name: Yipeng Yang, Yiqiao Tang, Hao Zhang, Jinqi Jiang, Jianfeng He, Rumo Chen, Xinghu Yu, Zhan Li, Huijun Gao

entry.summary: Presents passive fault-tolerant flight control for a biaxial-tilt overactuated hexacopter that preserves full 6-DOF actuation under abrupt total rotor failures without explicit fault detection. Extends attainable-wrench-space metrics with transient terms.

entry.title: Sparse Functional Singular Value Decomposition for Biclustering and Triclustering Longitudinal Data

author.name: Yue Zhao, Thierry Chekouo, Sandra Safo

entry.summary: Tri-SfSVD is a unified sparse functional SVD framework for discovering biclusters and triclusters in high-dimensional, sparsely-sampled, irregular longitudinal omics data, integrating continuous trajectory estimation. Applied to subtyping conditions like Inflammatory Bowel Disease.

entry.title: Function-Space Priors for Bayesian Neural ODEs with Application to Vessel Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Jaeyeong Lee, Wonmo Koo, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: Proposes function-space priors for Bayesian Neural ODEs that encode structural properties like smoothness and locality for vessel trajectory prediction from AIS data, improving over uninformative isotropic Gaussian weight priors. Provides calibrated uncertainty for maritime decision-making.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Sharing: Certified Cost Allocation with Participation Guarantees

author.name: Ieva Kazlauskaite

entry.summary: Conformal Risk Sharing formalizes the Certified Allocation Problem and pairs an interpretable sharing policy with split conformal calibration to provide each participant a distribution-free cap on future obligations and bound aggregate harm. Ensures no participant is made materially worse off.

entry.title: Mitigating the Curse of Dimensionality in Uniform Convergence of Deep Neural Networks via Smooth Activations

author.name: Yizhe Ding, Runze Li, Jia Liu, Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: This work establishes a lower bound showing ReLU networks can suffer the curse of dimensionality in uniform (worst-case) convergence even when L2-optimal, then shows smooth activations avoid this problem with new pseudo-dimension and approximation bounds. It matters for tasks requiring worst-case reliability guarantees.

entry.title: Residual Modeling for High-Fidelity Learned Compression of Scientific Data

author.name: Liangji Zhu, Sanjay Ranka, Anand Rangarajan

entry.summary: Proposes a residual-centric learned compression approach for scientific data, modeling the residual separately to handle high-fidelity regimes where existing guaranteed-autoencoder correction streams dominate the bitrate. It matters for efficiently storing massive simulation outputs.

entry.title: Epidemiology of Model Collapse: Modeling Synthetic Data Contamination via Bilayer SIR Dynamics

author.name: Xiangyu Wang

entry.summary: Models synthetic data contamination and model collapse in the AI ecosystem using a bilayer coupled SIR/SIRS epidemiological framework treating data corpora and models as interacting populations. Derives a basic reproduction number and accounts for immunity waning via filtered corpora.

entry.title: InfoShield: Privacy-Preserving Speech Representations for Mental Health Screening via Information-Theoretic Optimization

author.name: Xueyang Wu, Siyuan Liu, Kezhuo Yang, Guang Ling

entry.summary: Presents InfoShield, an information-theoretic method that minimizes mutual information between speech representations and sensitive demographic attributes while preserving depression classification accuracy. Introduces TimeAwareMINE to handle temporal-static misalignment in sequential speech.

entry.title: UNIVID: Unified Vision-Language Model for Video Moderation

author.name: Kejuan Yang, Yizhuo Zhang, Mingyuan Du, Yue Zhang, Dixin Zheng, Kaili Zhao, Yang Xiao, Hanzhong Liang, Kenan Xiao

entry.summary: Presents UNIVID, a unified vision-language model for video moderation that generates policy-aware captions as an interpretable intermediate representation supporting human-verifiable enforcement decisions. Addresses guardrail refusals and lack of fine-grained policy alignment in existing VLMs for moderation.

entry.title: Learning of Robot Safety Policies via Adversarial Synthetic Scenarios

author.name: Nikolai Dorofeev, Alexey Odinokov, Rostislav Yavorskiy

entry.summary: Proposes an agentic gamification framework for learning robot safety policies through synthetic adversarial scenarios, modeling scenario generation as a game between a Red Team constructing hazards and a Blue Team refining safety policies. Aims to efficiently discover high-risk edge cases for physical AI systems.

entry.title: CLEAR: Cognition and Latent Evaluation for Adaptive Routing in End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yining Xing, Zehong Ke, Zhiyuan Liu, Yanbo Jiang, Wenhao Yu, Jianqiang Wang

entry.summary: CLEAR is an end-to-end autonomous driving framework that replaces multi-step diffusion denoising with a single-step latent drift for fast generative planning, combined with a fine-tuned Qwen model for semantic reasoning and adaptive routing. It targets the latency-diversity trade-off in safety-critical driving.

entry.title: Will the Agent Recuse Itself? Measuring LLM-Agent Compliance with In-Band Access-Deny Signals

author.name: Thamilvendhan Munirathinam

entry.summary: Proposes a cooperative governance control called the Recuse Signal—a lightweight in-band deny signal (e.g., SSH banner, PostgreSQL NOTICE) asking autonomous LLM agents to voluntarily withdraw from off-limits resources, analogous to robots.txt. It measures whether agents comply, explicitly noting it is not a security boundary.

entry.title: LiftQuant: Continuous Bit-Width LLM via Dimensional Lifting and Projection

author.name: Liulu He, XuanAng Liu, Juntao Liu, Taolue Feng, Ting Lu, Chunsheng Gan, Zhiyv Peng, Yuan Du, Huanrui Yang, Yijiang Liu, Li Du

entry.summary: Bayes-Sufficient Representations formalizes representation learning relevance for a fixed supervised decision problem, defining a representation as Bayes-sufficient if some head can implement a Bayes-optimal rule, introducing the loss-dependent Bayes quotient and connecting to property elicitation. It clarifies what information a representation must preserve.

entry.title: Testing Neural Networks via Bayesian-Guided Exploration of Decision Landscapes

author.name: Bin Duan, Meiru Che, Guowei Yang

entry.summary: BayesWarp is a neural network testing framework that mutates decision-critical input regions identified via saliency techniques and uses uncertainty-aware Bayesian optimization to discover diverse failures while preserving distributional semantics. It targets efficient fault discovery in safety-critical models.

entry.title: Crafting Your Evolving Dreams: Concept-Incremental Versatile Customization

author.name: Jiahua Dong, Wenqi Liang, Hongliu Li, Yang Cong, Duzhen Zhang, Hanbin Zhao, Henghui Ding, Yulun Zhang, Salman Khan, Fahad Shahbaz Khan

entry.summary: CCDM is a continually customizable diffusion model that lets users incrementally add new personalized concepts over time using attribute-decoupled LoRA modules and relevance-guided aggregation. It mitigates catastrophic forgetting and concept neglect that plague static custom diffusion models.

entry.title: Fast & Faithful Function Vectors

author.name: Minh An Pham, Anton Segeler, Thomas Wiegand, Wojciech Samek, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Patrick Kahardipraja, Reduan Achtibat

entry.summary: This paper studies design choices in function vectors used to steer LLMs during in-context learning, finding that gradient-based attribution via Layer-wise Relevance Propagation improves both efficiency and accuracy in attention-head selection, and that distributed steering outperforms simple aggregation. It systematically explores the underexplored formulation of task representations.

entry.title: EMBER: Efficient Memory via Budgeted Evidence Retention for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yilong Li, Suman Banerjee, Tong Che

entry.summary: EMBER is a learned retention policy for long-horizon agents that decides which source evidence to store before queries are known, under a fixed token budget, using compact source-backed evidence capsules. It addresses budgeted pre-query memory retention.

entry.title: EDIT: Evidence-Diagnosed Intervention Training for Rule-Faithful LLM Grading

author.name: Zhihao Wu, Linhai Zhang, Taiyi Wang, Runcong Zhao, Peter Andrews, Cesare Aloisi, Yulan He

entry.summary: EDIT is a two-phase framework training rubric-faithful LLM graders by locating problematic reasoning steps via internal belief and grounding signals, then revising them. It targets evidence-grounded credit assignment in rubric grading rather than self-contained reasoning.

entry.title: LLM-Conditioned Synthesis of Pathological Gaits via Structured Gait-Language Representations

author.name: Mritula Chandrasekaran, Sanket Kachole, Jarik Francik, Dimitrios Makris

entry.summary: This work presents an LLM-guided framework for synthesizing pathological 3D gait data from structured text descriptions, addressing scarcity due to privacy and recruitment constraints. It introduces a pathology-aware tokenizer preserving pathology-specific motion characteristics during discrete representation learning.

entry.title: Computation-Aware Event-to-Frame Reconstruction via Selective Attention

author.name: Jingqian Wu, Yunbo Jia, Edmund Y. Lam

entry.summary: This work proposes an efficient event-to-frame reconstruction framework with causal temporal modeling using a recurrent encoder-decoder and selective context fusion. A lightweight hybrid attention mechanism enhances feature selectivity for robustness under fast motion and illumination variation.

entry.title: Visuotactile and Explicitly Force-Controlled Robotic Ultrasound for Abdominal Volumetric Reconstruction

author.name: Adrian Piedra, R Brooke Jeffrey, Oussama Khatib

entry.summary: Presents a robotic ultrasound system integrating stereo vision, force control, and expert-informed strategies for autonomous adaptive abdominal volumetric scanning. Records and replays expert radiologist motion and force data.

entry.title: Ensuring Interaction Safety in Multitask Exoskeleton Control: A Simulation-Trained Variable Impedance Framework

author.name: Muyuan Ma, Houcheng Li, Haotian Zhai, Lijun Han, Xinpan Meng, Xiuze Xia, Long Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes a simulation-trained variable impedance control approach with stability guarantees for multitask exoskeleton control, using PPO to generate human-exoskeleton motion data and a dual-modality policy fusing semantic instructions with proprioception. Ensures interaction safety across diverse tasks.

entry.title: TabSODA: Tabular Diffusion based Imputation with Skip Pattern Detection and Ordinal Awareness

author.name: Yuyu Chen, Taehyo Kim, Hai Shu, Yang Feng

entry.summary: TabSODA is an EM-based tabular diffusion imputer that detects structural skips (questionnaire-induced inapplicable cells) and respects ordinal response ordering, built on the Elucidated Diffusion Model framework. Avoids conflating structural skips with item nonresponse.

entry.title: An interpretable and trustworthy AI framework for large-scale longitudinal structure-pain association studies using data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI)

author.name: Jincheng Yu, Haoyang Li, Yiwen Liu, Shen Liu, Rachel Yuanbao Chen, C. Kent Kwoh, Hongxu Ding, Xiaoxiao Sun

entry.summary: Develops an interpretable framework combining deep-learning MRI knee-score prediction with conformal uncertainty and longitudinal statistical modeling to study structure-pain associations in osteoarthritis. It matters for trustworthy large-scale medical imaging research.

entry.title: Individual Gain, Collective Loss: Metacognitive Adaptation in AI-Assisted Creativity

author.name: Anna Mikeda

entry.summary: Proposes selective metacognitive adaptation to explain why AI assistance boosts individual creativity while reducing collective diversity, arguing routine AI use redistributes rather than uniformly diminishes metacognitive effort. It matters for understanding the cognitive mechanisms behind AI's creativity paradox.

entry.title: Entropy-Based Evaluation of AI Agents: A Lightweight Framework for Measuring Behavioral Patterns

author.name: Olasimbo Ayodeji Arigbabu

entry.summary: Proposes Entropy-Based Evaluation of AI Agents, a lightweight framework measuring action, trajectory, tool, and robustness entropy plus information gain to capture behavioral patterns beyond task success and cost. It matters for richer characterization of agent decision processes.

entry.title: Multi-ResNets for Subspace Preconditioning in Constrained Optimization

author.name: Merve Karakas, Christopher J. Williams, Emmanuel O. Balogun, Sadegh Sadeghi Tabas, Christian Brown, Nikhil Rao

entry.summary: Proposes MResOpt, a staged residual network for constrained optimization that decomposes constraint satisfaction by priority with stage-aware losses. Shows infinite-width equivalence to sequential Gaussian Process regression and improves on QP, QCQP, SOCP, and AC optimal power flow.

entry.title: Improving Heart-Focused Medical Question Answering in LLMs via Variance-Aware Rubric Rewards with GRPO

author.name: Arash Ahmadi, Parisa Masnadi, Sarah Sharif, Charles Nicholson, David Ebert, Mike Banad

entry.summary: Investigates GRPO post-training for heart-focused medical question answering using rubric-based rewards, proposing a Variance-Aware Reward Framework extending RaR aggregation strategies. Targets smaller efficient models suitable for privacy-constrained on-device medical use.

entry.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature

author.name: Hamed Nejat, Alexander Maier, Jesse Spencer-Smith, Andr\'e M. Bastos

entry.summary: Describes a local multi-LLM pipeline for ontology-constrained synthesis of the predictive coding neuroscience literature, scoring hypothesis support against an expert-defined 36-concept glossary across three hypotheses. Addresses fragmentation in interdisciplinary scientific literature.

entry.title: Exploring LLMs for South Asian Music Understanding and Generation

author.name: Faria Binte Kader, Mohtasim Hadi Rafi, Shah Wasif Sajjad, Santu Karmaker

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic evaluation of LLM competence in South Asian classical music traditions (Hindustani, Bengali Rabindra/Nazrul Sangeet) governed by raga and tala constraints distinct from Western harmony. Highlights gaps in handling structurally distinct low-resource musical traditions.

entry.title: Beyond Soft Masks: Hard-Perturbation Mixup Explainer for Robust GNN Explainability

author.name: Jialiang Yin, Zheng Zhao, Linsey Pang, Bo Dong, Bin Shi, Jiaxing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a hard-perturbation mixup explainer for GNN explainability that uses hard masks instead of soft masks to fully eliminate label-irrelevant information, addressing out-of-distribution issues from subgraph-based prediction. Aims to improve robustness and trustworthiness of GNN explanations.

entry.title: Compositional Boundaries for Density Fusion

author.name: Ratan Bahadur Thapa, Ali Darijani, J\"urgen Beyerer, Steffen Staab

entry.summary: Studies the algebraic compositionality of binary fusion rules for combining weighted probability densities along aggregation trees, establishing when local fusion can be executed hierarchically while remaining order-invariant. Provides a compositional boundary for distributed uncertainty-management systems.

entry.title: World-Language-Action Model for Unified World Modeling, Language Reasoning, and Action Synthesis

author.name: Yi Yang, Zhihong Liu, Siqi Kou, Yiyang Chen, Yanzhe Hu, Jianbo Zhou, Boyuan Zhao, Zhijie Wei, Xiao Xia, Xueqi Li, Pengfei Liu, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Measures the sensitivity of LLM-based structured extraction from clinical discharge summaries to prompt, model size, and schema choices without human-annotated ground truth, by holding the task fixed and varying one configuration at a time. Quantifies cross-prompt agreement via Cohen's kappa on MIMIC-IV discharge summaries.

entry.title: Learning to Route LLMs from Implicit Cost-Performance Preferences via Meta-Learning

author.name: Jiahao Zeng, Ming Tang, Ningning Ding

entry.summary: MetaRouter introduces a meta-learning, contextual-bandit framework for LLM routing that learns individual users' implicit cost-performance preferences from minimal interaction. It enables personalized routing across heterogeneous user needs.

entry.title: Adapting Diffusion Language Models for Lossless Pixel-Level Image Transmission

author.name: Tianqi Ren, Rongpeng Li, Xianfu Chen, Yingyu Li, Zhifeng Zhao

entry.summary: DDM-SSCC adapts a discrete diffusion language model for lossless pixel-level image transmission, using synchronized reverse arithmetic coding under bidirectional attention to code multiple masked tokens per denoising step over noisy channels. It bridges source and channel coding for exact image recovery.

entry.title: LatentWave: JEPA Pretraining for Wireless Foundation Models

author.name: Ahmed Mohamed, Ahmed Aboulfotouh, Hatem Abou-Zeid

entry.summary: LatentWave is a wireless foundation model pretrained with JEPA on spectrograms and channel-state information, predicting masked regions in latent space rather than reconstructing inputs to avoid biasing toward low-level signal details. It aims for more transferable representations across wireless tasks.

entry.title: Novel Aspects of IEEE SA P3109 Arithmetic Formats for Machine Learning

author.name: Andrew Fitzgibbon, Christoph M. Wintersteiger, Jeffrey Sarnoff

entry.summary: Discusses novel aspects of the IEEE P3109 draft standard for parameterized low-bit floating-point formats for machine learning, covering width/precision parameterization, explicit NaN/infinity handling, rounding/saturation modes, and stochastic rounding. From Microsoft authors, it documents standardization of ML arithmetic formats.

entry.title: When Offline Selectors Cannot Beat the Best Single Model: A Diagnostic Study on edX Dropout Prediction

author.name: Tyler Crosse, Alan Nadelsticher Ruvalcaba, Dustin Khang LeDuc, Thomas Trask, Nicholas Lytle, David Joyner

entry.summary: A diagnostic study examining why per-instance model selectors trained on logged data often fail to beat the single best predictor, using edX dropout prediction. It proposes a three-stage diagnostic to separate mismatched learners, uninformative states, and label shift as causes of failure.

entry.title: Training-Free Lexical-Dense Fusion for Conversational-Memory Retrieval

author.name: Christian Lysenst{\o}en

entry.summary: This single-author paper investigates training-free, CPU-only retrieval for long-term conversational memory, showing that score-level fusion of late-interaction dense retrieval with BM25 substantially boosts Hit@1 on LoCoMo across encoders. It replicates and extends recent turn-isolation retrieval findings.

entry.title: Literature-Guided Minimax Optimization of Virtual Epilepsy Neurostimulation

author.name: Cathy Liu

entry.summary: This single-author paper presents a literature-guided minimax optimization pipeline for virtual epilepsy neurostimulation, coupling PubMed-scale hypothesis extraction, Virtual Brain Epileptor simulations, and LLM-guided black-box optimization. It optimizes worst-case rather than average response across virtual patients.

entry.title: ChessMimic: Per-Rating Transformer Models for Human Move, Clock, and Outcome Prediction in Online Blitz Chess

author.name: Thomas Johnson

entry.summary: ChessMimic trains per-rating-band encoder-only transformers for predicting human moves, thinking time, and game outcomes in online blitz chess, outperforming Maia-2 on move prediction across all Elo bands. The per-skill calibration trades parameter efficiency for sharper human-like behavior modeling.

entry.title: Supportive Token Revealing for Fast Diffusion Language Model Decoding

author.name: Giries Abu Ayoub, Mario Barbara, Llu\'is Pastor-P\'erez, Tanja Bien, Aneesh Barthakur, Alaa Maalouf, Loay Mualem

entry.summary: AXON is a training-free module added on top of parallel decoding for diffusion language models that aims to make the remaining masked sequence easier to decode, not just avoid unsafe commits. It targets the quality-latency trade-off in discrete diffusion text generation.

entry.title: Bayesian learning for the stochastic shortest path problem

author.name: Chon Wai Ho, Sumeetpal S. Singh, Jiaqi Guo

entry.summary: This paper develops a Bayesian framework for the stochastic shortest path problem that directly constructs posterior beliefs over the optimal action-value function via Bellman's optimality equations, without unrealistic modeling assumptions or ad-hoc approximations. For deterministic rewards it characterizes the posterior as a manifold density.

entry.title: LANTERN: Layered Archival and Temporal Episodic Retrieval Network for Long-Context LLM Conversations

author.name: Rahul Subramani

entry.summary: LANTERN is a lightweight memory layer that proactively archives every conversation turn and restores compaction-lost details via hybrid retrieval with zero LLM calls and under 25ms latency. On 94 real multi-turn conversations it recovers 78.3% of verifiable lost facts, outperforming a MemGPT reimplementation.

entry.title: ComplexityMT: Benchmarking the Interaction Between Text Complexity and Machine Translation

author.name: Joseph Marvin Imperial, Junhong Liang, Belal Shoer, Abdullah Barayan, Rodrigo Wilkens, Omar Mussa, Dawn Knight, Eug\'enio Ribeiro, Ekaterina Kochmar, Sowmya Vajjala, Fernando Alva-Manchego, Harish Tayyar Madabushi

entry.summary: ComplexityMT is a benchmark across six languages assessing how text complexity (measured by CEFR levels) interacts with machine translation, evaluating whether translations preserve source complexity. Experiments show higher CEFR levels make texts harder to translate and that MT shifts complexity levels.

entry.title: AdaPLD: Adaptive Retrieval and Reuse for Efficient Model-Free Speculative Decoding

author.name: Runheng Liu, Jincheng Xie, Wen Hu, Xingchen Xiao, Heyan Huang

entry.summary: AdaPLD is a training-free model-free speculative decoding method that adaptively improves retrieval recall and draft construction beyond brittle deterministic span copying. It accelerates generation without auxiliary draft models.

entry.title: NAVIRA: Decoupled Stochastic Remasking for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Andrey Fomenko, Maksim Kryzhanovskiy, Svetlana Glazyrina, Roman Ischenko

entry.summary: NAVIRA is an inference-time decoding policy for masked diffusion language models that decouples token-quality scoring from logit computation and stochastically samples remasking positions, addressing PRISM's coupled-regeneration limitation. It improves correction of parallel-decoding errors.

entry.title: From Self to Other: Evaluating Demographic Perspective-Taking in LLM Hate Speech Annotation

author.name: Paloma Piot, Javier Parapar

entry.summary: Evaluates whether persona-conditioned LLMs reproduce human demographic disagreement patterns in hate speech annotation, testing inter-group disagreement, in-group sensitivity, and accuracy. It questions using personas to simulate diverse perspectives at scale.

entry.title: FOXGLOVE: Understanding Goal-Oriented and Anchored Writing Feedback from Experts and LLMs on Argumentative Essays

author.name: Yijun Liu, Yifan Song, John Gallagher, Sarah Sterman, Tal August

entry.summary: FOXGLOVE is a dataset of 696 expert-written feedback comments on 69 twelfth-grade argumentative essays paired with 1,644 LLM comments, with expert quality ratings, comparing goal-orientation, anchoring, and prioritization. It systematically contrasts expert and LLM writing feedback.

entry.title: ColBERTSaR: Sparsified ColBERT Index via Product Quantization

author.name: Eugene Yang, Andrew Yates, Dawn Lawrie, James Mayfield, Saron Samuel, Rohan Jha

entry.summary: ColBERTSaR sparsifies the ColBERT index via product quantization to reduce the heavy storage and the gather/decompress inefficiencies that limit ColBERT scalability. It targets disk footprint and query-time bottlenecks in neural retrieval.

entry.title: MemoryCard: Topic-Aware Multi-Modal Clue Compression for Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Qing Yang, Pengcheng Huang, Xinze Li, Zhenghao Liu, Yukun Yan, Yu Gu, Ge Yu, Gang Li, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: MemoryCard organizes long videos into self-contained, topic-aware multimodal Memory Cards to capture coherent event-level semantics for long-video QA, overcoming the limits of isolated-frame approaches. It compresses dispersed clues into event-level evidence units.

entry.title: Compress-Distill: Reasoning Trace Compression for Efficient Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Maxime Griot, Paul Steven Scotti, Tanishq Mathew Abraham

entry.summary: Studies post-hoc compression of long chain-of-thought traces before knowledge distillation, generating ~283k traces from two teachers and compressing to 8.6-21% of length, achieving 2-7.6x faster training and 3-19x shorter inference but with lower downstream accuracy than raw traces. A length-accuracy tradeoff study.

entry.title: Can We Predict The Human Preference For Text-to-Image Content Prior To Generation And Is It Even Useful To Do So?

author.name: Joong Ho Kim, Keith G. Mills

entry.summary: This work investigates whether human preference for text-to-image content can be predicted before generation, given that random noise seeds strongly affect output quality especially in small local models. It examines the practical utility of pre-generation preference prediction.

entry.title: Dual Feature Decoupling for Fine-Grained OOD Detection

author.name: Xiaokun Li, Yaping Huang, Qingji Guan

entry.summary: DFDNet addresses fine-grained out-of-distribution detection through feature disentanglement, targeting subtle inter-class variations in tasks like medical and vehicle recognition that most OOD methods overlook. It separates discriminative from background-interfering features.

entry.title: ReSAGE-PAR: Representational Similarity Assessment for Generative Expansion in Pedestrian Attribute Recognition

author.name: Pablo Ayuso-Albizu, Pablo Carballeira, Juan C. SanMiguel, Paula Moral

entry.summary: ReSAGE-PAR is a generate-score-autolabel pipeline using diffusion models to expand pedestrian attribute recognition datasets, bridging the domain gap to low-resolution surveillance crops. It uses representational similarity assessment for reliable attribute verification to prevent generative hallucinations.

entry.title: Synthetic Data Generation and Vision-based Wrinkle and Keypoint Detection for Bimanual Cloth Manipulation

author.name: Ariel Herrera, Xueyang Kang, Atal Anil Kumar

entry.summary: This work develops a Blender-based synthetic pipeline with auto-annotated keypoints combined with real data to train wrinkle and keypoint detectors for bimanual cloth manipulation. A proposed algorithm uses detected wrinkles to stretch folded garments, transitioning to keypoint-based ironing as corners emerge.

entry.title: GS-NFS: Bandwidth-adaptive Streaming of Dynamic Gaussian Splats and Point Clouds

author.name: Rajrup Ghosh, Haodong Wang, Haoran Hong, Eduardo Pavez, Amartya Chaudhuri, Weiwu Pang, Harsha V. Madhyastha, Antonio Ortega, Ramesh Govindan

entry.summary: GS-NFS accelerates compression and decompression of dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting for 3D video streaming on GPUs with bandwidth adaptation. It addresses the large data footprint of dynamic 3DGS frames for real-time streaming.

entry.title: From Prediction to Self: Developmental Conditions for Agency in Minimal Neural Systems

author.name: Evan Ye

entry.summary: Traces the emergence of agency in a minimal 192-dimensional GRU through 40 controlled experiments, identifying four ordered developmental conditions for distinguishing self-caused from world-caused change. Proposes a developmental sequence for self-modeling.

entry.title: Towards a Data Flywheel for Embodied Intelligence in Logistics

author.name: Anlan Yu, Zaishu Chen, Zhiqing Hong, Daqing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a logistics data flywheel for industrial embodied intelligence that converts daily operations into reusable data assets and uses world models to generate supervision for long-tail parcel manipulation. WM-DAgger feeds deployment feedback into policy improvement.

entry.title: Merging model-based control with multi-agent reinforcement learning for multi-agent cooperative teaming strategies

author.name: Christian Llanes, Spencer W. Jensen, Samuel Coogan

entry.summary: Combines multi-agent reinforcement learning with model-predictive control (MA-AC-MPC) to achieve safe, dynamically feasible cooperative multi-agent actions. Leverages MARL for long-horizon cooperation and MPC for short-horizon safety.

entry.title: HyFAD: Hybrid Time-Frequency Diffusion with Frequency-Aware Embedding for Time Series Imputation

author.name: Hongfan Gao, Wangmeng Shen, Bin Yang, Jilin Hu

entry.summary: HyFAD is a hybrid time-frequency diffusion model with frequency-aware embedding for time series imputation, performing reverse denoising sequentially from time to frequency domain for coarse-to-fine generation. Addresses high-frequency reconstruction and global-local balance.

entry.title: EML-CD: Causal Mechanism Recovery via EML Symbolic Trees in Structure Learning

author.name: Sota Asanuma

entry.summary: EML-CD integrates the EML operator into causal structure learning to recover interpretable closed-form causal mechanisms as gated binary trees rather than black-box neural weights. Enables analytical Jacobians and tested on Sachs protein signaling data.

entry.title: Adaptive state-action abstractions via rate-distortion

author.name: Fernando E. Rosas

entry.summary: This paper proposes a rate-distortion principle for dynamically adjusting the granularity of state-action abstractions in reinforcement learning: refine when learning error becomes comparable to abstraction error. It formalizes this with a performance certificate decomposing value error into learning and abstraction terms.

entry.title: Towards passive heart health monitoring via smartphone camera

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google Research describes work toward passive heart health monitoring using only a smartphone camera, leveraging optical signals to estimate cardiovascular metrics. It points to scalable, accessible consumer health screening without dedicated hardware.

entry.title: When Should We Protect AI? A Precautionary Framework for Consciousness Uncertainty

author.name: Anna Mikeda

entry.summary: Proposes a precautionary framework mapping evidence of AI consciousness across five welfare dimensions to graduated protective obligations, combining binary triggers with continuous scaling. It matters for operationalizing AI welfare decisions under deep uncertainty.

entry.title: Predict and Reconstruct: Joint Objectives for Self-Supervised Language Representation Learning

author.name: Aimen Boukhari

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid pretraining objective combining JEPA-style latent-space prediction with standard masked language modeling over a shared encoder, balanced by a learnable scalar. Aims to learn deeper semantic representations than surface-form MLM, evaluated against a pure-MLM baseline.

entry.title: NIV: Neural Axis Variations for Variable Font Generation

author.name: Nadav Benedek, Ariel Shamir, Ohad Fried

entry.summary: Introduces NIV (Neural Axis Variations), a method to automatically convert static fonts into functional variable fonts by predicting per-point glyph displacements along design axes. Uses a Property Embedding mechanism to capture multi-axis interactions operating directly on vector geometry.

entry.title: When Surface Form Changes Moderation Decisions: A Paired Study of Code-Mixed Workflow Instability

author.name: Suraj Babu Thimma Krishnaram

entry.summary: Studies how content moderation workflow decisions (ALLOW/FLAG/REVIEW) become unstable under code-mixed (Tamil-English) inputs compared to clean English, finding a 26.5% decision flip rate and increased review burden and false-flagging. Highlights deployment fragility beyond clean-input classification accuracy.

entry.title: GenTI: Benchmarking LLMs for Autonomous IDPS Rule Generation for Unseen Attacks

author.name: Hassan Jalil Hadi, Rehana Yasmin, Ali Shoker

entry.summary: Proposes GenTI, an LLM-driven benchmark and dataset (GTI, aggregating 150k+ rules from Snort, Suricata, etc.) for autonomous generation of IDPS rules targeting unseen and zero-day attacks. Addresses the limited adaptability of manually crafted signature-driven detection rules.

entry.title: Bridging the Semantic-Collaborative Gap: An Asymmetric Graph Architecture for Cold-Start Item Recommendation

author.name: Anh Truong, John Trenkle, Yuanbo Chen, Honghong Zhao, Abdullah Alchihabi, Effy Fang, Michael Tamir

entry.summary: Shallow-RHS is an asymmetric graph link-prediction architecture for cold-start item recommendation, formulated as inductive graph completion on a temporal bipartite device-content graph, deployed in Tubi's production retrieval system. It assigns standalone embeddings to new content with no interaction history.

entry.title: Bridging Domain Expertise and Generalization for Performance Estimation

author.name: Shuxuan Li, Zhilin Zhao, Quyu Kong, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: FRAP estimates model performance under distribution shift without labels by fusing predictions from an external foundation model and the base model to build a more reliable surrogate of ground-truth labels. It improves performance estimation correlation when base-model biases are amplified by shift.

entry.title: Hyper-ICL: Attention Calibration with Hyperbolic Anchor Distillation for Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Niloufar Alipour Talemi, Hossein Kashiani, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: Hyper-ICL is a training-based framework that reconstructs the effect of in-context demonstrations for multimodal LLMs without requiring the demonstrations at inference time, using a low-rank logit-level adapter and hyperbolic anchor distillation. It reduces the latency and instability of multimodal in-context learning.

entry.title: OA-CutMix: Correcting the Label Bias of CutMix

author.name: Tobias Christian Nauen, Stanislav Frolov, Federico Raue, Brian B. Moser, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: OA-CutMix corrects a label-bias flaw in CutMix, where area-based label assignment misattributes credit to background patches with no visible object; it uses precomputed segmentation masks to assign labels in proportion to visible object area. The authors quantify the bias at 21.5% mean discrepancy and zero visible-object pixels in 17% of samples.

entry.title: ProSPy: A Profiling-Driven SQL-Python Agentic Framework for Enterprise Text-to-SQL

author.name: Zhaorui Yang, Huawei Zheng, Sen Yang, Yuhui Zhang, Haoxuan Li, Zhizhen Yu, Xuan Yi, Chen Hou, Defeng Xie, Chao Hu, Minfeng Zhu, Dazhen Deng, Haozhe Feng, Danqing Huang, Yingcai Wu, Peng Chen, Wei Chen

entry.summary: ProSPy is a profiling-driven SQL-Python agentic framework for enterprise-scale text-to-SQL handling large schemas, incomplete metadata, and dialect-specific syntax via a four-stage reasoning process. It addresses real enterprise database complexity.

entry.title: ACE-SQL: Adaptive Co-Optimization via Empirical Credit Assignment for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Xiaobing Chen, Ai Jian, Eryu Guo, Zhiqi Pang

entry.summary: ACE-SQL is an RL framework that jointly optimizes schema retrieval and SQL generation under execution feedback, using an online column-set pool for empirical credit assignment rather than static gold supervision. It addresses suboptimal schema-linking targets.

entry.title: Revising Context, Shifting Simulated Stance: Auditing LLM-Based Stance Simulation in Online Discussions

author.name: Xinnong Zhang, Wanting Shan, Hanjia Lyu, Zhongyu Wei, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: Audits LLM-based stance simulation by applying controlled counterfactual context revisions and re-inferring a user's stance, testing whether simulations reflect stable user beliefs or are over-sensitive to semantically irrelevant context changes. Includes a multimodal revision strategy.

entry.title: An Embarrassingly Simple Detector for Model Extraction Attacks in Large Language Model API Traffic

author.name: Shuze Liu, Qianwen Guo, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: Formulates LLM model-extraction monitoring as benign-calibrated traffic-window distribution testing and shows a simple maximum mean discrepancy detector over query embeddings effectively detects extraction attacks using only benign-vs-benign comparisons. A lightweight defense for hosted APIs.

entry.title: GLASS: GRPO-Trained LoRA for Acoustic Style Steering in Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech

author.name: Jaehoon Kang, Yejin Lee, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: GLASS uses GRPO-trained LoRA adapters to learn composable acoustic style controls (speaking rate, pitch) in zero-shot TTS from post-generation rewards rather than style labels, with WER as an intelligibility anchor. It disentangles style from speaker identity in prompts.

entry.title: Inverse Manipulation through Symbolic Planning and Residual Operator Learning

author.name: Yigit Yildirim, Giuseppe Rauso, Riccardo Caccavale, Alberto Finzi

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid framework for inverse manipulation that derives inverse-skill objectives from STRIPS-like operators extracted from demonstrations, combining symbolic planning with residual operator learning. Restores forward-execution effects under continuous dynamics.

entry.title: Causal Atlases from Entropic Inference: Bayesian Networks beyond Optimal DAGs

author.name: Hazhir Aliahmadi, Irina Babayan, Greg van Anders

entry.summary: This paper uses entropy-based inference to generate atlases of plausible Bayesian network structures rather than committing to a single optimal DAG, capturing the inherent variability and multiple causal chains in data. It offers a more data-faithful representation of causal uncertainty.

entry.title: Insurance of Agentic AI

author.name: Quanyan Zhu

entry.summary: Examines the emerging insurance market for agentic AI and develops a framework for underwriting, pricing, reinsurance, and product design given novel exposures not fitting traditional liability categories. It matters for the economic and risk-management infrastructure around autonomous AI deployment.

entry.title: Framing, Judging, Steering: An Assessable Competency Model for Teach-ing Students to Reason With Generative AI

author.name: Alexander Apartsin, Yehudit Aperstein

entry.summary: Proposes CoRe-3 (FJS), a competency model decomposing productive generative-AI use into three assessable skills: Framing, Judging, and Steering, to diagnose why AI use succeeds or fails beyond a single prompting score. It matters for education assessment in an AI-augmented world.

entry.title: TokenMizer: Graph-Structured Session Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Context Management

author.name: Shweta Mishra

entry.summary: Presents TokenMizer, an open-source proxy that models LLM session history as a typed knowledge graph (14 node types, 7 edge types) for long-horizon context management. Preserves relational structure across sessions instead of treating history as flat text.

entry.title: From Scoring to Explanations: Evaluating SHAP and LLM Rationales for Rubric-based Teaching Quality Assessment

author.name: Ivo Bueno, Babette B\"uhler, Philipp Stark, Tim F\"utterer, Ulrich Trautwein, Dorottya Demszky, Heather Hill, Enkelejda Kasneci

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for sentence-level interpretability of rubric-based teaching quality scoring, combining SHAP attributions with LLM-generated rationales on classroom transcripts. Compares fine-tuned PLMs and prompted LLMs on scoring performance and explanation faithfulness using the NCTE corpus.

entry.title: Finite Element-Based Material Learning via Automatic Differentiation: Learning constitutive neural network models from full-field deformation data

author.name: Matthias Knipper, Chenyi Ji, Malte Brand, Kevin Linka

entry.summary: Presents FE-MAD, an end-to-end differentiable framework using finite elements and automatic differentiation to learn constitutive neural network material models from heterogeneous full-field deformation data. Balances generality, robustness, and efficiency versus FE model updating and neural operators.

entry.title: Executable Schema Contracts: From Automatic Ingestion to Multi-Source Retrieval

author.name: Padmaja Jonnalagedda, Yuguang Yao, Xiang Gao, Hilaf Hasson, Kamalika Das

entry.summary: Presents a system that automatically discovers executable schemas from raw multi-source data to drive knowledge graph construction and query-time retrieval with provenance awareness. Targets the challenge of integrating evidence across inconsistent schemas without costly manual engineering.

entry.title: Metamorphic Testing with the Rashomon Set: Explanation Faithfulness in Machine Learning

author.name: Helge Spieker, J{\o}rn Eirik Betten, Arnaud Gotlieb

entry.summary: Introduces a metamorphic-testing framework that assesses faithfulness of post-hoc explanations (SHAP, LIME) without ground-truth labels, using the Rashomon effect and five metamorphic relations. It offers a way to evaluate trustworthiness of feature attributions.

entry.title: PAMF: Prior-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Incomplete Time Series Data

author.name: Ziwen Kan, Wugeng Zheng, Tianlong Chen, Song Wang

entry.summary: PAMF is a prior-aware multimodal fusion method for incomplete time-series data in healthcare, explicitly estimating missing values across both within-modality and modality-level missingness patterns rather than relying on masks alone. It targets robustness when ECG segments or respiratory channels are lost.

entry.title: Variance Reduction for Heavy-Tailed Monetization Metrics in Ranking Experiments via Post-Stratification

author.name: Neeti Pokharna, Olivier Jeunen, Yatharth Saraf, Aleksei Ustimenko

entry.summary: Presents a practical variance-reduction framework for online ranking experiments with heavy-tailed monetization metrics, combining post-stratification with CUPED to leverage pre-experiment covariates and improve A/B sensitivity without extra traffic. Deployed at ShareChat, it substantially reduces variance in revenue experiments.

entry.title: Shortcomings and capacities of real-constrained neural networks in complex spaces

author.name: Andrew Gracyk

entry.summary: This single-author theoretical paper computes the asymptotic ratio between storage capacities of complex-valued neural networks when enforcing real versus complex pre-activations, using Gardner volume comparisons and the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber integral formula. It applies statistical mechanics tools nonstandard in ML literature.

entry.title: Worker Utility as Hysteresis: A Preisach Model of Transaction Acceptance in Gig Labour Markets

author.name: Piotr Frydrych

entry.summary: Models gig worker latent utility using a Preisach hysteresis framework, estimating acceptance and rejection utility surfaces via a dual-output neural network combined with XGBoost classification. It frames binary accept/reject transactions as emergent hysteresis from heterogeneous worker thresholds.

entry.title: VAMPS: Visual-Assisted Mathematical Problem Solving Benchmark

author.name: Amirhossein Dabiriaghdam, Shayan Vassef, Mohammadreza Bakhtiari, Yasamin Medghalchi, Ilker Hacihaliloglu, Mesrob Ohannessian, Lele Wang, Giuseppe Carenini

entry.summary: VAMPS is a bilingual benchmark of 1,168 multimodal multiple-choice math problems testing whether multimodal LLMs can externalize problems via visualization tools and reason over the tool output. It probes a gap where model performance degrades when relying on visual aids in tool-augmented reasoning.

entry.title: Global Sketch-Based Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Daniel Zhao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a global, sketch-based watermarking scheme for masked diffusion language models that controls a vector-valued sketch of the entire sequence rather than perturbing local token contexts. It enables detection decoupled from local contexts, yielding a more robust statistical signal.

entry.title: Distributional Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search for Uncertainty-Aware Retrieval

author.name: Olivier Jeunen

entry.summary: This paper proposes distributional approximate nearest neighbor search that models uncertainty in user/item embeddings rather than using single point estimates, to counter retrieval bias toward popular head items at the expense of long-tail niche content. It targets uncertainty-aware retrieval in recommender systems.

entry.title: AIP: A Graph Representation for Learning and Governing Agent Skills

author.name: Zachary Blumenfeld, Jim Webber

entry.summary: The Agent Instruction Protocol (AIP) models agent skills as directed execution graphs with discrete steps as nodes (backed by scripts or natural-language descriptions) connected by typed input/output edges and governed by a YAML schema. It aims to improve reliability and governability over free-form prose skill definitions.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Semantic Layer from Execution for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Youngwon Lee, Jaejin Kim, Seung-won Hwang

entry.summary: GATE bootstraps missing value groundings in text-to-SQL from execution feedback, keeping multiple grounding hypotheses open and confirming the one supported by observed query results. It addresses under-specification in expert domains.

entry.title: Towards Truly Multilingual ASR: Generalizing Code-Switching ASR to Unseen Language Pairs

author.name: Gio Paik, Hyunseo Shin, Soungmin Lee

entry.summary: Investigates whether code-switching ASR capabilities learned from limited seen language pairs can generalize to unseen pairs, addressing the combinatorial scalability problem. Aims toward truly multilingual code-switching ASR.

entry.title: Contextualized Prompting For Stance Detection On Social Media

author.name: Tilman Beck, Shakib Yazdani, Simon Kruschinski, Marcus Maurer, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Systematically investigates incorporating real-world, derived, and LLM-generated context into zero-shot prompting for social media stance detection across four datasets including a new German Twitter set. Gurevych group; finds context helps but with caveats.

entry.title: Human Adults and LLMs as Scientists: Who Benefits from Active Exploration?

author.name: Mandana Samiei, Eunice Yiu, Anthony GX-Chen, Dongyan Lin, Jocelyn Shen, Blake A. Richards, Alison Gopnik, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Compares human adults and LLMs as scientists in a blicket-detector causal learning task, asking whether active exploration helps overcome the conjunctive causal handicap. Active exploration substantially improves adults' conjunctive rule learning.

entry.title: MIRAI: Prediction and Generation of High-Impact Academic Research

author.name: Alex Li, Joseph Jacobson

entry.summary: MIRAI predicts paper impact (5-year PageRank and citations) from title, abstract, and date trained on the arXiv graph, then builds a research-ideation pipeline biased toward high impact. Ideas were judged more impactful than a non-MIRAI baseline.

entry.title: Scaffold, Not Vocabulary? A Controlled, Two-Tier, Pre-Registered Study of a Popperian Code-Generation Skill

author.name: Mehmet Iscan

entry.summary: A pre-registered two-tier ablation testing whether a Popperian falsificationist prompt skill improves code generation due to its content or merely the scaffold structure, controlling for placebo, labels-only, and judge biases. It scrutinizes LLM-as-judge-reported skill gains.

entry.title: Disentangled Fine-Grained Prototype Learning for Incomplete Image-Tabular Classification

author.name: Feixiang Zhou, Jianyang Xie, Zhuangzhi Gao, Qinkai Yu, Fu Wang, Yuheng Fan, Jing Li, Zheheng Jiang, Yitian Zhao, Yanda Meng, He Zhao, Gregory Y. H. Lip, Yalin Zheng

entry.summary: This work tackles missing-modality image-tabular classification via disentangled fine-grained prototype learning, addressing semantic and distributional misalignment that coarse global features miss. It targets applications like medical diagnosis and recommendation under incomplete modalities.

entry.title: ShotCrop$^3$: Cropping Human-Centric Images into Cinematic Triple-Shot Compositions

author.name: Dehong Kong, Lina Lei, Lingtao Zheng, Chenyang Wu, Ailing Zhang, Xinran Qin, Teng Ma, Jiaqi Xu, Zhixin Wang, Zhikai Chen, Xuecheng Qi, Renjing Pei, Fan Li

entry.summary: ShotCrop introduces Triple-Shot Compositions, generating establishing, medium, and close-up cinematic crops from a single human-centric image, each with shot descriptions for visual narration. It targets multi-shot creative workflows like commercial posters with limited expert annotations.

entry.title: Two-Way Is Better Than One: Bidirectional Alignment with Cycle Consistency for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Hongye Xu, Bartosz Krawczyk

entry.summary: BiCyc proposes bidirectional projection with cycle consistency for exemplar-free class-incremental learning, fixing systematic bias in one-directional drift compensation of prototypes. Aims to reduce representation drift accumulation across tasks.

entry.title: Dynamic Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery in Robotic Cellular Warehousing Systems

author.name: Cheng Ren, Ming Li, Xinping Guan, George Q. Huang

entry.summary: Formulates dynamic multi-agent pickup and delivery with internal order evolution for robotic warehouses and proposes event-triggered online replanning algorithms based on token passing. Handles SKUs appended to orders during execution.

entry.title: 3D Underwater Path Planning via Generative Flow Field Surrogates

author.name: Zachary Cooper-Baldock, Paulo E. Santos, Russell S. A. Brinkworth, Karl Sammut

entry.summary: Uses conditional GAN surrogates (PatchGAN and 2D3DGAN with self-attention) as drop-in replacements for expensive RANS CFD within a 3D energy-weighted A* path planner for AUV launch-and-recovery through propeller wakes. Avoids onboard CFD cost.
