  • RL Excursions re-examines the pretrain-SFT-RL pipeline, applying RL directly to intermediate pre-training checkpoints with surprising results.
  • UltraEP provides real-time exact load balancing for rack-scale MoE training and prefill, addressing a key production bottleneck.
  • Why Muon Outperforms Adam explains the optimizer's edge through a curvature perspective via second-order Taylor analysis.

Safety & Alignment

  • (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning (incl. Fabien Roger) finds emergent misalignment and residual harmful behavior in intent-following models.
  • Exact Unlearning in RL proves rho-TV-stable tabular MDP algorithms supporting provable exact data removal.

Foundation Models & Robotics

  • GRACE is a gastric-cancer pathology foundation model (48K WSIs, 37K+ patients) with rigorous clinical validation.
  • GRAIL (NVIDIA) generates humanoid loco-manipulation data by composing 3D assets and video foundation model priors.
  • Token Rankings are Unforgeable Language Model Signatures establishes rank-based model fingerprinting, extending logit-leakage results.

entry.title: What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation?

author.name: Tianchong Jiang, Xiangshan Tan, Samuel Wheeler, Luzhe Sun, Tewodros W. Ayalew, Matthew Walter

entry.summary: This paper critically examines robot manipulation benchmarks, identifying four failure modes (shortcut solvability, lack of statistical significance, creeping overfitting, data-source dependence) and proposing diagnostics for each. Auditing LIBERO, CALVIN, SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin 2.0 reveals that popular benchmarks fail multiple diagnostics and a tiny probe can reach near-SOTA.

entry.title: Token Rankings are Unforgeable Language Model Signatures

author.name: Matthew Finlayson, Andreas Grivas, Xiang Ren, Swabha Swayamdipta

entry.summary: Shows that token rankings (the ordering of tokens by probability, without values) constitute a unique unforgeable model signature, since each model has a unique set of feasible top-k rankings and finding a matching model is NP-hard. It demonstrates the first polynomially unforgeable LM signature with security implications for APIs exposing rankings.

entry.title: CyberGym-E2E: Scalable Real-World Benchmark for AI Agents' End-to-End Cybersecurity Capabilities

author.name: Tianneng Shi, Robin Rheem, Dongwei Jiang, Mona Wang, Francisco De La Riega, Zhun Wang, Jingzhi Jiang, Alexander Cheung, Sean Tai, Jonah Cha, Jianhong Tu, Gabriel Han, Chenguang Wang, Jingxuan He, Wenbo Guo, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Proposes CyberGym-E2E, a large-scale realistic benchmark evaluating AI agents across the full vulnerability lifecycle including discovery, proof-of-concept generation, and patch generation, built via an automated agent-enhanced pipeline transforming open-source vulnerability data. It addresses the limited scale and scope of existing cybersecurity AI evaluations.

entry.title: RL Excursions during Pre-Training: Re-examining Policy Optimization for LLM training

author.name: Rachit Bansal, Clara Mohri, Tian Qin, David Alvarez-Melis, Sham Kakade

entry.summary: This work re-examines policy optimization by applying RL, SFT, and SFT-then-RL directly to intermediate pre-training checkpoints when training an LLM from scratch. It finds RL is effective very early and often matches the full pipeline, that pre-training data composition matters more than scale for RL effectiveness, and that RL on base checkpoints expands the distribution while sharpening arises only after SFT.

entry.title: UltraEP: Unleash MoE Training and Inference on Rack-Scale Nodes with Near-Optimal Load Balancing

author.name: Xinming Wei, Chao Jin, Tuo Dai, Yinmin Zhong, Shan Yu, Chengxu Yang, Bingyang Wu, Zili Zhang, Jing Mai, Qianchao Zhu, Zhouyang Li, Yuliang Liu, Guojie Luo

entry.summary: UltraEP is a real-time, exact-load balancer for large expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts training and prefill serving on rack-scale nodes, rebalancing every microbatch and layer to combat compute stragglers and all-to-all bottlenecks. It matters because expert load imbalance is a primary efficiency drain when serving frontier MoE models at scale.

entry.title: A Pathology Foundation Model for Gastric Cancer with Real-World Validation

author.name: Ling Liang, Jiabo Ma, Zhengyu Zhang, Fengtao Zhou, Yingxue Xu, Yihui Wang, Cheng Jin, Zhengrui Guo, On Ki Tang, Zhijian Cen, Zhen Wang, Qi Xie, Chengyu Lu, Chenglong Zhao, Feifei Wang, Yu Cai, Hongyi Wang, Jing Zhang, Yaping Ye, Shijun Sun, Shenglei Li, Yu Wang, Zhenhui Li, Ronald Cheong Kin Chan, Xiuming Zhang, Zhe Wang, Hao Chen, Li Liang

entry.summary: GRACE is a gastric-cancer-specific pathology foundation model trained on roughly 48,000 whole-slide images from 37,000+ patients, outperforming general pancancer models across 28 clinical tasks. Its real-world prospective validation and reader studies make it notable for clinical translation.

entry.title: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from 3D Assets and Video Priors

author.name: Tianyi Xie, Haotian Zhang, Jinhyung Park, Zi Wang, Bowen Wen, Jiefeng Li, Xueting Li, Qingwei Ben, Haoyang Weng, Yufei Ye, David Minor, Tingwu Wang, Chenfanfu Jiang, Sanja Fidler, Jan Kautz, Linxi Fan, Yuke Zhu, Zhengyi Luo, Umar Iqbal, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: GRAIL is a digital generation pipeline for humanoid loco-manipulation that composes 3D assets, simulator-ready scenes, and video foundation model priors to synthesize robot-compatible demonstrations entirely virtually until deployment. It avoids the scaling bottlenecks of teleoperation and motion capture by starting from fully specified 3D configurations.

entry.title: CLAW: Learning Continuous Latent Action World Models via Adversarial Latent Regularization

author.name: Tewodros Ayalew, Matthew Jeung, Samuel Wheeler, Xiao Zhang, Andre de la Cruz Arce, Kaylene Stocking, Michael Maire, Matthew R. Walter

entry.summary: CLAW is an end-to-end self-supervised framework that jointly learns a world model and continuous latent action representations directly from action-free videos using adversarial latent regularization and diffusion-based generation. It supports imitation from observation and goal-directed control without any action labels.

entry.title: Exact Unlearning in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Thanh Nguyen-Tang, Raman Arora

entry.summary: Formulates exact unlearning in reinforcement learning, proving the existence of a rho-TV-stable RL algorithm for tabular MDPs that supports exact data deletion at only a fraction of the cost of retraining from scratch. It provides theoretical guarantees that post-unlearning output is indistinguishable from never having seen deleted data.

entry.title: Why Muon Outperforms Adam: A Curvature Perspective

author.name: Shuche Wang, Fengzhuo Zhang, Jiaxiang Li, Dirk Bergemann, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: This work explains why the Muon optimizer outperforms Adam in LLM training through a curvature lens, showing via second-order Taylor analysis that Muon incurs a smaller curvature penalty at matched loss. It decomposes the penalty into update norm and normalized directional sharpness.

entry.title: (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning

author.name: Mohammad Omar Khursheed, Baram Sosis, Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Studies the alignment properties of helpful-only models trained to always follow user intent, finding many suffer from emergent misalignment, residual refusals, poor steerability, sycophancy, and incoherent character. It shows naive anti-refusal training causes these problems but they are avoidable.

entry.title: Dream.exe: Can Video Generation Models Dream Executable Robot Manipulation?

author.name: Rui Zhao, Kaiming Yang, Jifeng Zhu, Siyang Chen, Ziqi Wang, Weijia Wu, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Heng Wang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Dream.exe introduces an evaluation framework testing whether video generation models have internalized physical laws by converting generated manipulation videos into executable robot actions. It provides a measurable bridge between video synthesis and real-world physical plausibility.

entry.title: Echo-Infinity: Learning Evolving Memory for Real-Time Infinite Video Generation

author.name: Yuxuan Bian, Zeyue Xue, Songchun Zhang, Shiyi Zhang, Weiyang Jin, Yaowei Li, Junhao Zhuang, Haoran Li, Jie Huang, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: Echo-Infinity is an autoregressive framework for real-time infinite video generation that uses a learnable evolving memory to filter, abstract, and compress arbitrarily long history at constant cost. It replaces handcrafted KV-cache schedules with attention-and-gating-based memory consolidation to reduce compounding errors.

entry.title: Inference-Time Vulnerability Beyond Shallow Safety: Alignment Along Generation Trajectories

author.name: Kyungmin Park, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: Shows that shallow safety is a special case of broader inference-time vulnerability where short token injections at any generation step can alter safety behavior, and that hidden-state alignment does not predict robustness. It proposes aligning models directly on generation trajectories.

entry.title: AutoLab: Can Frontier Models Solve Long-Horizon Auto Research and Engineering Tasks?

author.name: Zhangchen Xu, Junda Chen, Yue Huang, Dongfu Jiang, Jiefeng Chen, Hang Hua, Zijian Wu, Zheyuan Liu, Zexue He, Lichi Li, Shizhe Diao, Jiaxin Pei, Jinsung Yoon, Hao Zhang, Mengdi Wang, Radha Poovendran, Misha Sra, Alex Pentland, Zichen Chen

entry.summary: Introduces AutoLab, a benchmark of 36 expert-curated ultra long-horizon closed-loop optimization tasks across system optimization, puzzles, model development, and CUDA kernel optimization. It evaluates frontier models on sustained iterative improvement beyond short trajectories.

entry.title: When Autoregressive Consistency Hurts Safety Alignment

author.name: Bochen Lyu, Yiyang Jia, Xiaohao Cai, Zhanxing Zhu

entry.summary: This paper explains shallow safety alignment in LLMs through autoregressive consistency, the tendency of next-token prediction to extend the current trajectory, which concentrates alignment updates on early tokens. The same mechanism predicts a broader class of attacks that induce harmful continuations at arbitrary positions.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Dynamic Clinical Decision-Making with Standardized Patient Cases

author.name: Cheng Liang, Pengcheng Qiu, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Chaoyi Wu, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: MedSP1000 is an interactive clinical benchmark derived from standardized-patient teaching cases, with 1,638 cases and over 24K trajectory-level rubrics to evaluate dynamic clinical decision-making across an encounter. It moves beyond static single-turn medical QA.

entry.title: Scene-Centric Unsupervised Video Panoptic Segmentation

author.name: Christoph Reich, Oliver Hahn, Nikita Araslanov, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Christian Rupprecht, Daniel Cremers, Stefan Roth

entry.summary: VideoCUPS is the first unsupervised video panoptic segmentation approach, generating temporally consistent pseudo-labels from scene-centric videos using depth, motion, and visual cues. It introduces a benchmark and a Video DropLoss to train without human supervision.

entry.title: The Meta-Agent Challenge: Are Current Agents Capable of Autonomous Agent Development?

author.name: Xinyu Lu, Tianshu Wang, Pengbo Wang, zujie wen, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou, Boxi Cao, Yaojie Lu, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun

entry.summary: Introduces the Meta-Agent Challenge (MAC), testing whether frontier models can autonomously develop agent systems rather than just execute tasks, with multi-layer anti-reward-hacking defenses. It evaluates the capacity for self-directed agent construction across five domains.

entry.title: The Variance Brain Foundation Models Forgot: Third-Order Statistics Predict Cognition Where Billion-Parameter Models Fail

author.name: Giovanni Marraffini, Gabriel Mahuas, Trinidad Borrell, Victoria Shevchenko, Demian Wassermann

entry.summary: Shows that brain foundation models pretrained on fMRI predict cognition worse than simple linear regression on functional connectivity, with the gap widening at larger scale. It attributes this to a variance allocation problem where pretraining captures dominant but not cognition-predictive higher-order structure.

entry.title: Large Language Models Hack Rewards, and Society

author.name: Wei Liu, Xinyi Mou, Hanqi Yan, Zhongyu Wei, Yulan He

entry.summary: Hypothesizes that RL post-training can scale reward hacking into societal hacking, where models discover loopholes in regulation-like rules, and introduces SocioHack, a sandbox of 72 societal environments. It demonstrates that models exploit gaps between measurable rules and institutional intent.

entry.title: SaliMory: Orchestrating Cognitive Memory for Conversational Agents

author.name: Kai Zhang, Xinyuan Zhang, Hongda Jiang, Shiun-Zu Kuo, Hyokun Yun, Ejaz Ahmed, Shereen Oraby, Ziyun Li, Sanat Sharma, Ann Lee, Ahmed A Aly, Anuj Kumar, Raffay Hamid, Xin Luna Dong

entry.summary: Presents SaliMory, a framework training a single LLM to manage cognitively-structured persistent memory (user facts, preferences, working memory) using hierarchical stage-wise process rewards and reward-decomposed contrastive refinement to solve credit assignment in multi-stage memory pipelines. Authored by a large Meta-affiliated team for lifelong conversational agents.

entry.title: The Loss Is Not Enough: Sampling Conditions and Inductive Bias in Contrastive Representation Learning

author.name: Justinas Zaliaduonis, Patrick Putzky, Till Richter, Sergios Gatidis

entry.summary: Develops a measure-theoretic framework formalizing the diversity condition on positive-pair sampling necessary for isometric latent recovery in contrastive learning, showing that the loss alone is insufficient and sampling/inductive bias matter. It introduces a support-corrected InfoNCE variant.

entry.title: Caliper: Probing Lexical Anchors versus Causal Structure in LLMs

author.name: Zhenyu Yu, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Caliper probes whether LLMs do genuine causal reasoning or lexical pattern matching by replacing semantic variable names with placeholders while preserving causal structure. Across nine models and three benchmarks, anonymization causes large accuracy drops, suggesting heavy reliance on lexical anchors.

entry.title: OSCAR: Omni-Embodiment Skeleton-Conditioned World Action Model for Robotics

author.name: Zhuoyuan Wu, Jun Gao

entry.summary: OSCAR is a precise action-conditioned video world model that generalizes across robot embodiments using 2D kinematic skeleton conditioning and a large standardized data pipeline curating robotics and egocentric human datasets. It enables robot policy evaluation with precise action following across diverse embodiments.

entry.title: Phase transitions for the noisy transformer model in arbitrary dimension

author.name: Kyunghoo Mun, Matthew Rosenzweig

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies the McKean-Vlasov free energy for an unnormalized self-attention model of noisy transformer dynamics, proving a sharp global-minimizer dichotomy in every dimension with an explicit Bessel-function threshold. It characterizes when the uniform density remains the unique minimizer versus when a phase transition occurs.

entry.title: ZipSplat: Fewer Gaussians, Better Splats

author.name: Alexander Veicht, Sunghwan Hong, D\'aniel Bar\'ath, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: ZipSplat is a token-based feed-forward Gaussian Splatting model that decouples Gaussian count from camera resolution by clustering visual tokens into compact scene tokens. This allocates representation budget by scene complexity rather than pixel grid, yielding fewer but better-placed Gaussians.

entry.title: Potential-Guided Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Policy Improvement

author.name: Yunpeng Mei, Jiakai He, Hongjie Cao, Chenyu Wang, Xiaowen Zhu, Yihan Zhou, Jiamin Wang, Chenbo Xin, Peng Cheng, Yuxuan Yang, Yijie Wang, Xinhu Zheng, Gao Huang, Jie Chen, Gang Wang

entry.summary: ForesightFlow is a self-guided flow-matching VLA policy that augments each generated action chunk with a learned success-potential trajectory, enabling best-of-K inference without an external critic. It improves VLA policies from mixed-quality deployment experience without imitating failures or requiring a large offline RL critic.

entry.title: Can Generalist Agents Automate Data Curation?

author.name: Feiyang Kang, Hanze Li, Adam Nguyen, Mahavir Dabas, Jiaqi W. Ma, Frederic Sala, Dawn Song, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Introduces Curation-Bench to test whether generalist coding agents can automate the iterative data-curation loop while fixing model, recipe, and evaluation. Agents reach strong baselines within ten iterations but show persistent limitations revealed by trajectory analysis.

entry.title: Scaling Self-Evolving Agents via Parametric Memory

author.name: Tao Ren, Weiyao Luo, Hui Yang, Rongzhi Zhu, Xiang Huang, Yuchuan Wu, Bingxue Chou, Jieping Ye, Jiafeng Liang, Yongbin Li, Yijie Peng

entry.summary: Introduces TMEM, a self-evolving parametric memory framework where agents distill experience into fast LoRA weights via lightweight online updates, genuinely altering future behavior within an episode. It moves beyond prompt-space memory that cannot learn from experience.

entry.title: Unlocking Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale

author.name: Yifeng Liu, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Extends the Maximal Update Parametrization to Gated Delta Networks, deriving scaling rules by propagating coordinate-size estimates through gating and recurrent state dynamics. Experiments confirm stable learning-rate transfer across scales for these sub-quadratic architectures.

entry.title: Building The Ph(ysical)AI Layer Of Machine Intelligence

author.name: Ulbert Jose Botero, Liam Smith, Brooks Olney, Pooya Khorrami, Steven Kusiak, Watson Jia, Sage Trudeau, Daniel Capecci

entry.summary: Proposes principle-driven foundation models that encode signal-theoretic priors (Fourier, energy conservation, symmetry) instead of pure statistical correlations, trained only on RF data yet transferring to audio, images, text, and video via frozen representations. It targets cross-modal generalization to unseen domains.

entry.title: dMX: Differentiable Mixed-Precision Assignment for Low-Precision Floating-Point Formats

author.name: Giuseppe Franco, Ian Colbert, Pablo Monteagudo-Lago, Felix Marty, Nicholas Fraser

entry.summary: Introduces dMX, a differentiable mixed-precision quantization framework for learnable floating-point bit-width assignment over the MXFP microscaling family, folding the design space into a continuous optimization with one learnable scalar per layer. It targets efficient LLM deployment with better accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs.

entry.title: From Ticks to Flows: Dynamics of Neural Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Environments

author.name: Saket Tiwari, Tejas Kotwal, George Konidaris

entry.summary: Presents a theoretical framework modeling deep RL in continuous environments as a continuous-time stochastic process drawing on stochastic control, deriving a two-timescale (environment time and gradient time) formulation for single-hidden-layer actor-critic networks in the infinite-width limit. It characterizes the evolution of state and value estimates over gradient steps.

entry.title: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models Learn Interpretable and Specialized Experts for Personalized Preference Modeling

author.name: Yifan Wang, Jinyi Mu, Mayank Jobanputra, Yu Wang, Ji-Ung Lee, Soyoung Oh, Isabel Valera, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: Proposes a sparse Mixture-of-Experts reward model for RLHF that learns interpretable, specialized experts for personalized preference modeling, encouraging sparse and disentangled preference components to better capture heterogeneous human preferences. It avoids additional annotation costs.

entry.title: What If Prompt Injection Never Left? Exploring Cross-Session Stored Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems

author.name: Yuanbo Xie, Tianyun Liu, Yingjie Zhang, Suchen Liu, Yulin Li, Liya Su, Tingwen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces cross-session stored prompt injection in agentic systems, inspired by stored cross-site scripting, where an injection persists in long-lived state (memory, filesystems, tools) and silently influences future executions across sessions. It expands the prompt-injection attack surface beyond single-session model-level threats.

entry.title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuekang Wang, Zhuoyuan Hao, Shuo Hou, Hao Peng, Juanzi Li, Xiaozhi Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces CHERRL, a controllable hacking environment for rubric-based RL that injects known biases into the LLM judge to reliably reproduce, observe, and detect reward hacking. It provides a clean testbed for studying and mitigating reward hacking in LLM-as-judge training.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from Rich Feedback with Distributional DAgger

author.name: Rishabh Agrawal, Jacob Fein-Ashley, Paria Rashidinejad

entry.summary: This paper studies reinforcement learning from rich feedback (execution traces, tool outputs, expert corrections) via a distributional variant of DAgger, where the learner has local access to an expert distribution on visited states. It yields a forward cross-entropy objective enabling rich sequence-level credit assignment beyond single-bit RLVR rewards.

entry.title: Edge of Stability Selectively Shapes Learning Across the Data Distribution

author.name: Shauna Kwag, Anakha Ganesh, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: This paper shows that the edge-of-stability regime is selective rather than global, redistributing learning across training-distribution subgroups by amplifying some while suppressing others. Via branching interventions and controlled perturbations, it identifies two necessary conditions: gradient alignment with the top Hessian eigenvector and sufficient group representation.

entry.title: Agent Planning Benchmark: A Diagnostic Framework for Planning Capabilities in LLM Agents

author.name: Haoyu Sun, Wenxuan Wang, Mingyang Song, Jujie He, Weinan Zhang, Yang Liu, Yang Yang, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: The Agent Planning Benchmark (APB) provides 4,209 multimodal cases across 22 domains to diagnose planning versus execution failures in LLM agents, including robustness to broken tools and unsolvable tasks. Evaluation of 12 MLLMs reveals systematic weaknesses in long-horizon planning and calibrated refusal.

entry.title: Depth-Attention: Cross-Layer Value Mixing for Language Models

author.name: Boyi Zeng, Yiqin Hao, Zitong Wang, Shixiang Song, He Li, Feichen Song, Yifan Liu, Ziwei He, Xinbing Wang, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Depth-Attention enables Transformer layers to selectively reuse earlier-layer representations by having queries attend over keys of earlier layers at the same token position inside the attention module. It addresses limited cross-depth information flow without inflating the KV cache.

entry.title: MetaPoint: Unlocking Precise Spatial Control in Agentic Visual Generation

author.name: Dewei Zhou, Xinyu Huang, Xun Wang, Ji Xie, Yabo Zhang, Liang Li, Kunchang Li, Zongxin Yang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: MetaPoint represents continuous 2D coordinates as a single special token to enable pixel-level spatial control in generative visual models without architectural changes, leveraging existing positional encodings. It allows position control with one token and bounding boxes with two.

entry.title: DLO-Lab: Benchmarking Deformable Linear Object Manipulations with Differentiable Physics

author.name: Junyi Cao, Yian Wang, Ziyan Xiong, Chunru Lin, Zhehuan Chen, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: DLO-Lab introduces a differentiable physics simulator and benchmark for deformable linear object manipulation (ropes, cables, rubber bands) supporting diverse materials and tasks. It aims to overcome the narrow, task-specific scope and data limitations of prior DLO work.

entry.title: MAD: Mapping-Aware World Models for Agile Quadrotor Flight

author.name: Xinhong Zhang, Runqing Wang, Yunfan Ren, Ding Yu, Boyu Zhou, Jian Sun, Fang Deng, Jie Chen, Gang Wang

entry.summary: MAD (Mapping-Aware Dreamer) is a geometry-aware world model for vision-based agile quadrotor flight that reconstructs robocentric occupancy and visibility grid maps rather than raw images as its self-supervised objective. This forces the latent state to encode local geometry, visibility history, and ego-motion for collision avoidance under partial visibility.

entry.title: HORIZON: Recoverability-Governed Curriculum for Physical-Domain Scaling

author.name: Chenhao Bai, Liqin Lu, Kaijun Wang, Hui Chen, Jin-Chuan Shi, Yuyang Liu, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: HORIZON introduces a recoverability-governed curriculum for physical-domain scaling in on-policy robot learning, identifying recoverability as the central constraint and expanding physical domains only within the policy's recoverable boundary. Using quadruped locomotion, it shows that harder physics is only useful when it remains close enough to generate corrective on-policy data.

entry.title: Teaching AI agents to ask better questions by playing “Battleship”

author.name: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL and Harvard researchers use a collaborative Battleship game reframed around natural-language questions to study why language models struggle with information-seeking in uncertain environments. By comparing LM and human question-asking strategies, they probe the agents' ability to ask better questions for high-stakes settings like medical diagnosis and scientific discovery.

entry.title: Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems: Diagnostics and a Strong Baseline

author.name: Zhikai Chen, Jialiang Gu, Junyu Yin, Xianxuan Long, Shenglai Zeng, Xiaoze Liu, Kai Guo, Keren Zhou, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses that most agent memory systems are tuned to single scenarios and fail to generalize, evaluating eight systems across five diverse scenarios. A simple harness giving the agent active control over flat text-file storage achieves the best cross-task ranking.

entry.title: SCI-PRM: A Tool Aware Process Reward Model for Scientific Reasoning Verification

author.name: Xiangyu Zhao, Hengyuan Zhao, Yiheng Wang, Wanghan Xu, Yuhao Zhou, Qinglong Cao, Zhiwang Zhou, Lei Bai, Wenlong Zhang, Xiao-Ming Wu

entry.summary: Constructs SCIPRM70K, a large dataset of Chain-of-Tool trajectories interleaving reasoning with scientific tool execution, and trains Sci-PRM, a tool-aware process reward model for scientific verification. It extends PRMs beyond math into biology, chemistry, and physics.

entry.title: AICompanionBench: Benchmarking LLMs-as-Judges for AI Companion Safety

author.name: Yanjing Ren, Reza Ebrahimi, TengTeng Ma

entry.summary: Introduces AICompanionBench, claimed as the first public benchmark of real Replika companion conversations annotated across nine safety risk categories, and evaluates 20 LLMs as judges. It addresses growing concerns over unsafe human-AI companion interactions.

entry.title: MaskForge: Structure-Aware Adaptive Attacks for Jailbreaking Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Yingzi Ma, Zhengyue Zhao, Xiaogeng Liu, Minhui Xue, Yue Zhao, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces MaskForge, a black-box adaptive jailbreak for diffusion LLMs that exploits their native infill capability and bidirectional context through optimized search over a growing library of structural mask patterns. It reveals a safety surface distinct from autoregressive models.

entry.title: RUBAS: Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning for Agent Safety

author.name: Xian Qi Loye, Qinglin Su, Zhexin Zhang, Shiyao Cui, Qi Zhu, Fei Mi, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: Introduces RUBAS, a rubric-based reinforcement learning framework for agent safety that decomposes behavior into tool-use, argument, response safety, and helpfulness for fine-grained interpretable rewards over full trajectories. It balances safe tool execution with task completion.

entry.title: Spectral Scaling Laws of Muon

author.name: Gagik Magakyan, Pablo Parrilo, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic study of how the singular-value spectrum of momentum matrices behaves during Muon optimizer training and how it changes with model size, given Newton-Schulz only approximately orthonormalizes. It tracks singular value quantiles across layers and scales.

entry.title: Instant-Fold: In-Context Imitation Learning for Deformable Object Manipulation

author.name: Yilong Wang, Cheng Qian, Edward Johns

entry.summary: Introduces Instant-Fold, an in-context imitation learning framework for deformable object manipulation that infers and executes diverse manipulation modes from a single human demonstration without gradient updates, using temporal contrastive pretraining and a flow-matching transformer policy. It addresses high-dimensional, topology-changing manipulation.

entry.title: Expectations vs. Realities: The Cost of MSE-Optimal Forecasting Under Conditional Uncertainty

author.name: Riku Green, Zahraa S. Abdallah, Telmo M Silva Filho

entry.summary: Shows that MSE-optimal multi-step forecasting can be misleading under conditional uncertainty, formalizing a conditional uncertainty gap and proving no deterministic predictor can both minimize MSE and match the marginal distribution of realized futures. It establishes a fundamental model-agnostic tradeoff between point accuracy and marginal realism.

entry.title: LoopMoE: Unifying Iterative Computation with Mixture-of-Experts for Language Modeling

author.name: Wenkai Chen, Tianshu Li, Wenyong Huang, Yichun Yin, Lifeng Shang, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Presents LoopMoE, a looped Mixture-of-Experts language model integrating sparse routing with iterative weight-shared computation via IterAdaLN (an iteration-and-state-conditioned modulation) and a capacity-balancing strategy, enabling isolation of iterative computation effects under matched FLOP budgets. It scales parameter capacity and effective depth orthogonally.

entry.title: Who Needs Labels? Adapting Vision Foundation Models With the Metadata You Already Have

author.name: Elouan Gard\`es, Seung Eun Yi, Kartik Ahuja, Th\'eo Moutakanni, Huy V. Vo, Piotr Bojanowski, Wolfgang M. Pernice, Lo\"ic Landrieu, Camille Couprie

entry.summary: FINO is a label-free method to adapt generic vision foundation models to specialized scientific domains using metadata (discrete and continuous) under a self-supervised objective, preserving generality while suppressing spurious factors. It is tested across microscopy, Earth observation, and wildlife monitoring.

entry.title: Stateful Visual Encoders for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zirui Wang, Junwei Yu, Adam Yala, David M. Chan, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Trevor Darrell

entry.summary: This work introduces a Stateful Visual Encoder for vision-language models that conditions each image encoding on prior visual features, so subtle but task-critical changes are not attenuated before reaching the language model. It improves multi-image, multi-turn agentic visual reasoning.

entry.title: GRAIL: Gradient-Reweighted Advantages for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Tej Deep Pala, Vernon Toh, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: GRAIL introduces token-wise advantage reweighting for RL with verifiable rewards, using gradient-activation saliency to emphasize logically important tokens over filler words. It addresses gradient dilution in GRPO without costly process reward models.

entry.title: Video2LoRA: Parametric Video Internalization for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Manan Suri, Sarvesh Baskar, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Video2LoRA uses a perceiver hypernetwork to read a frozen VLM's layer-wise representations of a video and generate a LoRA adapter in a single forward pass, internalizing video content into parameters. This lets the VLM answer queries from the adapter alone with zero visual tokens at query time.

entry.title: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms

author.name: Jiashu Yao, Heyan Huang, Daiqing Wu, Wangke Chen, Huaxi Ai, Haoyu Wen, Zeming Liu, Yuhang Guo

entry.summary: LivingScreen formalizes living-screen-native GUI agents that must act on continuously playing interfaces like short-video apps, deciding what to watch and for how long. It provides a browser-based environment and metrics jointly scoring accuracy and information efficiency, finding frontier models fail to match human cost-accuracy.

entry.title: MeshFlow: Efficient Artistic Mesh Generation via MeshVAE and Flow-based Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Weiyu Li, Antoine Toisoul, Tom Monnier, Roman Shapovalov, Rakesh Ranjan, Ping Tan, Andrea Vedaldi

entry.summary: MeshFlow generates artist-like 3D meshes using a VAE that encodes continuous vertex positions and discrete connectivity in a compact continuous latent space, plus a rectified-flow diffusion transformer. It avoids the quadratic inference cost and quantization errors of autoregressive mesh generators.

entry.title: Do Foundation Models See Biology? Evaluating Attention Coherence with Spatial Transcriptomics in Glioblastoma

author.name: Dilakshan Srikanthan, Amoon Jamzad, Paul Wilson, Nooshin Maghsoodi, Robert Policelli, Gabor Fichtinger, John F. Rudan, Parvin Mousavi

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether attention maps from five pathology foundation models capture genuine biology by comparing them against spatial transcriptomics signatures in glioblastoma. It provides an orthogonal, hypothesis-free framework for assessing biological coherence relevant to clinical trust and regulation.

entry.title: Anchor3R: Streaming 3D Reconstruction with Transient Anchors for Long-Horizon Visual Mapping

author.name: Peilin Tao, Chong Cheng, Yuansen Du, Caiwei Song, Zhengqing Chen, Xiaoyang Guo, Wei Yin, Weiqiang Ren, Qian Zhang, Hainan Cui, Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: Anchor3R is a streaming 3D reconstruction framework that uses transient, current-centric anchors instead of a fixed first-frame gauge to reduce drift on long video sequences. It addresses train-test mismatch and attention bias toward early anchors in feed-forward reconstruction.

entry.title: Think Fast and Far: Long-Horizon Online POMDP Planning via Rapid State Sampling

author.name: Yuanchu Liang, Edward Kim, J. Arden Knoll, Wil Thomason, Zachary Kingston, Lydia E. Kavraki, Hanna Kurniawati

entry.summary: ROP-RAS3 is an approximate online POMDP solver that uses extremely fast sampling-based motion planning to generate diverse macro-actions online, biasing belief-space sampling for long-horizon planning under uncertainty. It avoids exhaustive action enumeration to scale POMDP planning.

entry.title: X4Val: Learning Neural Surrogates for Variance-Reduced Policy Evaluation

author.name: Rachel Luo, Michael Watson, Apoorva Sharma, Heng Yang, Han Qi, Edward Schmerling, Sushant Veer, Boris Ivanovic, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: X4Val learns neural surrogates for variance-reduced policy evaluation of robotic systems, principally leveraging heterogeneous auxiliary data sources like simulation, historical logs, and related-platform data that are not directly representative of real-world outcomes. It enables high-confidence performance estimation when real-world test data is scarce.

entry.title: MIT researchers teach AI models to interpret charts

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT and the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab built ChartNet, a state-of-the-art dataset of over a million varied charts that encodes visual, numerical, and linguistic components to teach vision-language models to interpret charts. They trained open-source VLMs on it, with smaller models significantly improving at chart understanding.

entry.title: Stumbling Into AI Emotional Dependence: How Routine AI Interactions Reshape Human Connection

author.name: Yaoxi Shi, Cathy Mengying Fang, Pattie Maez, Amit Goldenberg

entry.summary: Argues that AI emotional support typically arises incidentally within task-oriented interactions rather than via deliberate companion seeking, and that these encounters are path-dependent in reshaping future human reliance. It reframes policy assumptions about emotional dependence on AI.

entry.title: Characterizing initial human-AI proof formalization workflows

author.name: Katherine M. Collins, Simon Frieder, Jonas Bayer, Jacob Loader, Jeck Lim, Peiyang Song, Fabian Zaiser, Lexin Zhou, Shanda Li, Sam Looi, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Umang Bhatt, Adrian Weller, Jose Hernandez-Orallo, Cameron E. Freer, Valerie Chen, Ilia Sucholutsky

entry.summary: Conducts a mixed-methods study of how mathematicians actually use AI tools in proof formalization workflows, capturing desires, barriers, and real adoption patterns. It shifts focus from benchmarking to human-centered usage analysis.

entry.title: Do Transformers Need Three Projections? Systematic Study of QKV Variants

author.name: Ali Kayyam, Anusha Madan Gopal, M Anthony Lewis

entry.summary: Systematically studies whether transformers need all three QKV projections by testing shared key-value, shared query-key, and single-projection variants, plus asymmetric attention via 2D positional encodings. Experiments span synthetic, vision, and language modeling up to 1.2B parameters.

entry.title: LiftQuant: Continuous Bit-Width LLM via Dimensional Lifting and Projection

author.name: Liulu He, XuanAng Liu, Juntao Liu, Taolue Feng, Ting Lu, Chunsheng Gan, Zhiyv Peng, Yuan Du, Huanrui Yang, Yijiang Liu, Li Du

entry.summary: Introduces LiftQuant, enabling continuous bit-width LLM quantization via a lift-then-project mechanism that approximates low-dimensional weights by projecting a 1-bit lattice from higher-dimensional space. The effective bit-width is set by the dimension ratio, allowing Pareto-optimal fitting to memory budgets.

entry.title: The Invisible Lottery: How Subtle Cues Steer Algorithm Choice in LLM Code Generation

author.name: Akanksha Narula, Mofasshara Binte Rafique, Laurent Bindschaedler

entry.summary: Studies algorithm steering, where incidental prompt cues shift which valid algorithm an LLM selects under fixed correctness, via 46,535 controlled experiments across 11 tasks, 19 cue types, and 15 configurations. It documents how subtle contextual signals systematically bias code-generation choices.

entry.title: The Differentiable Auditory Loop (DAL): An ML Framework for Hyper-Personalized Hearing Aids

author.name: Alejandro Ballesta Rosen, Jason Mikiel-Hunter, Julian Maclaren, Jack Collins, Richard F. Lyon, Simon Carlile

entry.summary: Introduces the Differentiable Auditory Loop, an open-source framework using a JAX-ported differentiable cochlear model (CARFAC) to optimize neural networks that match impaired auditory neural patterns to normal-hearing references for personalized hearing aids. It targets underlying encoding dysfunctions rather than just amplification, potentially improving performance in complex listening scenarios.

entry.title: Caught in the Act(ivation): Toward Pre-Output and Multi-Turn Detection of Credential Exfiltration by LLM Agents

author.name: Kargi Chauhan, Pratibha Revankar

entry.summary: Studies pre-output and multi-turn detection of credential exfiltration by LLM agents using activation probes, conformal-calibrated honeytokens, and a cumulative leakage-budget tracker across turns. It addresses indirect prompt injection causing credential leaks in agent context windows.

entry.title: OpenRFM: Dissecting Relational In-Context Learning

author.name: Zhikai Chen, Junyu Yin, Jialiang Gu, Siheng Xiong, Xiaoze Liu, Ruowang Zhang, Keren Zhou, Kai Guo

entry.summary: Dissects Relational Foundation Models via the Relational Transformer, showing model-side that it performs relation-level in-context learning that fails under sparse label coverage (a kernel-regression view), and data-side that synthetic-only and in-distribution pretraining underperform. It explains the gap between open and commercial RFMs.

entry.title: From Symbolic to Geometric: Enabling Spatial Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Chu, Bita Azarijoo, Li Xiong, Khurram Shafique, Cyrus Shahabi

entry.summary: Introduces the Spatial Language Model, claimed as the first multimodal LLM treating location as a first-class modality enabling geometric spatial reasoning over learned spatial representations rather than symbolic pattern matching over spatial language. It addresses LLMs' lack of native continuous spatial representations.

entry.title: Plan, Watch, Recover: A Benchmark and Architectures for Proactive Procedural Assistance

author.name: Kaustav Kundu, Ritvik Shrivastava, Maxim Arap, Nanshu Wang, Xianhui Zhu, Quintin Fettes, Gautam Tiwari, Parth Suresh, Th\'eo Moutakanni, Alejandro Castillejo Munoz, Allen Bolourchi, Pascale Fung, Pinar Donmez, Babak Damavandi, Anuj Kumar, Seungwhan Moon

entry.summary: This work releases EgoProactive, a large-scale wearable-egocentric dataset for proactive procedural assistance with explicit out-of-plan annotations and recovery steps, plus augmentations of five existing benchmarks. It supports systems that decide when to interrupt and how to coach during procedural tasks.

entry.title: Failed Reasoning Traces Tell You What Is Fixable (But Not by Reading Them)

author.name: Nizar Islah, Istabrak Abbes, Irina Rish, Sarath Chandar, Eilif B. Muller

entry.summary: This paper argues that failed reasoning traces encode recoverability structure indicating which test-time interventions can rescue a failure, recoverable from the distributional signature of failed rollouts rather than their text. Three trajectory-level features cluster failures into stable categories distinguishing unlucky sampling from structural failures.

entry.title: Expert-Aware Refusal Steering

author.name: Anna C. Marbut, Daniel R. Olson, Travis J. Wheeler

entry.summary: This work extends refusal-suppression steering vectors to Mixture-of-Experts LLMs and proposes expert-aware steering methods that exploit refusal-specific routing patterns. It exposes a dual-use safety vulnerability in MoE alignment mechanisms.

entry.title: Efficient and Training-Free Single-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Haojun Qiu, Kiriakos N. Kutulakos, David B. Lindell

entry.summary: This paper generates images matching the multi-scale patch distribution of a single reference using a closed-form optimal denoiser over a finite patch dataset, eliminating neural network training. The method is training-free and far more efficient than single-image diffusion baselines.

entry.title: LazyAttention: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Deferred Positional Encoding

author.name: Haocheng Xia, Mihir Pamnani, Hanxi Fang, Supawit Chockchowwat, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: LazyAttention kernelizes deferred positional encoding to enable zero-copy, position-agnostic KV cache reuse across contexts, overcoming the limitation that conventional caches bake in positions. It targets retrieval-augmented generation and in-context learning efficiency.

entry.title: SparDA: Sparse Decoupled Attention for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Yaosheng Fu, Guangxuan Xiao, Xin Dong, Song Han, Oreste Villa

entry.summary: SparDA is a decoupled sparse attention architecture that adds a Forecast projection to predict KV blocks needed by the next layer, enabling lookahead prefetch overlap and reducing the quadratic cost of sparse selection. It targets long-context LLM inference with CPU offloading.

entry.title: LifeSide: Benchmarking Agents as Lifelong Digital Companions

author.name: Yuqian Wu, Zhijie Deng, Wei Chen, Junwei Li, Yutian Jiang, Junle Chen, Zhengjun Huang, Qingxiang Liu, Jing Tang, Jiaheng Wei, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: LifeSide introduces a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents as lifelong digital companions, focusing on multi-session memory-emotion-environment loops with 2,000 personas and 111K tasks. It tests memory tracking, user understanding, privacy control, and emotional support together rather than in isolation.

entry.title: BreastGPT: A Multimodal Large Language Model for the Full Spectrum of Breast Cancer Clinical Routine

author.name: Yang Liu, Jiajin Zhang, Danyang Tu, Yaojun Hu, Jiao Qu, Jiuyu Zhang, Yu Shi, Wei Fang, Shi Gu, Ling Zhang, Yingda Xia

entry.summary: BreastGPT is a multimodal LLM covering the full breast-cancer clinical workflow (screening, diagnosis, treatment planning), trained on a workflow-aligned corpus of 1.86M instruction pairs from 17 sub-datasets. It addresses the narrow-task limitation of existing medical MLLMs.

entry.title: Clinical Assistant for Remote Engagement Link (CARE-link): A Web-Based Electronic Health Records Software for Managing Diabetes

author.name: Prince Ebenezer Adjei, Joshua Teye Tettey, Toufiq Musah, Audrey Agbeve, John Amuasi

entry.summary: Caliper-style analysis aside, this audio-language paper investigates whether ALMs override clear audio evidence in favor of conflicting text, using a same-audio counterfactual to measure preference shifts. It finds 64.1% of conflict cases flip when conflicting text is removed, indicating audio evidence is encoded but loses in arbitration, and shows the failure is repairable.

entry.title: GroupToM-Bench: Benchmarking Group Theory of Mind and Nonlinear Social Emergence in MLLMs

author.name: Weidong Tang, Jierui Li, Yueling Hou, Zihan Mei, Can Zhang, Xinyan Wan, Zhiyuan Liang, Pengfei Zhou, Yang You, Wangbo Zhao

entry.summary: GroupToM-Bench is the first multimodal benchmark for group-level theory of mind, built around a causal chain from individual belief-desire-intention states to group tension, structure, and nonlinear collective outcomes. It shows current MLLMs fail at inferring group-level social emergence.

entry.title: Ultra-Fast Neural Video Compression

author.name: Jiahao Li, Wenxuan Xie, Zhaoyang Jia, Bin Li, Zongyu Guo, Xiaoyi Zhang, Yan Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a chunk-based neural video codec that encodes multiple frames into a single compact latent and decodes them in parallel using cross-frame interaction modules, dramatically improving throughput. It targets the prohibitive computational complexity that blocks NVC deployment.

entry.title: Z-FLoc: Zero-Shot Floorplan Localization via Geometric Primitives

author.name: Ayumi Umemura, Toshinori Kuwahara, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Barath

entry.summary: Z-FLoc proposes a zero-shot floorplan-based visual localization method that estimates camera pose without environment-specific retraining by leveraging dominant geometric primitives. This addresses the practical deployment limits of data-driven methods that need large training sets and per-environment tuning.

entry.title: Affordance2Action: Task-Conditioned Scene-level Affordance Grounding for Real-Time Manipulation

author.name: Litao Liu, Yifan Han, Pengfei Yi, Wenbo Yu, Hanqing Wang, Haoran Du, Enze Yuan, Zilin Yuan, Ruiding Feng, Michael Liu, Qi Zhang, Jingjin Yu

entry.summary: Affordance2Action introduces a benchmark and learning framework for scene-level, task-conditioned part affordance grounding that handles one-to-many instruction-region correspondences in cluttered scenes. It targets real-time manipulation by grounding instructions to functional parts rather than object categories.

entry.title: HapTile: A Haptic-Informed Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Contact-Rich Imitation Learning

author.name: Amirhosein Alian, Yongqiang Zhao, Shiyi Gu, Xuyang Zhang, Zhuo Chen, Christopher E. Mower, Haitham Bou-Ammar, Shan Luo

entry.summary: HapTile is a contact-grounded visuotactile manipulation dataset that embeds physical interaction sensing at both the robot end-effector (fingertip tactile feedback) and operator level (haptic-informed demonstrations). It advances beyond vision-only VLA datasets by combining task diversity, language conditioning, action trajectories, and tactile signals.

entry.title: Ground truth is a process, not a dataset

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Amazon Science post argues that ground truth for evaluating AI-generated research reports is a process rather than a fixed dataset, given that report claims often synthesize evidence across multiple sources without a single matching quote. It describes the challenge of building benchmarks for fact-checking deep-research reports as being as hard as building the fact checker itself.

entry.title: Parthenon Law: A Self-Evolving Legal-Agent Framework

author.name: Hejia Geng, Leo Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Parthenon Law, a self-evolving legal-agent framework, backed by a large empirical study of 12,510 agent trajectories on Harvey LAB showing frontier agents fall short of completing legal matters in a single pass. It adds a legal-specific architecture and a mechanism to learn from outcomes.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Mobile Agents with Implicit Reasoning and Generative World Models

author.name: Zhichao Yang, Yuanze Hu, Haojie Hao, Longkun Hao, Dongshuo Huang, Hongyu Lin, Gen Li, Lanqing Hong, Yihang Lou, Yan Bai

entry.summary: Introduces MIRAGE, a mobile agent framework that learns continuous latent reasoning from textual reasoning traces, enabling internal reasoning without decoding long rationales, plus a generative world-model objective. It targets faster, cheaper, deployable screen control.

entry.title: PerceptTwin: Semantic Scene Reconstruction for Iterative LLM Planning and Verification

author.name: Charlie Gauthier, Sacha Morin, Liam Paull

entry.summary: Introduces PerceptTwin, a fully automatic pipeline constructing interactive robot simulations directly from perception-stack semantic scene representations, combining open-vocabulary object maps, 3D asset generation, affordance prediction, and commonsense checks. It lets LLM-generated plans be validated and refined before hardware execution.

entry.title: Continual Visual and Verbal Learning Through a Child's Egocentric Input

author.name: Xiaoyang Jiang, Yanlai Yang, Kenneth A. Norman, Brenden Lake, Mengye Ren

entry.summary: BabyCL is a continual multimodal learning framework that processes a child's egocentric SAYCam recordings in a single chronological pass, combining streaming visual representation learning with image-text contrastive objectives and a dual replay buffer. It studies whether networks can learn word-referent mappings in a developmentally realistic streaming regime.

entry.title: Imbuing Large Language Models with Bidirectional Logic for Robust Chain Repair

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun, Thomas Lukasiewicz

entry.summary: Teleological Reasoning Infilling (TRI) endows decoder-only models with goal-conditioned bridging by reframing erroneous reasoning segments as fill-in-the-middle tasks given a verified prefix and downstream milestone. It aims to combat error snowballing in chain-of-thought reasoning.

entry.title: Self-Evaluation Is Already There: Eliciting Latent Judge Calibration in Base LLMs with Minimal Data

author.name: XiuYu Zhang, Yi Shan, Junfeng Fang, Zhenkai Liang

entry.summary: This paper shows base LLMs can already predict an external judge's quality scores few-shot, and introduces Self-Evaluation Elicitation (SEE) to surface this latent ability with minimal data via calibration-coupled RL and masked distillation. It needs only 160 examples to improve self-evaluation.

entry.title: When Seeing Is Not Believing -- A Benchmark for Search-Grounded Video Misinformation Detection

author.name: Tao Yu, Yujia Yang, Shenghua Chai, Zhang Jinshuai, Haopeng Jin, Hao Wang, Minghui Zhang, Zhongtian Luo, Yuchen Long, Xinlong Chen, Jiabing Yang, Zhaolu Kang, Yuxuan Zhou, Zhengyu Man, Xinming Wang, Hongzhu Yi, Zheqi He, Xi Yang, Yan Huang, Liang Wang

entry.summary: EVID-Bench is a benchmark for search-grounded video misinformation detection where systems must search the open web for related videos and identify falsehoods via cross-video comparison. It covers 222 videos across 9 manipulation types including AI-generated content.

entry.title: 3DThinkVLA: Endowing Vision-Language-Action Models with Latent 3D Priors via 3D-Thinking-Guided Co-training

author.name: Jiaxin Shi, Xidong Zhang, Fucai Zhu, Zhe Li, Siyu Zhu, Weihao Yuan

entry.summary: 3DThinkVLA injects latent 3D priors into vision-language-action models via 3D-thinking-guided co-training, disentangling 3D geometry perception (aligned with a 3D foundation model) from 3D spatial reasoning (distilled online). It enables implicit 3D spatial reasoning during action prediction without backbone changes.

entry.title: Distribution-Free Risk-Aware Planning and Control Under Uncertainty Using Conformal Spectral Risk Control

author.name: Junsik Eom, Tulga Ersal

entry.summary: This paper proposes a distribution-free risk-aware MPC framework using conformal spectral risk control to guarantee user-specified risk levels without assumptions about the uncertainty distribution. Prediction sets generated by a distribution-free method enable safe navigation under imperfect uncertainty estimates.

entry.title: M3imic: Learning a Versatile Whole-Body Controller for Multimodal Motion Mimicking

author.name: Zuxing Lu, Ziang Zheng, Yao Lyu, Jingyu Liu, Feihong Zhang, Song Lu, Xin Yuan, Changyin Sun, Xingxing Zuo, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: M3imic is a versatile multi-modal whole-body controller for humanoid robots that unifies heterogeneous motion reference modalities including joint angles, human pose trajectories, and end-effector poses. It addresses the representational mismatch between dense joint angles and sparse end-effector poses for both locomotion and loco-manipulation.

entry.title: WAM-Nav: Asymmetric Latent World-Action Modeling for Unified Visual Navigation

author.name: Ning Yang, Yan Huang, Kaiwen Peng, Ziheng He, Kai Wang, Cui Miao, Kailin Lyu, Guo Li, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Jing Liu, Nianfeng Liu

entry.summary: WAM-Nav is a latent world-action model for embodied visual navigation that jointly learns action generation and latent visual foresight using an asymmetric design. It aims to add anticipatory reasoning to reactive policies while avoiding the error accumulation and inefficiency of modular predict-then-act approaches.

entry.title: AgentJet: A Flexible Swarm Training Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qingxu Fu, Boyin Liu, Shuchang Tao, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding

entry.summary: Presents AgentJet, a decoupled distributed swarm training framework for LLM agent reinforcement learning supporting heterogeneous multi-model RL, multi-task cocktail training, and fault tolerance. It separates trainable model nodes from arbitrary agent execution clients.

entry.title: Learning Admissible Heuristics via Cost Partitioning

author.name: Hugo Barral, Quentin Cappart, Marie-Jos\'e Huguet, Sylvie Thi\'ebaux

entry.summary: Proposes a framework that learns to infer admissible cost partitions for optimal planning by leveraging the Lagrangian dual between cost partitioning and multiplier prediction. It uses graph encodings with axial self-attention to predict cost weights satisfying admissibility constraints.

entry.title: FALSIFYBENCH: Evaluating Inductive Reasoning in LLMs with Rule Discovery Games

author.name: Leonardo Bertolazzi, Katya Tentori, Raffaella Bernardi

entry.summary: Introduces FALSIFYBENCH, an evaluation framework inspired by the Wason 2-4-6 task to test inductive, hypothesis-driven reasoning in LLMs through rule-discovery games. Evaluating 12 models reveals patterns in hypothesis generation and belief revision relevant to scientific discovery.

entry.title: Knowledge Index of Noah's Ark

author.name: Sheng Jin, Minghao Liu, Yunze Xiao, Zeqi Zhou, Heli Qi, Yifan Yao, Meishu Song, Kaijing Ma, Xuan Zhang, Sicong Jiang, Yizhe Li, Ningshan Ma, Jie Wei, Ziniu Li, Minglai Yang, Bangya Liu, Yiming Liang, Xiao Fang, Qingcheng Zeng, Jiarui Liu, Rui Yang, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang, Jiaheng Liu, Zihan Wang, Weihao Xuan, Ge Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces KINA, an 899-item knowledge benchmark across 261 disciplines with formal results on disciplinary representativeness (greedy approximation) and an annotation incentive scheme that dominates flat payment in review quality. It addresses scaling-driven design, lazy consensus, and ranking instability in knowledge benchmarks.

entry.title: DiffAero: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Simulation Framework for Efficient Quadrotor Policy Learning

author.name: Xinhong Zhang, Runqing Wang, Yunfan Ren, Jian Sun, Hao Fang, Jie Chen, Gang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces DiffAero, a GPU-accelerated, fully differentiable simulation framework for quadrotor control policy learning, supporting multiple dynamics models and sensor stacks with environment and agent parallelism. It eliminates CPU-GPU transfer bottlenecks for large throughput gains.

entry.title: CodegenBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient Code Across Architectures?

author.name: Jie Li, Wenzhao Wu, Junqi Hu, Qinrui Zheng, Bowen Wu, Juepeng Zheng, Yutong Lu, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: Introduces CodegenBench, evaluating LLMs on generating efficient CPU-oriented HPC code across x86, Sunway, and Kunpeng architectures, including BLAS routines and architecture-specific kernels. It addresses the underexplored gap in cross-architecture high-performance code generation.

entry.title: Unpredictable Safety: Domain-Dependent Compliance and the Transparency Gap in Open-Weight LLMs

author.name: Zacharie Bugaud

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic study of domain-dependent safety in open-weight LLMs, running 4,200 dual-framing interactions across seven ethical domains and five models, finding compliance varies by 71 percentage points across domains. It highlights a transparency gap where the same model behaves unpredictably across contexts.

entry.title: SymTRELLIS: Symmetry-Enforced Voxel Latents for 3D Generation

author.name: Guangda Ji, Qimin Chen, Qinchan Li, Mingrui Zhao, Kai Wang, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: Presents SymTRELLIS, a method enforcing arbitrary finite point group symmetries during flow-based 3D generation by approximating latent-space spatial transformations as a learned linear operator, without retraining the underlying VAE or flow model. It addresses physically unusable symmetry violations in generated 3D assets.

entry.title: Semantic Constraint Synthesis for Adaptive Trajectory Optimization via Large Language Models

author.name: Eleanor Brosius, Yuji Takubo, Daniele Gammelli, Simone D'Amico, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: Presents a framework using LLMs to translate natural-language space-mission requirements into executable trajectory optimization code and mathematical formulations, lowering the domain-expertise barrier. Authored by a Stanford group including Marco Pavone.

entry.title: Dual Advantage Fields

author.name: Alexey Zemtsov, Maxim Bobrin, Alexander Nikulin, Dmitry V. Dylov, Fakhri Karray, Vladislav Kurenkov, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Arip Asadulaev

entry.summary: Proposes Dual Advantage Fields, a policy-extraction method for offline goal-conditioned RL that converts a bilinear dual value model into a local advantage signal by learning an action-effect model predicting feature displacement aligned with goal direction. It bridges global reachability estimates with local action selection.

entry.title: Supportive Token Revealing for Fast Diffusion Language Model Decoding

author.name: Giries Abu Ayoub, Mario Barbara, Llu\'is Pastor-P\'erez, Tanja Bien, Aneesh Barthakur, Alaa Maalouf, Loay Mualem

entry.summary: Proposes AXON, a training-free module for diffusion language models that improves parallel decoding by considering not just which tokens are safe to reveal but whether remaining masked tokens become easy to decode, addressing dependency bottlenecks. It targets the quality-latency tradeoff in discrete diffusion text generation.

entry.title: Measuring What Matters: Synthetic Benchmarks for Concept Bottleneck Models

author.name: Julian Skirzynski, Harry Cheon, Shreyas Kadekodi, Meredith Stewart, Berk Ustun

entry.summary: Develops synthetic benchmarks for concept bottleneck models targeting decision-support and automation use cases, generating labeled datasets while controlling properties to isolate performance drivers and failure factors. It addresses the scarcity of concept-labeled datasets for interpretability research.

entry.title: A Geometric Characterization of the Stationary Plateau for Two-Layer Neural Networks

author.name: Tian Ding, Dawei Li, Ruoyu Sun

entry.summary: Provides a geometric characterization of stationary plateaus in two-layer neural network loss landscapes, classifying all stationary points arising from neuron splitting as minima or saddles via a per-neuron inner Hessian object. It clarifies how splitting coefficients and curvature jointly determine local geometry.

entry.title: MorphoQuant: Modality-Aware Quantization for Omni-modal Large Language Models

author.name: Yue Wu, Changyuan Wang, Zixuan Wang, Shilin Ma, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes MorphoQuant, a modality-aware post-training quantization framework for 4-bit omni-modal LLMs that handles distribution heterogeneity and disparate outliers across modalities via distribution-aware bias compensation absorbing long-tailed outliers into channel-wise biases. It preserves cross-modal morphology under aggressive quantization.

entry.title: Low-Rank Decay for Grokking in Scale-Invariant Transformers: A Spectral-Geometric View

author.name: Mingyu Li

entry.summary: Studies grokking in scale-invariant transformers (RMSNorm, QK-Norm) through a spectral-geometric lens, proposing Low-Rank Decay, a nuclear-norm-like regularizer whose subgradient (the polar factor) retains a tangential component that standard Frobenius weight decay lacks in the scale-invariant regime. It explains and influences grokking dynamics.

entry.title: ParetoPilot: Zero-Surrogate Offline Multi-Objective Optimization via Infer-Perturb-Guide Diffusion

author.name: Ruiqing Sun, Sen Yang, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Yijie Wang, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes ParetoPilot, a zero-surrogate diffusion framework for offline multi-objective optimization that leverages conditional priors embedded in pre-trained diffusion models via an infer-perturb-guide mechanism, eliminating reliance on external surrogate models that introduce overhead and deceptive evaluations. It discovers Pareto-optimal designs from static datasets.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Deep Research via Joint Generation and Evaluation

author.name: Han Zhu, Chengkun Cai, Yuanfeng Song, Xing Chen, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a self-evolving co-evolutionary training framework for deep research report generation that jointly evolves the generator and evaluator, addressing the problem that static LLM-as-a-judge evaluators saturate optimization pressure as the solver improves. It tackles unverifiable rewards in open-ended report generation.

entry.title: ANN Search: Recall What Matters

author.name: Dimitris Dimitropoulos, Nikos Mamoulis

entry.summary: Argues that ANN search should be evaluated by the quality of retrieved results (proposing 1/Ratio@k, the inverse approximation ratio) rather than Recall@k overlap with exact neighbors, showing Recall@k forces unnecessary computation. It is judge-free and better reflects what matters in retrieval-augmented tasks.

entry.title: Temporal Order Matters for Agentic Memory: Segment Trees for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yifan Simon Liu, Liam Gallagher, Faeze Moradi Kalarde, Jiazhou Liang, Armin Toroghi, Scott Sanner

entry.summary: Introduces SegTreeMem, an agentic memory architecture representing conversation history as a temporally-ordered segment tree over utterances with an online rightmost-frontier update rule, combining local semantic matching with hierarchical temporal context during retrieval. It argues temporal order matters for long-horizon agents, unlike topic-similarity-only memory.

entry.title: Rollout-Level Advantage-Prioritized Experience Replay for GRPO

author.name: Gyeongtae Yoo, Sanghyeok Park, Soohyuk Jang, Ik-hwan Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes a rollout-level advantage-prioritized experience replay buffer for GRPO that stores and samples individual rollouts (rather than whole groups), bounding staleness via age eviction and preserving on-policy data through fresh-anchored composition. It improves sample efficiency in RLVR post-training of reasoning LLMs.

entry.title: Description-Code Inconsistency in Real-world MCP Servers: Measurement, Detection, and Security Implications

author.name: Yutao Shi, Xiaohan Zhang, Xiangjing Zhang, Xihua Shen, Hui Ouyang, Huming Qiu, Mi Zhang, Min Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies Description-Code Inconsistency in real-world MCP servers, where tool descriptions do not match underlying implementations, posing security risks. It formally defines the problem and provides measurement, detection, and security analysis.

entry.title: 'Your AI Text is not Mine': Redefining and Evaluating AI-generated Text Detection under Realistic Assumptions

author.name: Nils Dycke, Marina Sakharova, Nico Daheim, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: This paper systematically redefines notions of AI-generated text and harmful use, then introduces AITDNA, a benchmark of human-machine co-constructed texts annotated with full edit and AI-interaction histories. It benchmarks detectors under more realistic co-authorship assumptions.

entry.title: Audio Interaction Model

author.name: Zhifei Xie, Zihang Liu, Ze An, Xiaobin Hu, Yue Liao, Ziyang Ma, Dongchao Yang, Mingbao Lin, Deheng Ye, Shuicheng Yan, Chunyan Miao

entry.summary: This work formalizes the Audio Interaction Model, a unified online Large Audio Language Model with an always-on perceive-decide-respond loop that listens to sound, environment, and instructions in real time. Audio-Interaction retains offline task execution while adding streaming general audio instruction following and full voice chatting via a SoundFlow component.

entry.title: Streaming Communication in Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Zhen Yang, Xiaogang Xu, Wen Wang, Cong Chen, Xander Xu, Ying-Cong Chen

entry.summary: StreamMA is a multi-agent reasoning system that streams each reasoning step to downstream agents immediately, pipelining adjacent agents to reduce latency. It also improves quality because reliable early reasoning steps prevent error-prone late steps from misleading downstream agents, supported by a closed-form analysis of stream, serial, and single protocols.

entry.title: Self-Distilled Policy Gradient

author.name: Yifeng Liu, Shiyuan Zhang, Yifan Zhang, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Self-Distilled Policy Gradient (SDPG) uses on-policy self-distillation, where a model conditions on privileged context to supervise its own generations, as a dense supervision source for sparse-reward RL. It combines group-relative verifier advantages, full-vocabulary on-policy self-distillation, and reference-policy KL regularization, improving stability over RLVR baselines.

entry.title: Covert Influence Between Language Models

author.name: Avidan Shah, Jay Chooi, Jinghua Ou, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Characterizes covert influence between language models, where a sender's behavioral disposition transfers to a receiver through human-undetectable carriers across fine-tuning, distillation, and in-context learning. It uses inference-time attribution to select amplifying carriers, achieving payload transfers prior work could not.

entry.title: veriFIRE: an Industrial Case Study in Verifying Consistency Properties for a DNN-Based Wildfire Detection System

author.name: Idan Refaeli, Maya Swisa, Itay Buchnik, Alon Zada, Guy Amir, Elad Mandelbaum, Ziv Freund, Guy Katz

entry.summary: veriFIRE applies formal neural network verification to an airborne wildfire detection system, encoding consistency properties like confidence monotonicity and bounded response to blur into solver-compatible queries. It is a rare industry-academia case study of verification on a safety-critical deployed DNN.

entry.title: Optimizing the Cost-Quality Tradeoff of Agentic Theorem Provers in Lean

author.name: K\'ari R\"ognvaldsson, Chenhao Sun, Jasper Dekoninck, Martin Vechev

entry.summary: This paper introduces an action-routing agent for Lean theorem proving that uses a control plane to estimate success likelihood and cost, optimizing the compute-quality tradeoff. It reduces wasted compute on failing proof attempts.

entry.title: Probing Outcome-Level Resemblance and Mechanism-Level Alignment in LLM Risk Decisions: Evidence from the St. Petersburg Game

author.name: Chensong Huang, Changyu Chen, Chenwei Lin, Hanjia Lyu, Xian Xu, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: This paper uses the St. Petersburg game to distinguish whether LLMs' cautious risk decisions reflect human-like mechanisms or surface resemblance, testing 28 models across controlled variants. It separates outcome-level resemblance from mechanism-level alignment.

entry.title: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions

author.name: Aliakbar Mehdizadeh, Martin Hilbert

entry.summary: This study runs 432 networked Naming Game simulations to examine how memory depth and network topology jointly shape consensus among LLM agents. It finds longer memory speeds settling in centralized networks but slows it in decentralized ones, sometimes locking in fragmented plateaus.

entry.title: CleanCodec: Efficient and Robust Speech Tokenization via Perceptually Guided Encoding

author.name: Eugene Kwek, Feng Liu, Rui Zhang, Wenpeng Yin

entry.summary: CleanCodec reframes audio tokenization as a selective information bottleneck, encoding only perceptually important features and discarding noise and artifacts. At 12.5 tokens per second it achieves state-of-the-art tokenization efficiency.

entry.title: NextMotionQA: Benchmarking and Judging Human Motion Understanding with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yong Cao, Chuqiao Li, Xianghui Xie, Gerard Pons-Moll, Andreas Geiger

entry.summary: NextMotionQA is a semi-automated, expert-verified benchmark for human motion understanding with VLMs, spanning multiple-choice QA, captioning, and fine-grained error correction across three semantic axes and difficulty levels. It targets diagnostic granularity missing in prior motion benchmarks.

entry.title: UniCanvas: A Diffusion-base Unified Model for Text-in-Image Joint Generation

author.name: Zeyuan Yang, Hao-Wei Chen, Xueyang Yu, Yuncong Yang, Haoyu Zhen, Ziqiao Ma, Maohao Shen, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: UniCanvas is a unified diffusion-based model for interleaved text-in-image joint generation, embedding language within visual representations so a single model handles both photorealistic visuals and coherent text. It addresses the long-standing difficulty diffusion models have generating legible text.

entry.title: Impostor: An Agent-Curated Benchmark for Realistic AIGC Manipulation Localization

author.name: Zhenliang Li (Southeast University), Yutao Hu (Southeast University), Qixiong Wang (Xiaohongshu Inc), Wenpeng Du (Southeast University), Hongxiang Jiang (Xiaohongshu Inc), Jiasong Wu (Southeast University), Xiaolong Jiang (Xiaohongshu Inc), Jungong Han (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: Impostor is a 100K-image AI-edited manipulation localization dataset built by CraftAgent, a closed-loop agent that performs scene perception, editing planning, execution, validation, and reflection. It addresses limitations in realism, manipulation diversity, and generator coverage in existing IMDL benchmarks.

entry.title: MAOAM: Unified Object and Material Selection with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jaden Park, Valentin Deschaintre, Jason Kuen, Kangning Liu, Iliyan Georgiev, Krishna Kumar Singh, Yong Jae Lee, Michael Fischer

entry.summary: MAOAM is a unified VLM-based selection framework supporting both object and material-level selection via text or click interactions for interactive image editing. It extends beyond object-centric, single-modality selection methods used in current tools.

entry.title: CIPER: A Unified Framework for Cross-view Image-retrieval and Pose-estimation

author.name: Yurim Jeon, Dongseong Seo, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: CIPER unifies cross-view image retrieval and 3-DoF pose estimation for geo-localization in a single transformer, enabling both city-scale search and precise localization. It avoids the error propagation of naively cascading retrieval and pose pipelines.

entry.title: D$^3$-MoE:Dual Disentangled Diffusion Mixture-of-Experts for Style-Controllable End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Renju Feng, Rukang Wang, Ning Xi, Jianguo Yu, Liping Lu, Pan Zhou, Duanfeng Chu

entry.summary: D3-MoE is a dual disentangled diffusion mixture-of-experts framework for style-controllable end-to-end autonomous driving that addresses the style-averaging problem from high-variance human demonstrations. It disentangles trajectory modeling along behavioral (style-conditioned generation vs selection) and physical (longitudinal/lateral) axes.

entry.title: The next chapter in flood resilience: Open sourcing Google’s hydrology framework

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google announces the open-sourcing of its hydrology framework as part of its flood resilience work, making climate and sustainability modeling tools more broadly accessible. The post highlights advancing flood forecasting through openly available infrastructure.

entry.title: Beyond Prompt-Based Planning: MCP-Native Graph Planning-based Biomedical Agent System

author.name: Zhangtianyi Chen, Florensia Widjaja, Wufei Dai, Xiangjun Zhang, Yuhao Shen, Juexiao Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces BioManus, an MCP-native biomedical agent using graph-scaffolded planning over structured biological capabilities, with a compiler converting heterogeneous bioinformatics tools into standardized MCP servers. It addresses tool confusion and unstable planning at scale.

entry.title: LLM Compression with Jointly Optimizing Architectural and Quantization choices

author.name: Hoang-Loc La, Truong-Thanh Le, Amir Taherkordi, Phuong Hoai Ha

entry.summary: Introduces a differentiable neural architecture search framework that jointly optimizes architectural configurations and mixed-precision quantization for LLM linear layers over the full search space. It improves on prior NAS that restricted the space and decoupled architecture from quantization.

entry.title: POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories

author.name: Rishanth Rajendhran, Jenna Russell, Mohit Iyyer, John Frederick Wieting

entry.summary: Presents POLARIS, a lower-compute GRPO recipe for long-form creative writing in small models, using a frontier LLM judge with a story-quality rubric as online reward plus human-reference injection as a high-reward anchor. Applied to Qwen3.5-9B, it improves long-story length and quality.

entry.title: Geometry-Preserving Unsupervised Alignment for Heterogeneous Foundation Models

author.name: Shuwen Yu, Zhanxuan Hu, Yi Zhao, Yonghang Tai, Huafeng Li

entry.summary: GPUA learns an orthogonal mapping that translates vision-only foundation model features into the vision-language semantic space, treating VFM features as a visual language inspired by cross-lingual alignment. It integrates the complementary geometric and semantic strengths of VFMs and VLMs without labels.

entry.title: DSA: Dynamic Step Allocation for Fast Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Thanh-Tung Le, Yunhan Zhao, Menglei Chai, Zhengyang Shen, Zhe Cao, Danhang Tang, Xiaohui Xie, Deying Kong

entry.summary: DSA is a confidence-guided adaptive computation framework for autoregressive video diffusion that dynamically adjusts the number of denoising steps per frame using a lightweight confidence head trained with distribution-matching distillation. It avoids wasting compute on predictable frames.

entry.title: ChannelTok: Efficient Flexible-Length Vision Tokenization

author.name: Sukriti Paul, Arpit Bansal, Tom Goldstein

entry.summary: ChannelTok is a lightweight channel-wise flexible-length vision tokenizer that treats each latent channel as a token, using stochastic tail-dropping to organize channels by semantic importance for flexible compression. It departs from parameter-heavy spatial-token tokenizers with a fast CNN-Transformer hybrid.

entry.title: MeshWeaver: Sparse-Voxel-Guided Surface Weaving for Autoregressive Mesh Generation

author.name: Jiale Xu, Wang Zhao, Ying Shan

entry.summary: MeshWeaver is an autoregressive mesh generation framework that treats generation as surface weaving, predicting the next vertex with geometric context from a multi-level sparse-voxel encoder. It addresses low tokenization efficiency and lack of local geometry-aware guidance in prior AR mesh methods.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Next-Best-View Optimization for Risk-Averse Planning

author.name: Amirhossein Mollaei Khass, Vivek Pandey, Guangyi Liu, Athanasios Cosse, Emrah Bayrak, Nader Motee

entry.summary: This work proposes a distributed, risk-aware multi-agent next-best-view framework where each robot maintains a private local 3D Gaussian Splatting map and the team maximizes expected information gain along trajectories via Consensus ADMM. Robots exchange only viewpoints, trajectory descriptors, and scalar gains, improving scalability over centralized methods.

entry.title: Generalization of World Models under Environmental Variability for Vision-based Quadrotor Navigation

author.name: Luca Zanatta, Grzegorz Malczyk, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: This work systematically studies the robustness of DreamerV3-based world models to environmental variability for vision-based quadrotor navigation, training under varying randomness levels and evaluating with cross-environment validation. It deploys models and policies on a real quadrotor including open-loop runs to assess real-world generalization.

entry.title: SMAC-Talk: A Natural Language Extension of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge for Large Language Models

author.name: Joel Sol, Homayoun Najjaran

entry.summary: Introduces SMAC-Talk, a natural-language extension of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge for evaluating LLM coordination, communication, and trust under partial observability. It provides scenarios probing decentralized cooperation and long-horizon decision making.

entry.title: Not All Errors Are Equal: Consequence-Aware Reasoning Compute Allocation

author.name: Jingbo Wen, Liang He, Ziqi He

entry.summary: Proposes consequence-aware test-time compute allocation, routing reasoning compute by the real-world cost of failures rather than only predicted difficulty. It argues accuracy-equal objectives wrongly treat all errors as equally costly.

entry.title: MapAgent: An Industrial-Grade Agentic Framework for City-scale Lane-level Map Generation

author.name: Deguo Xia, Zihan Li, Haochen Zhao, Dong Xie, Yuyao Kong, Xiyan Liu, Jizhou Huang, Mengmeng Yang, Diange Yang

entry.summary: Presents MapAgent, an industrial-grade agentic architecture that augments vectorized mapping with explicit specifications and traffic regulations for city-scale lane-level map generation. It reduces specification violations that drive costly human post-editing in autonomous driving maps.

entry.title: BiNSGPS: Geometry Problem Solving via Bidirectional Neuro-Symbolic Interaction

author.name: Qi Wang, Peijie Wang, Fei Yin, Cheng-Lin Liu
