entry.summary: Proposes BiNSGPS, a bidirectional neuro-symbolic framework for geometry problem solving where an MLLM adviser and symbolic solver exchange feedback to rectify formal representations. It breaks the brittle unidirectional pipeline of prior hybrids.

entry.title: BiasGRPO: Stabilizing Bias Mitigation in High-Variance Reward Landscapes via Group-Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Saket Reddy, Ke Yang, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: Proposes BiasGRPO, applying Group Relative Policy Optimization to stabilize social-bias mitigation in the high-variance, subjective reward landscape where bias lacks ground truth. It avoids DPO's exploration limits and PPO's critic instability via group-relative baselines.

entry.title: Position: Deployed Reinforcement Learning should be Continual

author.name: Parnian Behdin, Kevin Roice, Golnaz Mesbahi

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that deployed reinforcement learning is inherently a continual RL problem, identifying four sources of post-deployment non-stationarity that necessitate never-ending learning. It draws on real-world examples to argue the best deployed agents never stop adapting.

entry.title: Beyond Static Priors: Dynamic Neural Guidance for Large-Scale Ant Colony Optimization

author.name: Dat Thanh Tran, Van Khu Vu, Yining Ma

entry.summary: Proposes DyNACO, which achieves dynamic neural guidance for ant colony optimization by periodically observing pheromone distribution and incumbent solutions, paired with a perturbation backend and scope-restricted refinement. It scales to 100,000-node TSP instances and outperforms neural baselines.

entry.title: A Goal-Set Characterization of Task Composition in the Boolean Task Algebra

author.name: Eduardo Terr\'es-Caballero, Herke van Hoof

entry.summary: Revisits the Boolean Task Algebra, formalizing a collapse where in deterministic MDPs every optimal extended Q-function is determined by the universal and empty tasks, making the logarithmic base-task set redundant. It introduces a goal-set composition method reducing learning costs.

entry.title: EvalStop: Using World Feedback to Detect and Correct Reward Overoptimization in Multi-Tenant RLHF Platforms

author.name: Guilin Zhang, Chuanyi Sun, Shahryar Sarkani, John M. Fossaceca

entry.summary: Proposes EvalStop, a scheduling primitive for multi-tenant RLHF platforms that terminates fine-tuning jobs after consecutive evaluation-score drops to detect reward overoptimization, freeing shared GPUs without human monitoring. It leverages downstream world-feedback signals rather than weaker training-loss proxies.

entry.title: A Systematic Analysis of Linguistic Features in AI-Generated Text Detection Across Domains and Models

author.name: Yassir El Attar, Esra D\"onmez, Maximilian Maurer, Agnieszka Falenska

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale empirical study of 284 interpretable linguistic features across 27 LLMs and ten domains to assess robustness of signals for detecting AI-generated text under cross-model and cross-domain settings. It finds linguistic-feature classifiers can reliably distinguish AI from human text but with caveats.

entry.title: Notarized Agents: Receiver-Attested Confidential Receipts for AI Agent Actions

author.name: Juan Figuera

entry.summary: Proposes Notarized Agents, a class of protocols (instantiated as Sello) inverting the trust boundary so the service receiving an agent's call signs an encrypted receipt published to a public transparency log, giving owners tamper-evident trails without trusting the agent or operator. It addresses self-logging integrity in agent observability.

entry.title: Recover-LoRA for Aggressive Quantization: Reclaiming Accuracy in 2-Bit Language Models via Low-Rank Adaptation with Knowledge Distillation on Synthetic Data

author.name: Devleena Das, Rajeev Patwari, Elliott Delaye, Ashish Sirasao

entry.summary: Extends Recover-LoRA to ultra-low-bit (2-bit) quantization using a selective mixed-precision strategy quantizing only MLP gate and up-projection layers, combined with knowledge distillation on synthetic data to recover accuracy. It targets edge and on-device LLM deployment.

entry.title: Scaling Novel Graph Generation via Lightweight Structure-Guided Autoregressive Models

author.name: Alessio Barboni, Massimiliano Lupo Pasini, Bishal Lakha, Edoardo Serra

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight autoregressive graph generation framework using structure-guided topological ordering to serialize graphs into regular edge sequences for near log-linear generation, plus two-phase training to promote novelty beyond imitating training graphs. It targets scalability and novelty limitations of diffusion and quadratic autoregressive methods.

entry.title: Multi-Granularity 3D Kidney Lesion Characterization from CT Volumes

author.name: Renjie Liang, Zhengkang Fan, Jinqian Pan, Chenkun Sun, Jiang Bian, Russell Terry, Jie Xu

entry.summary: Reformulates kidney CT characterization as a per-lesion set-prediction task, introducing LesionDETR, a DETR-style architecture with size-distance Hungarian matching and hierarchical loss that emits variable numbers of lesions with four clinical attributes. It uses a curated dataset plus zero-shot external validation on KiTS23.

entry.title: L-TGVN: Leveraging Longitudinal Priors for Personalized Rapid MRI

author.name: Arda Atal{\i}k, Sumit Chopra, Daniel K. Sodickson

entry.summary: Introduces L-TGVN, a longitudinal total-generalized-variation network for personalized rapid MRI that leverages a patient's most recent prior scan as subject-specific context to reconstruct under-sampled follow-up exams, handling temporal changes, misalignment, and protocol drift. It targets faster, lower-cost MRI without quality loss.

entry.title: MemoryDocDataSet: A Benchmark for Joint Conversational Memory and Long Document Reasoning

author.name: Qiyang Xie, Jialun Wu, Xinjie He, Su Liu, Shuai Xiao, Zhiyuan Lin, Weikai Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces MemoryDocDataSet, a synthetic benchmark of 50 micro-worlds and 1,000 QA pairs jointly evaluating multi-session conversational memory navigation and deep long-document reading comprehension, with hybrid questions requiring both capabilities over real long legal documents. No prior benchmark evaluated both simultaneously.

entry.title: SePO: Self-Evolving Prompt Agent for System Prompt Optimization

author.name: Wangcheng Tao, Han Wu, Weng-Fai Wong

entry.summary: Proposes SePO, a self-evolving prompt agent for system prompt optimization that treats the prompt agent's own system prompt as an optimization target alongside task agents' prompts via open-ended evolutionary search with a candidate archive. It removes the fixed hand-engineered prompt-agent design of prior methods.

entry.title: Adaptive Calibration for Fair and Performant Facial Recognition

author.name: Ryan Brown, Chris Russell

entry.summary: Introduces Adaptive Calibration, a calibration strategy for facial recognition that maps cosine similarity to well-calibrated probabilities using local context, correcting a mismatch where the same distance yields different match probabilities across embedding regions. It improves both accuracy and fairness without demographic metadata.

entry.title: GeoMin: Data-Efficient Semi-Supervised RLVR via Geometric Distribution Modeling

author.name: Guangcheng Zhu, Shenzhi Yang, Haobo Wang, Xing Zheng, Yingfan MA, Xuening Feng, Zhongqi Chen, Kai Tang, Zhengqing Zang, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes GeoMin, a data-efficient semi-supervised RLVR method that models global feature distributions on labeled data to decode structural discrepancies between correct and incorrect responses, addressing the data-efficiency bottleneck of methods relying on coarse performance heuristics. It improves utilization of unlabeled instances while avoiding model collapse.

entry.title: Dynamic Infilling Anchors for Format-Constrained Generation in Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Boyan Han, Yiwei Wang, Yi Song, Yujun Cai, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes tracing metacognitive pivots for efficient RLVR, investigating the pick-in-the-dark setup that selects beneficial unlabeled samples without prior supervision, bridging data selection (which needs labeled pools) and unsupervised RLVR (which underperforms). It aims for data-efficient reasoning model training.

entry.title: VISTA: Vision-Grounded and Physics-Validated Adaptation of UMI data for VLA Training

author.name: Siyuan Yang, Linzheng Guo, Ouyang Lu, Zhaxizhuoma, Daoran Zhang, Xinmiao Wang, Ting Xiao, Fangzheng Yan, Zhijun Chen, Yan Ding, Chao Yu, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: VISTA bridges the gap between scalable UMI robot data collection and VLA model training by addressing fisheye-view distribution mismatch and physically infeasible human trajectories. It uses vision-grounded and physics-validated adaptation including a large UMI-VQA dataset.

entry.title: Trace-Mediated Peak Bias: Bridging Temporal Credit Assignment and Cognitive Heuristics in Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Viktor Vesel\'y, Aleksandar Todorov, Erwan Escudie, Matthia Sabatelli

entry.summary: This paper identifies Trace-Mediated Peak Bias, a failure mode in deep RL where intermediate eligibility-trace depths cause agents to prefer high-reward-peak trajectories over higher-return ones. It links this to the cognitive Peak-End Rule via gradient shocks from distal TD errors.

entry.title: NoRA: Evaluating Grounded Reasonableness in Visual First-person Normative Action Reasoning

author.name: Sichao Li, Sai Ma, Daniel Kilov, Secil Yanik Guyot, Zhuang Li, Seth Lazar

entry.summary: NoRA is a visual first-person video benchmark for grounded normative action reasoning, requiring models to generate candidate next actions and justify them via explicit fact-reason-action support graphs. It argues that menu-based or text-only normative evaluations are insufficient for agents acting in social environments.

entry.title: Provably Auditable and Safe LLM Agents from Human-Authored Ontologies

author.name: Aaron Sterling

entry.summary: Agentic Redux is an LLM agent architecture using typed lambda calculus to prove that executions on appropriate domains are semantically correct with all decisions in an append-only ledger. It introduces Ontology-First Agent Design and demonstrates production domains in healthcare billing and security disclosure.

entry.title: Invariant Gradient Alignment for Robust Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: Invariant Gradient Alignment trains models to align gradient updates across logically isomorphic but semantically diverse examples, combating shortcut learning that breaks on out-of-distribution reasoning. It uses logical isomer sets and a continuous gradient conflict mask to improve robust reasoning distillation.

entry.title: Novel Aspects of IEEE SA P3109 Arithmetic Formats for Machine Learning

author.name: Andrew Fitzgibbon, Christoph M. Wintersteiger, Jeffrey Sarnoff

entry.summary: This paper describes novel aspects of the IEEE P3109 draft standard defining parameterized binary floating-point formats for machine learning, with formats parameterized over width, precision, signedness, and infinities. It details rounding, saturation, and explicit NaN/infinity handling via decoding to extended reals.

entry.title: Derivative Informed Learning of Exchange-Correlation Functionals

author.name: Eike S. Eberhard, Luca A. Thiede, Abdul Aldossary, Andreas Burger, Nicholas Gao, Vignesh Bhethanabotla, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: This paper introduces Derivative Informed XC-Loss for machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals, supervising first and second energy derivatives on the Grassmannian of density matrices to better distill from hybrid functionals like B3LYP. It aims to make O(N^3) ML-XC functionals competitive with O(N^4) hybrids.

entry.title: Sequential Data Poisoning in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Jack Sanderson, Yihan Wang, Xiaoqian Lu, Gautam Kamath, Yiwei Lu

entry.summary: Introduces a sequential data poisoning threat model where multiple adversaries separately poison SFT and preference datasets across LLM post-training stages. It reveals a single-attacker illusion where each attacker seems negligible alone but combined effects are significant.

entry.title: Deliberate Evolution: Agentic Reasoning for Sample-Efficient Symbolic Regression with LLMs

author.name: Xinyu Pang, Zhanke Zhou, Xuan Li, Fangrui Lv, Shanshan Wei, Sen Cui, Bo Han, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Deliberate Evolution is an agentic LLM framework for symbolic regression that decouples expression proposal from search control using adaptive operators, structural diagnosis tools, and reflective memory. It improves sample efficiency over methods relying solely on scalar MSE feedback.

entry.title: Flatness and Generalization: Learning Multi-Index Models with Homogeneous Neural Networks

author.name: Harsh Vardhan, Hossein Taheri, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: This theoretical paper establishes a connection between flatness and generalization for learning multi-index models with two-layer homogeneous neural networks, addressing prior critiques that flatness is rescaling-invariant and vacuous. It shows when flatness genuinely predicts generalization.

entry.title: D^2SD: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Dual Diffusion Draft Models

author.name: Liyuan Zhang, Jiarui Zhang, Jinwei Yao, Ran Yan, Yuchen Yang, Jiahao Zhang, Tongkai Yang, Yi Wu, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: D2SD accelerates speculative decoding by using dual diffusion draft models that organize multiple draft candidate sequences efficiently rather than committing to one, raising acceptance rates without redundant branch costs. It speeds up autoregressive LLM inference.

entry.title: Cartridges at Scale: Training Modular KV Caches over Large Document Collections

author.name: Momchil Hardalov, Gonzalo Iglesias, Adri\`a de Gispert

entry.summary: Cartridges at Scale is a training framework that distills large document collections into multiple composable KV caches with dynamic distractor mixing and a memory-efficient budget manager, fixing the failure of naively mixing isolated cartridges. It eliminates wasteful long-context prefilling while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Rethinking Continual Experience Internalization for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Jingwen Chen, Wenkai Yang, Shengda Fan, Wenbo Nie, Chenxing Sun, Shaodong Zheng, Yangen Hu, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: This work studies multi-iteration experience internalization in self-evolving LLM agents and finds existing methods cause progressive capability collapse rather than compounding gains. It identifies that principle-level experience is more durable than instance-level, informing continual agent learning.

entry.title: A General Framework for Dynamic Consistent Submodular Maximization

author.name: Paul D\"utting, Federico Fusco, Silvio Lattanzi, Ashkan Norouzi-Fard, Ola Svensson, Morteza Zadimoghaddam

entry.summary: This paper presents a general framework for dynamic consistent submodular maximization in the fully dynamic setting with both insertions and deletions, achieving the first constant-factor approximations with sublinear consistency. It extends prior insertion-only results.

entry.title: When Retrieval Doesn't Help: A Large-Scale Study of Biomedical RAG

author.name: Erfan Nourbakhsh, Rocky Slavin, Ke Yang, Anthony Rios

entry.summary: This large-scale study revisits whether retrieval-augmented generation helps biomedical question answering across five models (7B-72B), ten datasets, four retrievers, and four corpora, finding only small inconsistent gains. It shows backbone model choice matters far more than retriever or corpus.

entry.title: Off-Distribution Voices: Fanfiction Subgenres as Universal Vernacular Jailbreaks for Aligned LLMs

author.name: Zhongze Luo, Ruihe Shi, Zhenshuai Yin, Haoyue Liu, Weixuan Wan, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a jailbreak family that uses real Archive of Our Own fanfiction subgenres as universal attack carriers, embedding harmful behaviors as scene climaxes without any attacker LLM or per-target adaptation. It argues the real failure mode is an entire under-covered register of human writing rather than specific prompts.

entry.title: PersonaTree: Structured Lifecycle Memory for Person Understanding in LLM Agents

author.name: Yubo Hou, Jingwei Song, Hongbo Zhang, Zhisheng Chen, Bang Xiao, Tao Wan, Zengchang Qin

entry.summary: PersonaTree presents a structured lifecycle memory framework that abstracts interaction evidence into a three-level persona tree with explicit evidence-to-claim paths. It frames person understanding as schema formation for persistent LLM agents.

entry.title: Prospective Dynamic 3D MRI Reconstruction via Latent-Space Motion Tracking from Single Measurement

author.name: Lixuan Chen, Zhongnan Liu, Jesse Hamilton, James M. Balter, Jeong Joon Park, Liyue Shen

entry.summary: PDMR enables prospective dynamic 3D MRI reconstruction by learning a low-dimensional latent manifold of motion fields offline for rapid online adaptation under ultra-sparse sampling. It targets latency-critical applications like MRI-guided radiotherapy.

entry.title: FindIt: A Format-Informed Visual Detection Benchmark for Generalist Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Eshika Khandelwal, Jingjing Pan, Mingfang Zhang, Quan Kong, Lorenzo Garattoni, Hilde Kuehne

entry.summary: FindIt is a benchmark evaluating the promptable localization abilities of generalist MLLMs across object detection and related structured vision tasks, addressing the lack of standardized localization evaluation. It covers four core task categories with format-informed prompting.

entry.title: 4D Reconstruction from Sparse Dynamic Cameras

author.name: Kazuki Ozeki, Shun Kenney, Yuto Shibata, Eisuke Takeuchi, Takuya Narihira, Kazumi Fukuda, Ryosuke Sawata, Yuki Mitsufuji, Yoshimitsu Aoki

entry.summary: This paper studies 4D reconstruction from a sparse set of independently moving cameras, a practical middle ground between monocular (depth-ambiguous) and dense fixed-camera setups. It proposes a method resolving spatiotemporal inconsistencies across views and time that naive extensions fail to handle.

entry.title: StrokeTimer: Robust Representation Learning for Ischemic Stroke Onset-Time Estimation from Non-contrast CT

author.name: Weiru Wang, Susanne G. H. Olthuis, Elizaveta Lavrova, Robert J. van Oostenbrugge, Charles B. L. M. Majoie, Wim H. van Zwam, Ruisheng Su

entry.summary: StrokeTimer is an automated framework estimating ischemic stroke onset time from non-contrast CT using self-supervised disentanglement and energy-guided contrastive learning, handling class imbalance and scanner heterogeneity. Accurate onset-time estimation is critical for reperfusion-therapy eligibility.

entry.title: Recent Advances and Trends in Learning-based 3D Representations

author.name: Adrien Schockaert, Hamid Laga, Hazem Wannous, Vincent Magnier, Guillaume Dufaye, Jean-fran\c{c}ois Witz

entry.summary: This is a survey reviewing recent advances in learning-based 3D representations, from traditional meshes and point clouds to neural and primitive-based methods like 3D Gaussian Splatting. It guides design choices across reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, and generation tasks.

entry.title: InstantRetouch: Efficient and High-Fidelity Instruction-Guided Image Retouching with Bilateral Space

author.name: Jiarui Wu, Yujin Wang, Ruikang Li, Fan Zhang, Mingde Yao, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: InstantRetouch performs efficient, high-fidelity instruction-guided image retouching by predicting a low-resolution bilateral grid of affine transforms rather than editing pixels or latents directly. This compact, content-decoupled approach achieves both fidelity and speed over diffusion-based retouching.

entry.title: CoPark: Learning Reactive Parking via Self-Play

author.name: Jiarong Wei, Yanxing Chen, Sinuo Song, Yin Wu, Anna Rehr, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: CoPark uses multi-agent self-play reinforcement learning with a residual-policy architecture to learn reactive autonomous parking that balances high geometric precision with safe interaction among vehicles. An offline plan provides an action prior while a residual policy handles reactive deviations.

entry.title: BPDA-GMM: Bayesian Probabilistic Data Association via Gaussian Mixture Models for Semantic SLAM

author.name: Thanh Nguyen Canh, Haolan Zhang, Xiem HoangVan, Antonio Sgorbissa, Nak Young Chong

entry.summary: BPDA-GMM is an online Bayesian probabilistic data association framework for semantic SLAM that uses a Dirichlet-process/Chinese Restaurant Process prior to handle a growing object-level map without fixed landmark sets or hand-tuned null-hypothesis weights. Accumulated evidence favors existing landmarks while the concentration parameter assigns mass to new ones.

entry.title: When Freshness Is Not Enough: Distribution-Aware Age of Information for Networked LQR Control

author.name: Abdullah Y. Etcibasi, C. Emre Koksal, Eylem Ekici

entry.summary: This paper questions whether minimizing mean Age of Information is actually optimal for networked control, deriving that for scalar LTI systems with delayed intermittent updates the LQR tracking problem reduces to optimizing the distribution of inter-scheduling intervals. It shows freshness alone is insufficient and provides a control-theoretic distribution-aware reformulation.

entry.title: StepPRM-RTL: Stepwise Process-Reward Guided LLM Fine-Tuning for Enhanced RTL Synthesis

author.name: Prashanth Vijayaraghavan, Apoorva Nitsure, Luyao Shi, Ehsan Degan, Vandana Mukherjee

entry.summary: Presents StepPRM-RTL, combining stepwise trajectory modeling, process-reward modeling, and retrieval-augmented fine-tuning to improve LLM-based RTL hardware code generation. It provides dense intermediate feedback to raise functional correctness in Verilog and VHDL.

entry.title: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval

author.name: Jiaxi Li, Ke Deng, Yun Wang, Jingyuan Huang, Yucheng Shi, Qiaoyu Tan, Jin Lu, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval for web agents, retrieving skills based on current webpage state rather than only the initial task instruction. This addresses the mismatch between static task-level skill reuse and dynamic web execution.

entry.title: Simulate, Reason, Decide: Scientific Reasoning with LLMs for Simulation-Driven Decision Making

author.name: Yuhan Yang, Ruipu Li, Alexander Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Introduces MechSim, a mechanism-grounded neuro-symbolic reasoning framework that treats scientific simulators as structured mechanistic systems to reason about, rather than black-box interfaces. It aims to improve transparency and auditability in simulation-driven decision making.

entry.title: Beyond Objective Equivalence: Constraint Injection for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling on Vehicle Routing Problems

author.name: Xizi Luo, Changhong He, Dongdong Geng, Chenggong Shi, Yu Mei

entry.summary: Proposes constraint injection for LLM-based optimization modeling, using feasible and one-constraint-violating probes to expose spurious over-constraint and silent omission that objective-equivalence testing misses. It forms a dual verifier evaluated on vehicle routing problems.

entry.title: Counterfactual Explanations for Deep Two-Sample Testing

author.name: Wei-Cheng Lai, Marco Simnacher, Christoph Lippert

entry.summary: Proposes a counterfactual explanation framework for deep two-sample testing that generates sample-level edits moving observations toward a target group while reducing the measured discrepancy. It combines a diffusion autoencoder to reveal which features drive null rejection.

entry.title: Dive into the Scene: Breaking the Perceptual Bottleneck in Vision-Language Decision Making via Focus Plan Generation

author.name: Boyuan Xiao, Bohong Chen, Yumeng Li, Ji Feng, Yao-Xiang Ding, Kun Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Focus Plan Generation to break the perceptual bottleneck in embodied vision-language decision making, where visual hallucinations arise from failing to separate task-relevant objects from distractors. It argues one-step focus is ineffective and offers a more structured focusing approach.

entry.title: Selective Coupling of Decoupled Informative Regions: Masked Attention Alignment for Data-Free Quantization of Vision Transformers

author.name: Biao Qian, Yang Wang, Yong Wu, Jungong Han

entry.summary: Proposes MaskAQ, a Masked Attention Alignment approach for data-free quantization of Vision Transformers, revealing that self-attention semantics localize to a sparse subset of patches and aligning synthetic samples accordingly to reduce distribution mismatch. It improves DFQ performance without accessing real data.

entry.title: Evaluating Reasoning Fidelity in Visual Text Generation

author.name: Jiajun Hong, Jiawei Zhou

entry.summary: Evaluates reasoning fidelity in visual text generation, testing whether text-to-image models faithfully preserve reasoning when complete solutions must be expressed as rendered text across long text rendering, factual probing, context understanding, and multi-step reasoning. It finds current T2I models frequently produce semantic errors despite legible text.

entry.title: Activation Steering of Video Generation Models via Reduced-Order Linear Optimal Control

author.name: Jihoon Hong, Alice Chan, Qiyue Dai, Julian Skifstad, Glen Chou

entry.summary: LA-LQR applies reduced-order linear-quadratic optimal control to activation steering of text-to-video models, computing closed-loop feedback interventions to reduce harmful content while preserving quality. It improves over coarse non-anticipative steering that causes oversteering.

entry.title: M$^3$Eval: Multi-Modal Memory Evaluation through Cognitively-Grounded Video Tasks

author.name: Jie Huang, Ruixun Liu, Sirui Sun, Xinyi Yang, Yin Li, Yixin Zhu, Yiwu Zhong

entry.summary: M3Eval is a cognitively-grounded benchmark and framework for evaluating memory in multimodal video models, isolating what models retain, how faithfully information is preserved, and robustness under interference. It addresses the gap that existing video benchmarks focus on perception and reasoning rather than memory.

entry.title: MusaCoder: Native GPU Kernel Generation with Full-Stack Training on Moore Threads GPU

author.name: Kun Cheng, Songshuo Lu, Sicong Liao, Tankun Li, Yafei Zhang, Dong Yang, Qiheng Lv, Hua Wang, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: MusaCoder is a full-stack training framework for native GPU kernel generation on CUDA and MUSA backends combining data synthesis, rejection fine-tuning, and execution-feedback RL with stabilization techniques for sparse rewards and reward hacking. It improves LLM-generated efficient low-level kernels.

entry.title: Read the Trace, Steer the Path: Trajectory-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Anant Khandelwal, Manish Gupta

entry.summary: CAPR is a trajectory-aware reinforcement learning method for diffusion language models that exploits the denoising trace to provide tree-like supervision without tree-level compute, by caching and amortizing path refinement. It improves dLLM RL signal beyond flat single-reward rollouts.

entry.title: Can Crowdsourcing Survive the LLM Era? A Community Survey on Human Data Collection

author.name: Aswathy Velutharambath, Neele Falk, Sofie Labat, Tarun Tater, Amelie Wuehrl

entry.summary: This community survey of 155 NLP researchers examines how LLM use by crowdworkers threatens the validity of crowdsourced data. It finds 44% observed LLM usage and documents detection strategies and mitigation uncertainty.

entry.title: TaDA: Calibrated Probe Gating for Task-Domain LoRA Merging

author.name: Huy Quoc To, Fuyi Li, Guangyan Huang, Ming Liu

entry.summary: TaDA is a training-free method for merging task and domain LoRA adapters using calibrated per-layer gating, exploiting the observation that domain dominance increases with layer depth while shallow layers retain task signals. It enables asymmetric, structure-aware adapter merging.

entry.title: Imagine Before You Draw: Visual Prompt Engineering for Image Generation

author.name: Liyu Jia, Fengda Zhang, Jiachun Pan, Kesen Zhao, Saining Zhang, Wang Lin, Weijia Wu, Yue Liao, Aojun Zhou, Hanwang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes internal visual prompt engineering that generates a visual semantic plan before image generation within a single model, avoiding the information bottleneck of two-stage external pipelines. It improves detail preservation in downstream tasks like editing.

entry.title: Controllable Dynamic 3D Shape Generation via 3D Trajectories and Text

author.name: Jaeyeong Kim, Ines Kim, Jahyeok Koo, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: T2Mo is a feed-forward framework for controllable dynamic 3D shape generation conditioned on both 3D trajectories and text, using trajectories to resolve language ambiguity in motion. A shape-grounded trajectory embedding handles arbitrary dense-to-sparse trajectory inputs.

entry.title: TransTac: Visuo-Tactile Modality Transition via Ultraviolet-Encoded Transparent Elastomers

author.name: Lingyue Yang, Bin Fang

entry.summary: TransTac is a transparent UV-encoded binocular vision-based tactile sensor that integrates global visual observation with marker-based tactile reconstruction in a single compact device. It uses UV-reflective markers in transparent elastomer and prior-guided Delaunay stereo matching for robust contact geometry recovery.

entry.title: Real-World Deployment of a 5G-Connected Edge-Controlled Aerial Robot in Industrial Subterranean Mines

author.name: Achilleas Santi Seisa, Emanuele Pagliari, Gerasimos Damigos, Elias Small, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: This paper reports the first real-world autonomous flight of a 5G-connected aerial robot controlled by an edge-offloaded Model Predictive Controller in an active industrial subterranean mine. Communication uses 5G NR Standalone, with the edge MPC generating collision-free paths from human-selected waypoints.

entry.title: Neural Response to Familiar Names Predicts Outcome of Comatose ICU Patients: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Nature Communications study prospectively evaluates whether neural responses to familiar names can predict recovery outcomes in comatose ICU patients. It links EEG-measured brain responses to clinical prognosis in a cohort study.

entry.title: VAMPS: Visual-Assisted Mathematical Problem Solving Benchmark

author.name: Amirhossein Dabiriaghdam, Shayan Vassef, Mohammadreza Bakhtiari, Yasamin Medghalchi, Ilker Hacihaliloglu, Mesrob Ohannessian, Lele Wang, Giuseppe Carenini

entry.summary: Introduces VAMPS, a bilingual benchmark of 1,168 graph-assisted math problems testing whether multimodal LLMs can externalize problems via visualization tools and reason over the output. It exposes a performance gap when models rely on visual aids.

entry.title: AIP: A Graph Representation for Learning and Governing Agent Skills

author.name: Zachary Blumenfeld, Jim Webber

entry.summary: Introduces the Agent Instruction Protocol (AIP), modeling agent skills as directed execution graphs with typed input/output edges and schema-validated specifications instead of free-form prose. It aims to improve reliability and governability of agent skills.

entry.title: Strabo: Declarative Specification and Implementation of Agentic Interaction Protocols

author.name: Samuel H. Christie V, Amit K. Chopra, Munindar P. Singh

entry.summary: Presents Strabo, applying declarative interaction-protocol modeling (Langshaw/Peach) to Google's Universal Commerce Protocol for AI-agent e-commerce, demonstrating interoperability with UCP agents. It connects multiagent declarative protocol research to industry agentic standards.

entry.title: MimeLens: Position-Agnostic Content-Type Detection for Binary Fragments

author.name: Michael J. Bommarito II

entry.summary: Introduces MimeLens, small BERT-style encoders pretrained on byte windows sampled at random offsets to classify content type (125 MIME labels) from header-less binary fragments anywhere in a file. It addresses the failure of whole-file classifiers like Magika on packets, carved fragments, and disk blocks.

entry.title: DetectZoo: A Unified Toolkit for AI-Generated Content Detection Across Text, Audio, and Image Modalities

author.name: Sajad Ebrahimi, Nima Jamali, Bardia Shirsalimian, Kelly McConvey, Wentao Zhang, Jalehsadat Mahdavimoghaddam, Maksym Taranukhin, Maura Grossman, Vered Shwartz, Yuntian Deng, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: Introduces DetectZoo, an extensible unified toolkit standardizing the full empirical pipeline for AI-generated content detection across text, audio, and image modalities to enable fair comparison and reproducibility. It addresses fragmentation among incompatible existing detectors.

entry.title: MM-BizRAG: Rethinking Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for General Purpose Enterprise Q&A

author.name: Hanoz Bhathena, Parin Rajesh Jhaveri, Rohan Mittal, Prateek Singh, Aymen Kallala, Rachneet Kaur, Yiqiao Jin, Zhen Zeng, Adwait Ratnaparkhi, Denis Kochedykov

entry.summary: Proposes MM-BizRAG, a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation system for enterprise Q&A that explicitly extracts and represents document structure via orientation-specific ingestion and layout-aware parsing, rather than relying on page-level image embeddings. It targets rich structured information in complex enterprise documents.

entry.title: Can I Take Another Dose? Evaluating LLM Decision-Making Under Temporal Uncertainty in OTC Dosing QA

author.name: Maroof Kousar, Yibo Hu

entry.summary: Introduces DOSEBENCH, a benchmark of 81 curated OTC dosing scenarios (acetaminophen, ibuprofen) requiring tracking dose timing and rolling 24-hour intake, and evaluates four LLMs on decision correctness, consistency, and explanation verifiability under temporal uncertainty. It exposes a safety-relevant gap in everyday health QA.

entry.title: Archi: Agentic Operations at the CMS Experiment

author.name: Pietro Lugato, Luca Lavezzo, Jason Mohoney, Hasan Ozturk, Muhammad Hassan Ahmed, Juan Pablo Salas, Viphava Ohm, Krittin Phornsiricharoenphant, Gabriele Benelli, Mariarosaria D'Alfonso, Manasvita Joshi, Warren Nam, Aron Soha, Samantha Sunnarborg, Austin Swinney, Jack Tucker, Dmytro Kovalskyi, Tim Kraska, Christoph Paus

entry.summary: Archi is an open-source framework deploying configurable private agents that ingest heterogeneous data and reason over documentation, historical data, and live monitoring for the CMS experiment at CERN. It has been in production since February 2026 supporting computing operations teams.

entry.title: DAR: Deontic Reasoning with Agentic Harnesses

author.name: Guangyao Dou, William Jurayj, Nils Holzenberger, Benjamin Van Durme

entry.summary: DAR introduces Deontic Agentic Reasoning, where an LLM interacts with long cross-referenced statutes on demand rather than receiving all rules upfront, evaluated on hard subsets of DeonticBench. It shows agentic harnesses can advance rule-application tasks like tax liability and immigration appeals.

entry.title: Stein Kernelized Molecular Dynamics for Active Learning of Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Joanna Zou, Fraser Birks, Dallas Foster, Youssef Marzouk

entry.summary: Stein Kernelized Molecular Dynamics (SKMD) is an enhanced sampling method using interacting particle dynamics (a stochastic Stein variational variant) to acquire informative configurations for active learning of machine-learned interatomic potentials. It uses a symmetry-aware kernel of global atomic descriptors and asynchronous particle updates.

entry.title: Discourse-Role Labels as Presentation-Time Variables for Context Use in Language Models

author.name: Jianguo Zhu

entry.summary: This paper probes how discourse-role labels (Reference, Evidence, Instruction, Note, Example) wrapping injected content affect whether models adopt misleading assertions, finding adoption shifts of 56-84 points across labels. Testing GPT-5.5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Llama-3, and Qwen2.5, it shows binding labels increase adoption while Example suppresses it.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Learnable Rank

author.name: Arpit Garg, Simon Lucey, Hemanth Saratchandran

entry.summary: LR-LoRA makes the adapter rank learnable per layer during training rather than fixing a uniform rank, finding substantial layer-wise rank variation in attention versus MLP layers. It questions the fixed-rank inductive bias of standard LoRA.

entry.title: SemBlock: Semantic Boundary Dynamic Blocks for Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Xinrui Song, Zhuoran Wang, Mingju Gao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: SemBlock proposes semantic-boundary-driven dynamic block decoding for diffusion LLMs, training lightweight predictors on frozen hidden states to align blocks with discourse and reasoning units. It introduces a supporting semantic-boundary dataset.

entry.title: Boosting Self-Consistency with Ranking

author.name: Maria Marina, Daniil Moskovskiy, Sergey Pletenev, Mikhail Salnikov, Alexander Panchenko, Viktor Moskvoretskii

entry.summary: RISC reformulates self-consistency answer selection as a ranking problem, using a lightweight LambdaRank model with features capturing frequency, semantic centrality, and trace consistency. It recovers correct answers that majority voting misses.

entry.title: Read What You Hear: Reference-Free Hypotheses Evaluation with Acoustic Discrepancy

author.name: Zhihan Li, Hankun Wang, Yiwei Guo, Bohan Li, Xie Chen, Kai Yu

entry.summary: READ is a reference-free ASR hypothesis evaluation metric that uses a pretrained autoregressive TTS model to compute the conditional likelihood of speech given a text hypothesis, measuring acoustic discrepancy. It enables hypothesis refinement without additional training.

entry.title: Pinpoint: Grounded Worldwide Image Geolocation via Cross-Source Retrieval and Reranking

author.name: Nika Chuzhoy, Brian Hu, Amit A. Arora, Jae Ro, Sarthak S. Sahu

entry.summary: Pinpoint is a retrieve-and-rerank architecture for worldwide image geolocation that combines internet photos and street-view imagery in a coarse-to-fine pipeline using a contrastive image-GPS embedder. It unifies two previously separate geolocation tasks.

entry.title: Motion-Guided Causal Disentanglement for Robust Multi-View Cine Cardiac MRI Diagnosis

author.name: Chuankai Xu, Cristiane De Carvalho Singulane, Mohammad Abuannadi, Stephen Chandler, Jeremy Slivnick, Karolina Zareba, Jane Cao, Vidya Nadig, Fabio Fernandes, Seth Uretsky, Diego Perez de Arenaza, Amit Patel, Jianxin Xie

entry.summary: This work proposes motion-guided causal disentanglement for multi-view cine cardiac MRI diagnosis, separating view-specific anatomical variation from view-invariant pathological features to avoid shortcut learning. It targets low-data regimes for underrepresented cardiac conditions.

entry.title: INTACT: Ego-Guided Typed Sparse Evidence Retrieval for Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception

author.name: Chen Li, Shengrong Yuan, Jialong Zuo, Xinzhong Zhu, Nong Sang, Changxin Gao

entry.summary: INTACT is an ego-guided typed sparse evidence retrieval framework for heterogeneous collaborative perception that avoids the translation-first paradigm of aligning collaborator features before fusion. It makes newly joined heterogeneous agents cheaper to integrate.

entry.title: ReConFuse: Reconstruction-Error Guided Semantic Fusion for AI-Generated Video Detection

author.name: Xiaojing Chen (Anhui University), Xinyu Lu (Anhui University), Changtao Miao (Ant Group), Yunfeng Diao (Hefei University of Technology)

entry.summary: ReConFuse uses reconstruction error from a pretrained WF-VAE as a discriminative forensic cue for AI-generated video detection, fusing it with semantic features to capture spatial artifacts and temporal dynamics. It aims to generalize across evolving generative models.

entry.title: Food-R1: A Unified Multi-Task Food Vision-Language Model with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yu Zhu, Yongkang Li, Wenjie Zhu, Haoyi Jiang, Wenyu Liu, Wei Yang, Bin Li, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Food-R1 is a unified multi-task food VLM trained with reinforcement learning and chain-of-thought, paired with CalorieBench-80K, the first food image benchmark with CoT calorie reasoning annotations. It aims to improve reasoning and generalization over standard supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: PureLight: Learning Complex Luminaires with Light Tracing

author.name: Pedro Figueiredo, Zixuan Li, Beibei Wang, Milo\v{s} Ha\v{s}an, Nima Khademi Kalantari

entry.summary: PureLight proposes a neural formulation for estimating the appearance of complex luminaires with difficult light transport using light tracing and a normalizing-flow model of outgoing radiance. The learned appearance is distilled into a lightweight MLP for efficient rendering inference.

entry.title: RSC: Decentralized Rigid Formation Flocking for Large-Scale Swarms via Hybrid Predictive Control and Online Reconfiguration

author.name: Ganyu Zou, Linhan Wang, Chen Dai, Siji Chen, Chang-Tien Lu

entry.summary: RSC is a decentralized control framework for large-scale rigid formation flocking that integrates hybrid predictive control with online reconfiguration to maintain strict inter-agent distances in cluttered environments. It addresses local-minima deadlocks and control oscillations that plague existing decentralized methods.

entry.title: MineXplore: An Open-Source Reinforcement Learning Exploration Benchmark for GNSS-Denied Underground Environment

author.name: Abhishek S, Badrikanath Praharaj, Sreeram MV

entry.summary: MineXplore is an open-source MuJoCo-based RL navigation benchmark for GNSS-denied underground mines, reconstructed from a real Chilean copper mine dataset with realistic tunnel geometry, terrain friction zones, inclines, and lighting. It fills a gap for GPU-accelerated learning benchmarks grounded in real production-mine geometry.

entry.title: Toward Pre-Deployment Assurance for Enterprise AI Agents: Ontology-Grounded Simulation and Trust Certification

author.name: Thanh Luong Tuan, Abhijit Sanyal

entry.summary: Proposes an ontology-grounded framework for pre-deployment verification of enterprise AI agents, combining an operational envelope, automated scenario generation, and machine-readable trust certificates. It targets the gap between capability benchmarking and production governance assurance.

entry.title: The Saturation Trap and the Subjectivity of Intervention Timing: Why Affect-Based Triggers and LLM Judges Fail to Time Interventions on Autonomous Agents

author.name: Manvendra Modgil

entry.summary: Studies when to interrupt autonomous agents using an 18-dimensional affective-dynamics engine as a probe, evaluating four intervention triggers against human annotations on SWE-bench debugging traces. It identifies a state-saturation trap and the subjectivity of timing that undermine affect-based and LLM-judge triggers.

entry.title: Cascading Hallucination in Agentic RAG: The CHARM Framework for Detection and Mitigation

author.name: Saroj Mishra

entry.summary: Formalizes cascading hallucination in multi-step agentic RAG, where early errors propagate and amplify, and presents CHARM, a framework with a four-type taxonomy for detecting and interrupting such cascades. It addresses a failure mode missed by standard hallucination detectors.

entry.title: R-APS: Compositional Reasoning and In-Context Meta-Learning for Constrained Design via Reflective Adversarial Pareto Search

author.name: Jo\~ao Pedro Gandarela, Thiago Rios, Stefan Menzel, Andr\'e Freitas

entry.summary: Introduces R-APS, a reflective adversarial Pareto search method that decomposes agentic reasoning into separate modes (abductive, counterfactual, meta-inductive, corrective, inductive) to address error localization, worst-case evaluation, and stale knowledge. It targets reliable delivery in constrained design tasks.

entry.title: Channel-Oriented Design for EEG-to-Music Reconstruction

author.name: Jiaxin Qing, Junwei Lu, Lexin Li

entry.summary: Studies EEG-to-music reconstruction, finding that early channel mixing destroys weak discriminative EEG signals, and proposes a channel-oriented design with per-electrode tokenization and channel-wise self-distillation. It tackles an under-explored, noisy brain-decoding setting.

entry.title: Proof-Carrying Agent Actions: Model-Agnostic Runtime Governance for Heterogeneous Agent Systems

author.name: Zexun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Proof-Carrying Agent Actions, a runtime-neutral governance model centered on action certificates rather than vendor-specific logs to consistently authorize and audit high-risk agent actions across heterogeneous runtimes. It addresses a growing governance gap in agentic systems.

entry.title: Smart Transportation Without Neurons -- Fair Metro Network Expansion with Tabular Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dimitris Michailidis, Sennay Ghebreab, Fernando P. Santos

entry.summary: Reformulates the Metro Network Expansion Problem as a Non-Markovian Rewards Decision Process and shows tabular RL achieves results comparable to Deep RL while being far cheaper, more interpretable, and more environmentally friendly. It argues against unnecessary use of deep RL for fair transit planning.

entry.title: Ekka: Automated Diagnosis of Silent Errors in LLM Inference

author.name: Yile Gu, Zhen Zhang, Shaowei Zhu, Xinwei Fu, Jun Wu, Yida Wang, Baris Kasikci

entry.summary: Ekka is an automated diagnosis system for silent errors in LLM inference, where output quality degrades without explicit signals. It frames diagnosis as differential debugging by aligning intermediate execution states between a target and a reference implementation to localize root causes.

entry.title: Learning While Acting: A Skill-Enhanced Test-Time Co-Evolution Framework for Online Lifelong Learning Agents

author.name: Bo Mao, Jie Zhou, Yutao Yang, Xin Li, Xian Wei, Qin Chen, Xingjiao Wu, Liang He

entry.summary: LifeSkill is a two-stage RL framework for online lifelong learning agents that internalize test-time feedback through verifier-guided skill learning and test-time co-evolution, rather than relying on static retrieval. It aims to let agents continuously improve like human learners in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: UniCAD: A Unified Benchmark and Universal Model for Multi-Modal Multi-Task CAD

author.name: Jingyuan Chen, Sheng Jin, Haopeng Sun, Wentao Liu, Chen Qian

entry.summary: UniCAD is a unified benchmark for multi-modal multi-task CAD covering point-to-CAD reconstruction, text/image-to-CAD generation, and CAD QA, accompanied by UniCAD-MLLM, a universal model ingesting text, images, sketches, and point clouds. It addresses the lack of a unified benchmark for multi-task CAD learning.

entry.title: A Geometric View of Counterfactual Behavior: Interaction of Boundary Proximity and Local Support

author.name: Ioanna Gemou, Matteo Gamba, Randall Balestriero, Ritambhara Singh

entry.summary: This work offers a geometric view of counterfactual explanations, analyzing how boundary proximity and local data support interact to determine feasibility and distance of nearby counterfactuals in representation spaces. It uses a standardized local search probe across pretrained encoders, showing models with similar accuracy differ in counterfactual achievability.

entry.title: Validity Threats for Foundation Model Research

author.name: Gunnar K\"onig, Martin Pawelczyk, Ulrike von Luxburg, Sebastian Bordt

entry.summary: Argues that cost-saving alternatives to controlled experiments at foundation-model scale (proxy experiments, scaling laws, observational studies, single-run designs) introduce hidden validity threats that can invalidate research claims. It catalogs these threats to help researchers reason about their assumptions.

entry.title: EpiFormer: Learning Antigen-Antibody Interactions for Epitope Prediction via Geometric Deep Learning

author.name: Mansoor Ahmed, Huirong Chai, Haoxin Wang, Hemanth Venkateswara, Murray Patterson

entry.summary: EpiFormer is a geometric deep learning encoder-decoder using interleaved cross-attention within GNN encoders to jointly model antibody-antigen interactions for epitope prediction, addressing class imbalance and data scarcity. It targets immune recognition understanding and antibody engineering.

entry.title: CaloTrilogy: Toward a Breakthrough in One-Step, End-to-End, Physics-Guided Shower Generation for Modern Calorimeters

author.name: Cheng Jiang, Sitian Qian, Kevin Pedro, Oz Amram, Huilin Qu, Maggie Voetberg

entry.summary: CaloTrilogy is a one-step end-to-end physics-guided generative framework for fast calorimeter shower simulation, using an average velocity field integrator to cut inference cost while preserving physics fidelity. It addresses the growing compute burden of Monte Carlo simulation at colliders.

entry.title: Nonlocal Mean Field Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge with Learned Interactions

author.name: Daisuke Inoue, Mathieu Lauri\`ere, Dante Kalise

entry.summary: This work develops a mean-field extension of the Schrodinger Bridge problem for interacting particle systems and replaces costly nonlocal interaction terms with neural surrogates, cutting per-step cost from quadratic to linear. It includes Gronwall-type stability bounds.

entry.title: Global Sketch-Based Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Daniel Zhao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a global, sketch-based watermark for masked diffusion language models that controls a vector-valued sketch of the whole sequence rather than local next-token contexts. The decoupled formulation makes detection more robust than context-dependent autoregressive watermarks.

entry.title: GENEB: Why Genomic Models Are Hard to Compare

author.name: Daria Ledneva, Mikhail Nuridinov, Denis Kuznetsov

entry.summary: GENEB is a large-scale diagnostic benchmark evaluating frozen representations from 40 genomic foundation models across 100 tasks under a unified probing protocol, exposing that aggregate leaderboards are unstable. It enables controlled comparison across scale, architecture, and tokenization.

entry.title: COP-Q: Safety-First Reinforcement Learning for Robot Control via Cholesky-Ordered Projection

author.name: Guopeng Li, Moritz A. Zanger, Matthijs T. J. Spaan, Julian F. P. Kooij

entry.summary: COP-Q is a safety-first off-policy reinforcement learning method for robot control that incorporates inter-objective covariance into vector-valued Q estimation via Cholesky-ordered projection. It reduces overly conservative value estimates and improves sample efficiency under safety constraints.

entry.title: Fast & Faithful Function Vectors

author.name: Minh An Pham, Anton Segeler, Thomas Wiegand, Wojciech Samek, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Patrick Kahardipraja, Reduan Achtibat

entry.summary: This paper studies design choices for function vectors used to steer LLMs during in-context learning, showing that gradient-based head selection via Layer-wise Relevance Propagation improves efficiency and accuracy, and distributed steering beats simple aggregation. It refines task-representation steering methods.

entry.title: Geometry Gaussians: Decoupling Appearance and Geometry in Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Hongyu Zhou, Zorah L\"ahner

entry.summary: Geometry Gaussians shows that default 3D Gaussian Splatting cannot simultaneously represent texture and geometry well, and adds a single geometry-opacity parameter per splat plus an optional transparency-curated optimization to decouple them. It improves geometric surface extraction without harming appearance.

entry.title: VCIFBench: Evaluating Complex Instruction Following for Video Understanding

author.name: Huangchen Xu, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: DLLG is a dynamic logit-level ensembling framework that learns token-level fusion of multiple specialized LLM experts from sparse response-level supervision via a lightweight gating module, avoiding premature routing or merging interference. It outperforms routing, heuristic ensembling, and parameter merging on reasoning and code tasks.

entry.title: DuDi: Dual-Signal Distillation with Cross-Lingual Verbalizer

author.name: Patomporn Payoungkhamdee, Tinnakit Udsa, Jian Gang Ngui, Sarana Nutanong, Alham Fikri Aji, Peerat Limkonchotiwat

entry.summary: DuDi is a dual-signal multilingual distillation framework combining sequence-level and token-level signals with a cross-lingual verbalizer to improve small language models on Southeast Asian languages. It addresses degradation of multilingual ability at sub-billion scales.

entry.title: SAID: Accelerating Diffusion-Based Language Models via Scaffold-Aware Iterative Decoding

author.name: Na Li, Chengda Wang, Mingju Gao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: SAID accelerates diffusion LLMs by allocating more denoising computation to scaffold tokens that establish coarse structure, then completing detail tokens with fewer steps. It adds a confidence-hierarchical layered generation mechanism for block-wise decoding.

entry.title: SocialCoach: Personalized Social Skill Learning with RL-based Agentic Tutoring and Practice

author.name: Tianfu Wang, Max Xiong, Jianxun Lian, Hongyuan Zhu, Zhengyu Hu, Yuxuan Lei, Linxiao Gong, Xiaofang Li, Peiting Tsai, Nicholas Jing Yuan, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: SocialCoach is an LLM-powered agentic tutoring system for personalized social skill training (e.g., negotiation, leadership), building a theory-to-practice knowledge corpus and adaptive practice scheduling with RL. It targets scalable coaching where expert tutors are scarce.

entry.title: Intra-Modal Neighbors Never Lie: Rectifying Inter-Modal Noisy Correspondence via Graph-Based Intra-Modal Reasoning

author.name: Yang Liu, Wentao Feng, Shu-Dong Huang, Yalan Ye, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: IN2R rectifies noisy inter-modal correspondences in cross-modal retrieval by leveraging the geometric stability of intra-modal neighbors to synthesize reliable supervision targets, rather than selecting discrete proxy labels. It addresses single-point fragility and discretization error.

entry.title: End-to-End Text Line Detection and Ordering

author.name: Benjamin Kiessling (ALMAnaCH)

entry.summary: Orli is an end-to-end image-to-sequence model that jointly performs text-line detection and reading-order prediction for historical documents, replacing hand-coded geometric heuristics. It autoregressively generates baselines directly in reading order via a chord-frame parameterization.

entry.title: Spatial Artifact Coherence Determines Codec Robustness in Patch-Based rPPG

author.name: Achraf Ben Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper identifies Spatial Artifact Coherence (SAC) as the physical quantity governing when patch-based remote photoplethysmography outperforms global projection under video codec compression, and introduces a codec-aware PatchPCA algorithm family. It evaluates 280 subjects across three datasets and many compression variants.

entry.title: Robust Multi-view Clustering against Imperfect Information

author.name: Zhichao Huang, Haochen Zhou, Hao Wang, Mouxing Yang, Xi Peng

entry.summary: This paper addresses multi-view clustering under both incomplete views and noisy correspondences, arguing both arise from imperfect cross-view counterpart information. It proposes a unified method robust to absent and unreliable counterparts simultaneously.

entry.title: IRIS-GAN: Staged Specialist Detection of Deepfake Faces

author.name: Jaume M. Trenchs, Veronica Sanz

entry.summary: IRIS-GAN is a specialist forensic detector for GAN-generated deepfake faces using staged training across increasingly difficult GAN families, achieving over 99% detection. Grad-CAM analysis reveals generator-dependent spatial signatures useful for secondary classification.

entry.title: TGSD: Topology-Guided State-Space Diffusion for EEG Spatial Super-Resolution

author.name: Zijian Kang, Weiming Zeng, Yueyang Li, Shengyu Gong, Hongjie Yan, Wai Ting Siok, Nizhuan Wang

entry.summary: TGSD is a topology-guided state-space diffusion framework that recovers dense-channel EEG from sparse low-density recordings for spatial super-resolution. It uses a hierarchical spatial prior encoder to incorporate electrode topology and address whole-channel missingness.

entry.title: Teaching Robots to Say 'I Don't Know' : SENTINEL for Uncertainty-Aware SLAM

author.name: Abhishek S, Badrikanath Praharaj, Sreeram MV

entry.summary: SENTINEL is a training-free, label-free reliability estimation framework giving low-cost range-only 2D LiDAR a diagnostic signal by combining scan geometry statistics with cross-modal LiDAR-RGB-D depth consistency. Below-threshold scans are rejected and the robot falls back to wheel odometry to prevent silent SLAM corruption.

entry.title: Plan First, Judge Later, Run Better: A DMAIC-Inspired Agentic System for Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yongzi Yu, Ao Li, Le Wang, Ziyue Li, Fugee Tsung, Yuxuan Liang, Man Li

entry.summary: Presents DMAIC-IAD, a Plan First, Judge Later multi-agent system for industrial anomaly detection inspired by the DMAIC quality-management framework. It emphasizes strategy formulation over pure execution to handle heterogeneous modalities cost-effectively.

entry.title: What Type of Inference is Active Inference?

author.name: Wouter W. L. Nuijten, Mykola Lukashchuk, Thijs van de Laar, Bert de Vries

entry.summary: Provides a variational analysis clarifying that Expected Free Energy minimization in active inference can be rewritten as predictive-model VFE plus explicit entropy-correction and planning-correction terms. It characterizes which corrections are required for proper EFE-based planning.

entry.title: Optical-Guided Neural Collapse for SAR Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning

author.name: Fan Zhang, Sijin Zheng, Fei Ma, Qiang Yin, Yongsheng Zhou, Fei Gao, Xian Sun

entry.summary: Proposes an optical-guided SAR few-shot class-incremental learning framework inspired by neural collapse, deriving orthogonal feature subspaces from a data-rich optical ATR dataset as geometric priors and projecting SAR features onto them via principal-angle constraints to transfer discriminative structure. It addresses SAR data scarcity, azimuth sensitivity, and catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: TIDE: Proactive Multi-Problem Discovery via Template-Guided Iteration

author.name: Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Minki Kang, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: TIDE is a template-guided iterative framework enabling agents to proactively discover multiple hidden problems from user context, grounded in evidence and paired with actions, rather than only acting on explicit requests. It counters the tendency of single-pass prediction to anchor on the most salient cases.

entry.title: From Agent Traces to Trust: Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu, Qingqiang Sun, Zequn Sun, Zhangkai Wu, Mingkai Zhang, Yanming Zhu

entry.summary: This paper addresses evidence tracing and execution provenance in LLM agents, modeling how retrieved evidence, tool outputs, memory, and intermediate claims connect throughout execution to support verification, debugging, and auditing. It argues final-answer accuracy alone cannot explain agent behavior.

entry.title: KODA: Contrastive Representation Comparison and Alignment for Vision-Language Foundation Models

author.name: Youqi Wu, Mohammad Jalali, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: KODA is a kernel-based framework for contrastive comparison and alignment of vision-language foundation models (CLIP, SigLIP) via a Contrastive Embedding Clustering task that finds subsets weakly clustered under one representation but strongly under another. It constructs unified multimodal kernels and formulates discrepancy analysis to explain structural differences.

entry.title: Learning What to Learn: Stage-Specific Data Sets for SFT-then-RL in Small Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Chongyang He, Rui Zhang, Zixuan Wang, Xin Li

entry.summary: This paper argues data strategy should match the distinct roles of SFT and RL in small language model reasoning, using SFT for not-yet-mastered skills and RL to consolidate partially accessible ones, with a Bridge mechanism transforming teacher traces into learnable supervision. It organizes training into difficulty-aware stage-specific sets.

entry.title: Entity Binding Failures in Speech LLM Reasoning: Diagnosis and Chain-of-Thought Intervention

author.name: Ming-Hao Hsu, Xiaohai Tian, Jun Zhang, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: This work diagnoses that speech LLMs collapse to chance on logical entity-tracking tasks due to entity binding failure, where continuous speech features lose precise entity-property associations, while matching text models on spatial, syntactic, and factual tasks. It proposes Entity-Aware Chain-of-Thought forcing explicit entity enumeration before reasoning.

entry.title: GARL: Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent Strategic Prioritisation

author.name: Yuxiao Ye, Yiwen Zhang, Huiyuan Xie, Yuqin Huang, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: GARL is a game-theoretic RL framework for multi-agent strategic prioritisation, formalizing the task as a two-stage game where agents allocate resources and an arbiter produces final rankings. It grounds reward design in interaction structure rather than task-specific heuristics.

entry.title: Reflection Separation from a Single Image via Joint Latent Diffusion

author.name: Zheng-Hui Huang, Zhixiang Wang, Yu-Lun Liu, Yung-Yu Chuang

entry.summary: This paper fine-tunes a diffusion model for single-image reflection separation, jointly generating transmission and reflection layers with a cross-layer self-attention mechanism and disjoint sampling to reduce interference. It targets hard cases like glare and weak reflections.

entry.title: XSSR: Cross-Domain Self-Supervised Representative Selection for Efficient Annotation in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Byunghyun Ko, Aleksei Anisimov, Kobe Ke, Suhas Bharthepude, Jeongkyu Lee

entry.summary: XSSR minimizes target-domain annotation in cross-domain medical image segmentation via a masked autoencoder for shared embeddings, a greedy density/novelty/diversity selection algorithm, and a U-Net segmentation stage. It addresses costly labeling under domain shift.

entry.title: COMBINER: Composed Image Retrieval Guided by Attribute-based Neighbor Relations

author.name: Zixu Li, Yupeng Hu, Zhiwei Chen, Haokun Wen, Xuemeng Song, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: COMBINER improves composed image retrieval by representing cross-modal features through attribute prototypes and neighbor relations, addressing cases where images look alike but differ in attributes. It tackles attribute-semantic entanglement, cross-modal inconsistency, and missing supervision.

entry.title: CDPM-Align: Multi-Scale Guidance-Aligned Diffusion Pretraining for Robust Few-Shot Anatomical Landmark Detection

author.name: Roberto Di Via, Irina Voiculescu, Francesca Odone, Vito Paolo Pastore

entry.summary: CDPM-Align introduces a multi-scale guidance-aligned conditional diffusion pretraining approach for few-shot anatomical landmark detection in medical images. It explores representation learning to improve reliability and robustness under limited annotation regimes.

entry.title: Drift-Augmented Scoring: Text-Derived Noise Robustness for Zero-Shot Audio-Language Classification

author.name: Tu Vo, Sheir Zaheer, Chan Y. Park

entry.summary: Drift-Augmented Scoring adds a small text-derived per-class bonus to zero-shot audio-language classification scores to improve robustness under acoustic noise. The bonus rewards classes when noisy embeddings drift in directions predicted by noise-conditioned text prompts, computed once with no gradients.

entry.title: CADENCE: Predicting Realized MAPF Execution Time Beyond Sum of Costs

author.name: Abhishek S, Badrikanath Praharaj, Sreeram MV

entry.summary: CADENCE is a hardware study examining which pre-execution features best predict realized wall-clock completion time for multi-agent path finding, beyond standard metrics like sum-of-costs and makespan. Experiments on a 7x7 workcell with seven differential-drive robots compare planned travel cost, primitive motion burden, and other predictors.

entry.title: Tree-Based Formalization of Multi-Agent Complementarity in Human-AI Interactions

author.name: Andrea Ferrario

entry.summary: Provides a tree-based formalization of complementarity in multi-agent human-AI interaction, modeling how agent predictions compose into workflow-sensitive protocols via rooted binary trees. It closes a gap in formal treatment of when human-AI teams beat the best member.

entry.title: SpurAudio: A Benchmark for Studying Shortcut Learning in Few-Shot Audio Classification

author.name: Giries Abu Ayoub, Morad Tukan, Loay Mualem

entry.summary: Introduces SpurAudio, a benchmark for studying shortcut learning and spurious foreground-background correlations in few-shot audio classification. It enables controlled multi-level evaluation of contextual exploitation in audio, an under-studied modality.

entry.title: Bayes-Sufficient Representations in Supervised Learning

author.name: Vasileios Sevetlidis

entry.summary: Defines Bayes-sufficiency for supervised representations as the property that a prediction head can implement a Bayes-optimal action rule, making target information loss-dependent. It introduces the Bayes quotient and connects the framework to property elicitation.

entry.title: AgenticDiffusion: Agentic Diffusion-based Path Planning for Vision-Based UAV Navigation

author.name: Faryal Batool, Muhammad Ahsan Mustafa, Fawad Mehboob, Valerii Serpiva, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: Introduces AgenticDiffusion, a multi-view UAV indoor navigation framework combining language-guided reasoning, open-vocabulary grounding, diffusion-based planning, and NMPC control over synchronized first-person and top-view observations. It improves reasoning about occlusions and global scene structure.

entry.title: ChessMimic: Per-Rating Transformer Models for Human Move, Clock, and Outcome Prediction in Online Blitz Chess

author.name: Thomas Johnson

entry.summary: Presents ChessMimic, three small encoder-only transformers for human move, thinking-time, and outcome prediction in online blitz chess, fitted separately per 100-Elo rating band to sharpen per-skill calibration. It outperforms Maia-2 on human move prediction across all Elo bands and matches Maia-3 efficiency tiers.

entry.title: Treat Traffic Like Trees: A Semantic-Preserving Hierarchical Graph-Based Expert Framework for Encrypted Traffic Analysis

author.name: Yuantu Luo, Jun Tao, Linxiao Yu, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes PTGAMoE, a semantic-preserving hierarchical graph-based mixture-of-experts framework for encrypted traffic analysis that represents traffic as protocol trees mirroring protocol-layer/field hierarchy, avoiding the obscuring of protocol semantics by complex preprocessing. It exploits protocol-specification structure underused in prior learning frameworks.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End Co-Design of Neural Network Processors: From Training and Mapping to Fabrication

author.name: Yuyang Du, Yujun Huang, Gioele Zardini

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified, monotone co-design framework composing four interoperable blocks spanning neural network training, chip mapping, wafer fabrication, and compute allocation for neural network processors. It addresses uncertainty across the end-to-end hardware-software pipeline.

entry.title: SharedRequest: Privacy-Preserving Model-Agnostic Inference for Large Language Models

author.name: Peihua Mai, Xuanrong Gao, Youlong Ding, Xianglong Du, Wei Liu, Yan Pang

entry.summary: SharedRequest is a model-agnostic framework for privacy-preserving LLM inference that obscures sensitive prompts by mixing them with noisy variants and batching semantically equivalent instructions to amortize cost. It aims to protect prompt privacy without sacrificing much utility or efficiency.

entry.title: Query-based Cross-Modal Projector Bolstering Mamba Multimodal LLM

author.name: SooHwan Eom, Jay Shim, Gwanhyeong Koo, Haebin Na, Mark A. Hasegawa-Johnson, Sungwoong Kim, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a query-based cross-modal projector to improve Mamba-based multimodal LLMs by compressing visual tokens via cross-attention, avoiding manual 2D scan-order design. It targets the efficiency advantages of state-space models for vision-language tasks.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Incremental Segmentation via Semantic Anchors and Spatial Arbitration

author.name: Zhonggai Wang, Kai Fang, Guangyu Gao

entry.summary: SASA tackles weakly incremental semantic segmentation by using learnable semantic anchors as rigid class references plus elastic residual adaptation and spatial arbitration to resist feature drift. It aims to prevent newly learned classes from overwriting old ones under noisy supervision.

entry.title: SBP-Net: Learning Thin Structure Reconstruction with Sliding-Box Projections

author.name: Ofir Gilad, Andrei Sharf

entry.summary: SBP-Net reconstructs thin 3D structures (e.g., vasculature, pipes) using local orthographic depth projections from a sliding box, processed by a network to recover missing 2D thin geometry then fused into 3D. It targets failures of dense-surface neural methods on sparse thin structures.

entry.title: VT-3DAD: Cross-Category 3D Anomaly Detection via Visual-Text Normal Space Alignment

author.name: Zi Wang, Katsuya Hotta, Yawen Zou, Koichiro Kamide, Yijin Wei, Chao Zhang, Jun Yu

entry.summary: VT-3DAD is a training-free framework for few-shot cross-category 3D anomaly detection that aligns multi-view CLIP visual features with text in a normal space to avoid confusion among geometrically similar categories. It uses depth maps from frozen CLIP encoders for visual-text alignment.

entry.title: Multi-Camera AR Guidance System for Surgical Instrument Handling and Assembly: Investigating Workload and Efficiency

author.name: Shiyu Li, Julian Kreimeier, Hannah Schieber, Dirk M\"uller, Bernhard Kainz, R\"udiger von Eisenhart-Rothe, Daniel Roth

entry.summary: This work presents a marker-free multi-camera AR guidance system using 6D pose estimation and head-mounted display visualization to assist scrub nurses with surgical instrument handling and assembly. A user study investigates workload and efficiency, with the pose network trained purely on synthetic data.

entry.title: Cooperative Circumnavigation for Multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicles Without External Localization

author.name: Xueming Liu, Lin Li, Xiang Zhou, Tianjiang Hu, Qingrui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a cooperative target circumnavigation framework for multiple unmanned surface vehicles operating without external localization, using only onboard range, displacement, and bearing measurements. A heterogeneous perception strategy and relative position estimation maintain uniform circular formation around a non-cooperative target.

entry.title: Trivium: Temporal Regret as a First-Class Objective for Causal-Memory Controllers

author.name: Edward Y. Chang

entry.summary: Introduces Trivium, proposing long-horizon temporal regret and epistemic regret as first-class objectives alongside outcome regret for causal-memory controllers. It targets why and when failures persist rather than only what failed.

entry.title: HighTide: An Agent-Curated Open-Source VLSI Benchmark Suite

author.name: Benjamin Goldblatt, Paolo Pedroso, Farhad Modaresi, Ethan Sifferman, Matthew R. Guthaus

entry.summary: Introduces HighTide, an evolving AI-assisted open-source VLSI benchmark suite spanning multiple design languages and technology nodes with Bazel-based incremental RTL-to-GDS compilation and agent-curated design skills with decision logs. It supports the open hardware ecosystem.

entry.title: ADAPTOOD: Uncertainty-Aware Fine-Tuning for Out-of-Distribution ECG Time Series Models

author.name: Sotirios Vavaroutas, Yu Yvonne Wu, Ali Etemad, Cecilia Mascolo

entry.summary: Introduces ADAPTOOD, an uncertainty-aware fine-tuning method for out-of-distribution ECG time-series models that accounts for shift severity rather than assuming fixed distribution shifts. It targets robustness degradation across diverse sensors, populations, and settings.

entry.title: DSIRM: Learning Query-Bridged Discrete Semantic Identifiers for E-commerce Relevance Modeling

author.name: Bokang Wang, Xing Fang, Mingmin Jin, Jing Wang, Zhentao Song, Guangxin Song, Jianbo Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes DSIRM, a Discrete Semantic Identifier Relevance Model for e-commerce search that explicitly models discrete relevance features via a query-bridged supervised approach rather than unsupervised quantization, addressing difficulty in capturing fine-grained attribute distinctions. It improves query-dependent ranking.

entry.title: QO-Bench: Diagnosing Query-Operator-Preserving Retrieval over Typed Event Tuples

author.name: Mengao Zhang, Xiang Yang, Chang Liu, Tianhui Tan, Ke-wei Huang

entry.summary: QO-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark for query-operator question answering over typed event tuples extracted from text, testing whether RAG systems can execute database-style queries rather than just retrieve relevant passages. Answers are deterministically computed and exact-matched, avoiding LLM-judge ambiguity.

entry.title: Scenario Generation for Risk-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Probably Approximately Safe Guarantees

author.name: Mohit Prashant, Arvind Easwaran

entry.summary: This work develops scenario generation for risk-aware RL with probably-approximately-safe guarantees, constructing probabilistic barrier certificates by sampling trajectories and approximating violation distributions under transition perturbations. It tightens bounds in insufficiently explored states.

entry.title: Self-Reflective APIs: Structure Beats Verbosity for AI Agent Recovery

author.name: Arquimedes Canedo, Grama Chethan

entry.summary: This paper shows that self-reflective APIs returning machine-readable recovery suggestions on validation failure substantially improve AI agent task completion versus plain-English error messages. A leak-audited pilot finds large gains on Anthropic models but not on gpt-4o-mini, with better token efficiency.

entry.title: GeM-NR: Geometry-Aware Multi-View Editing for Nonrigid Scene Changes

author.name: Josef Bengtson, Yaroslava Lochman, Fredrik Kahl

entry.summary: GeM-NR is a fast, training-free approach for general multi-view consistent image editing that handles nonrigid edits substantially changing scene geometry, unlike methods restricted to rigid or appearance-only edits. It is geometry-aware to maintain cross-view consistency.

entry.title: Variance Reduction for Heavy-Tailed Monetization Metrics in Ranking Experiments via Post-Stratification

author.name: Neeti Pokharna, Olivier Jeunen, Yatharth Saraf, Aleksei Ustimenko

entry.summary: This paper presents a practical variance-reduction framework for online ranking experiments with heavy-tailed monetization metrics, combining post-stratification with CUPED using pre-experiment covariates. Deployed at ShareChat, it substantially reduces variance and improves experiment sensitivity without extra traffic.

entry.title: Offline-to-Online Learning in Linear Bandits

author.name: Kushagra Chandak, Toshinori Kitamura, Xiaoqi Tan

entry.summary: This paper studies offline-to-online learning in stochastic linear bandits, proposing an algorithm that relies on offline data early and increasingly favors exploration as the horizon grows. It establishes regret bounds competitive with both purely online and purely offline solutions.

entry.title: PointAction: 3D Points as Universal Action Representations for Robot Control

author.name: Mutian Tong, Han Jiang, Qiao Feng, Lingjie Liu, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: Presents PointAction, a framework that bridges video-prediction models to robot actions by fine-tuning a video generation foundation model to jointly predict future RGB frames and dynamic 3D pointmaps, using points as universal action representations. It resolves the ambiguity of grounding actions from RGB-only video rollouts.

entry.title: Toward a Generalized Defense Across Sparse, Continuous, and Structured Parameter Attacks

author.name: Bin Duan, Zeyu Bai, Guowei Yang

entry.summary: ParDef proposes a generalized defense against sparse, continuous, and structured parameter (weight tampering) attacks on deployed models, aiming to handle unpredictable attack forms without retraining. It targets integrity risks across cloud, CI/CD, and edge deployment pipelines.

entry.title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models via Part-Factorized Attention

author.name: Dhanesh Ramachandram

entry.summary: This work introduces a part-factorized concept bottleneck model on a frozen DINOv3 backbone that uses a foreground gate and fixed concept-to-part routing so each attribute reads only from its anatomical region. It improves spatial faithfulness and auditability of concept-based decisions.

entry.title: Hyper-ICL: Attention Calibration with Hyperbolic Anchor Distillation for Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Niloufar Alipour Talemi, Hossein Kashiani, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: Hyper-ICL is a demonstration-free multimodal in-context learning framework that learns a low-rank logit-level adapter using hyperbolic anchor distillation to reconstruct demonstration effects without including examples at inference. It reduces latency and instability from demonstration sensitivity.

entry.title: Distributional Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search for Uncertainty-Aware Retrieval

author.name: Olivier Jeunen

entry.summary: This paper extends approximate nearest neighbor search to operate over distributions rather than point embeddings, incorporating embedding uncertainty to counter retrieval bias toward popular head items. It aims for fairer long-tail recommendation retrieval.

entry.title: Beyond Symmetric Alignment: Spectral Diagnostics of Modality Imbalance in Vision-Language Models in the Medical Domain

author.name: Alessandro Gambetti, Qiwei Han, Cl\'audia Soares, Hong Shen

entry.summary: This work introduces the Spectral Alignment Score, an asymmetric metric projecting modalities onto an anchor eigenbasis to reveal which modality drives cross-modal degradation in medical vision-language models. It diagnoses modality information imbalance hidden by symmetric metrics.

entry.title: CRAFT: Cost-aware Refinement And Front-aware Tuning of Prompts

author.name: Shanu Kumar, Shubhanshu Khandelwal, Akhila Yesantarao Venkata, Parag Agrawal, Yova Kementchedjhieva, Manish Gupta

entry.summary: CRAFT is a Pareto-front prompt optimizer that treats target-LLM validation calls as a scarce resource and allocates them near the candidate frontier, avoiding scalarization collapse from fixed weighted objectives. It jointly optimizes prompt accuracy and token cost.

entry.title: FoeGlass: Simple In-Context Learning Is Enough for Red Teaming Audio Deepfake Detectors

author.name: Sepehr Dehdashtian, Jacob H Seidman, Vishnu N Boddeti, Gaurav Bharaj
