entry.summary: Reframes meme understanding as literal-pragmatic decomposition and proposes Intent Projection, which separates surface content from pragmatic intent at representation, output, and objective levels within an LVLM. It addresses models describing what an image shows rather than what authors mean.

entry.title: HybridThinker: Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Compressed Memory and Transient Thought Steps

author.name: Xin Liu, Runsong Zhao, Xinyu Liu, Junhao Ruan, Pengcheng Huang, Shichao Dong, Chunyang Xiao, Chenglong Wang, Changliang Li, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes HybridThinker, which compresses chain-of-thought into memory tokens while transiently retaining full thought steps to preserve fine-grained detail and prevent error propagation. It addresses training shortcuts where models bypass memory tokens.

entry.title: Pixel Cube: Diffusion-based Portrait Video Relighting Through Realistic Lighting Reproduction

author.name: Yufan Zhang, Yu Ji, Ayo Ajiboye, Rundi Wu, Yu Guo, Changxi Zheng, Jinwei Ye

entry.summary: Presents a diffusion-based method for relighting dynamic portrait videos with photorealism and temporal consistency, trained on a hybrid real and rendered dataset captured via an LED lighting system. It uses per-frame HDR environment maps as lighting control over video diffusion priors.

entry.title: ATLAS: A Large-Scale Evaluation Benchmark for Adversarial LiDAR Perception

author.name: Mellon M. Zhang, Siddhant Panse, Zimo Fan, Akshal Dhal, Rishit Sarkar, Glen Chou

entry.summary: Introduces ATLAS, a large-scale benchmark for adversarial LiDAR perception that captures structured and physically realizable sensor anomalies inducing black-box failures. It addresses the gap left by clean-data benchmarks and prior attack-hardware-focused studies.

entry.title: TGV-KV: Text-Grounded KV Eviction for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jizhihui Liu, Ruizi Han, Miao Zhang, Rui Shao, Xuebo Liu, Weili Guan, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TGV-KV, a text-grounded KV-cache eviction method for vision-language models that grounds visual token importance in textual guidance to reduce memory while limiting degradation. It addresses the modality gap that hampers language-model-designed eviction methods in VLMs.

entry.title: JAVEDIT: Joint Audio-Visual Instruction-Guided Video Editing with Agentic Data Curation

author.name: Yinan Chen, Chuming Lin, Zhennan Chen, Yuxiang Zeng, Junwei Zhu, Yali Bi, Xijie Huang, Chengming Xu, Donghao Luo, Zhucun Xue, Xiaobin Hu, Chengjie Wang, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: Presents JAVEdit-100k, the first large-scale dataset for instruction-guided joint audio-visual video editing, with about 100k editing triplets across five categories and an agent-in-the-loop quality control. It also introduces an evaluation benchmark for the task.

entry.title: Eliciting Complex Spatial Reasoning in MLLMs through Wide-Baseline Matching

author.name: Hao Zhong, Muzhi Zhu, Shenyan Zeng, Anzhou Li, Cong Chen, Hua Geng, Duochao Shi, Wentao Ye, Tao Lin, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: ReasonMatch-Bench evaluates MLLM spatial reasoning via wide-baseline matching, revealing a large gap (84 vs 37 F1) between humans and the best baseline. The authors propose training methods to elicit fine-grained correspondence reasoning in physical environments.

entry.title: NewtPhys: Do Foundation Models Understand Newtonian Physics?

author.name: Sebastian Cavada, Soumava Paul, Tuan-Hung Vu, Andrei Bursuc, Raoul de Charette

entry.summary: NewtPhys is a 4D physically-annotated dataset from multiview real-world scenes with dense 3D forces and amodal per-pixel quantities, used to evaluate 56 VLMs on low-level Newtonian physics understanding. It bridges the gap between simplistic synthetic benchmarks and realistic visual complexity.

entry.title: Worth Remembering: Surprise-Gated Robot Episodic Memory

author.name: Nicolas Gorlo, Derek K. Wise, Alberto Speranzon, Luca Carlone

entry.summary: This work proposes using Bayesian surprise as a gating mechanism for selective long-term robot episodic memory, retaining only high-utility episodes in a semantically rich V-JEPA-2 latent space. It enables grounding instructions that reference notable past events without storing all experience.

entry.title: Optimized Labeling Resource Allocation for Prediction-Assisted Inference via OPAL

author.name: Virginia L. Ma, Emmanuel J. Cand\`es

entry.summary: OPAL learns an optimal labeling allocation policy within a tractable class of smooth policies for prediction-assisted active statistical inference, turning a black-box model's noisy uncertainty scores into a variance-minimizing, data-adaptive labeling strategy. It addresses the brittleness of active inference when uncertainty estimates are noisy.

entry.title: CORE: Conflict-Oriented Reasoning for General Multimodal Manipulation Detection

author.name: Jinjie Shen, Yaxiong Wang, Yujiao Wu, Lechao Cheng, Tianrui Hui, Nan Pu, Zhihui Li, Zhun Zhong

entry.summary: CORE endows multimodal LLMs with conflict-oriented reasoning to detect manipulated multimodal misinformation by identifying intrinsic semantic or physical inconsistencies. It aims for better generalization to emerging manipulation types than manipulation-specific models.

entry.title: Code-on-Graph: Iterative Programmatic Reasoning via Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Weiwei Ding, Zixuan Li, Long Bai, Zhuo Chen, Kun Su, Fei Wang, Xiaolong Jin, Jin Zhang, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Code-on-Graph is a programmatic reasoning framework that lets LLMs write iterative code to query knowledge graphs, overcoming the inflexibility of predefined operators and the unscalability of injecting facts into prompts. It improves compositional expressiveness for complex KG questions.

entry.title: EvoDS: Self-Evolving Autonomous Data Science Agent with Skill Learning and Context Management

author.name: Zherui Yang, Fan Liu, Yansong Ning, Hao Liu

entry.summary: EvoDS is a self-evolving autonomous data science agent that expands its skills via autonomous skill acquisition and adaptively manages long-term context through agentic reinforcement learning. It addresses static action sets and poor long-horizon context management in multi-stage data science pipelines.

entry.title: Inference Cost Attacks for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Chengliang Liu, Liangbo Ning, Yujuan Ding, Wenqi Fan

entry.summary: RA-ICA introduces an inference cost attack on RAG-enhanced LLMs that poisons external knowledge bases rather than relying on impractical direct prompt manipulation, inflating computational cost. It targets the multi-stage retrieval and synthesis pipeline as a vulnerability.

entry.title: "**Important** You should give me full credits!": Exploring Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Automatic Grading Systems

author.name: Hang Li, Fedor Filippov, Yuling Lin, Pengfei He, Kaiqi Yang, Yucheng Chu, Yingqian Cui, Hui Liu, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Empirically demonstrates prompt injection attacks on LLM-based automatic grading systems, where adversarial text in student answers can force artificially high scores. Highlights a real security threat in educational deployment of LLM graders.

entry.title: AugMask: Training Diffusion Models on Incomplete Tabular Data via Stochastic Augmentation and Masking

author.name: Jungkyu Kim, Taeyoung Park, Kibok Lee

entry.summary: AugMask is a plug-and-play training framework that adapts missing-unaware diffusion model backbones to incomplete tabular data by separating conditioning from supervision via stochastic augmentation and observed-coordinate masking. Connected to a Rao-Blackwellization argument.

entry.title: Analyzing Stream Collapse in Hyper-Connections: From Diagnosis to Mitigation

author.name: Ekaterina Alimaskina, Gleb Molodtsov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Diagnoses stream collapse in Hyper-Connections, where multi-stream Transformer residual streams concentrate signal and interpretable features in a dominant stream rather than balancing, with residual mixing remaining near identity. Proposes mitigations to restore multi-stream capacity utilization.

entry.title: Mitigating False Credit Propagation: Probabilistic Graphical Reward Aggregation for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Can Lv, Mingju Chen, Heng Chang, Shiji Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies False Credit Propagation, where flat scalarization of rubric-based RL rewards counts credit even when prerequisite conditions are absent. Proposes GEAR, a probabilistic graphical framework modeling each criterion as a latent Bernoulli event in a typed rubric graph for dependency-aware aggregation.

entry.title: Skill-RM: Unifying Heterogeneous Evaluation Criteria via Agent Skill

author.name: Tao Chen, Gangwei Jiang, Pengyu Cheng, Siyuan Huang, Yihao Liu, Jingwei Ni, Jiaqi Guo, Mengyu Zhou, Kai Tang, Junling Liu, Qinliang Su, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes Skill-RM, a unified reward modeling framework that reformulates reward computation as the execution of a reusable Reward-Evaluation Skill, providing a consistent interface to orchestrate heterogeneous evaluation criteria like rule-based verifiers, references, checklists, and rubrics. Treats reward evaluation as a structured agentic task.

entry.title: EntSQL: A Benchmark for Grounding Text-to-SQL in Long-Context Enterprise Knowledge

author.name: Chengxi Liao, Tao Xu, Zulong Chen, Chuanfei Xu, Yiyan Wang, Xinyun Wang, Yanlong Zhang, Xiaojun Chen, Zhibo Yang, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: Introduces EntSQL, an enterprise-oriented text-to-SQL benchmark requiring long-context grounding over proprietary business documents and organizational knowledge. It contains over 1,000 bilingual examples needing domain knowledge beyond schema and question.

entry.title: Pathway-Structured Privileged Distillation for Deployable Computational Pathology

author.name: Yongxin Guo, Hao Lu, Onur Koyun, Zhengjie Zhu, Muhammet Demir, Metin Gurcan

entry.summary: Proposes MoPE, a privileged-distillation framework that transfers RNA pathway supervision to histology-only inference via pathway-indexed pathology experts for deployable computational pathology. It is motivated by partial observability between transcriptomics and whole-slide images.

entry.title: MLP Splatting: Object-Centric Neural Fields

author.name: Shinjeong Kim, Yuzhou Cheng, Xin Kong, Paul H. J. Kelly, Andrew J. Davison

entry.summary: MLP-Splatting models scenes as a few expressive light-field MLP primitives with localized spatial support, enabling photorealistic novel-view synthesis with built-in object-level decomposition. It avoids the extra segmentation needed by Gaussian or NeRF representations, from Davison's lab.

entry.title: Video-Mirai: Autoregressive Video Diffusion Models Need Foresight

author.name: Yonghao Yu, Lang Huang, Runyi Li, Zerun Wang, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Video-Mirai is a training-only method for autoregressive video diffusion that closes a representation-level planning gap by distilling foresight from a frozen non-causal encoder reading the completed rollout. It keeps causal inference unchanged while improving long-term consistency.

entry.title: AURA: Action-Gated Memory for Robot Policies at Constant VRAM

author.name: Josef Chen

entry.summary: AURA-Mem proposes a constant-size recurrent memory for robot vision-language-action policies that writes only when an observation would change the next action, addressing edge hardware memory constraints. It tackles the mismatch between datacenter KV-cache and embodied agent memory needs.

entry.title: SkillDAG: Self-Evolving Typed Skill Graphs for LLM Skill Selection at Scale

author.name: Tong Bai, Zhenglin Wan, Pengfei Zhou, Xingrui Yu, Wangbo Zhao, Yang You, Ivor W. Tsang

entry.summary: SkillDAG models inter-skill relationships as a typed directed graph exposed to LLM agents as an inference-time structural retrieval interface that evolves during execution. It captures dependencies, conflicts, and duplications invisible to embedding similarity.

entry.title: ClinicalMC: A Benchmark for Multi-Course Clinical Decision-Making with Large Language Models

author.name: Ruihui Hou, Siyi Zhu, Ziyue Huai, Guangya Yu, Yongqi Fan, Chunming Wang, Tong Ruan

entry.summary: ClinicalMC is a bilingual benchmark for multi-course clinical decision-making where a patient's condition evolves across stages from admission to discharge. It contains over 7000 samples spanning triage, diagnosis, treatment, and final diagnosis.

entry.title: StepFinder: A Temporal Semantic Framework for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Taiyu Zhu, Yifan Wu, Weilin Jin, Ying Li, Gang Huang

entry.summary: StepFinder is a temporal semantic framework for failure attribution in multi-agent systems, identifying the root-cause step of cascading failures while reducing the cost and noise of LLM-based reasoning over full trajectories. It addresses interference from redundant execution logs.

entry.title: Bridging Auxiliary Constraints to Resolve Instruction Following in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhengyi Zhao, Shubo Zhang, Huimin Wang, Zezhong Wang, Yutian Zhao, Yefeng Zheng, Binyang Li, Yulan He, Kam-Fai Wong, Xian Wu

entry.summary: Formalizes the Constraint Adherence Problem for large reasoning models that struggle to follow multiple instructions, representing instructions as a knowledge graph of constraints. The CRGC method discovers bridge constraints that help models reconcile competing requirements.

entry.title: SkillPyramid: A Hierarchical Skill Consolidation Framework for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Yuan Xiong, Ziqi Miao, Qian Chen, Lijun Li, Yequan Wang, Shizhu He, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: SkillPyramid is a hierarchical skill consolidation framework for self-evolving agents that reuses, accumulates, and transfers skills across tasks to avoid redundant capability construction. It operates on a hierarchical skill topology with a self-evolution mechanism for generalization.

entry.title: Lean-GAP: A Dataset of Formalized Graduate Algebra Problems

author.name: Seewoo Lee, Byung-Hak Hwang, Hyojae Lim, Jihoon Hyun, Ilkyoo Choi, Yeachan Park, Jineon Baek, Hyukpyo Hong, Keewoo Lee, Jaeseong Heo, Hyungryul Baik, Chul-hee Lee, Kyu-Hwan Lee

entry.summary: Lean-GAP provides 430 formalized graduate-level algebra problems from Dummit and Foote, built via a PDF-to-LaTeX, autoformalization, and verification pipeline in Lean 4. It contributes a structured dataset and methodology for formalizing textbook mathematics.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning of ECG and Angiography Representations for Severe Stenosis Classification

author.name: Nikola Cenikj, \"Ozg\"un Turgut, Alexander M\"uller, Alexander Steger, Jan Kehrer, Marcus Brugger, Daniel Rueckert, Philip M\"uller

entry.summary: FiRe-OPD rethinks optimization granularity in on-policy distillation by jointly adjusting supervision at trajectory and token levels: filtering low-quality rollouts then soft-reweighting informative tokens. It contrasts with hard token selection in recent selective distillation methods.

entry.title: FSA-GRPO: Teaching Auditory LLMs to Use Few-shot Demonstrations

author.name: Haolong Zheng, Siyin Wang, Xulin Fan, Zengrui Jin, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson

entry.summary: FSA-GRPO is an RL post-training recipe that teaches auditory LLMs to better exploit few-shot demonstrations via a reward encouraging use of in-context examples, improving low-resource tasks like children's speech recognition. Training on adult ASR data improves general few-shot adaptation.

entry.title: See Less, Specify More: Visual Evidence Budgets for Generalizable VLAs

author.name: Yueh-Hua Wu, Tatsuya Matsushima, Kei Ota

entry.summary: S2 (See Less, Specify More) improves vision-language-action generalization by relabeling trajectories with refined subtask-level language and imposing an explicit visual evidence budget so the executor attends only to control-relevant image regions. It aims to handle distractors, appearance shifts, and similar tasks better.

entry.title: Plan2Map: A Multimodal Benchmark for Document-Grounded Geospatial Boundary Reconstruction from Planning Records

author.name: Fabian Degen, Oishi Deb, Jindong Gu, Junchi Yu, Samuele Marro, Philip Torr, Jialin Yu

entry.summary: Plan2Map is a 208-case multimodal benchmark for reconstructing geospatial boundaries from UK planning documents, requiring systems to derive machine-readable boundaries from notice text, schedules, and map plates. It introduces GeoPlanAgent, a tool-in-the-loop system decomposing the task into extraction, localization, registration, segmentation, and verification.

entry.title: ConTraIRL: Factorized Contrastive Abstractions for Transferable IRL

author.name: Yikang Gui, Bikramjit Banerjee, Prashant Doshi

entry.summary: ConTraIRL factorizes inverse RL reward representations into separate dynamics and goal latent spaces via dual contrastive learning, enabling compositional reward transfer to unseen dynamics-goal combinations. Tackles a genuine generalization gap in IRL.

entry.title: Regret Pre-training: Bridging Prior and Posterior Views for Enhanced Knowledge Grounding

author.name: Mingkuan Zhao, Xiayu Sun, Wentao Hu, Suquan Chen, Jiaxuan Li, Xiaoyan Zhu, Xin Lai, Jiayin Wang

entry.summary: Regret Pre-training augments causal language modeling with a future-conditioned teacher distribution, transferring future-aware signals to the causal student via KL regret loss under the privileged information paradigm. Aims to improve knowledge grounding.

entry.title: AI Rater Discrimination Depends on Scoring Protocol in Complex Clinical Decision-Making

author.name: Sangwon Baek, Kyu Yeon Hur, Kyunga Kim

entry.summary: Factorial study showing that LLM-as-rater discrimination in complex clinical decision-making (type 2 diabetes pharmacotherapy) depends heavily on whether a rubric-anchored or rubric-free scoring protocol is used. Cautions against unprincipled clinical AI evaluation.

entry.title: AirDreamer: Generalist Drone Navigation with World Models

author.name: Zian Liu, Andong Yang, Chunkai Yang, Ruidong An, Chao Gao, Guyue Zhou

entry.summary: AirDreamer is a generalist drone navigation framework combining an RL policy with world-model-based environment understanding and a sparse reward without hand-crafted shaping. Aims for generalization to unseen cluttered environments inspired by animal navigation.

entry.title: RRISE: Robust Radius Inference via a Surrogate Estimator

author.name: Jong-Ik Park, Shreyas Chaudhari, Carlee Joe-Wong, Jos\'e M. F. Moura

entry.summary: Presents RRISE, a framework that compresses randomized smoothing certification into a single forward pass via a learned surrogate, removing the costly per-input Monte Carlo sampling. Uses conformal calibration to guarantee conservative certified robustness radii.

entry.title: KForge: LLM-Driven Cross-Platform Kernel Generation for AI Accelerators

author.name: Taras Sereda, Burak Bartan, Ankita Nayak, Tom St. John, Natalie Serrino, Zain Asgar

entry.summary: Introduces KForge, an LLM-driven system for generating high-performance GPU/accelerator kernels across heterogeneous hardware backends and programming models. Addresses the systems challenge of cross-platform kernel generation for production inference pipelines.

entry.title: Spatial Transcriptomics-Guided Alignment Enhances Molecular Profiling in Pathology Foundation Model

author.name: Fengtao Zhou, Yingxue Xu, Zhengyu Zhang, Yihui Wang, Zhengrui Guo, Ling Liang, Jiabo Ma, Cheng Jin, Ziyi Liu, Huajun Zhou, Hongyi Wang, Du Cai, Chenglong Zhao, Xi Wang, Can Yang, Yu Wang, Wenbin Li, Feng Gao, Zhe Wang, Zhenhui Li, Xiuming Zhang, Li Liang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes using spatial transcriptomics to provide spatially-resolved molecular supervision for pathology foundation models, aligning subtle morphological features in H&E whole-slide images with genomic alterations. Aims to enable molecular profiling without prohibitive costs and turnaround times.

entry.title: When Graph Tokens Sink: A Mechanistic Analysis of Graph Language Models

author.name: Ding Zhang, Runtao Zhou, Wenqing Zheng, Rizal Fathony, Bayan Bruss, Chirag Agarwal

entry.summary: Conducts a mechanistic analysis of how LLMs internally process graph tokens in Graph Language Models, finding that graph token saliency does not equal information utilization and that graph sink tokens emerge as activation-level outliers. Questions whether graph tokens meaningfully carry graph structure.

entry.title: VESTA: Visual Exploration with Statistical Tool Agents

author.name: William Rudman, Abhishek Divekar, Kanishk Jain, Sebastian Joseph, Stella S. R. Offner, Matthew Lease, Kyle Mahowald, Greg Durrett, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: Introduces VESTA, a framework equipping vision-language models with a dynamically growing toolkit of data transformations, hypothesis-driven visualizations, and statistical tests to iteratively propose and refine quantitative models from data. Actively explores data before and during refinement rather than relying on iterative critique alone.

entry.title: Data-Driven Forecasting of three-Component Seismograms Using Transformer Architectures

author.name: Waleed Esmail, Stuart Russell, Jana Klinge, Alexander Kappes, Christine Thomas

entry.summary: Presents SeeTraceAct, a demo-conditioned vision-language-action framework that improves one-shot imitation by predicting visibility-aware future end-effector traces for precise spatial grounding, with a cross-embodiment evaluation benchmark. Authors include Dieter Fox and collaborators from robotics labs.

entry.title: DMT-CBT: Longitudinal Therapeutic State Modeling for CBT Counseling

author.name: Chang Liu, Shuyi Zhang, Changsheng Ma, Yongfeng Tao, Minqiang Yang, Bin Hu

entry.summary: Reframes LLM-based CBT counseling as longitudinal therapeutic state modeling across sessions rather than single-turn empathetic replies, capturing multimodal and delayed cross-session effects. It argues current formulations mismatch real psychotherapy dynamics.

entry.title: Selective Token-Level Cryptographic Redaction for Privacy-Preserving Clinical Deployment of Large Language Models

author.name: Farhan Sheth, Ziyuan Yang, Yongying Lan, Si Yong Yeo

entry.summary: Proposes HERALD, a token-level cryptographic redaction framework that selectively encrypts sensitive health tokens to enable privacy-preserving clinical LLM deployment without encrypting entire datasets. It balances privacy and usability against prohibitive full-encryption overhead.

entry.title: Can LLM Rerankers Predict Their Own Ranking Performance?

author.name: Shiyu Ni, Keping Bi, Jiafeng Guo, Jingtong Wu, Zengxin Han, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Studies reranker-internal query performance prediction, asking whether an LLM reranker can estimate the quality of the ranking it just produced using self-consistency and verbalized confidence. Experiments on TREC Deep Learning show self-consistency is competitive.

entry.title: GeoDrive-Bench: Benchmarking Region-Specific Multimodal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yingzi Ma, Chaowei Xiao, Ming Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces GeoDrive-Bench, a benchmark of over 5,000 human-validated QA pairs across six countries for evaluating region-specific traffic-rule reasoning in autonomous-driving VLMs. It covers perception, prediction, planning, and region reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Automated Report-Derived Oncology VQA Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language Models on 3D Medical Imaging

author.name: Bo Liu, Hanxue Gu, Xiangru Li, Zheren Zhu, Jacob Ellison, Kang Wang, Janine M. Lupo, Yang Yang, Hui Lin

entry.summary: Presents an automated agent-driven pipeline that generates multiple-choice VQA datasets from paired private radiology reports and 3D oncology imaging, avoiding pretraining leakage. It produces RADS-style and report-derived questions verified against source reports.

entry.title: SaluNet: Enabling Total Plasticity in Normalization-Free Deep Networks

author.name: Mourad Zaied (University of Gabes, Tuisia)

entry.summary: Demonstrates that normalization layers can be fully replaced by a single learnable bounded activation called SALU, identifying a plasticity-suppression effect induced by standard normalization. It proposes SaluNet, a normalization-free network achieving total plasticity.

entry.title: Ask When It Pays: Cost-Aware Open-Ended Interaction for Instance Goal Navigation

author.name: Xunyi Zhao, Sihao Lin, Gengze Zhou, Zerui Li, Shijie Li, Wei Tao, Jiajun Liu, Qi Wu

entry.summary: Recasts interactive instance goal navigation as a cost-sensitive uncertainty-reduction problem where an embodied agent asks the question that most reduces navigation uncertainty rather than spamming high-information queries. It distinguishes lightweight clarification from route-level guidance.

entry.title: MemoGen: Can Past Experience Improve Future Text-to-Image Generation?

author.name: Wenshuo Chen, Kuimou Yu, Bowen Tian, Jianfei Song, Shaofeng Liang, Haozhe Jia, Kan Cheng, Haosen Li, Kaishen Yuan, Lei Wang, Jiemin Wu, Songning Lai, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Proposes MemoGen, a training-free framework that lets text-to-image systems continually improve by preserving and reusing past generation successes and failures via an agentic memory, without updating the generator. It targets prompts requiring implicit constraints, relational reasoning, or external knowledge.

entry.title: BA-T: An Iterative Transformer for Two-View Bundle Adjustment

author.name: Ganlin Zhang, Weirong Chen, Daniel Cremers, Xi Wang

entry.summary: BA-T is an iterative Transformer that mimics classical bundle adjustment as a lightweight repeatable layer in token space for two-view 3D reconstruction. It improves multi-view consistency without heavy decoder stacks, from a credible group (Cremers lab).

entry.title: Attend to Anything: Foundation Model for Unified Human Attention Modeling

author.name: Wenzhuo Zhao, Ronghao Xian, Keren Fu, Qijun Zhao

entry.summary: The Attend to Anything Model is a multimodal foundation model unifying human attention/saliency prediction across image, video, and audio-visual tasks via hierarchical hyperbolic embeddings driven by language prompts. It reframes attention as a general-to-specific cognitive entailment.

entry.title: Investigating Adversarial Robustness of Multi-modal Large Language Models

author.name: Hashmat Shadab Malik, Muzammal Naseer, Salman Khan

entry.summary: This paper systematically investigates adversarial robustness of multimodal LLMs, arguing that strict alignment to CLIP's embedding space during adversarial fine-tuning fundamentally limits achievable robustness. It introduces a diagnostic protocol predicting which robust vision encoders transfer well.

entry.title: Unified Video-Action Joint Denoising for Dexterous Action and Data Generation

author.name: Dingrui Wang, YuAn Wang, Jinkun Liu, Yue Zhang, Mattia Piccinini, Yu Sun, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: Donk is a unified video-action joint denoising model for dexterous hands that models the joint space of interaction videos and bimanual hand trajectories under multiple conditioning regimes. It can act as an action policy or a data generator depending on conditioning.

entry.title: OVO-S-Bench: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Streaming Spatial Intelligence in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Yifei Li, Pengyiang Liu, Yuhang Zang, Zhongyue Shi, Qi Fu, Hongye Hao, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: OVO-S-Bench is a fully human-annotated benchmark for streaming spatial intelligence in MLLMs, with 1,680 questions over 348 videos requiring reasoning about layouts using out-of-view evidence. Models see only the prefix before each query, testing online spatial memory.

entry.title: AAD-1: Asymmetric Adversarial Distillation for One-Step Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Haobo Li, Yanhong Zeng, Yunhong Lu, Jiapeng Zhu, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Ka Leong Cheng, Yujun Shen, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: AAD-1 is an asymmetric adversarial distillation framework for one-step autoregressive image-to-video generation that breaks generator-discriminator symmetry, using a bidirectional discriminator over the full sequence. This addresses motion collapse and training instability in prior distillation methods.

entry.title: SimuScene: Simulation-Ready Compositional 3D Scene Reconstruction from a Single Image

author.name: Inhee Lee, Sangwon Baik, Sungjoo Kim, Hyeonwoo Kim, Hyunsoo Cha, Hanbyul Joo

entry.summary: SimuScene reconstructs simulation-ready compositional 3D scenes from a single image by putting a physics engine in the loop as a diagnostic tool during shape and layout estimation. It resolves interpenetrating, hovering, and sinking objects that collapse under simulation.

entry.title: GN0: Toward a Unified Paradigm for Generation, Evaluation, and Policy Learning in Visual-Language Navigation

author.name: Xinhai Li, Xiaotao Zhang, Yuehao Huang, Jiankun Dong, Tianhang Wang, Sunyao Zhou, Yunzi Wu, Chengnuo Sun, Yunfei Ge, Qizhen Weng, Chi Zhang, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: GN0 proposes a unified paradigm for visual-language navigation spanning data generation, evaluation, and policy learning, including the large GN-Matrix dataset, a 3D Gaussian Splatting simulation platform, and GN-Bench, a BEV benchmark with dynamic avatars for human-robot interaction. It targets the data scarcity that limits VLN generalization.

entry.title: Making Embodied AI Reliable: A Community Agenda from Testing to Formal Verification

author.name: Xi Zheng, Dulanga Weerakoon, Yintong Huo, Teresa Yeo, Guy Van Den Broeck, Vijay Ganesh, Daniel Neider, Biplav Srivastava, Ivan Ruchkin, Archan Misra, Corina Pasareanu

entry.summary: This community-agenda article, drawn from an AAAI'26 bridge program, argues that reliability in embodied AI is a lifecycle assurance problem and identifies three directions: trustworthy scenario-based testing, compositional formal verification via symbolic representations, and runtime monitoring of emergent behaviors. It frames assurance across tightly coupled, uncertain, human-interacting systems.

entry.title: Traj-Evolve: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Patient Trajectory Modeling in Lung Cancer Early Detection

author.name: Sihang Zeng, Matthew Thompson, Ruth Etzioni, Meliha Yetisgen

entry.summary: Traj-Evolve is a self-evolving multi-agent system for lung cancer early detection that uses a non-parametric experience pool and multi-agent reinforcement learning to leverage similar prior patient cases. It mimics how clinicians use accumulated experience.

entry.title: ToolGate: Token-Efficient Pre-Call Control for Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Agents

author.name: Anjie Liu, Yan Song, Zhixun Chen, Ziqin Gong, Zhongwei Yu, Jun Wang

entry.summary: ToolGate is a lightweight external controller for tool-augmented vision-language agents that decides whether to execute or skip proposed perceptual tool calls before they enter context. It addresses poor local selectivity in baseline agents to save tokens.

entry.title: DELTAMEM: Incremental Experience Memory for LLM Agents via Residual Trees

author.name: Haoran Tan, Zeyu Zhang, Zhicheng Cao, Rui Li, Xu Chen

entry.summary: DeltaMem organizes LLM agent experience memory into residual trees, treating new experience as incremental variations of existing knowledge to reduce redundancy and retrieval conflicts. It separates goal-conditioned skills from scene-level environment knowledge.

entry.title: CP-Agent: Context-Aware Multimodal Reasoning for Cellular Morphological Profiling under Chemical Perturbations

author.name: Yuxin Zhang, Yiyao Li, Ping Shu Ho, Simon See, Zhenqin Wu, Kevin Tsia

entry.summary: CP-Agent is an agentic multimodal LLM for Cell Painting morphological profiling that incorporates experimental context like cell line and dosing schedule to generate interpretable mechanism-of-action rationales. It targets faster, cheaper, more interpretable drug screening.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Tabular Diffusion

author.name: David Turtora Zagardo

entry.summary: Geometry-Aware Tabular Diffusion augments tabular diffusion denoisers with pairwise angles and lengths from column differences as inputs and auxiliary targets to better capture inter-column relationships. It achieves state-of-the-art tabular synthesis with up to 25x fewer parameters.

entry.title: Attention Calibration for Position-Fair Dense Information Retrieval

author.name: Andrianos Michail, Elias Schuhmacher, Juri Opitz, Simon Clematide, Rico Sennrich

entry.summary: This paper adapts inference-time attention calibration to reduce positional bias in dense retrieval—where relevance degrades when key information appears later in a passage—without retraining, adding a strength coefficient to interpolate calibration. It studies trade-offs between positional fairness and retrieval effectiveness.

entry.title: Representational Capacity: Geometric Limits on Feature Representation in Transformer Language Models

author.name: Alexander Guha

entry.summary: This paper develops a framework for estimating how many near-orthogonal feature directions a transformer can represent given its model dimension, grounded in the linear representation and superposition hypotheses. It uses the embedding matrix's cosine similarity distribution as a measurable proxy for representational capacity.

entry.title: WRIT: Write-Read Intensive Trajectory Synthesis for Multi-Turn User-Facing Agents

author.name: Hengrui Gu, Xiaotian Han, Kaixiong Zhou

entry.summary: WRIT is a trajectory synthesis method for multi-turn user-facing agents that creates read-intensive tasks where the agent must gather and compare substantial tool evidence before its action arguments become identifiable, contrasting with write-intensive composed tasks. It targets a harder, underrepresented form of agentic difficulty.

entry.title: Conditional Hypothesis Generation for LLM-Based Text Analysis with Researcher-Specified Covariates

author.name: Paiheng Xu, Jing Liu, Wei Ai

entry.summary: Introduces conditional hypothesis generation for LLM-based text analysis, incorporating researcher-specified covariates to steer discovery of language differences within relevant subgroups rather than confounded global patterns. Targeted at computational social science.

entry.title: PhotoCraft: Agentic Reasoning with Hierarchical Self-Evolving Memory for Deep Image Search

author.name: Kailin Lyu, Zhiqiang Yuan, Jianwei He, Qiwei Yan, Xuanbo Su, Nanxing Hu, Yang Liu, Ce Hao, Shengqian Qin, Lianyu Hu, Jinchao Zhang, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: PhotoCraft is a training-free hierarchical memory system (working, episodic, semantic) for MLLM photo-search agents to maintain long-horizon context and transfer experience across tasks. Addresses execution drift in stateless reactive agents.

entry.title: AI-Generated Traces for Novice Programmers: Learning Effects and Learner Differences in a Multi-Institutional Study

author.name: Yuri Noviello, Naaz Sibia, Anastasiia Birillo, Thomas Overklift Vaupel Klein, Michael Liut, Gosia Migut

entry.summary: Multi-institutional study (N over 1100 students) comparing AI-generated animated execution traces (GATs) to textual explanations in introductory programming courses. Finds selective immediate learning benefits but mixed effects on engagement and exam performance.

entry.title: FlowGuard: Flow Matching for Identity-Independent Detection of Data-Free Model Stealing Attacks on Energy System Intrusion Detection Systems

author.name: Maxime Schwarzer, Laurin Holz, Tobias Huerten, Johannes Loevenich, Thies Moehlenhof, Roberto Rigolin F. Lopes, Veit Hagenmeyer

entry.summary: FlowGuard is an identity-independent defense against data-free model stealing on energy-system intrusion detection systems, using flow matching to classify incoming queries as out-of-distribution before processing. Works for hard-label deployments where prediction poisoning is inapplicable.

entry.title: FORGE: Multi-Agent Graduated Exploitation and Detection Engineering

author.name: Farooq Shaikh

entry.summary: FORGE is a five-agent system bridging proof-of-concept generation, vulnerability prioritization, and detection rule engineering through graduated exploitation depth, producing partial-progress signals instead of binary pass/fail. Connects three previously siloed security research communities.

entry.title: High-Precision APT Malware Attribution with Out-of-Scope Resilience

author.name: Peter Williams, Adam Sobey, Erisa Karafili

entry.summary: Presents a high-precision APT malware attribution method with out-of-scope resilience, recognizing that operational classifiers encounter samples from groups not seen during training. Moves beyond closed-set classification that forces misleading attributions onto known groups.

entry.title: BYORn: Bootstrap Your Own Responses to Defend Large Vision-Language Models Against Backdoor Attacks

author.name: Ivan Saboli\'c, Marin Or\v{s}i\'c, Josip \v{S}ari\'c, Sven Lon\v{c}ari\'c

entry.summary: Proposes BYORn, a backdoor-robust fine-tuning framework for vision-language models that detects semantically implausible poisoned responses and replaces them with model-generated alternatives, breaking trigger-target correlations. Targets open-ended generation settings where existing defenses fail.

entry.title: Speedrunning Tabular Foundation Model Pretraining

author.name: Salih Bora Ozturk, Alexander Pfefferle, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Introduces a community speedrun for tabular foundation model pretraining (nanoTabPFN) where contributors compete to reach a fixed downstream ROC AUC on one GPU, achieving an 81x speedup over baseline with 22x fewer synthetic datasets. Provides an open protocol to accumulate and verify pretraining improvements.

entry.title: TreeFlash: Parallel AR-Approximation for Faster Speculative Decoding

author.name: Peer Rheinboldt, Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Proposes TreeFlash, which improves one-shot block drafters for speculative decoding by adding an MLP layer conditioned on the drafter's hidden state and previous token, restoring autoregressive dependence between draft tokens. Addresses distribution divergence in tree-based drafting where branches share marginals.

entry.title: Correcting Neural Operator Spectral Bias via Diffusion Posterior Sampling with Sparse Observations

author.name: Niccol\`o Perrone, Fanny Lehmann, Stefania Fresca, Filippo Gatti

entry.summary: Addresses spectral bias in neural operator PDE surrogates (systematic attenuation of high frequencies) by treating neural operator predictions as auxiliary observations in a diffusion posterior sampling framework, combined with sparse sensor measurements. Proposes FreqNO-DPS to recover fine-scale structure.

entry.title: RogueMerge: Robust and Unified Attacks against LLM Model Merging

author.name: Jinghuai Zhang, Yetian He, Kunlin Cai, Han Zhao, Fnu Suya, Yuan Tian

entry.summary: Introduces RogueMerge, a robust unified attack against LLM model merging that exploits the supply-chain risk of aggregating unverified task vectors, enabling diverse downstream threats beyond prior static backdoor attacks. Demonstrates attacks on generative LLMs handling autoregressive decoding drift.

entry.title: SenseJudge: Human-Centric Preference-Driven Judgment Framework

author.name: Rui Li, Junfeng Liu, Xiangwen Kong, Linhai Xu, Zhifang Sui

entry.summary: Proposes SenseJudge, a customizable preference-driven LLM-as-judge framework, plus SenseBench, a benchmark from real multi-turn interactions for personalized judging and model ranking. Aims to capture diverse user preferences ignored by fixed-preference judges.

entry.title: Re-Ranking Through an Attribution Lens for Citation Quality in Legal QA

author.name: Mohamed Hesham Elganayni, Selim Saleh

entry.summary: Re-ranks passages for legal QA using perturbation-based attribution rather than semantic similarity, training a cross-encoder on continuous attribution signals. It shows semantic similarity poorly predicts which passages get usefully cited.

entry.title: Reasoning over Grammar: Can Synthetic Linguistic Reasoning Traces Enhance Low-Resource Machine Translation?

author.name: Renhao Pei, Yihong Liu, Sampo Pyysalo, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Shaoxiong Ji

entry.summary: Investigates whether synthetic linguistic reasoning traces generated from Universal Dependencies treebanks, dictionaries, and grammar banks can improve low-resource machine translation via ICL, SFT, and other settings. It tests if structured grammatical reasoning helps LLMs apply linguistic knowledge.

entry.title: KC-3DGS: Kurtosis-Constrained Gaussian Splatting for High-Fidelity View Synthesis

author.name: Vivekjyoti Banerjee, Abhay Yadav, Rama Chellappa, Aniket Roy

entry.summary: Proposes KC-3DGS, augmenting 3D Gaussian Splatting with wavelet-domain supervision and kurtosis constraints based on natural image statistics to penalize missing high-frequency detail. It reduces oversmoothing and structural artifacts, especially in sparse-view settings.

entry.title: Enginuity: A Dataset and Benchmark for Vision-Language Understanding of Engineering Diagrams

author.name: Abhishek Kumar, Isha Motiyani, Tilak Kasturi, Ethan Seefried, Prahitha Movva, Tirthankar Ghosal

entry.summary: Enginuity is the first open benchmark for evaluating vision-language models on complex engineering diagrams, with tasks like structured parts-table extraction from military service manuals. It fills a gap not covered by flowchart or scientific-figure datasets.

entry.title: PersistGS: Differentiable Physics for Object Permanence in 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Adrian Ramlal, John S. Zelek

entry.summary: PersistGS couples differentiable rigid body simulation with 4D Gaussian Splatting to maintain object permanence during full occlusions, where photometric supervision vanishes. It enforces physical correctness rather than relying on generative priors.

entry.title: GARDEN: Gravity-Aligned Reconstruction of Disentangled ENvironments from RGB images

author.name: Jiahao Sun, Dingkun Wei, Zehong Shen, Hongyu Zhou, Yujun Shen, Liang Li

entry.summary: GARDEN is an RGB-only framework that reformulates multi-view reconstruction as physically-grounded scene factorization, producing gravity-aligned, disentangled foreground objects and background for simulation-ready environments. It avoids slow CAD retrieval-and-replacement.

entry.title: PixVOD: Pixel-Distributed Direct Visual Odometry and Depth Estimation

author.name: Shinjeong Kim, Ignacio Alzugaray, Callum Rhodes, Paul H. J. Kelly, Andrew J. Davison

entry.summary: PixVOD proposes fully parallelizable visual odometry and depth estimation distributed across pixels, where focal-plane sensor-processors exchange information via Gaussian Belief Propagation to reach consensus on camera motion. It targets in-sensor computation to reduce off-sensor data transmission.

entry.title: BEAST3D: Animal behavioral analysis and neural encoding from multi-view video via Gaussian splatting

author.name: Yanchen Wang, Lenny Aharon, Wangshu Zhu, Kyle Daruwalla, Linghua Zhang, Jiaru Zou, Selmaan Chettih, Helen Hou, Liam Paninski, Matthew R Whiteway

entry.summary: BEAST3D is a self-supervised pretraining framework that learns 3D visual representations from unlabeled calibrated multi-view animal video by predicting 3D Gaussian splats and segmenting subjects, for behavioral analysis and neural encoding. It avoids extensive manual pose annotation in laboratory settings.

entry.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Joint Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Jaemin Jung, Kyeongha Rho, Inkyu Shin, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: This paper presents the first comprehensive study of Inference-Time Scaling for joint audio-video generation, showing a multi-verifier framework is essential to balance heterogeneous semantic and synchronization objectives. It extends training-free ITS from single-modality to multimodal generation.

entry.title: Partially Observable Adversarial Patch Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models in Robotics

author.name: Xiaofei Wang, Mingliang Han, Tianyu Hao, Yi Yang, Yun-Bo Zhao, Keke Tang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a more realistic partially observable adversarial patch threat model against VLA-based robots, where the attacker sees only a short trajectory prefix and applies a fixed patch to all subsequent frames. It uses attention maps to localize and optimize an effective patch.

entry.title: Denoising Tells When to Replan: Denoising-Variance Adaptive Chunking for Flow-Based Robot Policies

author.name: Xiangdong Feng, Yuxuan Cheng, Chen Shi, Boyao Han, Yuxuan Yan, Yitong Hong, Zhuotao Tian, Li Jiang

entry.summary: DVAC observes that flow-based policy denoising encodes an intrinsic task-phase signal—clean-action estimates stay stable during predictable motion but fluctuate near contact-rich phases—and uses denoising variance to adaptively decide replanning frequency. This replaces fixed empirical action-chunk horizons.

entry.title: ChatHealthAI: Aligning Electronic Health Record Representations with Large Language Models for Grounded Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Bo-Hong Wang, Baicheng Peng, Ruilin Wang, Jun Bai, Ziyang Song, Yue Li

entry.summary: ChatHealthAI aligns structured longitudinal EHR representations from a foundation model with a frozen LLM's semantic space via a task-aware resampler. The goal is to combine predictive patient modeling with interpretable language-based clinical reasoning.

entry.title: AUDITFLOW: Executable Symbolic Environments for Structured Financial Reporting Verification

author.name: Yan Wang, Xuguang Ai, Jaisal Patel, Xueqing Peng, Fengran Mo, Yupeng Cao, Haohang Li, Mingyu Cao, Lingfei Qian, V\'ictor Guti\'errez-Basulto

entry.summary: AuditFlow is a graph-grounded multi-agent framework for financial audit verification that separates adaptive search from deterministic verification using US-GAAP taxonomy and XBRL filing graphs. It exposes typed tools for fact retrieval and numerical checking.

entry.title: From Long News to Accurate Forecast: Importance-Aware Fusion and PRM-Guided Reflection for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Mingyang Liu, Qingcan Kang, Yuke Wang, Shixiong Kai, Kaichao Liang, Hui-Ling Zhen, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan, Linqi Song

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for news-aware time series forecasting combining importance-aware news compression with process-level retrieval supervision via a learned importance reward model. It handles long news exceeding context windows and unguided iterative retrieval.

entry.title: Overlaying Governance: A Compositional Authorization Framework for Delegation and Scope in Agentic AI

author.name: Amjad Ibrahim, Yong Li

entry.summary: Proposes a compositional authorization framework for agentic AI supporting recursive delegation, time-limited authority, contextual boundaries, and dynamic scoping as executable governance primitives. It addresses limitations of traditional IAM systems for autonomous agents.

entry.title: When to Re-Plan: Subgoal Persistence in Hierarchical Latent Reasoning

author.name: Ayushi Chadha

entry.summary: Studies the stability-adaptivity tradeoff in latent hierarchical reasoning by extending the Hierarchical Reasoning Model with a manager-worker interface where a slow module emits persistent directional subgoals. It finds subgoal persistence aids long-horizon reasoning on ARC tasks.

entry.title: Proof-Refactor: Refactoring Generated Formal Proofs into Modular Artifacts

author.name: Yiming Fu, Peixuan Liu, Zichen Wang, Kun yuan

entry.summary: Proof-Refactor refactors LLM-generated formal proofs into modular, readable, maintainable, and reusable artifacts, addressing the monolithic ad hoc scripts produced by compile-first generation objectives. It tackles quality dimensions beyond length-based optimization.

entry.title: ReLoRA: Knowledge-Reusing Adaptation for Fast Rollout of Evolving LLM Services

author.name: Yang Xu, Zihuai Xu, Hongli Xu, Yunming Liao, Zhiwei Yao, Xitong Fu

entry.summary: ReLoRA is a knowledge-reusing re-adaptation framework that efficiently restores task-specific LoRA adapters when the underlying base model is updated, avoiding full retraining. It targets service providers managing many evolving LLM services with adapter-backbone incompatibility issues.

entry.title: Echo-POSED: Geometric Self-Distillation for Echocardiography Guidance

author.name: Elias Stenhede, Edvart Gr\"uner Bjerke, Joanna Sulkowska, Eivind Bj{\o}rkan Orstad, Ole Jakob Elle, Ulysse C\^ot\'e-Allard, Arian Ranjbar

entry.summary: Echo-POSED is a self-supervised framework for real-time echocardiography guidance that recommends probe adjustments from 2D images without expert-labeled views or tracked trajectories, training on slices from 3D volumes. It learns an SO(3)xSO(3) pose representation enforcing equivariance to probe motion.

entry.title: SegTune: Structured and Fine-Grained Control for Song Generation

author.name: Yuejiao Wang, Zihao Ji, Pengfei Cai, Xu Li, Haorui Zheng, Zewen Song, Zhongliang Liu, Chen Zhang, Pengfei Wan

entry.summary: SegTune is a Diffusion Transformer framework for song generation enabling fine-grained, segment-level control via local musical descriptions broadcast to time windows, with an LLM-based duration predictor for lyric-to-music alignment. It addresses the lack of temporally varying control in existing song generators.

entry.title: AdaWeather: Adaptively Mixing Probabilistic Weather Forecasts with Logarithmic Regret

author.name: Saptarishi Dhanuka (Ashoka University), Sarvesh Iyer (Ashoka University), Manmeet Singh (Western Kentucky University), Mihir More (Ashoka University), Rushil Gupta (Ashoka University), Dhruman Gupta (Ashoka University), Parthasarathi Mukhopadhyay (Ashoka University), Sandeep Juneja (Ashoka University)

entry.summary: AdaWeather is an adaptive framework that combines multiple probabilistic weather forecasts using both machine learning and mixture-of-experts methods with logarithmic regret guarantees. It addresses that no single forecasting model dominates spatio-temporally.

entry.title: Which Defense Closes Which Threat? Attributing OWASP-LLM-Top-10 Coverage and Its Brittleness Under Paraphrasing

author.name: Alexandre Cristov\~ao Maiorano

entry.summary: This paper measures which LLM defense families (refusal filters, token budgets, model allowlists, rate limits, tool-registry auth) close which OWASP-LLM-Top-10 threats, moving beyond single aggregate coverage numbers. It tests defense layers across four synthetic endpoints and examines brittleness under paraphrasing attacks.

entry.title: Echelon: Auditable Aggregate-Only Language-Model Adaptation Across Privacy Boundaries

author.name: Hina Dixit, Punit Kumar, Irene Tenison, Nevasini Sasikumar

entry.summary: Echelon is a boundary-first training architecture for cross-organization LLM adaptation that enforces device-level model-state non-export as a systems invariant, exchanging only securely aggregated boundary-level deltas and minimal coordination metadata. It targets hard governance constraints where device state cannot leave administrative boundaries.

entry.title: Learn When and Where to Connect: Adaptive Virtual Nodes for Dynamic Message Passing on Graphs

author.name: Jaejun Lee, Joyce Jiyoung Whang

entry.summary: MAVN is a differentiable message-passing framework that adaptively introduces virtual nodes on demand, deciding when (which layer) and where (which nodes) to connect based on evolving representations. Removes rigidity of fixed virtual-node connectivity in GNNs.

entry.title: OpenAgenet/OAN: Open Infrastructure for Trusted Agent Interconnection

author.name: Jinliang Xu

entry.summary: OpenAgenet (OAN) is an open infrastructure project providing a protocol-neutral trust layer for verifying agent identity provenance, governance state, and pre-connection trust evidence in open multi-operator agent networks. Complements interaction protocols like MCP and A2A.

entry.title: Fully Automated Identification of Lexical Alignment and Preference-Stage Shifts in Large Language Models

author.name: Thomas Stephan Juzek, Xiaoyang Ming, Jose A. Hernandez

entry.summary: Introduces two curation-free metrics, Lexical Alignment Score and Triangulated Preference Shift, to automatically detect lexical overuse and attribute it to human preference learning in LLMs. Applied to PubMed abstracts across six model families.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Scale Hypergraph for High-Order Brain Connectivity Analysis

author.name: Jaeyoon Sim, Soojin Hwang, Seunghun Baek, Guorong Wu, Won Hwa Kim

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive multi-scale hypergraph learning method for high-order brain connectivity analysis to classify neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. Overcomes limitations of predefined hyperedges and pairwise-only graph models.

entry.title: dstack-capsule: Pod-Level Remote Attestation for Confidential Workloads on Kubernetes

author.name: Yang Yang, Kevin Wang, Yuanhai Luo, Hang Yin, Jie Cai, Shunfan Zhou, Wenfeng Wang

entry.summary: dstack-capsule enables pod-level remote attestation on Intel TDX for confidential Kubernetes workloads, allowing multiple pods to share one confidential VM while each retains hardware-backed identity proof. Addresses cost and granularity limits of existing confidential containers for LLM-as-a-Service.

entry.title: FGRPO: Federated GRPO with Adaptive Aggregation on Non-IID Data

author.name: Pengyu Chen, Shaowei Li, Kai Wang, Yunsheng Yuan, Kai Han, Jun Luo, Feng Li

entry.summary: Introduces FGRPO, a federated version of GRPO for decentralized reasoning-model fine-tuning across heterogeneous data owners without centralizing private data. Uses adaptive aggregation based on relative reward scales to handle divergent reward distributions across non-IID tasks.

entry.title: A Geometric Lens on Physics-Aligned Data Compression

author.name: Aleix Segui, Wesley Armour

entry.summary: Develops a local geometric theory explaining the rate-distortion tradeoffs of physics-informed losses in learned scientific data compressors, showing that preserving a physical observable can degrade reconstruction fidelity due to misaligned latent sensitivities. Frames the tradeoff as anisotropic error allocation governed by directional alignment.

entry.title: Easy-to-Use Shielding for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Stefan Pranger, Bettina K\"onighofer

entry.summary: Provides easy-to-use end-to-end shielding infrastructure connecting formal shield synthesis with standard RL frameworks for safe exploration, addressing the engineering and formal-methods barriers that have limited shielding adoption. Aims to prevent harmful agent decisions during exploration.

entry.title: MAdam: Metric-Aware Multi-Objective Adam

author.name: Fengbei Liu, Rachit Saluja, Sunwoo Kwak, Ruibo Wang, Ruining Deng, Heejong Kim, Johannes C. Paetzold, Mert R. Sabuncu

entry.summary: Introduces MAdam, a metric-aware multi-objective Adam optimizer that fixes two gaps when MOO solvers hand reconciled directions to Adam: a weighting mismatch where Adam's second moment entangles preference vectors with gradient statistics, and a geometric mismatch where Adam's adaptive metric distorts assumed Euclidean geometry. Aims to faithfully execute solver intent across Pareto trade-offs.

entry.title: The Geometry of LLM-as-Judge: Why Inter-LLM Consensus Is Not Human Alignment

author.name: Sourabrata Mukherjee, Hamna Hamna, Kalika Bali, Sunayana Sitaram

entry.summary: Measures the geometry of LLM-as-judge evaluation across Indic datasets and 41 judges, showing judges use less than half the human score range and that their evaluation axis is nearly orthogonal to the human one. Argues inter-LLM consensus reflects shared bias rather than human alignment.

entry.title: Principled Reflection Separation via Nonlinear Superposition and Feature Interaction

author.name: Qiming Hu, Mingjia Li, Yuntong Li, Xiaojie Guo

entry.summary: Revisits single-image reflection separation, showing the standard linear composition model in sRGB fails to capture nonlinear coupling from real image signal processing. It introduces a learnable nonlinear superposition model to improve decomposition fidelity.

entry.title: Towards Characterizing Scientific Image Utility and Upgradability

author.name: WenZhe Li, Qihang Yan, Liang Chen, Junying Wang, Farong Wen, Yijin Guo, Chunyi Li, Zicheng Zhang, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: SIU2A is a framework for evaluating scientific images on utility (error detection and correction feasibility) rather than perceptual quality, addressing AI-generated content threats to research integrity. It introduces new evaluation dimensions for scientific image validity.

entry.title: TrAction: Action Recognition with Sparse Trajectories

author.name: Jan F. Meier, Felix B. Mueller, Alexander Ecker, Timo L\"uddecke

entry.summary: TrAction proposes sparse point-trajectory based action recognition using a simple Transformer with masked-trajectory pretraining, avoiding appearance/background shortcuts of dense RGB models. It achieves competitive accuracy with a fraction of the input.

entry.title: Knowledge-Preserved Model Tuning in Null-Space for Robust Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Haoxuan Chen, Xianqin Liu, Jian-Fang Hu

entry.summary: Null-Space Tuning injects learnable residuals into the null space of frozen weights to adapt spatio-temporal video grounding models to low-quality inputs without disrupting pretrained knowledge. It exploits the geometric property that null-space additions leave outputs unchanged.

entry.title: Beyond False Stability: High-Noise Drift Gating for Test-Time Adversarial Defenses in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hashmat Shadab Malik, Muzammal Naseer, Salman Khan

entry.summary: This work identifies a high-noise drift gating regime for test-time adversarial defenses in CLIP-style VLMs, improving the clean-robust trade-off that prior stochastic defenses degrade. It revisits how CLIP representations respond across noise regimes.

entry.title: Demo2Tutorial: From Human Experience to Multimodal Software Tutorials

author.name: Zechen Bai, Zhiheng Chen, Yiqi Lin, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Difei Gao, Xiangwu Guo, Xin Wang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Demo2Tutorial transforms screen recordings and interaction logs into structured multimodal software tutorials via an action parser, step planner, and tutorial composer producing hierarchical task graphs. It aims to teach both humans and agents from authentic untrimmed interactions.

entry.title: Depth from Dual Differential Defocus and Stereo Consensus

author.name: Junjie Luo, Wei Xu, Dylan Chu, Emma Alexander, Qi Guo

entry.summary: D3S Consensus is a physics-based closed-form algorithm unifying depth-from-defocus and stereo for accurate depth estimation beyond camera depth-of-field, achieving comparable range with a 10x smaller baseline. It enforces consensus between physically independent cues to reject unreliable estimates.

entry.title: GeoAlign: Beyond Semantics with State-Guided Spatial Alignment in VLA Models

author.name: Yizhi Chen, Zhanxiang Cao, Xinyi Peng, Yixiao Zheng, Xiaxi Si, Yiheng Li, Liyun Yan, Keqi Zhu, Xueyun Chen, Shengcheng Fu, Tianyue Zhan, Yufei Jia, Jinming Yao, Yan Xie, Kun Wang, Cewu Lu, Yue Gao

entry.summary: GeoAlign augments VLA policies with state-guided spatial alignment, post-training an RGB geometry branch using RGB-D supervision and querying geometry tokens with proprioceptive state for action prediction. It reports strong results including 99% on LIBERO and 78.8% on geometry-critical real-world ALOHA tasks.

entry.title: OpenEAI-Platform: An Open-source Embodied Artificial Intelligence Hardware-Software Unified Platform

author.name: Jinyuan Zhang, Luoyi Fan, Leiyu Wang, Yeqiang Wang, Yicheng Zhu, Cewu Lu, Nanyang Ye

entry.summary: OpenEAI-Platform is a fully open-source embodied AI stack pairing a low-cost 6+1-DoF robotic arm with a reproducible VLA model built on Qwen3-VL-4B and a diffusion-transformer action head. The arm reportedly outperforms two commercial arms under the same policy, and the VLA is trained only on open datasets.

entry.title: The Value Function Semi-Algebraic Set in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Ryan A. Anderson, Guido Montufar

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the feasible set of value functions in infinite-horizon POMDPs under memoryless stochastic policies as a semi-algebraic set defined by explicit polynomial inequalities from the model's dynamics, observations, and rewards. It extends the known polytope structure for MDPs to the nonlinear partially observable setting.

entry.title: Visual Graph Scaffolds for Structural Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Runlin Lei, Xiaokui Xiao, Zhewei Wei

entry.summary: This paper explores using graph-structured mind maps as an internal reasoning scaffold for LLMs in multi-hop question answering, rather than just as external knowledge. It identifies a modality gap where flattening graphs into text loses their organizational value.

entry.title: Perceive Before Reasoning: A Pre-Reasoning Perception Framework for Efficient and Reliable Proactive Mobile Agents

author.name: Zhijie Ding (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation, Zhongnan University of Economics and Law), Weinan Hong (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation, Jilin University), Zicheng Zhu (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen), Lei Li (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation), Dezhi Kong (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation), Hao Wang (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation), Peng Zhou (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation), Xuchu Jiang (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation), Jiaming Xu (HyperAI Team, Xiaomi Corporation)

entry.summary: The Pre-Reasoning Perception Framework (PRPF) for proactive mobile agents separates the decision of when to intervene from how to assist, using a lightweight multimodal perceptor for intervention gating. It aims to avoid goal misalignment and redundant inference when agents should stay silent.

entry.title: Distilling Answer-Set Programming Rules from LLMs for Neurosymbolic Visual Question Answering

author.name: Thomas Eiter, Nelson Higuera Ruiz, Johannes Oetsch

entry.summary: Presents a method for distilling answer-set programming rules from LLMs to extend a neurosymbolic visual question answering reasoning theory when task requirements change. It prompts an LLM to extend an answer-set program guided by VQA examples.

entry.title: A formal definition and meta-model for a machine theory of mind

author.name: Fabio Cuzzolin

entry.summary: Proposes a rigorous formal definition and holistic meta-model for Machine Theory of Mind, grounded in cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and AI. It uses this lens to examine state-of-the-art efforts and benchmarking, setting a research agenda.

entry.title: PyraMathBench: Evaluating and Improving Mathematical Capability in Large Language Models

author.name: Zetian Ouyang, Linlin Wang, Gerard de Melo, Liang He

entry.summary: PyraMathBench is a hierarchical benchmark of 32505 questions derived from math word problems integrating numerical processing and mathematical reasoning across cognitive aspects and modalities. It introduces the SOLVE module to address weaknesses in numerical computation and abstract numerical reasoning.

entry.title: scTranslation: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Single-Cell Multi-Omics Modality Translation

author.name: Jiabei Cheng, Jingbo Zhou, Jun Xia, Changkai Li, Zhen Lei, Chang Yu, Stan Z. Li

entry.summary: scTranslation is a comprehensive benchmark for single-cell multi-omics modality translation, integrating diverse datasets, state-of-the-art models, and standardized evaluation metrics. It addresses a gap in systematic benchmarking for converting between biological measurement types in single cells.

entry.title: Learning to Refine: Spectral-Decoupled Iterative Refinement Framework for Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Yunlong Zhou, Chen Zhao, Danyang Peng, Fanfan Ji, Xiao-Tong Yuan

entry.summary: SDIR reformulates precipitation nowcasting as progressive frequency-decoupled refinement, extracting a stable low-frequency synoptic skeleton then iteratively refining high-frequency textures under physical constraints. It aims to avoid both over-smoothed regression outputs and unanchored diffusion hallucinations.

entry.title: Exact equivariance, kept through training, buys zero-shot generalisation across the symmetry group

author.name: Hongbo Wang (Stony Brook University)

entry.summary: Demonstrates that an equivariant world model preserves exact symmetry through training, enabling zero-shot generalization across an entire symmetry group from training on a restricted slice of orientations. Verified empirically at small scale with modern optimizers.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network with Transformer-Guided Adaptive Diffusion for Preclinical Alzheimer Classification

author.name: Jaeyoon Sim, Minjae Lee, Guorong Wu, Won Hwa Kim

entry.summary: Multi-modal GNN with transformer-guided adaptive diffusion for preclinical Alzheimer classification, addressing the limitations of convolutional aggregation over distant neighborhoods and attention methods' weakness at node-centric information. Integrates multiple imaging modalities over brain ROI graphs.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs' Effectiveness on Real-World Consumer Device Repair Questions

author.name: Atm Mizanur Rahman (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), Md Arid Hasan (University of Toronto), Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed (University of Toronto), Sharifa Sultana (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)

entry.summary: Benchmarks six state-of-the-art LLMs on 991 real-world consumer device repair questions from Reddit (phone, computer, data recovery), with Bangla translations for cross-lingual evaluation. Assesses correctness, completeness, practicality, and safety against technician references.

entry.title: BaltiVoice: A Speech Corpus and Fine-tuned Whisper ASR System for the Balti Language

author.name: Muhammad Ali

entry.summary: BaltiVoice provides the first publicly available ASR resources for Balti, a low-resource Tibetic language, with a 16.8-hour read-speech corpus and a fine-tuned Whisper-small model reducing WER from 182% zero-shot to 30%. Dataset, model, and demo are publicly released.

entry.title: Spectral-Progressive Thought Flow for Lightweight Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Yixian Shen, Zhiheng Yang, Qi Bi, Changshuo Wang, Shuai Wang, Jia-Hong Huang, George Floros, Prayag Tiwari, Anuj Pathania

entry.summary: Proposes SpecFlow, a lightweight multimodal reasoning framework that represents intermediate visual thoughts in a fixed-size discrete cosine (frequency) space to reduce the memory and compute cost of long visual-textual reasoning chains. Uses energy compaction to preserve global layout while adding high-frequency detail only when needed.

entry.title: Synthetic Hallucinations, Real Gains: Hard Negatives from Frontier Models for FIM Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Mahdi Erfanian, Nelson Daniel Troncoso, Aashna Garg, Amabel Gale, Xiaoyu Liu, Pareesa Ameneh Golnari, Shengyu Fu

entry.summary: Proposes an execution-free method to reduce hallucinated fill-in-the-middle code completions by using frontier models to synthesize plausible-but-wrong completions as hard negatives, then fine-tuning small code models on the contrast with ground-truth edits. Avoids per-language sandboxes and large human-labeled corpora.

entry.title: Learning Temporal Causal Structure via Smooth Differentiable Optimization

author.name: Tong Zhao, Ce Guo, Wayne Luk, Emil Lupu, Ray Dipojjwal

entry.summary: Proposes learning temporal causal structure with instantaneous effects by using the Gumbel-Sinkhorn operator to learn a differentiable variable permutation and triangularize the instantaneous coefficient matrix of an SVAR model. Converts acyclicity from a hard constraint into a parameterization, reducing computational cost.

entry.title: The Deliberative Illusion: Diagnosing Factual Attrition and Stance Homogenization in Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation

author.name: Herun Wan, Jiaying Wu, Minnan Luo, Fanxiao Li, Ningnan Wang, Nancy F. Chen, Min-Yen Kan

entry.summary: Identifies the deliberative illusion in multi-agent LLM systems where consensus masks factual attrition (loss of issue-critical facts) and stance homogenization (collapse of diverse positions), and introduces DelibTrace to measure these dynamics. Tests across ethical and news deliberation with three LLM families.

entry.title: Beyond Semantics: Modeling Factual and Affective Perceptual Experiences from Vision-Language Data

author.name: Youssef Mohamed, Kenneth Ward Church, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: Introduces P-Topics modeling to discover affective and cross-cultural perceptual experiences from image-caption data, each with factual and affective aspects, via the PercepT transformer. It clusters visual-textual perception experiences and associates images to them.

entry.title: Inverting the Generation Process of Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models: Empirical Evaluation and a Novel Method

author.name: Yan Zeng, Masanori Suganuma, Takayuki Okatani

entry.summary: Studies inverting the DDIM generation process to recover initial noise maps from generated images, proposing a hybrid approach combining gradient-descent inversion for the first step with a fixed-point method thereafter. It introduces a self-interpolation test for evaluating inversion quality.

entry.title: FAF-CD: Frequency-Aware Fusion for Change Detection under Imperfect Multimodal Remote Sensing

author.name: Yufan Wang, Sokratis Makrogiannis, Chandra Kambhamettu

entry.summary: Proposes FAF-CD, a frequency-aware hybrid change-detection framework with a DINOv3 ConvNeXt encoder and VMamba decoder, using deformable alignment plus Fourier and wavelet comparisons for imperfect multimodal remote sensing. It targets EO-SAR disaster mapping under asynchronous cross-sensor conditions.

entry.title: FreeStreamGS: Online Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from Unposed Streaming Inputs

author.name: Ruiyang Chen, Feiran Li, Chu Zhou, Zonglin Li, Zhanyu Ma, Heng Guo

entry.summary: FreeStreamGS proposes an online feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that produces high-quality novel view synthesis from streaming, unposed image inputs. It addresses the strict multi-view consistency requirements of NVS that prior online geometry methods could not satisfy.

entry.title: A unified multi-task framework enables interpretable chest radiograph analysis

author.name: Lijian Xu, Ziyu Ni, Xinglong Liu, Xiaosong Wang, Hongsheng Li, Shaoting Zhang

entry.summary: IMT-CXR is an interpretable multi-task Transformer for chest X-ray analysis that emulates radiologist workflows across disease recognition, attribute characterization, and traceable report generation. It emphasizes trust and interpretability in clinical diagnosis.

entry.title: EvoMemNav: Efficient Self-Evolving Fine-Grained Memory for Zero-Shot Embodied Navigation

author.name: Zuhao Ge, Xiaosong Jia, Chao Wu, Yuchen Zhou, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: EvoMemNav builds a self-evolving Visual-Semantic Memory Graph that keeps raw views as first-class memory for zero-shot embodied navigation, preserving fine-grained detail for disambiguation. It balances fidelity against the cost of 3D-reconstruction memory methods.

entry.title: SLU-2K: A Question-Based Benchmark for Semantic Evaluation of Sign Language Translation

author.name: Zeno Testa, Antonino Furnari, Lorenzo Baraldi, Natalia D\'iaz-Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: SLU-2K is a question-based benchmark shifting sign language evaluation from surface metrics like BLEU toward semantic understanding, measuring whether translations preserve key meaning. It targets the assistive-technology goal of meaning preservation.

entry.title: Where Do We (Not) Need Temporal Context in Low-Resource Video Task Adaptation?

author.name: Luc P. J. Str\"ater, Hazel Doughty

entry.summary: This work systematically studies how temporal context should be distributed across backbone, PEFT, and probe components when adapting foundation models to low-resource video tasks. It compares image-pretrained and video-pretrained PEFT settings rarely examined together.

entry.title: Adaptive Causal Alignment for High-Confidence Adversarial Training

author.name: Zhiming Luo, Kejia Zhang, Yingxin Lai, Junwei Wu, Juanjuan Weng, Shaozi Li

entry.summary: HICAT is a high-confidence causally-aligned adversarial training framework that distinguishes supportive context priors from spurious confounders, replacing blind background suppression with a measure-debias-align pipeline. It resolves a paradox where high-confidence predictions stem from non-causal correlations.

entry.title: GPU-Parallel Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning with Demonstration Guided Policy Optimization

author.name: Rui Zhang, Qiwei Wu, Zhengyu Zhang, Tao Li, Yunrong Guo, Junjie Lai, Renjing Xu, Weihua Zhang

entry.summary: This work presents a methodology for turning structured manipulation task families into GPU-parallel multi-task RL benchmarks, instantiated as MT-Libero in Isaac Lab, plus DGPO, an on-policy demonstration-guided optimization method for sparse-reward settings. It enables simultaneous RL over heterogeneous task suites with parallel rendering and physics randomization.

entry.title: Rashomon-Seeded Annealing for Robust Bayesian Inference in Factorial Designs

author.name: Yiyang Fan, Soumyakanti Pan, Tyler H. McCormick

entry.summary: This paper proposes Rashomon-seeded annealing, which repurposes Rashomon sets of high-performing models as a warm start for annealed importance sampling to estimate multimodal posteriors in factorial designs. It addresses MCMC convergence failures caused by the combinatorial explosion of interaction effects in Bayesian model averaging.

entry.title: Announcing the ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge

author.name: Jacob_Hilton

entry.summary: ARC announces the White-Box Estimation Challenge with AIcrowd, a contest to improve algorithms that estimate the expected output of wide random MLPs from their weights, with a prize pool of at least $100,000. It follows ARC's recent work on wide random MLPs and uses a FLOP-constrained evaluation scheme.

entry.title: Announcing the ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge

author.name: Jacob_Hilton

entry.summary: This is the Alignment Forum cross-post of ARC's White-Box Estimation Challenge, a contest with at least $100,000 in prizes to improve algorithms estimating the expected output of wide random MLPs from their weights under FLOP constraints. It follows ARC's wide-random-MLP research and is hosted with AIcrowd.

entry.title: Think-Before-Speak: From Internal Evaluation to Public Expression in Multi-Agent Social Simulation

author.name: Kaiqi Yang, Tai-Quan Peng, Sanguk Lee, Hui Liu

entry.summary: TBS (Think-Before-Speak) is an interval-based multi-agent social simulation framework separating agents' private internal evaluation from public utterance, modeling dissonance, speaking intention, and opinion climate. It enables study of internal processes behind silence and expression in opinion dynamics.

entry.title: TSQAgent: Rating Time Series Data Quality via Dedicated Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Shunyu Wu, Dan Li, Haozheng Ye, Weibin Feng, Jian Lou, Bo Zhang, Wenjie Feng, Chenjuan Guo, See-Kiong Ng

entry.summary: TSQAgent rates time series data quality through dedicated agentic reasoning, moving beyond manually predefined dimensions and text-only reasoning. It introduces TSQBench to evaluate whether LLMs can identify relevant quality dimensions and perform grounded quantitative comparisons.

entry.title: Enhancing Protein-Protein Interaction Prediction with Hierarchical Motif-based Multimodal Protein Embedding

author.name: Zaifei Yang, Samuel Ping-Man Choi, James Kwok

entry.summary: MMM-PPI is a hierarchical motif-based multimodal encoder for protein-protein interaction prediction that integrates sequence, structure, and function across micro, meso, and macro scales. It emphasizes meso-scale motifs that critically regulate interactions.

entry.title: Too Much of a Good Thing: When sim2real Efforts Impede Policy Learning (And What to Do About It)

author.name: Kyle Morgenstein, Bharath Masetty, Stephen Welch, Luis Sentis

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that excessive sim2real engineering creates misaligned incentives and simulator lock-in that impede robot policy learning, proposing a sim2sim2real paradigm using only robot kinematics as the design constraint. It diagnoses how real-world constraints overly restrict policy exploration.

entry.title: The Epi-LLM Framework: probing LLM behavioral priors through epidemiological agent-based models

author.name: Petra Ferenz, Ava Keeling, Tobias O'Keefe, Lorenzo Stigliano, Francesco Di Lauro, Andres Colubri, Jasmina Panovska-Griffiths

entry.summary: The Epi-LLM framework integrates agent-based modeling, real-life epigames, and LLMs to simulate a synthetic society reasoning and adapting during an outbreak. LLM agents reduced peak infections with quarantine compliance peaking at 58-65%, and the analysis identifies perceived health severity as a key behavioral driver.

entry.title: Reproducibility is the New Copyleft: Defining AGI-oriented Reproducible Builds

author.name: Masayuki Hatta

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that copyleft licensing assumes a reproducible source-to-binary relationship that LLMs and AGI systems violate, since reconstructing a model requires code, data, weights, hyperparameters, toolchain, and hardware. Proposes reproducible builds as the new locus of openness.

entry.title: Decoupled Smart Contract Audits: Lightweight LLM Framework via Distillation and Aggregation

author.name: Bagus Rakadyanto Oktavianto Putra, Muhamad Risqi Utama Saputra, Widyawan, Guntur Dharma Putra

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight LLM framework (0.6B-4B params) for smart contract security audits, decoupling detection, explanation, severity classification, and remediation via distillation and aggregation. Targets efficient end-to-end auditing without massive compute.

entry.title: OpenAgenet/OAN: Technical Architecture for Trust-Governed Agent Identity and Discovery

author.name: Jinliang Xu

entry.summary: Companion technical architecture paper to OAN specifying role architecture, identity objects, registration workflow, root-governed lifecycle, and signed trusted invocation for agent identity and discovery. Designed to support heterogeneous frameworks including MCP and A2A.

entry.title: What Do Students Learn? A Feature-Level Analysis of Dark Knowledge

author.name: Seungu Kang, Songkuk Kim

entry.summary: Analyzes knowledge distillation at the feature level using an Interaction Tensor framework, finding that effective KD acts as a regularizer pruning low-frequency sample-specific features to encourage reusable features. Proposes Confusion Distillation, a teacher-free self-distillation using the model's own evolving confusion matrix.

entry.title: FederatedSkill: Federated Learning for Agentic Skill Evolution

author.name: Jingbo Yang, Guanyu Yao, Yang Zhang, Ramana Rao Kompella, Gaowen Liu, Shiyu Chang
