entry.summary: Proposes FederatedSkill, a privacy-preserving framework for collaborative LLM-agent skill evolution that shares structured semantic skill diffs rather than raw trajectories. Uses server-side evolution to accommodate client heterogeneity while protecting privacy.

entry.title: IdEst: Assessing Self-Supervised Learning Representations via Intrinsic Dimension

author.name: Julie Mordacq, Vicky Kalogeiton, Steve Oudot

entry.summary: Introduces IdEst, a method for evaluating self-supervised learning representations via intrinsic dimension using a minimum spanning tree estimator, as a cheaper alternative to linear probing. Shows strong correlation with downstream linear probe accuracy across datasets and SSL objectives.

entry.title: Neural Navigation Functions for Zero-Shot Generalizable Motion Planning

author.name: Benjamin D. Shaffer, Pei-An Hsieh, Brooks Kinch, Nathaniel Trask, M. Ani Hsieh

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Navigation Functions, a learned reactive navigation function that achieves zero-shot transfer across unseen geometries by mapping Laplacian features to local PDE coefficients within a structured elliptic planner, guaranteeing collision-free monotonic descent to the goal by construction. Combines learning with provable planner structure.

entry.title: Visual Instruction Tuning Aligns Modalities through Abstraction

author.name: Luis Palacios, Lorenzo Basile, Diego Doimo, Alberto Cazzaniga

entry.summary: Shows that visual instruction tuning primarily acts as a bridge embedding visual features directly into intermediate semantic layers of the LLM backbone while bypassing early unimodal layers, validated via probing and causal interventions. Reveals these intermediate layers are the semantic core of vision-language processing.

entry.title: Does Language Shift Break Medical Vision-Language Models? Indonesian Radiology Visual Question Answering Case Study

author.name: Pieter Christy Yan Yudhistira, Dzaki Rafif Malik, Novanto Yudistira

entry.summary: Introduces IndoRad-VQA, an Indonesian adaptation of VQA-RAD, to test whether medical vision-language models retain radiology reasoning under non-English clinical language. It quantifies a language robustness gap across general, SEA-multilingual, and medical-specific VLMs.

entry.title: Characterizing Detectability in 3DGS Poisoning: A Stage-wise Benchmark

author.name: Quoc-Anh Bui-Huynh, Thanh Duc Ngo, Xue Geng, Kaixin Xu, Wang Zhe, Xulei Yang, Ngai-Man Cheung

entry.summary: This work presents a stage-wise benchmark for detecting poisoning attacks on 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines, exploiting that forensic signals are stage-dependent across the reconstruction process. It addresses the underexplored defense side of 3DGS security.

entry.title: AmbientEye: A Dataset for Pupil Segmentation under Natural Ambient Infrared Illumination

author.name: Mingyu Han, Hyunyoung Han, Nitheekulawatn Thommakoon, Gangtae Park, Jieun Han, Xucong Zhang, Ian Oakley

entry.summary: AmbientEye is a large-scale dataset of 2.6M eye images from 35 participants in 19 countries for pupil segmentation under passive infrared illumination using only natural sunlight. It investigates power-efficient all-day outdoor eye tracking for smart glasses.

entry.title: Template Collapse and Information-Theoretic Limits in Camera rPPG Pulse Morphology Restoration

author.name: Achraf Ben Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the information-theoretic limits of recovering single-cycle pulse waveform morphology from camera rPPG, finding no architecture recovers subject-specific morphology and identifying template collapse. It introduces cross-subject Pearson r to distinguish real recovery from collapse.

entry.title: Electromagnetic Navigation for Femoral Osteotomy Using High-Accuracy X-ray-to-CT Registration

author.name: Roman Flepp, Arend Nieuwland, Bastian Sigrist, Philipp F\"urnstahl, Lilian Calvet, Thomas Dreher

entry.summary: This paper presents an electromagnetic tracking navigation system for femoral osteotomies that uses high-accuracy X-ray-to-CT registration from just two fluoroscopic images, enabling fluoroscopy-free intraoperative navigation. It greatly reduces radiation exposure versus free-hand and PSI methods.

entry.title: Exploring Easy Boosts for Lidar Semantic Scene Completion

author.name: Tetiana Martyniuk, Jonathan Seele, Alexandre Boulch, Gilles Puy, Renaud Marlet, Raoul de Charette

entry.summary: This paper identifies free-lunch boosts for LiDAR semantic scene completion, showing that semantic pseudo-labels from off-the-shelf segmentors and visibility information substantially improve existing architectures. It finds high-quality semantic priors are the primary driver of gains.

entry.title: Bridging Predictive Uncertainty and Safe Action: Sample-Conditioned Differentiable Planning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chengzhen Meng, Pei Liu, Zhiyu Huang, Chen Lv, Jun Ma

entry.summary: This paper introduces a sample-conditioned differentiable planning framework for autonomous driving that feeds diffusion-generated future trajectories into a differentiable optimizer rather than collapsing predictions to a single future or using black-box end-to-end models. It links expressive uncertainty modeling to interpretable, safe motion planning.

entry.title: Local and Global Contraction Principles for MCMC Mixing

author.name: Alireza Daeijavad, Shahab Asoodeh

entry.summary: This paper develops a contraction-based framework for proving MCMC mixing-time bounds using global and local contraction coefficients under E-gamma divergence. For projected Langevin Monte Carlo on compact convex domains, it derives explicit global contraction from Gaussian smoothing, giving direct exponential convergence proofs for general smooth, possibly non-convex potentials.

entry.title: A Negative Result on Cross-Model Activation Transfer in a Pythia Multi-Hop Setting

author.name: Peiyan Zhang

entry.summary: A negative-result study testing whether one language model can transmit useful intermediate reasoning state to another by translating and injecting hidden activations at inference time. Despite a strong learned linear map, injected activations failed to transfer reasoning in a Pythia multi-hop setting.

entry.title: Dynamic Objective Selection with Safeguards and LLM Oversight for Financial Decision-Making

author.name: Keigo Sakurai, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama, Anjyu Anan, Kei Nakagawa

entry.summary: DOSS is a learning-based dynamic objective selector for financial decision-making that chooses the decision-relevant optimization objective at each time point from interpretable statistical signals, with LLM oversight and safeguards. It addresses suboptimality of fixed objectives across market regimes.

entry.title: Enhancing Operational Safety via Agentic Dialogue Hazard Identification Analysis

author.name: Sanjay Das, Ran Elgedawy, Ethan Seefried, Ryan Burchfield, Tirthankar Ghosal

entry.summary: HAZDIAL investigates whether structured multi-agent, multi-turn dialogue improves NLP-based hazard identification for operational safety over single-pass baselines. It compares adversarial debate and constructive discussion modalities.

entry.title: AVTrack: Audio-Visual Tracking in Human-centric Complex Scenes

author.name: Yaoting Wang, Yun Zhou, Zipei Zhang, Henghui Ding

entry.summary: AVTrack introduces a human-centric audio-visual instance segmentation dataset for tracking active speakers in complex, dynamic scenes with fine-grained annotations. It addresses limitations of existing datasets that rely on simple, static audio-visual co-occurrence.

entry.title: CRAM-ER: Error-Resilient Spintronic Computational Random Access Memory for Scalable In-Memory Computation

author.name: Sohan Salahuddin Mugdho, Md. Shahedul Hasan, Brahmdutta Dixit, Yang Lv, Jian-Ping Wang, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: CRAM-ER proposes an error-resilient spintronic computational RAM architecture for in-memory deep neural network computation, addressing probabilistic MRAM switching errors and slow sequential writes that limit scalability. It aims for dense, energy-efficient in-situ logic without peripheral overhead.

entry.title: SCOPE: Real-Time Natural Language Camera Agent at the Edge

author.name: Nikolaj Hindsbo, Sina Ehsani, Pragyana Mishra

entry.summary: SCOPE is a modular natural-language camera agent for open-vocabulary pan-tilt-zoom control and visual scene understanding, designed for edge deployment running perception, planning, and control locally. It is evaluated in both Blender simulation and on a physical camera with deployment-critical metrics like latency and accuracy.

entry.title: Optimizing Explicit Unit-Distance Lower-Bound Certificates

author.name: Michael T. M. Emmerich

entry.summary: Formulates the parameter-selection task for explicit unit-distance lower-bound certificates (following the 2026 disproof of Erdos's conjecture) as nonlinear integer programming and provides an open-source verification pipeline. Reproduces and computationally improves Sawin's bound.

entry.title: Will Accurate Fields Mislead Photonic Design? FromGlobal Accuracy to Port Readout

author.name: Yitian Zhang, Yonghong chen, Youming Chen, Yiyang Li, Xing Zhe, Renhe Lu, Shaolin Liao, Yuzhe Ma, Zhong Guan

entry.summary: Presents MOSAIC, a scheduling framework for Mixture-of-Agents LLM workloads using an ILP-based scheduler to optimize expert placement and prompt assignment, mitigating GPU idling from skewed demand and variable generation lengths. Improves throughput on limited GPUs.

entry.title: Bayesian Tensor Decomposition with Diffusion Model Prior

author.name: Zerui Tao, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: Presents DECA, a decentralized block-wise Adam method enabling full-parameter fine-tuning of billion-scale LLMs across distributed clients with non-IID data, without a central server. Addresses the resource-prohibitive nature of decentralized FPFT.

entry.title: Let There Be Light: Reflection, Refraction and Scattering for Neural Operators

author.name: Keke Wu, Yixuan Zhang, Jingrun Chen

entry.summary: Proposes LiNO, a Light-inspired neural operator for parametric PDEs whose latent evolution decomposes into reflection, refraction, and scattering mechanisms inspired by optics. Aims to balance physical interpretability, nonlocal communication, mesh scalability, and cost.

entry.title: APIC: Amortized Physics-Informed Calibration using Neural Processes

author.name: Aishwarya Venkataramanan, Sai Karthikeya Vemuri, Joachim Denzler

entry.summary: Introduces APIC, an amortized population-level extension of the Kennedy-O'Hagan physics-model calibration framework using Neural Processes to perform scalable Bayesian inference across related systems. Disentangles instance-specific physical parameters from shared structural discrepancies.

entry.title: Compress then Merge: From Multiple LoRAs into One Low-Rank Adapter

author.name: Zhengbao He, Ruiqi Ding, Zhehao Huang, Ruikai Yang, Tao Li, Xiaolin Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Compress-then-Merge (CtM), a reversed pipeline for merging multiple task-specific LoRAs into a single rank-r adapter that compresses before merging to preserve low-rank structure, unlike Merge-then-Compress approaches that may destroy it. Improves recovery of effective rank-r adapters.

entry.title: Attribution via Distributional Paths for Information Revelation

author.name: Kieran A. Murphy, Shameen Shrestha

entry.summary: Proposes attribution via distributional paths, lifting path-based feature attribution from input space to distribution space to control the resolution at which features are queried. Addresses how input-space paths give the baseline-adjacent trajectory equal footing with the input itself.

entry.title: See, Infer, Intervene: Proactive World Modeling for Goal-Oriented Social Intelligence

author.name: Honghui Zhang, Chenmeinian Guo, Yichen Yu, Guanyu Liu, Yongming Qin, Chongguo Song, Mengyue Yang, Lei Yu, Tianyu Shi

entry.summary: Presents the See-Infer-Intervene framework with a Proactive Intent World Model for retail agents that infer latent customer intent and decide whether and how to assist before a request. It uses AIDA purchasing phases and BDI psychological modeling to select interventions.

entry.title: KletterMix: Climbing Toward High-Quality German Pretraining Data

author.name: Maurice Kraus, Ruben H\"arle, Sebastian Sztwiertnia, Abbas Goher Khan, Mehdi Ali, Michael Fromm, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: Introduces KletterMix, a high-quality German pretraining corpus built by translating a state-of-the-art English corpus while preserving structure, metadata, and topical diversity. It is validated through controlled training experiments to address weak German data resources.

entry.title: Any2Poster: Any-Source Poster Generation Across Modalities and Domains

author.name: Amogh Vinaykumar, Aiden Li, Suozhi Huang, Shilong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Any2Poster Bench for any-source poster generation across eight input modalities and five domains, with quiz-based factual probes and VLM-based visual quality judgments. It enables reproducible assessment beyond paper-only inputs.

entry.title: FCUS-rPPG: A Fast-Converging Unsupervised Framework for Remote Photoplethysmography via Gradient Oscillation Suppression

author.name: Jiajie Li, Yu Liu, Rencheng Song, Xun Chen, Juan Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes FCUS-rPPG, a fast-converging unsupervised remote photoplethysmography framework using gradient oscillation suppression and a spectrally shared backbone for BVP feature disentanglement. It improves convergence speed and cross-domain generalization for contactless heart-rate sensing.

entry.title: SAMatcher: Co-Visibility Modeling with Segment Anything for Robust Feature Matching

author.name: Xu Pan, Qiyuan Ma, Mingyue Dong, He Chen, Wei Ji, Xianwei Zheng

entry.summary: SAMatcher reformulates feature matching via co-visibility modeling, predicting jointly visible region masks using SAM as structured priors before establishing correspondences. It improves robustness over pixel/patch-level matchers.

entry.title: A Fast Methane Detection Pipeline on Board Satellites Based on Mag1c-SAS and LinkNet

author.name: Jon\'a\v{s} Herec, V\'it R\r{u}\v{z}i\v{c}ka, Rado Pito\v{n}\'ak, Jan Sedmidubsky

entry.summary: This work accelerates onboard satellite methane detection with a faster Mag1c-SAS algorithm and a LinkNet segmentation model, enabling low-power onboard processing to overcome slow downlink rates. It targets early greenhouse-gas leak detection for climate mitigation.

entry.title: TeX-1500: A Paired Real-World LWIR Hyperspectral Dataset and Benchmark for Temperature-Emissivity-Texture Decomposition

author.name: Cheng Dai, Jiale Lin, Hongyi Xu, Bingxuan Song, Ziyang Xie, Fanglin Bao

entry.summary: TeX-1500 is a large paired real-world LWIR hyperspectral dataset and benchmark for supervised temperature-emissivity-texture decomposition, addressing the lack of paired supervision. It draws from DARPA imagery across diverse locations, seasons, and times.

entry.title: Seg2Track++: Probabilistic Track Validation and Data Association for Multi-Object Tracking and Segmentation

author.name: Diogo Mendon\c{c}a, Tiago Barros, Cristiano Premebida, Urbano J. Nunes

entry.summary: Seg2Track++ integrates instance segmentation with SAM2 plus a track management module for zero-shot multi-object tracking and segmentation, adding probabilistic track validation and confidence-aware cost modulation. It addresses SAM2's unreliable association and false-positive propagation.

entry.title: PatchScene: Patch-based Voxel Diffusion for Large-Scale Scene Completion

author.name: Qingdong Xu, Jiajun Zhu, Shilin Zhu, Xinjing He, Chao Lu, Huanran Wang, Jiyao Zhang

entry.summary: PatchScene is a patch-based voxel diffusion framework for large-scale LiDAR scene completion that generates fine-grained local geometry with confidence-guided spatio-temporal fusion. An Annular-Flow strategy exploits LiDAR radial density to propagate information from near to far range.

entry.title: MARIO: Motion-Augmented Real-Time Multi-Sensor Inertial Odometry

author.name: Yiquan Li, Taeyoung Yeon, Chenfeng Gao, Vasco Xu, Xuanyou Liu, Karan Ahuja

entry.summary: MARIO grounds learning-based inertial odometry in human kinematics via a learned IMU-inferred pose prior that enforces physically consistent motion constraints, reducing drift on daily-activity datasets. It improves IMU-only tracking for AR and wearables.

entry.title: GTBench: A Curriculum-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs as Mathematical Research Assistants in Graph Theory

author.name: Noujoud Nader, Ibrahem Aljabea, Patrick Diehl, Deepti Gupta

entry.summary: GTBench is a curriculum-grounded benchmark evaluating LLMs as graph theory research assistants across 63 problems spanning undergraduate definitions to graduate proofs. It tests frontier models including GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini.

entry.title: CARVE: Certified Affordable Repair of Vetoed Maneuvers via Envelopes for Interactive Driving

author.name: Yifan Wang

entry.summary: CARVE formulates interactive repair certification for autonomous driving, producing a runtime proof object specifying which bounded multi-agent edit repairs an infeasible maneuver, who owns the edit, and whether the request is right-of-way affordable. It addresses cases where small lawful accommodations could restore feasibility.

entry.title: Improvise, Adapt, Overcome: An On-The-Fly Multifidelity Algorithm for Efficient Machine Learning

author.name: Vivin Vinod, Peter Zaspel

entry.summary: This paper introduces an adaptive on-the-fly multifidelity machine learning framework that autonomously determines training dataset composition across fidelities, rather than relying on predefined scaling factors. It reduces redundant high-fidelity data generation in quantum chemistry while saturating model accuracy.

entry.title: Hand Trajectory Fusion for Egocentric Natural Language Query Grounding

author.name: Enmin Zhong, Carlos R. del-Blanco, Fernando Jaureguizar, Narciso Garc\'ia

entry.summary: This paper introduces a hand-trajectory encoder for egocentric natural language query grounding that converts hand skeleton sequences into semantic kinematic features, fused with video-text features via cross-attention with adaptive gating. It is motivated by the finding that about 41% of Ego4D NLQ queries are answered at hand-object manipulation moments.

entry.title: Towards Compact Autonomous Driving Perception with Balanced Learning and Multi-sensor Fusion

author.name: Oskar Natan, Jun Miura

entry.summary: This paper presents a compact multi-task deep learning model for autonomous driving perception that performs semantic segmentation, depth estimation, LiDAR segmentation, and bird's-eye-view projection in one forward pass. It includes an adaptive loss weighting algorithm for imbalanced multi-task learning and intermediate fusion of camera, DVS, and LiDAR inputs.

entry.title: Spike-Aware C++ INT8 Inference for Sparse Spiking Language Models on Commodity CPUs

author.name: Ting Liu

entry.summary: Implements a C++ CPU inference runtime that treats sparse binary spike states as an execution primitive for spiking language models, with INT8 quantization and AVX2 kernels. Reports throughput gains on commodity CPUs by exploiting activation sparsity.

entry.title: PSViT: A Methodology for Structurally Pruning Spiking Vision Transformers

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Achyuta Muthuvelan, Alberto Marchisio, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: PSViT applies structured pruning to Spiking Vision Transformers, enabling efficient acceleration on standard hardware without the specialized accelerators that unstructured pruning requires. Improves deployability on resource-constrained embedded platforms.

entry.title: PrimeSVT: An Automated Memory-aware Pruning Framework with Prioritized Compression Policy for Spiking Vision Transformers

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Achyuta Muthuvelan, Alberto Marchisio, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: PrimeSVT is an automated memory-aware structured pruning framework for spiking vision transformers with a prioritized compression policy, removing the manual design effort and specialized-hardware requirements of prior unstructured pruning. Targets efficient embedded inference.

entry.title: SPADE: Sketch-guided Path Planning Augmented with Diffusion Experts

author.name: Charbel Abi Hana, Tatiana Ghantous, Mikael Khalil, Anthony Rizk

entry.summary: SPADE enhances sketch-guided path planning for autonomous mobile robots with a ROS 2 annotation tool and diffusion-based augmentation to improve generalization and robustness in demonstration-based imitation learning. Addresses poor generalization to unseen environments.

entry.title: Learning to See via Epiretinal Implant Stimulation in silico with Model-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jacob Lavoie, Marwan Besrour, William Lemaire, Jean Rouat, R\'ejean Fontaine, Eric Plourde

entry.summary: Uses model-based deep reinforcement learning in silico to learn stimulation patterns for epiretinal implants that produce isotropic pixel-like percepts by avoiding axon fascicle activation. Aims to improve vision restoration for retinal degeneration patients.

entry.title: A Graph Foundation Model with Spectral Parsing and Prototype-Guided Spatial Propagation

author.name: Ankang Yang, Jitao Zhao, Dongxiao He, Liang Yang, Di Jin, Weixiong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a graph foundation model combining spectral parsing with prototype-guided spatial propagation to enable cross-graph transfer despite differing features and structures. Addresses limitations of discrete structural tokens and predefined substructure vocabularies.

entry.title: Multi$^2$: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Decision-Making with LLM-Based Agents in Interactive Environments

author.name: Sangeun Park, Minhae Kwon

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-squared, a hierarchical multi-agent framework decomposing LLM-agent behavior into a high-level sub-goal generation agent (SFT) and a low-level action-execution agent (offline-to-online RL) to combat objective drift in long-horizon decision-making. Aims to stabilize sustained interaction with dynamic environments.

entry.title: Two-Action Apple Tasting with Switching Costs

author.name: Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni

entry.summary: Studies the two-action apple-tasting problem with switching costs against an oblivious adversary, resolving the regret rate for this specific partial-feedback setting. Investigates whether the apple-tasting graph is the missing obstruction for the T^(2/3) lower bound.

entry.title: The Road Ahead in Autonomous Driving: The KITScenes Multimodal Dataset

author.name: Richard Schwarzkopf, Fabian Immel, Alexander Blumberg, Jonas Merkert, Nils Rack, Kaiwen Wang, Fabian Konstantinidis, Julian Truetsch, Carlos Fernandez, Annika B\"atz, Kevin R\"osch, Marlon Steiner, Willi Poh, Yinzhe Shen, Royden Wagner, Felix Hauser, Dominik Strutz, Jaime Villa, Gleb Stepanov, Holger Caesar, \"Omer \c{S}ahin Ta\c{s}, Frank Bieder, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Christoph Stiller

entry.summary: Presents KITScenes Multimodal, a high-fidelity European autonomous driving dataset combining global-shutter cameras, long-range lidar beyond 400m, 4D imaging radar, and the most complete HD maps with full 3D traffic elements and topology. Addresses gaps in sensor fidelity and map completeness.

entry.title: Expert-Aware Causal Tracing of Factual Recall in Sparse MoE Language Models

author.name: Yuetian Lu, Ali Modarressi, Yihong Liu, Hinrich Sch\"utze

entry.summary: Formulates expert-aware causal tracing for sparse mixture-of-experts language models, identifying which routed expert contributions matter for factual recall using CounterFact corruption-restoration interventions on Qwen3-30B-A3B. Extends interpretability beyond dense transformers.

entry.title: VLESA: Vision-Language Embodied Safety Agent for Human Activity Monitoring

author.name: Hanjiang Hu, Yiyuan Pan, Jiaxing Li, Xusheng Luo, Alexander Robey, Na Li, Yebin Wang, Changliu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces VLESA, a vision-language embodied safety agent that monitors human activities from egocentric video and triggers real-time interventions for intent-dependent dangerous actions, with a goal-conditioned safety Q-filter trained via GRPO. Addresses context-dependent physical safety.

entry.title: Do Value Vectors in Deep Layers Need Context from the Residual Stream?

author.name: Muyu He, Yuchen Liu, Qingya Huang, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Finds that model performance improves when deeper transformer layers learn context-free value vectors preserving original token information, with the context-dependent component adding little aggregate benefit. Suggests value vectors in deep layers can be stored as sparse lookups.

entry.title: Structures Facilitate Retrieve, Rerank, and Generate

author.name: Yeqin Zhang, Haomin Fu, Xujie Zhang, Cam-Tu Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes SF-Re2G, a document-grounded dialogue system that exploits document structure to improve passage representation, reranking, and generation. It contrasts passages within sections and builds a structure-enhanced reranker.

entry.title: A Pocket Offline Model for Simultaneous Speech Translation as CUNI Submission to IWSLT 2026

author.name: Aziz Sharipov Ortega, Dominik Mach\'a\v{c}ek

entry.summary: A CUNI IWSLT 2026 submission adapting the offline Canary speech translation model for simultaneous translation using the AlignAtt policy. It offers high quality with only 1B parameters and supports 25 source and 25 target languages.

entry.title: SRENet: Spectral Re-Entry Network for Point Cloud Action Recognition

author.name: Qiuxia Wu, Jiarui Lan, Wenxiong Kang, Zhiyong Wang, Kun Hu

entry.summary: Proposes SRENet, a spectral-aware framework for point cloud action recognition using a wavelet-based Spectral Decomposition Block to disentangle features along temporal and spatial axes. It captures both global motion context and fine-grained temporal dynamics from a frequency perspective.

entry.title: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6: Expanding the Frontier of Document Parsing with Under-Optimized Region Refinement and Progressive Post-Training

author.name: Zelun Zhang, Hongen Liu, Suyin Liang, Yubo Zhang, Yiqing Xiang, Jiaxuan Liu, Ting Sun, Manhui Lin, Yue Zhang, Changda Zhou, Tingquan Gao, Cheng Cui, Yi Liu, Dianhai Yu, Yanjun Ma

entry.summary: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 is a compact 0.9B document parsing model that uses region-aware data optimization and progressive post-training including RL to refine weak areas of its predecessor. It targets practical, efficient document understanding.

entry.title: Preference-Calibrated Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zeyi Liu, Guangyao Liu, Yinuo Qu, Yuquan Xue, Bofang Jia, Chunhua Yang, Weihua Gui, Keke Huang, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: PACT is a preference-calibrated actor-critic framework for human-in-the-loop RL that avoids uniformly propagating terminal rewards through suboptimal trajectory segments that triggered human intervention. It calibrates credit assignment to each transition's actual contribution to task success, preventing Q-value overestimation.

entry.title: Abstraction Boundaries and Bubbles of Legibility

author.name: Adam Chlipala

entry.summary: This LessWrong/Substack post argues for redesigning parts of the world to be more legible to automated reasoning, encapsulating intelligent systems within well-defined verifiable interfaces so alignment challenges concentrate at boundaries rather than spreading throughout a system. It draws an analogy to end-to-end formal verification of layered computer systems.

entry.title: DMF: A Deterministic Memory Framework for Conversational AI Agents

author.name: Matteo Stabile, Enrico Zimuel

entry.summary: The Deterministic Memory Framework replaces LLM-based summarization in conversational agent memory with a fully deterministic CPU-first pipeline using classical NLP, vector geometry, and a logistic survival score. It aims to reduce non-determinism, token costs, and opacity in pruning.

entry.title: From Control Boundary to Insurance Claim: Reconstructing AI-Mediated Losses Through the CER Framework

author.name: Alex Leung, Rex Zhang, Kentaroh Toyoda, SiewMei Loh

entry.summary: Introduces the CER framework for reconstructing AI-mediated losses to support insurance claims, addressing failures where an insured organization's generative or agentic AI system is in the causal chain. It emphasizes state reconstruction over mere event reconstruction for losses like prompt injection and RAG poisoning.

entry.title: Link Prediction or Perdition: the Seeds of Instability in Knowledge Graph Embeddings

author.name: Guillaume M\'erou\'e, Fabien Gandon, Pierre Monnin

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic stability analysis of knowledge graph embedding models, showing that high-performing models produce divergent triple-level predictions and highly variable embedding spaces across random seeds. Isolates stochastic factors like initialization, triple ordering, and negative sampling.

entry.title: Limit Analysis of Graph Neural Networks with Wireless Conflict Graphs

author.name: Romina Garcia Camargo, Zhiyang Wang, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: Establishes theoretical transferability results for graph neural networks over conflict graphs derived from sparse random geometric graphs, used to model interference in wireless resource allocation. Shows models trained on small graphs generalize to large deployments with little performance loss.

entry.title: Contrastive Neural Algorithmic Reasoning for Graph Coloring

author.name: Thien Le, Tianyu Zhao, Melanie Weber

entry.summary: Proposes a contrastive learning framework for neural algorithmic reasoning on approximate graph coloring, learning transferable coloring geometry where same-color nodes align and adjacent nodes are pushed apart. Unlike per-instance unsupervised GNN methods, it generalizes across graph sizes and distributions.

entry.title: A Quantitative Approximation Framework for Flow Distillation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Weiguo Gao, Ming Li, Lei Shi, Hanfei Zhou

entry.summary: Develops a quantitative approximation framework for diffusion distillation, viewing few-step sampling as error propagation under compositions of learned flow maps and showing local errors amplify in low-noise multimodal stiff regimes. Provides constructive Lp approximation guarantees in a tractable Gaussian-mixture setting.

entry.title: Rethinking the Idiomaticity Decomposability Hypothesis: Evidence from Distributional Learning

author.name: Maggie Mi, Golzar Atefi, Atsuki Yamaguchi, Felix Gers, Aline Villavicencio, Nafise Sadat Moosavi

entry.summary: Uses contextualized language models as controlled distributional learners to test the idiomaticity decomposability hypothesis, proposing a model-internal decomposability measure. It finds weak correlation with human judgments and a small negative relationship with syntactic flexibility.

entry.title: Hierarchical Federated Learning with Dynamic Clustering and Adaptive Regularization for Robust Infrastructure Inspection

author.name: Yuhu Feng, Keisuke Maeda, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical federated learning framework with dynamic gradient-based clustering and adaptive regularization to handle double heterogeneity across nationwide infrastructure inspection data. It tackles macro-level physical divergence and micro-level statistical imbalance.

entry.title: UnsOcc: 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction in Unstructured Scene via Rendering Fusion

author.name: Ye Wu, Ruiqi Song, Baiyong Ding, Nanxin Zeng, Junjie Cheng, Yunfeng Ai

entry.summary: UnsOcc tackles 3D semantic occupancy prediction in unstructured driving scenes via rendering fusion, addressing scene sparsity and severe long-tail distributions. It introduces a dedicated unstructured-scene dataset for validation.

entry.title: SparseStreet: Sparse Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Street Scene Simulation

author.name: Qingpo Wuwu, Xiaobao Wei, Peng Chen, Nan Huang, Zhongyu Zhao, Hao Wang, Ming Lu, Ningning Ma, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: SparseStreet is a compression framework for street-scene Gaussian Splatting that prunes low-contributing primitives while preserving dynamic objects and visually critical regions. It addresses prohibitive storage and slow rendering in driving scene reconstruction.

entry.title: RelGT-AC: A Relational Graph Transformer for Autocomplete Tasks in Relational Databases

author.name: Phillip Jiang

entry.summary: RelGT-AC extends a relational graph transformer to autocomplete tasks on relational databases, predicting existing column values from relational context like an intelligent form-filler. It adds column masking and other targeted contributions to RelBench v2.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Token Arbitrage: Optimizing Code Agent Context Windows via Local LLM Preprocessing

author.name: Mehmet Utku Colak

entry.summary: Introduces an edge-side prompt-rewriting middleware that uses a local Llama 3.2 3B model to translate non-English prompts to English and structurally compact conversational prompts before sending to cloud coding agents. It reduces input-token costs while guaranteeing the optimized prompt is never larger than the original.

entry.title: Sparse-View Lung Nodule Volumetry from Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs via AReT: Anatomy-Regularized TensoRF

author.name: Spoorthi M, Suja Palaniswamy

entry.summary: This paper identifies a previously unreported failure mode in TensoRF for X-ray attenuation fields—the default density shift suppresses gradients—and resolves it for sparse-view reconstruction. AReT then enables anatomy-regularized volumetric lung nodule reconstruction from only three orthogonal X-ray projections.

entry.title: SVHalluc: Benchmarking Speech-Vision Hallucination in Audio-Visual Large Language Models

author.name: Chenshuang Zhang, Kyeong Seon Kim, Chengxin Liu, Tae-Hyun Oh

entry.summary: This causal analysis of 21,098 UK Biobank participants compares DXA-derived hip skeletal phenotypes for hip fracture risk using backdoor-adjusted average treatment effects and a prespecified DAG. It assesses whether phenotypes ranked by adjusted effects improve risk stratification.

entry.title: Glass Box at Orbit: A Constitutional AI Verification Framework for Trustworthy Autonomous CubeSat Intelligence

author.name: Karthik Barma, Anil Sanneboyina, V C Premchand Yadav

entry.summary: Glass Box proposes a runtime constitutional AI verification layer for autonomous CubeSats that intercepts every candidate action from an onboard AI policy and evaluates it against six physics-grounded constitutional constraints before execution. It targets governance of autonomous AI in orbital data centers where no human is in the loop.

entry.title: BAHSD: Bridging the Long-tail Gap via Adaptive Distillation in Black-box Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Xi Zhou, Famin Wu, Mingming Li, Hongyue Zhang, Jiao Dai, Jizhong Han, Tao Guo

entry.summary: BAHSD is a black-box adaptive distillation framework for extracting sequential recommendation models that handles long-tail signal heterogeneity via multi-scale consistency probing. Differentiates treatment of dense head and sparse tail sequences.

entry.title: Tonal parsimony in chord-sequence analysis: combining modulation cost and tonal vocabulary

author.name: Fran\c{c}ois Pachet

entry.summary: Studies tonal parsimony for assigning local tonalities to chord sequences, combining modulation cost and tonal vocabulary minimization with exact algorithms exploiting the fixed 24-tonality universe. Evaluated on over 31,000 chord sequences from the Lakh MIDI dataset.

entry.title: Gate AI: LLM Security Benchmark Evaluation Methodology and Results

author.name: Ryle Goehausen, Marcus Sousa

entry.summary: Describes Gate AI, an evaluation methodology for LLM prompt-injection and jailbreak detectors that addresses per-dataset threshold tuning and undisclosed operating points by using cross-validation across 16 benchmarks with a single global operating point. Includes near-duplicate leakage diagnostics.

entry.title: Finding Needles in the Haystack: Transductive Active Labeling in Ecology

author.name: Rupa Kurinchi-Vendhan, Sara Beery

entry.summary: Argues that active learning in ecology should be evaluated transductively (labeling an entire data pool efficiently) rather than inductively on held-out test sets, which underestimates the value of continued labeling especially for rare long-tail classes. Demonstrates the importance of the human-in-the-loop for ecologically important rare species.

entry.title: Multi-Segment Attention: Enabling Efficient KV-Cache Management for Faster Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Chunan Shi, Yilei Chen, Yilin Chen, Xupeng Miao, Bin Cui

entry.summary: Proposes AsymCache, a computation-latency-aware KV cache management system for LLM inference that aligns cache residency decisions with GPU attention kernel efficiency rather than access frequency heuristics. Enables faster lossless LLM serving.

entry.title: Hierarchies of Calibration: Classification meets Regression

author.name: Johannes Resin, Lu Yang, Tilmann Gneiting

entry.summary: Reviews, extends, and unifies notions of calibration across classification and regression tasks, emphasizing hierarchical relations and introducing modal calibration for nominal outcomes. Bridges probabilistic prediction concepts across data types from credible statisticians.

entry.title: Bregman meets L\'evy: Stochastic mirror descent with heavy-tailed noise in continuous and discrete time

author.name: Pierre-Louis Cauvin, Panayotis Mertikopoulos

entry.summary: Studies robustness of stochastic mirror descent under heavy-tailed infinite-variance noise, introducing a continuous-time Levy mirror flow model and analyzing convergence in both continuous and discrete time. Establishes when SMD retains guarantees despite jump discontinuities.

entry.title: Topics as Proxies for Sociodemographics: How Conversational Context Affects LLM Answers

author.name: Vera Neplenbroek, Gabriele Sarti, Arianna Bisazza, Raquel Fern\'andez

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs struggle to infer user sociodemographics from a single conversation history and that resulting outcome disparities between groups are minimal, with topics rather than demographics being the main driver. Challenges assumptions about demographic bias in conversational LLMs.

entry.title: Hint-Guided Diversified Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhiyu Cao, Kaixin Wu, Mingjie Zhong, Peifeng Li, Xiaobo Li, Can Ye, Qiaoming Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes Hint-Guided Diversified Policy Optimization (HDPO), an RLVR method that has the model first list candidate solution outlines as hints to incentivize diverse solution exploration, addressing the lack of diversity signals in outcome-only rewards. Inspired by human multi-approach problem solving.

entry.title: Entropy Gate: Entropy Quenching for Near-Lossless Token Compression in LLM Pipelines

author.name: Justice Owusu Agyemang, Jerry John Kponyo, Kwame Opuni-Boachie Obour Agyekum, Francisca Adoma Acheampong, Kwame Agyeman-Prempeh Agyekum, James Dzisi Gadze

entry.summary: Introduces Entropy Gate, a token-compression framework using a thermodynamic-inspired entropy-quenching schedule to remove low-information tokens while preserving semantic fidelity. Each token gets a multi-factor energy score with an adaptive quenching schedule.

entry.title: TASE: Truncation-Aware Semantic Embeddings for 3D Scene Understanding and Editing

author.name: Tim-Felix Faasch, Jochen Kall, Lucas Nunes, Jens Behley, Cyrill Stachniss

entry.summary: TASE projects pretrained 2D semantic features into a truncation-aware embedding space enabling flexible, controllable editing of 3D scene semantics. The hierarchical channel design trades detail for abstraction for robotics and simulation applications.

entry.title: From 3D Perception to Safety Reasoning: A Graph-Based Framework for Real-Time Underground Mine Monitoring

author.name: Pasindu Ranasinghe, Simit Raval, Dibyayan Patra, Bikram Banerjee, Ismet Canbulat

entry.summary: This paper presents a graph-based framework converting colorized 3D point clouds into structured safety reasoning for real-time underground mine monitoring. It combines 3D perception, anomaly detection, and rule-based hazard checks for hazardous environments.

entry.title: ConTrack: Constrained Hand Motion Tracking with Adaptive Trade-off Control

author.name: Yutong Liang, Quanquan Peng, Ri-Zhao Qiu, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: ConTrack is an RL framework for dexterous hand manipulation that treats object tracking as a hard constraint and allocates remaining control to motion fidelity, avoiding per-sequence reward tuning. It targets long-horizon, contact-rich reference tracking that scales with demonstration data.

entry.title: Multi-Robot Bearing-only Pose Estimation via Angle Rigidity

author.name: J. Francisco Presenza, Leonardo J. Colombo, Ignacio Mas, Juan I. Giribet

entry.summary: This letter presents a distributed bearing-only pose estimator for time-varying multi-robot systems that recovers 3D positions from body-frame angle measurements without orientation knowledge, then reconstructs SO(3) orientations. It requires only an angle-rigid sensing topology, a weaker condition than bearing rigidity, with proven exponential stability.

entry.title: Neural Posterior Estimation for Stochastic Epidemic Models Using Final Outcome Data

author.name: Theodore Kypraios

entry.summary: This paper applies neural posterior estimation, a simulation-based likelihood-free Bayesian method, to stochastic SIR epidemic models observed only through final outcome data, for both homogeneously mixing and household-structured populations. It offers a faster, easier alternative to slow data-augmentation MCMC and approximate methods.

entry.title: Compute Verification on Short Timelines

author.name: skunnavakkam

entry.summary: This post examines compute verification as a coordination mechanism for AI governance on short timelines, arguing that die-level hardware verification is likely intractable before 2030 and that focus should shift to post-hoc chip modifications and robust software verification. It grounds the analysis in NVIDIA's Blackwell/Rubin/Feynman manufacturing roadmap.

entry.title: Effect of Demographic Bias on Skin Lesion Classification

author.name: Ralf Raumanns, Gerard Schouten, Veronika Cheplygina, Josien P. W. Pluim

entry.summary: Studies how demographic bias in training data affects skin lesion classification using ResNet models, employing linear programming to create datasets with controlled demographics. It finds sex-specific training and including male patients improves male-subgroup performance.

entry.title: ROBUST-WT: Robust Uncertainty-aware Segmentation Transform via Whitening and Training Enhancements

author.name: Aqsa Naseer, Maryam Bibi, Syeda Samiya Urooj, Muhammad Khurram Shahzad

entry.summary: ROBUST-WT enhances a published whitening-transform medical image segmentation method with better augmentations and loss functions for robust cross-domain generalization. Systematically addresses four identified limitations of the original framework.

entry.title: A Robust Optimization Approach to Sparse Principal Component Analysis

author.name: David V\"avinggren, Francis Bach, Andr\'e M. H. Teixeira, Dave Zachariah, Ant\^onio H. Ribeiro

entry.summary: Proposes Adversarial PCA (AdvPCA), achieving sparse principal component analysis via robust optimization against bounded worst-case latent perturbations rather than explicit L1 penalties, with a closed-form reduction and practical iterative algorithm. From credible authors including Francis Bach.

entry.title: CoralBay: A Self-Supervised CT Foundation Model

author.name: Ioannis Gatopoulos, Nicolas K\"anzig, Sebastian Ot\'alora, Fei Tang

entry.summary: Introduces CoralBay, a self-supervised CT foundation model using a self-distillation framework extending DINO with a hierarchical 3D Swin backbone applied to concatenated multi-scale features for volumetric medical imaging. Addresses the gap between 2D natural-image pretraining and 3D CT structure.

entry.title: Beyond Compression: Quantifying Spectral Accessibility in Vision Representations

author.name: Akayou A. Kitessa, Yijun Zhao

entry.summary: This study quantifies how vision-language projection layers alter spatial-frequency accessibility of visual features, introducing a Residual Spectral Loss to isolate effects beyond dimensionality reduction. It reveals consistent frequency-dependent changes in recoverable information.

entry.title: Face versus Body Tracking for Human-Robot Interaction: An Egocentric Dataset

author.name: Jessica Wenninger, Gabriel Skantze

entry.summary: This work introduces a custom-annotated egocentric dataset from a Furhat social robot to study face versus body tracking for human-robot interaction under social dynamics like occlusion and frame exit. It systematically isolates detection errors from tracking logic to address identity switches.

entry.title: GeoSem-WAM: Geometry- and Semantic-Aware World Action Models

author.name: Fulong Ma, Daojie Peng, Wenjun Yue, Jiahang Cao, Bintao Wang, Qiang Zhang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: GeoSem-WAM enhances world action models for embodied decision-making by adding geometric and semantic supervision to latent representations, rather than relying solely on RGB future prediction. It probes whether WAM gains come from representation learning versus explicit future imagination.

entry.title: SplitAdapter: Load-Aware Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Factorized Adaptation

author.name: Jeonguk Kang, Hanbyel Cho, Sanghyun Kang, Donghan Koo

entry.summary: SplitAdapter improves humanoid loco-manipulation under varying object loads by factorizing adaptation into separate object/load and dynamics context encoders, freezing a pretrained policy. It uses split world-model objectives and adversarial regularization to improve sim-to-real robustness under heavy loads.

entry.title: Towards Non-Monotonic Entailment in Propositional Defeasible Standpoint Logic

author.name: Nicholas Leisegang, Thomas Meyer, Ivan Varzniczak

entry.summary: Lifts non-monotonic rational entailment relations from KLM-style defeasible reasoning to a fragment of propositional defeasible standpoint logic, extending beyond prior monotonic entailment work. It addresses inferentially weak monotonic notions in modal defeasible reasoning.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Query Routing in RAG: Empirical Analysis of Retrieval Depth Tradeoffs

author.name: Sanjay Mishra

entry.summary: Cost-Aware RAG introduces a per-query routing framework that selects retrieval-depth strategy bundles to balance factual grounding against token cost and latency. It tailors retrieval effort to query complexity rather than using a static configuration.

entry.title: Brief Announcement: Generative Markov Model for Distributed Computing Systems

author.name: Alfreds Lapkovskis, Ali Beikmohammadi, Sindri Magn\'usson, Praveen Kumar Donta

entry.summary: Proposes modeling heterogeneous distributed computing systems as a factorized generative Markov model over structured state variables, enabling tractable simulation, inference, and policy learning. A brief announcement bridging systems and probabilistic modeling.

entry.title: Outsmarting the Chameleon: Counterfactual Decoupling for Tactical OOD Shifts in Live Streaming Risk Assessment

author.name: Yiran Qiao, Jing Chen, Jiaqi Xu, Yang Liu, Qiwei Zhong, Xiang Ao

entry.summary: Tackles tactical out-of-distribution shifts in live streaming risk detection, where malicious actors keep stable goals but redesign packaging to evade detection. Proposes a latent causal framework with counterfactual decoupling to separate intent from tactics.

entry.title: TiWeaver: Unified Temporal Dynamics Modeling via Contextual Patching

author.name: Zhe Li, Jindong Tian, Hao Miao, Zhi Lei, Chenjuan Guo, Bin Yang

entry.summary: Proposes TiWeaver, a unified time series forecasting framework using contextual patching to adaptively handle diverse temporal dynamics, missing values, and non-uniform sampling across channels. Captures fine-grained asynchronous inter-channel dependencies.

entry.title: Validation-Gated Multi-Agent Governance for Online Adaptation of Thermal-Hydraulic Surrogate Models under Operating-Regime Shift

author.name: Doyeong Lim, Seungyoon Lee, In Cheol Bang

entry.summary: Develops a validation-gated multi-agent governance framework for online adaptation of thermal-hydraulic surrogate models that become condition-locked under operating-regime shifts. Role-separated agents (Monitor, Diagnosis, Adaptation, Safety-Auditor, Orchestrator) manage continual adaptation while deterministic champion-challenger gates retain final authority.

entry.title: Text-attributed Graph Condensation via Text Selection and Attribute Matching

author.name: Haowei Han, Yuxiang Wang, Guojia Wan, Hao Wang, Shanshan Feng, Hao Huang, Jiawei Jiang, Xiao Yan

entry.summary: Proposes TAGSAM, a condensation method for text-attributed graphs that compresses both text descriptions (via subgraph text selection maximizing mutual information) and graph topology (via attribute similarity matching) while preserving training accuracy. Reduces space and time costs of jointly training GNNs and language models.

entry.title: Scalable Derivative Gaussian Processes via Exact Gradient Reduction

author.name: Hyunseok Seung, Matthias Katzfuss

entry.summary: Introduces TERA, a scalable derivative Gaussian process method using target-specific exact gradient reduction, proving that orthogonal gradient components are conditionally independent for stationary kernels. Dramatically reduces the cubic computational cost of derivative GP inference.

entry.title: GLINT: Sparsely Gated Vision-Language Alignment for Fine-Grained Radiology Representations

author.name: Jonggwon Park, Seongeun Lee, Junhyun Park, Hannah Yun, Hyunwoong Kim, Sohyun Jeong, Hyewon Kang, Byungmu Yoon, Kyoyun Choi

entry.summary: Introduces GLINT, a sparsely gated vision-language alignment framework for radiology that uses a sigmoid gate to concentrate weight on the sparse image regions relevant to each finding, addressing the scale mismatch between global supervision and local findings. Targets fine-grained radiology representations.

entry.title: On the Persistent Effects of Lexicality in Large Language Mod

author.name: Hammad Rizwan, Muhammad Umair Haider, Nishant Subramani, Mona T. Diab, A. B. Siddique, Hassan Sajjad

entry.summary: Investigates how lexical overlap rather than semantic content shapes LLM representations, using adversarial semantic stress tests and information-theoretic analysis. Finds lexical influence persists across model depth, architectures, and training regimes.

entry.title: SEA-Embedding: Open and Reproducible Text Embeddings for Southeast Asia

author.name: Peerat Limkonchotiwat, Raymond Ng, Sarana Nutanong, Jian Gang Ngui

entry.summary: Presents SEA-Embedding, a fully open and reproducible text embedding pipeline for Southeast Asian languages trained only on public data, studying data composition, training objectives, and base encoder initialization. Achieves state-of-the-art on SEA-BED with reproducibility.

entry.title: The Word and the Way: Strategies for Domain-Specific BERT Pre-Training in German Medical NLP

author.name: Henry He, Johann Frei, Raphael Schmitt

entry.summary: Presents ChristBERT, a family of domain-specific German clinical RoBERTa models trained on a 13.5GB biomedical corpus, comparing continued pretraining, from-scratch training, and vocabulary adaptation. It addresses the gap in German biomedical language models.

entry.title: Tiny Collaborative Inference for Occlusion-Robust Object Detection

author.name: Chieh-Tung Cheng, Mustafa Aslanov, Eiman Kanjo

entry.summary: Evaluates occlusion-robust object detection on ultra-low-end devices with under 1MB SRAM by combining an MCUNet backbone, YOLOv2 head, and TFLite quantization. It compares feature-level and decision-level collaborative inference, finding weighted boxes fusion best under occlusion.

entry.title: MariData: One-Step Unpaired Image Translation for Maritime Environments

author.name: Santeri Henriksson, Mehdi Asadi, Amin Majd, Juha Kalliovaara

entry.summary: Introduces a framework using CycleGAN-turbo one-step unpaired image translation to generate synthetic maritime imagery for adverse weather and low-light conditions, with zero-convolution skip connections to preserve small navigational objects. It addresses data scarcity for autonomous surface ship perception.

entry.title: IDO: Incongruity-aware Distribution Optimization for Multimodal Fake News Detection

author.name: Hengyang Zhou, Rongman Hong, Yuxuan Zhou, Jing Wang, Zhaoyan Pan

entry.summary: IDO is a multimodal fake news detection method that explicitly models semantic incongruity through channel-wise reweighting and Gaussian distribution modeling for factual and modality mismatches. It moves beyond cross-modal consistency to detect deceptive content.

entry.title: Beyond Single Solution: Multi-Hypothesis Collaborative Deep Unfolding Network for Image Compressive Sensing

author.name: Wenxue Cui, Hualin Li, Yuhang Qin, Yifu Xu, Xiaopeng Fan, Debin Zhao

entry.summary: MHC-DUN is a deep unfolding network for image compressive sensing that explicitly models multiple plausible solution hypotheses, jointly optimizing across diverse solution spaces via proximal gradient descent. It addresses the ill-posedness ignored by single-solution methods.

entry.title: Fixed-Time Dynamic Landing of Quadrotors using Adaptive Unscented Kalman Filtering and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control

author.name: Mohammadreza Izadi, Zeinab Shayan, Steven Waslander, Reza Faieghi

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether short-term synaptic plasticity stabilizes goal-conditioned dynamics in a PFC-inspired reservoir model with basal-ganglia-style temporal-difference readout for multistep goal-directed action planning. It finds goal identity is decodable without STP but examines STP's role in maintaining action-usable dynamics.

entry.title: eMEM: A Hybrid Spatio-Temporal Memory System For Embodied Agents

author.name: A. Haroon Rasheed, Maria Kabtoul

entry.summary: eMEM is a hybrid graph-based memory system for embodied agents that indexes experience simultaneously by meaning, space, and time using SQLite, HNSW semantic search, and an R-tree for spatial queries. A tiered consolidation pipeline compresses raw observations, inspired by hippocampal-neocortical consolidation.

entry.title: Recovering Direct Price Effects of Environmental Amenities in Housing Markets: Regression and Causal Machine Learning Model Assessment with Empirical Monte Carlo Simulation

author.name: Zhenshan Chen (Virginia Tech), Klaus Moeltner (Virginia Tech), Matthew Mair (Virginia Tech)

entry.summary: This study uses an empirical Monte Carlo simulation grounded in over a million real property transactions to compare traditional hedonic regression and causal machine learning for estimating direct, unmediated price effects of environmental amenities (DUET). By randomly assigning treatment over a real data-generating process, it avoids parametric simulation assumptions.

entry.title: TriEval: A Resource-Efficient Pipeline for LLM Bias, Toxicity, and Truthfulness Assessment

author.name: Akshatha Srikantha, Manpreet Singh, Yash Jajoo, Shyamal Lakhanpal

entry.summary: TriEval is a resource-efficient pipeline for jointly assessing LLM bias, toxicity, and truthfulness while minimizing compute. It aims to make multi-parameter LLM evaluation accessible to researchers without large resources.

entry.title: IdiomX A Multilingual Benchmark for Idiom Understanding, Retrieval, and Interpretation

author.name: Ayman Ali Sharara

entry.summary: IdiomX is a large-scale multilingual benchmark for idiom understanding, retrieval, and interpretation, containing over 190K contextualized examples across 12K+ idioms built via a multi-stage pipeline. It targets the persistent NLP challenge of non-compositional, cross-lingual idiomatic meaning.

entry.title: ERP-XTTN: Interpretable Prototype-Guided Cross-Attention for Cross-Subject ERP Classification

author.name: Charlotte Genevier Wyman, Leanne Hirshfield

entry.summary: Proposes ERP-XTTN, an interpretable cross-attention architecture for cross-subject EEG event-related potential classification that routes inputs to fixed difference-wave prototypes via query-key-only attention, making attention faithfulness structural. Aims for calibration-free generalization across subjects.

entry.title: Rethinking Neural Width for Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow Proxies

author.name: Dhruvi Khandelwal, Anurag Basistha, Ayushi Jolotia, Parikshit Pareek

entry.summary: Investigates how wide a neural network must be to approximate the AC optimal power flow manifold, introducing a Loss-Guided Neural Densification algorithm that incrementally adds capacity only when needed. Achieves baseline performance with up to 10x fewer neurons per layer, aiding formal verification.

entry.title: Topology-Aware Gaussian Graph Repair for Robust Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Anubha Goel, Juho Kanniainen

entry.summary: Proposes TAGR (Topology-Aware Gaussian Repair), a graph repair framework for robust GNN message passing that can both remove noisy edges and recover missing connections, unlike methods that only prune. Avoids the optimization complexity of full graph structure learning.

entry.title: Low-Frequency Shortcuts in Texture-Driven Visual Learning

author.name: Utku \c{S}irin, Cathy Hou, David Alvarez-Melis, Stratos Idreos

entry.summary: Analyzes shortcut learning in texture-driven visual domains, showing they suffer from low-frequency shortcuts where decisions rely on a few low-frequency components despite classification information residing in higher-frequency details. Extends shortcut analysis beyond standard shape-driven benchmarks.

entry.title: Set-Preserving Calibration from Conformal P-Values to E-Values

author.name: Nabil Alami, Jad Zakharia, Souhaib Ben Taieb

entry.summary: Identifies limitations of classical p-to-e calibrators in conformal prediction, showing they are not set-preserving and lead to conservative prediction sets, and proposes a novel P2E calibrator that converts conformal p-values to e-values without altering the induced prediction set. Bridges p-value and e-value conformal formulations.

entry.title: Quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons exhibit less fragmented loss landscapes and outperform leaky integrate-and-fire neurons in spike-based gradient descent

author.name: Carlo Wenig, Raoul-Martin Memmesheimer, Christian Klos

entry.summary: Demonstrates that quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons exhibit less fragmented loss landscapes and outperform leaky integrate-and-fire neurons in exact spike-based gradient descent for spiking neural networks. Shows that smoother spike dynamics translate into practical training advantages.

entry.title: Memory Retrieval for Changing Preferences

author.name: Yuehan Qin, Li Li, Linxin Song, Wei Yang, Jiate Li, Yuqing Yang, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes a unified framework for memory access and selection in long-context dialogue that handles changing user preferences, quantifying memory turn utility via a Bayes factor measuring likelihood improvement rather than semantic similarity. Addresses both when and which memory to retrieve.

entry.title: Framing Migration News with LLMs: Structured CoT as a Support for Human Interpretation

author.name: David Alonso del Barrio, Jing Wen, Daniel Gatica-Perez

entry.summary: Studies a locally deployable open-source LLM with Structured Chain-of-Thought prompting to support interpretable, auditable frame analysis of migration news. It emphasizes privacy, reproducibility, and equitable access for media researchers.

entry.title: PHAF-Personalized Hand Avatars in a Flash

author.name: Meghana Shankar, Akanxit Upadhyay, Anmol Namdev, Green Rosh KS, Pawan Prasad BH

entry.summary: PHAF generates personalized photorealistic hand avatars from just two images using semantic-guided mesh alignment and densified texture extraction, enabling real-time edge deployment. It avoids slow optimization-based texture techniques.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Semi-supervised Multi-modal Crowd Counting

author.name: Haoliang Meng, Xiaopeng Hong, Yabin Wang, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: This paper builds the first benchmark for semi-supervised multi-modal crowd counting, defining a standardized labeled/unlabeled protocol and tailoring representative baselines. It establishes reference points for an unexplored task.

entry.title: TTT-VLA: Test-Time Latent Prompt Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Jianxiong Li, Shuai Yang, Sijin Chen, Jiajun Liu, Lingqiao Liu, Xiao Ma

entry.summary: TTT-VLA proposes a test-time training method for vision-language-action models that adapts a learned latent prompt during deployment to counter distribution shifts. It treats the prompt itself as a steerable interface that can be optimized from interaction, with an auxiliary proxy task during training.

entry.title: EaDex: A Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation Framework from Low-Cost Demonstrations

author.name: Qian Zhao, Xin Tong, Chengdong Wu, Yang Yang, Yingtian Li

entry.summary: EaDex is a cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation framework that generates demonstration data cheaply from a single RGB-D camera using MANO-based hand modeling and motion retargeting. It aims to cut the high data and training costs of dexterous manipulation learning.

entry.title: Human2Humanoid: Physics-Aware Cross-Morphology Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Tianchen Huang, Feiyang Yuan, Junchi Gu, Shurui Fang, Xiaohu Zhang, Yu Wang, Wei Gao, Shiwu Zhang

entry.summary: Human2Humanoid is an unsupervised motion retargeting framework that transfers human motion to humanoid robots using a CycleGAN with a skeleton-aware graph convolutional network to handle topology and scale mismatch without paired data. It targets teleoperation, imitation learning, and human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Multimodal Transformer Based Generic Mixture Density Network for Scattering Timescale Estimation of Fast Radio Bursts

author.name: Bikash Kharel, Emmanuel Fonseca, Srinjoy Das, Mason Ng, Paul Scholz, Mawson W. Simmons, Lordrick Kahinga, Afrokk Khan

entry.summary: MT-GMDN is a multimodal transformer-based mixture density network that ingests fast radio burst dynamic spectra to estimate scattering timescales quickly and robustly, replacing slow, initialization-sensitive template fitting and deconvolution. It targets the parameter-extraction bottleneck created by rising FRB discovery rates.

entry.title: Taking the Training Wheels Off: Aligning LLMs without Personas

author.name: Matthew Khoriaty

entry.summary: This post argues that nearly all current alignment techniques (RLHF, steering vectors, prompting) rely on eliciting good personas already present in the model and contends this approach will not scale to superhuman models, since there is no human-level persona data to extrapolate beyond human capabilities. It motivates moving toward alignment methods that do not depend on personas.

entry.title: Acceptance-Test-Driven Evaluation Protocols for Business-Centric LLM Systems

author.name: Eric Liang

entry.summary: This paper proposes an acceptance-test-driven evaluation protocol for business LLM systems, translating stakeholder goals into executable behavioral contracts, release gates, monitoring signals, and evidence artifacts. It adapts red-green-refactor discipline to bridge deterministic requirements with probabilistic generative components.

entry.title: RMPrior: Bridging Propagation Priors and Diffusion Refinement for Efficient Radio Map Construction

author.name: Zixuan Guo, Xiucheng Wang, Nan Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes RMPrior, a mid-start diffusion sampling strategy for radio map construction that initializes from a perturbed classical propagation prior rather than pure Gaussian noise, focusing computation on multipath-aware refinement. Reduces sampling cost for dynamic wireless systems.

entry.title: Flicker-DDPM: Accelerating Denoising Diffusion via 1/f Colored Noise Injection

author.name: Kexiang Mao

entry.summary: Proposes Flicker-DDPM, a diffusion model that injects 1/f colored noise (inspired by self-organized criticality) instead of white noise to better match the power-law spectra of natural images. Theoretically links a spatial correlation kernel parameter to the spectral exponent for adaptation.

entry.title: HiSE: A Lightweight Hierarchical Semantic Explainer for Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Zongrui Li, Yuhang Zhao, Ying Zhao, Yuanzhao Guo, Qiang Huang, Yuan Tian

entry.summary: Proposes HiSE, a lightweight feature-oriented explainer for heterogeneous graph neural networks that reflects the model's inherent semantic hierarchy while avoiding costly search or perturbation. Aims to improve fidelity and efficiency of HGNN explanations.

entry.title: How Visible Are Silent Manipulation Failures? An Observability Study of False-Success Detection in Simulated Robot Episodes

author.name: Aarav Bedi (University of California, Berkeley)

entry.summary: An observability study examining how detectable false-success failures are in simulated robot manipulation episodes, asking how much overturning information comes from proprioception versus vision. Builds a bimanual ALOHA testbed with privileged ground-truth labels.

entry.title: A 3D Isovist World Model -- Revealing a City's Unseen Geometry and Its Emergent Cross-City Signature

author.name: Xuhui Lin, Stephen Law, Nanjiang Chen, Kunyao Li, Tao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a 3D isovist world model that predicts navigable geometry an agent can traverse rather than scene appearance or flattened occupancy grids, preserving multi-level 3D structure for embodied navigation. Reveals an emergent cross-city geometric signature.

entry.title: MLSkip: Data Skipping for ML Filters via Lightweight Metadata

author.name: Mihail Stoian, Mark Gerarts, Pascal Ginter, Andreas Zimmerer, Jan Van den Bussche, Andreas Kipf

entry.summary: Initiates the study of data skipping for ML filter predicates in databases, showing that Parquet's default min-max metadata can enable pruning of non-qualifying row groups for black-box ML model filters. Connects to ML query languages and neural network verification.

entry.title: Mixed-Modality Dual Face-Hair Retrieval

author.name: Quoc-Anh Bui-Huynh, Mai-Tuyen Lam, Dai-Anh-Tuan Nguyen, Thanh Duc Ngo

entry.summary: Dual Face-Hair Retrieval introduces a mixed-modality retrieval task where queries combine a face identity image with a hairstyle reference (image or text), plus a 180K-triplet benchmark. It requires disentangling identity and hairstyle from heterogeneous modalities.

entry.title: AvatarMix: Identity-Preserving Cross-Avatar Composition for Outfit Personalization

author.name: Zhaorong Wang, Yoshihiro Kanamori, Yuki Endo

entry.summary: AvatarMix composes head and body from two high-fidelity Gaussian avatars for outfit personalization, avoiding intersection artifacts and identity degradation. It adds a SeamFix diffusion module to refine joins after body reshaping.

entry.title: An Attention-Based Denoising Model for Diffusion Weighted Imaging

author.name: Prithviraj Verma, Pawan Kumar, Chandan Deshani, Prasun Chandra Tripathi

entry.summary: This work proposes a noise-aware attention denoising framework for diffusion-weighted MRI combining Swin Transformer window attention with gated refinement and explicit noise-level conditioning. It targets signal-dependent Rician noise from fast acquisitions.

entry.title: Bionic Human-Motion Style Transfer for Physically Executable Whole-Body Control of Humanoid Robots

author.name: Tianchen Huang, Mingkuan Zhao, Yang Gao, Feiyang Yuan, Junchi Gu, Xiaohu Zhang, Dongdong Zhao, Shi Yan, Yu Wang, Wei Gao, Shiwu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a generation-to-control framework for transferring human motion style (gait rhythm, posture, arm swing) onto humanoid robots from a short exemplar while producing physically executable whole-body motion. It aims to reuse a demonstrated style across different motion contents.

entry.title: CANMOT: Class-Aware Noise Modeling for Multi-Object Tracking in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Timo Osterburg, Stefan Sch\"utte, Torsten Bertram

entry.summary: CANMOT introduces class-aware noise modeling for Kalman-filter-based 3D multi-object tracking in autonomous driving, replacing globally shared process/measurement covariances with class-specific, object-frame-aligned matrices that preserve longitudinal-lateral anisotropy. It systematically evaluates the impact of this refinement.

entry.title: Toward a Modular Architecture for Embedded AI Agent Systems at the Edge

author.name: Marcus R\"ub, Michael Gerhards

entry.summary: Proposes a modular tiered reference architecture for deploying agentic AI on embedded microcontrollers, decoupling low-latency on-device agents from heavier cloud reasoning. It targets the gap between server-class agent frameworks and edge constraints.

entry.title: The Violation Situation Pattern: A Knowledge-Graph Pattern for Compliance Violations

author.name: Nima Kamali Lassem, Fuqi Song, Seyid Amjad Ali

entry.summary: The Violation Situation Pattern reifies detected compliance violations as persistent knowledge-graph nodes with rule identifiers, temporal validity, lifecycle state, and PROV-O-aligned audit history. It is instantiated on a legal entity and contract lifecycle property graph.

entry.title: Calibrating Urban Traffic Simulation from Sparse Road Observations via Genetic Optimization

author.name: Hunter Sawyer, Jesse Roberts, Simon Matei

entry.summary: Presents a genetic algorithm framework for calibrating urban traffic simulations from sparse road observations without requiring detailed employment or job-location data. It addresses two key data limitations for realistic city-scale traffic simulation using the SUMO platform.

entry.title: A Hybrid Approach For Malware Classification Using Secondary Features Fusion

author.name: Raja Khurram Shahzad, Muhammad Mustaqeem, Haroon Elahi

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid malware classification method using feature fusion of API calls and n-grams with customized feature selection to both detect malware and classify it into families. Aims to improve malware mitigation beyond binary detection.

entry.title: A Nonmonotone Gradient-Based Algorithm for Symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization and Graph Clustering

author.name: Ryan Swart, Johannes Brust

entry.summary: Introduces SNMPBB, the first adaptation of nonmonotone projected Barzilai-Borwein methods to symmetric nonnegative matrix factorization, with extensions for graph clustering and low-rank approximations. Proves global convergence and shows gradient methods are more effective than previously believed.

entry.title: Coherent Swap Regret and Channel-Proof Learning

author.name: Sohail Sarkar

entry.summary: Introduces coherent swap regret as a regret benchmark against local CPTP quantum deviations in quantum games, with an algorithm achieving sublinear regret via entropic mirror ascent. Establishes a three-level deviation-class landscape connecting quantum and classical online learning.

entry.title: Resource-Constrained Adaptive Inference for Sequential Pricing

author.name: Ruicheng Ao, Jiashuo Jiang, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: Formalizes a support-exclusion failure in resource-constrained sequential pricing where the resource state can make target-price inference impossible, and designs a target-aware controller that certifies feasible bands and logs continuous densities for valid inference. Provides regret-information accounting under resource constraints.

entry.title: DiffUNet^2: Bidirectional Prediction, Probabilistic Generation and Collaborative Visual Discovery for Scientific Data

author.name: Mengdi Chu, Jiaxin Yang, Angus G. Forbes, Nathan Debardeleben, Earl Lawrence, Ayan Biswas, Han-Wei Shen

entry.summary: Presents DiffUNet2, a conditional diffusion model enabling bidirectional any-to-any generation across time for scientific data, integrated with interactive visual analytics supporting branching timelines and probabilistic exploration. Adds backward reasoning and uncertainty to scientific forecasting.

entry.title: Predicting Inference-Time Scaling Gains from Labeled Validation-Set Output Statistics

author.name: Luyang Zhang, Jingyan Li

entry.summary: Studies predicting best-of-N inference scaling gains in advance using cheap statistics from a single labeled validation-set sampling pass, fitting ridge predictors and using bootstrap-Lasso for stability. Identifies a compact stable predictor of best-of-N accuracy gain.

entry.title: When Does Complexity Conditioning Help a Frozen Sentence Embedding? A Controlled Study of Per-Sentence and Pair-Level Difficulty Adaptation

author.name: Suhwan Hwang

entry.summary: A controlled study testing whether conditioning frozen sentence embeddings on input difficulty helps, finding the naive per-sentence complexity approach fails and provides no advantage over controls. It cautions against an intuitive but unsupported design idea.

entry.title: Diagnosis of Human Object Interaction Detectors for Real World Educational Applications

author.name: Divya Mereddy, Ashwin Tudur Sadashiva, Marcos Quinones-Grueiro, Gautam Biswas

entry.summary: Presents a diagnosis-driven framework with a triplet-level HOI error taxonomy and error-factor attribution for human-object interaction detection in real-world educational video, using mixed-reality medical training data. It analyzes failure modes from domain objects, occlusions, and complex conditions.

entry.title: Cross-Modality Feature Fusion Based on Structured State Space Duality for Multimodal Image Registration Network

author.name: Zhikang Li, Yan Wu, Xin Hu, Yi Dai, Ming Li

entry.summary: RegNetMamba-2 applies Structured State Space Duality (Mamba-style) for efficient cross-modality feature fusion in multi-modal image registration. It targets shared structural feature extraction with better efficiency than Transformers.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Mixed Masked Pretraining and Spatial Continuity Regularization for Printed Circuit Board Defect Detection

author.name: Peitong Wang, Nuo Wang, Enxin Qin, Chengjin Yu, Hanyu Xuan, Yuanting Yan

entry.summary: This paper combines structure-guided mixed masked pretraining with spatial continuity regularization for PCB defect detection, targeting tiny low-contrast defects in dense backgrounds. It leverages unlabeled images via sparse convolutional masked pretraining.

entry.title: Short-Term Synaptic Plasticity Stabilizes Goal-Conditioned Dynamics in a PFC-Inspired Reservoir Model for Multistep Goal-Directed Action Planning

author.name: Jin Nakamura, Yuichi Katori

entry.summary: This work evolves pairs of CTRNN agents that use communication for predator avoidance, finding three dominant survival strategies including self-regulatory calling where agents depend on hearing their own vocalizations. It explores communication as more than information transfer in natural-like systems.

entry.title: NVIDIA Isaac Sim: Enabling Scalable, GPU-Accelerated Simulation for Robotics

author.name: Sicong Gao, Maurice Pagnucco, Tomasz Bednarz, Yang Song

entry.summary: This survey reviews NVIDIA Isaac Sim from system and application perspectives, detailing its GPU-accelerated architecture, synthetic data pipeline, and usage patterns, and comparing it against widely used robotics simulators. It also analyzes representative studies and limitations.

entry.title: Semantic-weighted ICP for LiDAR Odometry: Class-Aware Residual Reweighting for Robust Scan Registration

author.name: Vasco Carvalho, Tiago Barros, Urbano J. Nunes

entry.summary: This work proposes semantic class-weighted ICP for LiDAR odometry, reweighting registration residuals by class relevance rather than treating all environmental elements equally. It improves robustness in dynamic and unstructured scenes with moving objects, vegetation, and ambiguous structures.

entry.title: Claude Opus 4.8: Capabilities and Reactions

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's post aggregates benchmarks, model-card tests, and community reactions to characterize Claude Opus 4.8, arguing that understanding a new model requires many calibrated data points rather than a few benchmarks. It synthesizes capability and model-welfare information into a coherent picture of the model's behavior.

entry.title: Large AI Models in Dental Healthcare: From General-Purpose Systems to Domain-Specific Foundation Models

author.name: Sema Helali, Lina Abu Nadab, Sausan Alqawas, Alaa Abd-Alrazaq, Faleh Tamimi, Rafat Damseh

entry.summary: A PRISMA-guided scoping review of large AI models in dentistry, classifying language-generative, vision foundation, and dental-specific foundation models across 97 studies. It proposes a two-dimensional classification framework.

entry.title: From Prompt to Service: An SLM-Based Agent Orchestration Gateway for AI-Driven Virtual Worlds

author.name: Louis Nisiotis, Aimilios Hadjiliasi

entry.summary: Presents an SLM-based agent orchestration gateway for AI-driven virtual worlds that uses an edge-deployed small language model to classify user intent and route requests to heterogeneous AI backends. It decouples virtual world clients from backend models for extensibility.

entry.title: Leveraging BART to Assess CS1 C++ Programming Assignments using Rubric-based Criteria

author.name: Kelsey Rainey, Jesse Roberts

entry.summary: Uses a BART encoder-decoder with LoRA adaptation and multitask fine-tuning to automatically grade introductory C++ programming assignments according to rubric criteria, with a distribution-matching term to align predicted and empirical grade distributions. It aims to better reflect instructor grading behavior than general-purpose LLMs.

entry.title: Wavelet as Tokenizer: Preliminary Results on a Shared Wavelet Token Schema for Natural Signals

author.name: Shenghao Ding

entry.summary: This preliminary work studies whether audio, images, and video can share a common wavelet token schema using a Haar DWT/IDWT frontend and shared encoder-decoder trunk, rather than modality-specific latents. It reports reconstruction PSNRs across speech, satellite imagery, and video.

entry.title: CL-DMDF:Dynamic Multimodal Data Fusion Model Based on Contrastive Learning

author.name: Dong Li, Lingling Zhang, Binghao Han, Linlin Ding, Yue Kou

entry.summary: CL-DMDF is a dynamic multimodal data fusion model using contrastive learning to handle uncertain or missing modality inputs while capturing global complementary cues rather than over-emphasizing local interactions. It targets robustness in real-world multimodal settings.

entry.title: BotDirector: Robot Storytelling Across the Symmetrical Reality with Multi-modal Interactions

author.name: Zhe Sun, Meng Wang, Lei Wang, Yuxi Wang, Wanxin Li, Yujia Peng, Zhenliang Zhang

entry.summary: BotDirector is an interactive robot storytelling system where children arrange a physical playground and create narratives with an LLM agent, which are transformed into motion sequences executed by swarm robots.
