entry.title: Thinking Economically: A Hierarchical Framework for Adaptive-Complexity Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Yubo Gao, Haotian Wu, Hong Chen, Junquan Huang, Yibo Yan, Jungang Li, Zihao Dongfang, Sicheng Tao, Puay Siew Tan, Jie Zhang, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Hierarchical Adaptive Budgeter that allocates reasoning compute based on intrinsic task and step demands rather than uniform compression, addressing chain-of-thought overthinking. It exploits the heterogeneity of reasoning complexity across problems and within individual steps.

entry.title: DrugClaw and DrugAudit: A Primary-Source-Grounded Agent and Authority-Aware Benchmark for Drug-Information Question Answering

author.name: Qing Wang, Bo Li, Jialu Liang, Daling Shi, Bob Zhang, Qianqian Song

entry.summary: DrugClaw is a multi-agent retrieval-augmented system for drug-information QA grounded in primary regulatory or peer-reviewed records via a reflection-driven state machine, paired with DrugAudit, an authority-aware benchmark scoring source match and citation faithfulness. It targets the high-stakes need for provenance in clinical drug information.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM-as-a-Judge for Long-Form Output Evaluation

author.name: Junjie Chen, Yuxi Dong, Haitao Li, Weihang Su, Yujia Zhou, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu, Qinyao Ai

entry.summary: LongJudgeBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM judges on long-form outputs across diverse scenarios and judging protocols, addressing the gap that prior meta-evaluations focus on short-form outputs. It examines document-level demands that distinguish long-form from short-form evaluation.

entry.title: Physical Object Understanding with a Physically Controllable World Model

author.name: Rahul Venkatesh, Klemen Kotar, Lilian Naing Chen, Wanhee Lee, Gia Ancone, Seungwoo Kim, Luca Thomas Wheeler, Jared Watrous, Honglin Chen, Daniel Bear, Stefan Stojanov, Daniel LK Yamins

entry.summary: This paper introduces a class of probabilistic world models trained efficiently via autoregressive sequence modeling that support estimating the probability of any visual variable conditioned on others. Rich object understanding emerges, enabling inference of physical scene structure from raw videos.

entry.title: Thinking in Blender: Staged Executable Inverse Graphics with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Guangzhao He, Rundong Luo, Wei-Chiu Ma, Hadar Averbuch-Elor

entry.summary: SEIG is an agentic framework that uses pretrained VLMs to perform inverse graphics directly, reconstructing single images into editable Blender programs through staged refinement of geometry, materials, and lighting. Avoids specialized 3D foundation models or differentiable rendering.

entry.title: Breaking the Cascade: Compact Nonlinear Optical Computing with Single-Layer Encoder-Decoder Co-Localization

author.name: Yuntian Wang, Alexander Chen, Md Sadman Sakib Rahman, Aydogan Ozcan

entry.summary: Demonstrates that nonlinear computing can be achieved with a single linear diffractive surface via encoder-decoder co-localization and coherent interference, proven to be a universal approximator for band-limited nonlinear functions. Eliminates need for nonlinear materials or multiple layers.

entry.title: GraspGen-X: Cross-Embodiment 6-DOF Diffusion-based Grasping

author.name: Beining Han, Yu-Wei Chao, Erwin Coumans, Clemens Eppner, Balakumar Sundaralingam, Jia Deng, Stan Birchfield, Adithyavairavan Murali

entry.summary: GraspGen-X extends diffusion-based 6-DOF grasping to condition on gripper morphology via a swept-volume heuristic, trained on procedural grippers and 2 billion grasps for zero-shot generalization to novel real-world grippers and objects. Also serves as good initialization for finetuning.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Pairwise Preferences in Long-Term Decision Problems

author.name: Jonathan Cola\c{c}o Carr, Prakash Panangaden, Doina Precup, Benjamin Van Roy

entry.summary: Proposes the Markov decision contest as a new model for RL with pairwise preferences, addressing inefficiency in long-horizon problems and the lack of guarantees on Markov versus history-dependent policies. Proves theoretical results bridging preference-based RL theory and practice.

entry.title: Detect Before You Leap: Mirage Detection in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury, Md. Shaown Miah

entry.summary: This work addresses the mirage failure mode where vision-language models answer confidently despite missing visual evidence, proposing a model-agnostic method that probes CLIP encoder patch tokens to decide whether to answer or abstain before generation. It targets safety-critical medical and document VQA.

entry.title: Linguistics-Aware Non-Distortionary LLM Watermarking

author.name: Shinwoo Park, Hyejin Park, Hyeseon An, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: LUNA is a linguistically adaptive, non-distortionary LLM watermark using model-free detection that estimates next-tag entropy from part-of-speech contexts to set sampler depth, supporting multilingual deployment. It is evaluated across six typologically diverse languages.

entry.title: Scaling Behavior of Single LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jialing Li, Zhouhong Gu, Yin Cai, Hongwei Feng

entry.summary: This paper studies scaling behavior of homogeneous single-LLM multi-agent systems using a minimalist sequential framework to isolate collaboration effects, finding that performance does not scale monotonically with agent count. It characterizes intrinsic collective dynamics.

entry.title: SORA: Free Second-Order Attacks in Fast Adversarial Training

author.name: Mazdak Teymourian, Ramtin Moslemi, Farzan Rahmani, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: SORA introduces second-order attacks into fast adversarial training nearly for free, formalizing Epsilon Overfitting and showing perturbation variability improves robust generalization. It also proposes PertAlign, a cheap metric predicting catastrophic overfitting onset via gradient alignment.

entry.title: Lodestar: An Online-Learning LLM Inference Router

author.name: Gangmuk Lim, Wanyu Zhao, Brighten Godfrey, Jiaxin Shan, Le Xu, Liguang Xie

entry.summary: Lodestar is an online-learning request router for distributed LLM inference clusters that continually adapts to input-dependent execution, batching, KV-cache coupling, and heterogeneous accelerators to optimize latency and GPU utilization. It outperforms traditional load balancers and LLM-specific heuristics.

entry.title: Plausibility Is Not Prediction: Contrastive Evidence for LLM-Based Cellular Perturbation Reasoning

author.name: Xinyu Yuan, Xixian Liu, Jianan Zhao, Yashi Zhang, Hongyu Guo, Jian Tang

entry.summary: Demonstrates with contrastive evidence that LLM-based cellular perturbation reasoning produces biologically plausible explanations but fails to predict actual perturbation effects, often underperforming simple frequency baselines. A critical assessment of LLMs as virtual cell simulators.

entry.title: What Makes a Strong Model? A Unified Spectral Analysis of Knowledge Transfer over High-dimensional Linear Regression

author.name: Wendao Wu, Fangqing Zhang, Haihan Zhang, Cong Fang

entry.summary: Establishes a unified spectral analysis of SGD dynamics in high-dimensional linear regression explaining knowledge transfer efficiency across knowledge distillation and weak-to-strong generalization. Identifies distinct mechanisms like spectral horizon expansion.

entry.title: AgentRedBench: Dynamic Redteaming and Integration-Aware Defense for LLM Agents over SaaS Integrations

author.name: Hiskias Dingeto, Will Leeney

entry.summary: Introduces AgentRedBench, a dynamic LLM-driven red-teaming benchmark of 215 underspecified-authorization indirect prompt injection scenarios across 24 enterprise SaaS integrations. Argues existing benchmarks under-measure realistic tool-use threats and that open guards are trained on the wrong data.

entry.title: World Models: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Methodologies, Reasoning Paradigms, and Applications

author.name: Arif Hassan Zidan, Yi Pan, Hanqi Jiang, Ruiyu Yan, Wei Ruan, Zihao Wu, Lifeng Chen, Weihang You, Xinliang Li, Bowen Chen, Huawen Hu, Peilong Wang, Sizhuang Liu, Jing Zhang, Siyuan Li, Zhengliang Liu, Yu Bao, Lin Zhao, Lichao Sun, Dajiang Zhu, Xiang Li, Jinglei Lv, Quanzheng Li, Wei Liu, Tianming Liu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Surveys world models as internal environment simulators, proposing a multi-axis taxonomy across architecture, methodology, reasoning paradigms, and applications spanning RL, robotics, autonomous driving, and video generation. Aims to unify a fragmented field central to AGI pursuits.

entry.title: Generate in Reconstruction Space, Match in Semantic Space: Transport Geometry for One-Step Generation

author.name: Hugues Van Assel, Edward De Brouwer, Saeed Saremi, Gabriele Scalia, Aviv Regev

entry.summary: Proposes a one-step generation framework that decouples generation in reconstruction space from matching in frozen SSL semantic space using Sinkhorn divergence, clarifying why SSL features help generative training. Authors include researchers from Genentech/Regev lab.

entry.title: Normalized Relevance Measure as a Unifying Framework to Explain Neural Network Latent Structures

author.name: Ping Xiong, Thomas Schnake, Gr\'egoire Montavon, Klaus-Robert M\"uller, Shinichi Nakajima

entry.summary: Proposes the Normalized Relevance Measure framework attributing relevance to arbitrary sets of neurons across layers and architectures, unifying explanation methods for latent structures. Builds on the LRP/explainability lineage with strong authors.

entry.title: Local MixVR: Breaking the Communication-Sample Dependence in Distributed Learning

author.name: Tehila Dahan, Bassel Hamoud, Roie Reshef, Martin Jaggi, Kfir Y. Levy

entry.summary: Introduces Local MixVR, the first distributed learning method whose communication-round complexity is independent of total sample count N, scaling only with the number of workers via local updates plus variance reduction. Outperforms state-of-the-art when worker count is small relative to samples.

entry.title: Physics from Video: Identifiability of Time-Invariant Second-Order ODEs under Minimal Trajectory Conditions

author.name: Yuanyuan Wang, Wenjie Wang, Kun Zhang, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: Studies structural identifiability of continuous-time physical laws from raw video pixels, proving conditions under which second-order linear ODE parameters can be uniquely recovered and characterizing minimal data requirements across damping regimes. Advances theoretical foundations for video-based world models.

entry.title: The Representation-Rationalizability Tradeoff in Reward Learning

author.name: Jing Dong, Yaoliang Yu, Pascal Pourpart

entry.summary: Analyzes a representation-rationalizability tradeoff in RLHF reward learning, extending social-choice impossibility results to settings with infinite candidate response spaces rather than fixed finite alternatives. Provides theoretical grounding for limits of scalar reward models.

entry.title: Quantifying the Salience of Geo-Cultural Values for Pluralistic Safety Alignment

author.name: Arkadiy Saakyan, Charvi Rastogi, Lora Aroyo

entry.summary: Conducts a meta-analysis showing most safety evaluation datasets omit geo-cultural information and demonstrates via multilevel modeling that cultural zone membership explains variance in safety ratings beyond demographics. Argues for pluralistic, culturally representative safety alignment.

entry.title: Internalize the Temperature: On-Policy Self-Distillation as Policy Reheater for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuewei Yang, Jiachen Yu, Jie Wu, Shaoning Sun, Junjie Wang, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Temperature-Scaled On-Policy Self-Distillation to internalize exploratory temperature effects into model parameters, mitigating entropy collapse in RL from verifiable rewards for LLM reasoning. Acts as a lightweight policy reheating method from an entropy-collapsed checkpoint.

entry.title: Unlocking the Black Box of Latent Reasoning: An Interpretability-Guided Approach to Intervention

author.name: Shuochen Chang, Tong Bai, Xiaofeng Zhang, Qianli Ma, Qingyang Liu, Zhaohe Liao, Yibo Miao, Li Niu

entry.summary: Analyzes latent reasoning in LLMs using structural, causal, and geometric probes, finding that continuous thought vectors encode faithful compressed reasoning steps with early vectors acting as causal hubs. It then introduces training-free decode-time interventions to refine latent reasoning.

entry.title: Parameter Alignment Mitigates Catastrophic Forgetting in Multilingual Expert Language Models

author.name: Sanchit Ahuja, Terra Blevins

entry.summary: This work links catastrophic forgetting in multilingual continual pretraining to parameter drift and proposes five layer-aware alignment strategies including freezing, regularization, weight reversion, and model merging. It systematically compares these across 32 training languages from five families.

entry.title: Citation Grounding: Detecting and Reducing LLM Citation Hallucinations via Legal Citation Graphs

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: This paper proposes citation grounding, a metric verifying LLM-generated legal citations against a ground-truth graph built from over 100 million Ukrainian court decisions, decomposing into precision, relevance, and temporality. It enables differential diagnosis of legal citation hallucination types.

entry.title: Decoding in Order-Agnostic Language Models: Chain-Rule Deviation and Uniform Spreading

author.name: Lin Yao

entry.summary: This paper analyzes decoding in order-agnostic language models including diffusion LLMs, showing that learned conditionals do not form a coherent joint distribution and reveal order shifts log-likelihood by up to 0.49 nats/token. It examines confidence-first decoding behavior and proposes diagnostics for uniform spreading.

entry.title: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems

author.name: Mingju Chen, Can Lv, Guibin Zhang, Heng Chang, Shiji Zhou

entry.summary: HarnessForge is a meta-adaptive framework that jointly evolves an agent system's external harness and internal reasoning policy as a coupled harness-policy pair, addressing the unoptimized compatibility between structure and execution. It enables full-system adaptation across heterogeneous task regimes.

entry.title: RoboDream: Compositional World Models for Scalable Robot Data Synthesis

author.name: Junjie Ye, Rong Xue, Basile Van Hoorick, Runhao Li, Harshitha Rajaprakash, Pavel Tokmakov, Muhammad Zubair Irshad, Vitor Guizilini, Yue Wang

entry.summary: RoboDream is an embodiment-centric world model that synthesizes photorealistic robot demonstrations with novel objects, scenes, and viewpoints by anchoring generation to rendered robot motion and scene priors. Addresses costly teleoperation data collection.

entry.title: $\tau_0$-WM: A Unified Video-Action World Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Pengfei Zhou, Shengcong Chen, Di Chen, Jiaxu Wang, Rongjun Jin, Bingwen Zhu, Yike Pan, Songen Gu, Kuanning Wang, Shufeng Nan, Xingyu Qiu, Chenhao Qiu, Pu Yang, Yunuo Cai, Jianxiong Gao, Yifan Li, Yanwei Fu, Xiangyu Yue, Zhi Chen, Jianlan Luo

entry.summary: tau0-WM is a unified video-action world model integrating policy learning, video prediction, and action evaluation on a shared video diffusion backbone, offering both a video-action policy and an action-conditioned video simulator for rolling out and scoring candidate actions. Targets executable manipulation with consequence anticipation.

entry.title: Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact

author.name: Todd Nief, Harvey Yiyun Fu, Mark Muchane, Ari Holtzman

entry.summary: This paper argues that subliminal learning—transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated finetuning data—is a LoRA artifact, showing an inverted U-shaped dependence on LoRA rank and that it disappears under full finetuning. It also finds strong dependence on finetuning and evaluation context.

entry.title: The Case for Model Science: Verify, Explore, Steer, Refine

author.name: Przemyslaw Biecek, Luca Longo, Jianlong Zhou, Thomas Fel, Andreas Holzinger, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: This position paper argues for consolidating model analysis into a systematic discipline termed Model Science, organized around verify, explore, steer, and refine, to move beyond benchmark-driven progress that reveals whether but not why models succeed or fail. It draws analogies from established sciences.

entry.title: Food Noise & False Safety: A Systematic Evaluation of How LLMs Fail to Adapt to Eating Disorder Queries with Clinician Feedback

author.name: Giulia Pucci, Emily Hemendinger, Ruizhe Li, Gavin Abercrombie, Tanvi Dinkar, Arabella Sinclair

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates how LLMs fail to safely handle eating-disorder queries, finding with clinician input that specific linguistic cues increase unsafe, uncritically adaptive responses that may facilitate self-harm. Highlights real harms from perceived AI expertise.

entry.title: CardioLens: Revealing the Clinical Reality Gap of MLLMs via Multi-Sequence Cardiac MRI Evaluations

author.name: Zixian Su, Hongkai Zhang, Fan Gao, Encheng Su, Taiping Qu, Jingwei Guo, Nan Zhang, Hui Wang, Zhen Zhou, Kairui Bo, Yan Chen, Yue Ren, Shuai Li, Lei Xu, Henggui Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CardioLens, a leakage-resistant evaluation testbed for multi-sequence cardiac MRI built from private hospital archives with nearly 474k slices and 13.5k verified QA pairs. Evaluating 24 MLLMs reveals a substantial clinical reality gap on real diagnostic tasks.

entry.title: Emergence of Exploration in Policy Gradient Reinforcement Learning via Retrying

author.name: Soichiro Nishimori, Paavo Parmas, Sotetsu Koyamada, Tadashi Kozuno, Toshinori Kitamura, Shin Ishii, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Introduces ReMax, an RL objective evaluating policies by expected maximum return over M samples while accounting for return uncertainty, inducing stochastic exploration as an emergent property without explicit bonuses. Derives a new policy-gradient formulation and ReMax PPO (RePPO).

entry.title: StressDream: Steering Video World Models for Robust Policy Evaluation and Improvement

author.name: Junwon Seo, Sushant Veer, Ran Tian, Wenhao Ding, Apoorva Sharma, Karen Leung, Edward Schmerling, Marco Pavone, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: Proposes StressDream, which steers diffusion-based video world model imaginations toward high-impact yet plausible outcomes by optimizing initial noise at inference time for robust policy evaluation and improvement. It avoids needing prohibitively many samples to capture rare high-impact futures.

entry.title: Zamba2-VL Technical Report

author.name: Hassan Shapourian, Kasra Hejazi, Olabode M. Sule, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: Presents Zamba2-VL, vision-language models built on a hybrid Mamba2 state-space plus shared-transformer backbone, competitive with leading Transformer VLMs like Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 while delivering roughly an order of magnitude lower time-to-first-token. It substantially outperforms prior SSM-based and hybrid VLMs.

entry.title: A Distribution-Free Framework for Rewrite-Based Human-text Detection via Knockoff Filtering

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: This paper reframes rewrite-based detection of LLM-generated text as a knockoff-filtering multiple hypothesis testing problem, giving existing detectors finite-sample false discovery rate guarantees via calibration without retraining. It validates across multiple detectors, domains, and LLMs.

entry.title: SPADER: Step-wise Peer Advantage with Diversity-Aware Exploration Rewards for Multi-Answer Question Answering

author.name: Qiming Shi, Zhaolu Kang, Yunfan Zhou, Di Weng, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: SPADER is an RL framework for multi-answer QA with tool-augmented agents, introducing step-wise peer advantage for credit assignment and diversity-aware exploration rewards to discover comprehensive answer sets. It tackles fine-grained credit and exploration beyond high-frequency entities.

entry.title: MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs

author.name: Qingshan Liu, Guoqing Wang, Wen Wu, Jingqi Huang, Xinqi Tao, Dejia Song, Jie Zhou, Liang He

entry.summary: MemPro treats the entire memory construction-retrieval pipeline of an agent as an evolvable program rather than just adapting the memory bank, enabling system-level evolution to handle heterogeneous failure modes. It targets long-horizon autonomous agents.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Conformal Prediction with Personalized Statistical Validity

author.name: Martin V. Vejling, Christophe A. N. Biscio, Adrien Mazoyer, Petar Popovski, Shashi Raj Pandey

entry.summary: PFWCP is a personalized federated conformal prediction framework combining local density-ratio weighting with weighted quantile aggregation to provide valid uncertainty quantification under heterogeneity and privacy constraints. It yields asymptotically valid personalized coverage guarantees.

entry.title: GenPT: Beyond Self-Report for Reliable LLM Psychometrics via Generative Projective Testing

author.name: Ming Wang, Shuang Wu, Bixuan Wang, Lu Lin, Yuxin Chen, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Shi Feng, Yifei Zhang, Yufan Sun

entry.summary: GenPT reformulates projective psychological tests (TAT, Rorschach, SCT) with newly generated stimuli to assess persona-conditioned LLM agents, avoiding contamination and directional bias of self-report questionnaires. It organizes assessment into a standardized three-stage pipeline.

entry.title: Accuracy, Stability, and Repeated-Run Reliability of Large Language Models on Deterministic Programming Tasks

author.name: Yongxi Zhou, Lai Yun Choi, Jiaxi Wen, Wenbo Ye

entry.summary: This paper shows that run-level pass rate overstates retry-free coverage by up to 17.8 points, with the gap largest for mid-performing systems, and introduces a repeated-run evaluation protocol measuring accuracy, retry-free coverage, and per-problem variability on deterministic programming tasks. It highlights stability as a distinct deployment requirement.

entry.title: Explainable deep reinforcement learning reveals energy-efficient control strategies for turbulent drag reduction

author.name: Federica Tonti, Ricardo Vinuesa

entry.summary: Combines multi-agent deep reinforcement learning with SHAP-based explainability to discover energy-efficient flow control strategies for reducing drag in turbulent flows. The SHAP-guided rewards based on skin-friction and wall-pressure outperform standard opposition control baselines.

entry.title: Strong Stochastic Flow Maps

author.name: Sam McCallum, Zander W. Blasingame, Timothy Herschell, Niklas Rindtorff, Alexander Tong, James Foster

entry.summary: Proposes Strong Stochastic Flow Maps for learning the strong solution map of SDEs, extending flow-map methods beyond ODE marginals to recover solution paths. Enables few-step sampling that captures pathwise behavior.

entry.title: RLVR without Ineffective Samples: Group Prioritized Off-Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yixiu Mao, Yun Qu, Qi Wang, Heming Zou, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Proposes Group Prioritized Off-Policy Optimization for RLVR, addressing the prevalence of ineffective zero-variance training samples by reusing off-policy data without costly rollout filtering. Improves data efficiency for LLM reasoning training.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Memory: Mechanistic Diagnostics of Latent Visual Reasoning

author.name: Garvin Guo, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Xinpei Zhao, Huaxing Liu, Shuai Dong

entry.summary: Decomposes latent visual reasoning tokens into latent slots, boundary markers, and format to diagnose the true source of gains, finding that latent slots fail every prediction of the visual-evidence hypothesis. Challenges the assumption that continuous latent tokens encode visual information.

entry.title: Efficient Exploration for Iterative Nash Preference Optimization

author.name: Tianlong Nan, Xiaopeng Li, Christian Kroer, Tianyi Lin

entry.summary: Provides learning-theoretic foundations for scalable Nash Learning from Human Feedback, addressing efficient exploration for iterative Nash preference optimization where preferences may be cyclic or non-transitive. Bridges the gap between oracle-based regret guarantees and easier-to-implement iterative methods.

entry.title: Move the Query, Not the Cache: Characterizing Cross-Instance Latent Attention Redistribution Across GPU Fabrics

author.name: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald K\"ostler, Gerhard Wellein

entry.summary: This work characterizes cross-instance attention for sparse-attention LLMs, arguing that with Multi-head Latent Attention it is cheaper to route compressed queries than to move KV-cache blocks across GPUs. It addresses agentic workloads where many sub-agents query a large shared codebase partitioned across GPUs.

entry.title: Defenses & Enablers For Skill Injection Attacks on Terminal Based Agents

author.name: Yoshinari Fujinuma, Varun Gangal, Traian Rebedea, Makesh Narasimhan Sreedhar, Prasoon Varshney, Rebecca Qian, Anand Kannappan

entry.summary: This work studies skill-injection attacks on terminal-based LLM agents, proposing guardian-based defenses (dynamic mediator and static rewriter) that cut attack success rates by over half while preserving utility. It also stress-tests defenses with attack reframing variants.

entry.title: Cross-modal linkage risk in clinical vision-language models

author.name: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Mahshad Lotfinia, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn

entry.summary: Formalizes cross-modal linkage risk in clinical vision-language models, showing de-identified chest radiographs can be re-linked to their original reports via embedding cosine similarity. Audits this image-to-report retrieval risk across 406,241 pairs and increasingly specialized VLMs.

entry.title: Policy and World Modeling Co-Training for Language Agents

author.name: Ning Lu, Baijiong Lin, Shengcai Liu, Jiahao Wu, Haoze Lv, Yanbin Wei, Lingting Zhu, Shengju Qian, Xin Wang, Ying-Cong Chen, Qi Wang, Ke Tang

entry.summary: Proposes PaW, a co-training framework that adds auxiliary world-modeling supervision to on-policy RL for LLM agents using transitions already present in rollouts, without separate simulators or extra inference cost. Teaches agents what actions do to the environment, not just which yield reward.

entry.title: Dialectics of Alignment: Harnessing Unsafe Knowledge for Dynamic Safety Routing

author.name: Maryam Hashemzadeh, Jerry Huang, Minseon Kim, Marc-Alexandre C\^ot\'e, Sarath Chandar

entry.summary: Challenges the erasure paradigm in LLM alignment, proposing SafeMoE, a Mixture-of-Experts framework that isolates unsafe knowledge into dedicated experts and uses dynamic safety routing to give nuanced informative responses instead of blanket refusals. Argues unsafe data encodes useful domain knowledge.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Pure Machine Unlearning for Smooth Strongly Convex Losses

author.name: Matthew Regehr, Gautam Kamath, Andrew Lowy

entry.summary: This work nearly resolves the fundamental statistical cost of machine unlearning for smooth strongly convex losses, proving tight upper and lower bounds on excess population risk. The optimal rate interpolates between full retraining and no unlearning.

entry.title: CANARY: Zero-Label Detection of Fine-Tuning Contamination in Language Models

author.name: Swapnil Parekh

entry.summary: CANARY is a zero-label auditor that detects fine-tuning data poisoning from hidden-state geometry using two forward passes and a sparse autoencoder, achieving perfect AUROC at 1 percent contamination. It detects latent harmful behavior invisible to output-level defenses.

entry.title: On the Scaling of PEFT: Towards Million Personal Models of Trillion Parameters

author.name: Mind Lab, :, Song Cao, Vic Cao, Kaijie Chen, Bunny Fan, Hera Feng, Huan Feng, Arthur Fu, Jun Gao, Hongquan Gu, Aaron Guan, Mutian Hong, Hailee Hou, Peixuan Hua, Charles Huang, Miles Jiang, Nora Jiang, Yuyi Jiang, Autumn Jin, Fancy Kong, Kyrie Lei, Alexy Li, Dawn Li, Ray Li, Theo Li, Wenhao Li, Jiayi Lin, Domini Liu, Heshan Liu, Kairus Liu, Logan Liu, Maeve Luo, Runism Lv, Pony Ma, Verity Niu, Anson Qiu, Vincent Wang, Maxwell Yao, Regis Ye, Wenlin Ye, Yanying Ye, Josh Ying, Danney Zeng, Salmon Zhan, Anya Zhang, Ruijia Zhang, Shiyang Zhang, Sueky Zhang, Ya Zhang, Wei Zhao, Ada Zhou, Sizer Zhou, Xinyue Zhu, Murphy Zhuang

entry.summary: Reframes parameter-efficient fine-tuning as persistent per-instance local state atop strong shared foundation models, studying scaling up, down, and out toward millions of personal adapters. Proposes MinT infrastructure for managing adapter identity and revision at scale.

entry.title: UniPinRec: Unifying Generative Retrieval and Ranking at Pinterest Scale

author.name: Hanyu Li, Yi-Ping Hsu, Aditya Mantha, Prabhat Agarwal, Laksh Bhasin, Jialu Wang, Hongtao Lin, Bella Huang, Yaxin Li, Xinyi Li, Chuxi Wang, Kousik Rajesh, Hooshmand Shokri Razaghi, Shunyao Li, Zongyue Qin, Jaewon Yang, James Li, Dhruvil Deven Badani, Jiajing Xu, Charles Rosenberg

entry.summary: Presents UniPinRec, a full-stack unification of retrieval and ranking at Pinterest scale with one input format, one shared transformer model, one training stage, and existing serving infrastructure. Reduces duplicated parameters and serving cost in industrial recommendation.

entry.title: Taming the Loss Landscape of PINNs with Noisy Feynman-Kac Supervision: Operator Preconditioning and Non-Asymptotic Error Bounds

author.name: Nathanael Tepakbong, Hanyu Hu, Chengyu Liu, Xiang Zhou

entry.summary: Shows that adding a pointwise data-fidelity term to PINN losses acts as an operator-level preconditioner that provably reduces the condition number, with non-asymptotic error bounds using Feynman-Kac supervision. Helps explain and remedy ill-conditioned PINN training.

entry.title: How Optimality Structures Sparse Dictionaries: A Theory for Understanding SAE Representations

author.name: William Dorrell

entry.summary: Develops a theory of what sparse autoencoders extract by analyzing how optimality structures sparse dictionaries, addressing the gap in understanding which properties a concept must satisfy for an SAE to recover it. It moves beyond simplistic data-generating models toward realistic representations.

entry.title: Agreement Metrics for LLM-as-Judge Evaluation: What to Report and Why

author.name: Delip Rao, Chris Callison-Burch

entry.summary: This paper surveys how LLM-as-judge evaluations report agreement metrics with human annotations and shows that for binary criteria many correlation statistics collapse to a single number, making redundant reporting misleading. It offers practical guidance on which metrics to report and why, addressing widespread methodological confusion in evaluation studies.

entry.title: SALSA: Speech Aware LLM Adaptation via Learned Steering Activation Vectors

author.name: Yekaterina Yegorova, Argyrios Gerogiannis, Haolong Zheng, Julia Hockenmaier, Chang D. Yoo, Mark A. Hasegawa-Johnson

entry.summary: SALSA is a lightweight adaptation method for speech-aware LLMs that learns layer-wise steering vectors via a supervised objective rather than contrastive activation differences. It shows large gains on children's speech, multilingual, and code-switching benchmarks.

entry.title: Agentic Clustering: Controllable Text Taxonomies via Multi-Agent Refinement

author.name: Simon L\"owe, Emily Silcock

entry.summary: Agentic Clustering replaces fixed programmatic text-clustering pipelines with an orchestrator LLM that dispatches specialized agents (proposer, synthesizer, auditor, investigator, critic) adapting to the corpus. It enables controllable taxonomies that incorporate user constraints like target cluster count or intent.

entry.title: LongAttnComp: Cross-Family Context Compression for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Mengmeng Ji, Ravi Shanker Raju, Jonathan Lingjie Li, Chen Wu

entry.summary: LongAttnComp adapts attention-based context compression for long-context reasoning by fine-tuning a cross-attention scoring layer with token-level chunking, top-p budgeting, positional reordering, and a format-agnostic query parser. It reduces prefill costs while preserving accuracy on demanding tasks like code reasoning.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Emotion Control in Text-to-Speech

author.name: Hongfei Du, Jiacheng Shi, Sidi Lu, Gang Zhou, Ye Gao

entry.summary: This work uses sparse autoencoders to analyze emotion-related variation in LLM-based TTS hidden states, finding emotional variation is distributed across multiple sparse features. Intervening on a small subset enables interpretable emotion control in text-to-speech.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Diffusion Draft Trees for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shuai Zhang, Huachuan Qiu, Hongliang He, Yong Dai

entry.summary: CaDDTree improves speculative decoding for diffusion drafters by directly optimizing token throughput rather than acceptance length, jointly selecting tree structure under verification cost. It addresses that acceptance length always favors larger trees with no principled budget basis.

entry.title: "I Strongly Suspect This Website Is a Scam": Benchmarking PII Leakage and Detection without Defense in Autonomous Web Agents

author.name: Soham Roy, Sarthakbrata Halder, Arya Bharaty, Vaibhav Bhaskar, Yash Sinha, Dhruv Kumar, Srikant Panda, Murari Mandal

entry.summary: Scammer4U is a pre-registered benchmark of 91 attacker-controlled environments testing how social-engineering web content manipulates autonomous web agents into leaking users' PII to attacker endpoints. It shows frontier web agents are highly susceptible to extracting critical-tier PII.

entry.title: Auteur: Language-Driven Cinematographic Framing for Human-Centric Video Generation

author.name: Muhammed Burak Kizil, Enes Sanli, Niloy J. Mitra, Xuelin Chen, Erkut Erdem, Aykut Erdem, Duygu Ceylan

entry.summary: Presents Auteur, a method for language-driven, human-centric camera framing in generative video that parameterizes shots relative to the actor (shot size, angle, composition) rather than as world-space trajectories. Brings cinematographic intentionality to camera control.

entry.title: Explainable Forensics of Manipulated Segments in Untrimmed Long Videos

author.name: Yue Feng, Jingjing Li, Qijia Lu, Wei Ji, Jingrou Zhang, Fei Shen, Xiao Li, Yizhen Jia, Qiang Chen, Limin Wang, Wentong Li, Jie Qin

entry.summary: Formulates Temporal AI-Generated Segment Localization and Explanation for detecting and explaining manipulated segments sparsely embedded in untrimmed long videos, and introduces TASLE, a large-scale benchmark of 12,472 untrimmed videos. Addresses the realistic scenario beyond short-clip forensics.

entry.title: Policy-based Foveated Imaging and Perception

author.name: Howard Xiao, Jan Ackermann, Boyang Deng, Gordon Wetzstein

entry.summary: Introduces a real-time, task-aware foveated imaging system that dynamically allocates pixel bandwidth to relevant regions at acquisition time using dual-stream sensors. Matters for ultra-high-resolution perception under bandwidth, latency, and power constraints.

entry.title: Position: Good Embodied Reward Models Need Bad Behavior Data

author.name: Ran Tian, Yilin Wu, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that reliable embodied reward models require investment in failed, suboptimal, and hazardous robot data, showing that three state-of-the-art reward models systematically over-reward behaviors humans would penalize. Attributes failures to scarcity of negative embodied data.

entry.title: Beyond One-shot: AI Agents for Learning in Field Experiments

author.name: Junjie Luo, Ritu Agarwal, Gordon Gao

entry.summary: Tests whether tool-augmented agentic AI can autonomously learn from prior experimental data to design new interventions, via large two-stage healthcare messaging field experiments (693k visits) comparing human+chatbot vs autonomous AI methods. Addresses underutilization of A/B test data.

entry.title: From Rashomon Theory to PRAXIS: Efficient Decision Tree Rashomon Sets

author.name: Zakk Heile, Hayden McTavish, Varun Babbar, Margo Seltzer, Cynthia Rudin

entry.summary: Presents PRAXIS, an algorithm approximating decision-tree Rashomon sets (collections of near-optimal models) with orders-of-magnitude improvements in runtime and memory. It enables uncertainty-aware, robust decision-making with interpretable model classes.

entry.title: Demystifying the Optimal Fair Classifier in Multi-Class Classification

author.name: Li Zhang, Yuyuan Li, XiaoHua Feng, Jiaming Zhang, Fengyuan Yu, Chaochao Chen

entry.summary: This work characterizes the optimal accuracy-fairness frontier in multi-class classification and designs practical algorithms to attain it across training phases, extending fairness techniques beyond binary settings. It tackles the complexity of multi-dimensional outputs and fairness mechanisms.

entry.title: COPF: An Online Framework for Deployment-Stable Counterfactual Fairness in Evolving Graphs

author.name: Sheng'en Li, Dongmian Zou

entry.summary: COPF is an online framework for deployment-stable counterfactual fairness in evolving link-recommendation graphs, accounting for the performative nature where recommendations alter future link formation. It uses exposure counterfactuals, propensity logging, and exploration for valid fairness monitoring.

entry.title: Evolutionary Discovery of Bivariate Bicycle Codes with LLM-Guided Search

author.name: Juan Cruz-Benito, Andrew W. Cross, David Kremer, Ismael Faro

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-guided evolutionary workflow where language models mutate Python programs generating bivariate-bicycle quantum LDPC code candidates, screened via a staged validation pipeline. Reports large-scale search across ~200k candidates with modest compute and cost.

entry.title: Ghost Tool Calls: Issue-Time Privacy for Speculative Agent Tools

author.name: Bardia Mohammadi, Lars Klein, Akhil Arora, Laurent Bindschaedler

entry.summary: Identifies ghost tool calls—speculative tool invocations that leak inferred user intent to external services before an agent commits to a branch—as a timing-based privacy problem unaddressed by authorization controls. Proposes Speculative Tool Privacy Contracts as a runtime abstraction and evaluates twelve policies.

entry.title: Escaping the Mode Lottery: Multi-Response Training Improves Language Model Generalization

author.name: Hasan Amin, Kian Ahrabian, Ming Yin, Rajiv Khanna

entry.summary: Identifies the mode lottery problem where single-response fine-tuning underrepresents valid alternative completions, and develops a theory of multi-response training showing prompts and responses are distinct statistical resources. Demonstrates improved generalization.

entry.title: Enhancing LLM Metacognition via Cognitive Pairwise Training

author.name: Weitao Li, Hao Zhou, Xuanyu Lei, Fandong Meng, Yuanhang Liu, Jingyi Ren, Ante Wang, Xiaolong Wang, Yuanchi Zhang, Fuwen Luo, Guangwen Yang, Lin Gan, Weizhi Ma, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Cognitive Pairwise Training, a mid-training alignment stage that learns from pairwise comparisons over reasoning traces to build a reasoning-quality discrimination boundary, improving LLM metacognition and reliability. Addresses overconfidence induced by outcome-level RLVR rewards.

entry.title: PRISM: Gauge-Invariant Tangent-Space Differentially Private LoRA

author.name: Shihao Wang, Xueru Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes PRISM, a gauge-invariant differentially private LoRA mechanism that resolves the non-identifiability of the AB factorization, avoiding unbounded noise amplification in naive DP-LoRA. Operates in a low-dimensional tangent space.

entry.title: When Parallelism Pays Off: Cohesion-Aware Task Partitioning for Multi-Agent Coding

author.name: Xu Yang, Lunyiu Nie, Ethan Chandra, Stanislav Gannutin, Fangru Lin, Swarat Chaudhuri

entry.summary: Formalizes multi-agent LLM coding orchestration as a graph partitioning problem capturing communication-computation trade-offs, and presents Co-Coder, which builds dependency graphs from static analysis to partition tasks cohesively. Shows when parallelism actually pays off in agentic coding.

entry.title: Is Zero-Shot Super-Resolution Possible in Operator Learning?

author.name: Unique Subedi, Ambuj Tewari

entry.summary: Provides a systematic theoretical study of zero-shot super-resolution in operator learning, proving it can be information-theoretically impossible even in benign cases while identifying Holder smoothness as a sufficient condition. Clarifies when neural operators generalize across grid resolutions.

entry.title: DeepLatent: Think with Images via Parallel Latent Visual Reasoning

author.name: Dongchen Lu, Zhimo Li, Mao Shu, Huo Cao

entry.summary: Proposes DeepLatent, a parallel framework for latent visual reasoning in vision-language models using learnable 2D tokens and LatentFormer to generate context-conditioned latent visual states. Aims to close the gap between tool-assisted and latent thinking-with-images methods.

entry.title: An Algebraic View of the Expressivity of Recurrent Language Models

author.name: Franz Nowak, Ryan Cotterell, Reda Boumasmoud

entry.summary: Develops a unified algebraic account of recurrent neural language model expressivity, reconciling conflicting Turing-completeness versus regular-language results by formalizing the underlying arithmetic model. It reduces expressivity to algebraic questions like syntactic monoid wreath-product divisibility.

entry.title: The Lie We Tell: Correcting the Euclidean Fallacy in Vision Language Action Policies via Score Matching on Tangent Space

author.name: Bing-Cheng Chuang, I-Hsuan Chu, Bor-Jiun Lin, YuanFu Yang, Min Sun, Chun-Yi Lee

entry.summary: Identifies the Euclidean Fallacy in diffusion vision-language-action policies that represent SE(3) poses as flat vectors, causing manifold drift and broken equivariance. It introduces Lie Diffuser Actor that operates intrinsically on SE(3) via left-invariant SDEs and tangent-space score prediction.

entry.title: ProactiveLLM: Learning Active Interaction for Streaming Large Language Models

author.name: Junlong Tong, Yao Zhang, Anhao Zhao, Yingqi Fan, Yunpu Ma, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: ProactiveLLM enables streaming LLMs to decide when to interact with an input stream using endogenous model states rather than hard-coded timing or costly external signals. It uses mask-based streaming modeling and synchronized privileged training to perceive semantic sufficiency.

entry.title: Learning to Retrieve: Dual-Level Long-Term Memory for Text-to-SQL Agents

author.name: Yibo Wang, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Philip S. Yu, Zhewei Yao, Yuxiong He

entry.summary: MERIT is a dynamic multi-horizon memory retrieval framework for text-to-SQL agents that learns to retrieve memories useful at different interaction stages rather than from sparse final outcomes. It addresses the limitation that memory usefulness varies across planning and execution.

entry.title: A Finite-Calibration Regime Map for LLM Judge Panels

author.name: Bin Zhu, Yanghui Rao

entry.summary: This paper provides a finite-calibration regime map for LLM judge panels, characterizing when low-dimensional stackers versus joint output tables should calibrate panels under limited human-label budgets. It finds scalar/reliability aggregation wins most real dataset-budget cells across multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: Before and After Temperature: A Distributional View of Creative LLM Generation

author.name: V. S. Raghu Parupudi, Harsha Ponnada, Aditi Kaushal, S. Shria Parupudi, Saiteja Dasari, Sahiti Bulusu

entry.summary: This paper shows that how sampling temperature reshapes a model's token distribution before sampling provides a strong signal for predicting creative generation quality. A single per-token feature predicts within-prompt creativity rank with high correlation against LLM and human judges on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.

entry.title: Beyond Topical Similarity: Contrastive Evidence Retrieval with Interpretable Attention Alignment in RAG

author.name: Francielle Vargas, Jo\~ao Robiatti, Diego Alves, Lucas Pascotti Valem, Maximilian Seeth, Sebasti\'an Ferrada, Ameeta Agrawal, Daniel Pedronette, Andr\'e Freitas

entry.summary: CERA is a retrieval framework employing subjectivity-based hard negative selection and an evidential inductive bias via attention alignment loss supervising CLS-to-token attention with POS-weighted factual rationales. It improves factuality and interpretability in RAG on clinical trial reports.

entry.title: Honey, I Shrunk the Arc de Triomphe!

author.name: Yuanbo Xiangli, Hanyu Chen, Xueqing Tsang, Noah Snavely

entry.summary: Identifies a scale-collapse phenomenon where metric monocular geometry foundation models underestimate distant landmarks, attributing it to a training data bottleneck of vehicle-LiDAR or short-range indoor scans. Curates MetricScenes, an in-the-wild metrically-grounded dataset from internet photos and stereo images.

entry.title: MORPHOS: Autoregressive 4D Generation with Temporal Structured Latents

author.name: Minkyung Kwon, Jinhyeok Choi, Youngjin Shin, Jaeyeong Kim, JongMin Lee, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Presents MORPHOS, an autoregressive 4D generation framework producing dynamic 3D assets from videos across meshes, Gaussians, and radiance fields using Temporal Structured Latents (T-SLAT) that jointly encode geometry and appearance over time. Handles topological changes and long-video temporal consistency via causal attention.

entry.title: LEGS: Fine-Tuning Teleop-Free VLAs for Humanoid Loco-manipulation in an Embodied Gaussian Splatting World

author.name: Hojune Kim, Timothy Chen, Jiankai Sun, Lars W. Osterberg, Qianzhong Chen, Ke Wang, Mac Schwager

entry.summary: LEGS is a hybrid simulator compositing mesh foregrounds over photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting backgrounds, with a procedural motion-primitive generator that synthesizes labeled demonstrations at scale without human teleoperation for finetuning humanoid loco-manipulation VLAs. Achieves sim-to-real transfer where prior simulator-finetuned VLAs failed.

entry.title: The Deterministic Horizon: When Extended Reasoning Fails and Tool Delegation Becomes Necessary

author.name: Dongxin Guo, Jikun Wu, Siu Ming Yiu

entry.summary: This paper argues that extended chain-of-thought reasoning degrades performance on deterministic state-tracking tasks due to information-theoretic limits of decoder-only attention, deriving an Attention Bottleneck Theorem and a Deterministic Horizon beyond which tool delegation becomes necessary. It validates across 12 models and 8 task domains.

entry.title: Reasoning4Sciences: Bridging Reasoning Language Models to All Scientific Branches

author.name: Teddy Ferdinan, Bart{\l}omiej Koptyra, Miko{\l}aj Langner, Tomasz Adamczyk, {\L}ukasz Radli\'nski, Maciej Markiewicz, Aleksander Szcz\k{e}sny, Stanis{\l}aw Wo\'zniak, Tymoteusz Romanowicz, Dzmitry Pihulski, Mateusz Zbrocki, Mateusz \'Smigielski, Micha{\l} Rajkowski, Mateusz Biedka, Konrad Kie{\l}czy\'nski, Konrad Wojtasik, Jacek Duszenko, Jan Eliasz, Piotr Matys, Micha{\l} Bernacki-Janson, Maria Bellaniar Ismiati, Latius Hermawan, Wiktoria Mieleszczenko-Kowszewicz, Anna Kubicka-Sowinska, Grzegorz Chodak, Karol Postawa, Pawe{\l} Zyblewski, Tomasz Szanda{\l}a, {\L}ukasz Sterczewski, Adrian Chajec, Pawel Niewiadomski, Piotr Gruber, Marcin Wdowikowski, S{\l}awomir Czarnecki, Bart{\l}omiej Kryszak, Dominik Drabik, Tomasz Kajdanowicz, Kamil Mamak, Pawe{\l} Pre\'s, Katarzyna Paczkowska, Joachim Sobczuk, Tomasz Zi\k{e}ba, Jan Koco\'n, Maciej Piasecki, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko

entry.summary: This large-collaboration survey maps reasoning language model adoption across 28 scientific disciplines, exposing a widening productivity gap between hard sciences and other fields. It introduces a maturity-oriented assessment framework based on domain-specific resources.

entry.title: Science Earth: Towards A Planet-Scale Operating System for AI-Native Scientific Discovery

author.name: Zhe Zhao, Haibin Wen, Yingcheng Wu, Jiaming Ma, Yifan Wen, Jinglin Jian, Jiacheng Ge, Xiangru Tang, Bo An, Ming Yin, Sanfeng Wu, Mengdi Wang, Le Cong

entry.summary: Science Earth proposes a planet-scale scientific runtime where heterogeneous capabilities such as simulation clusters, wet-lab robots, and proof engines connect via an EACN protocol, with collaboration structure emerging from the scientific question. It targets breaking down siloed AI-for-science systems.

entry.title: TRON: Targeted Rule-Verifiable Online Environments for Visual Reasoning RL

author.name: Tianze Yang, Yucheng Shi, Ruitong Sun, Jingyuan Huang, Ninghao Liu, Jin Sun

entry.summary: TRON provides an online environment substrate for visual reasoning RL where a controllable generator-verifier program produces fresh image-question-answer instances on demand with exact verification, enabling unbounded curriculum-tuned training streams. The suite contains 520 organized environments.

entry.title: Token Predictors Are Not Planners: Building Physically Grounded Causal Reasoners

author.name: Zheng Lu, Mingqi Gao, Qinlei Xie, Wanqi Zhong, Hanwen Cui, Heng Cao, Zirui Song, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Bei Liu, Yiming Li

entry.summary: This work argues embodied planning benchmarks favor linguistic next-token prediction over physically grounded next-state reasoning, and introduces Causal-Plan-Bench plus a million-scale reasoning-trace corpus to evaluate and train physically grounded causal reasoners across four causal dimensions. It calls for a shift from token prediction to causal reasoning.

entry.title: SafeMCP: Proactive Power Regulation for LLM Agent Defense via Environment-Grounded Look-Ahead Reasoning

author.name: Lichao Wang, Zhaoxing Ren, Tianzhuo Yang, Jiaming Ji, Chi Harold Liu, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai

entry.summary: SafeMCP is a server-side defense plugin for LLM agents using the Model Context Protocol that constrains tool acquisition via internal-world-model look-ahead reasoning about future safety risks, implementing proactive tool filtering and a two-tier defense. It targets power-seeking risks from expanding agent action spaces.

entry.title: LLM-Evolved Pattern Generators for Optimal Classical Planning

author.name: Windy Phung, Dominik Drexler, Arnaud Lequen, Jendrik Seipp

entry.summary: Presents the first method for learning domain-dependent heuristics that are admissible by design for optimal classical planning, using an LLM-driven evolutionary program-synthesis framework to construct abstraction pattern collections. This preserves A* optimality guarantees unlike prior learned heuristics.

entry.title: Iteris: Agentic Research Loops for Computational Mathematics

author.name: Leheng Chen, Zihao Liu, Wanyi He, Bin Dong

entry.summary: Iteris is an agentic research system for open problems in computational mathematics, generating numerical evidence, adversarial constructions, and proof drafts for two open Simons Workshop problems. Targets the underexplored numerical/experimental side of math discovery.

entry.title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment

author.name: Hao Li, Jingkun An, Zijun Song, Pengyu Zhu, Rui Li, Hao Wang, Wendi Feng, Yesheng Liu, Lijun Li, Jin-Ge Yao, Lei Sha

entry.summary: SafeSteer performs localized on-policy distillation confined to sparse safety tokens, using an activation-steering teacher and a token selection algorithm, to align LLMs without massive general data or reward models while minimizing the alignment tax. Argues alignment needs localized rather than global modifications.

entry.title: ClinEnv: An Interactive Multi-Stage Long Horizon EHR Environment for Agents

author.name: Yuxing Lu, Yushuhong Lin, Wenqi Shi, J. Ben Tamo, Xukai Zhao, Jinzhuo Wang, May Dongmei Wang

entry.summary: ClinEnv is an interactive benchmark evaluating LLMs as attending physicians over real inpatient admissions via Longitudinal Inpatient Simulation, requiring sequential irreversible decisions and active querying of specialized agents. It moves beyond static multiple-choice medical benchmarks.

entry.title: A Multi-Domain Red Teaming Framework for Safety, Robustness, and Fairness Evaluation of Medical Large Language Models

author.name: Andrei Marian Feier, Veysel Kocaman, Yigit Gul, Ahmet Korkmaz, Alexander Thomas, Aleksei Zakharov, Jay Gil, Mehmet Butgul, David Talby

entry.summary: Develops a multi-domain red teaming framework evaluating eleven LLMs across 690 clinically grounded adversarial scenarios spanning nine domains, finding substantial variance and complete failures even in high-performing systems on safety-critical cases. Uses a seven-dimension rubric with human validation.

entry.title: DLLM-JEPA: Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Sangdae Nam

entry.summary: DLLM-JEPA pairs Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures with masked-diffusion language models, exploiting bidirectional attention to generate two views via different masking rates without explicit paired data and requiring only one gradient-carrying forward pass, cutting training FLOPs by 33% versus LLM-JEPA. Eliminates two key costs of the prior autoregressive port.

entry.title: On Effectiveness and Efficiency of Agentic Tool-calling and RL Training

author.name: Tong Liu, Cheng Qian, Matej Cief, Yuan He, Daniele Dan, Nikolaos Aletras, Gabriella Kazai

entry.summary: SPARROW is an open-source hardware-software platform combining solar power, edge AI inference, and satellite communication for autonomous biodiversity monitoring in remote regions. Developed by a Microsoft AI for Good team and collaborators, it enables continuous on-device ecological sensing with LEO satellite transmission.

entry.title: Geometric Erasure by Contrastive Velocity Matching in Rectified Flows

author.name: Jonas Henry Grebe, Tobias Braun, Anna Rohrbach, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: Introduces GEM, a concept erasure framework for Rectified Flow Transformers that bridges trajectory-based unlearning from Generative Flow Networks with teacher-guided erasure via contrastive velocity matching. It adapts concept erasure to the modern shift from U-Net diffusion to rectified flow models.

entry.title: PrivacyPeek: Auditing What LLM-Based Agents Acquire, Not Just What They Say

author.name: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiahui Han, Dadi Guo, Songze Li, Guanchu Wang, Na Zou, Dongrui Liu, Xia Hu

entry.summary: Introduces PrivacyPeek, a benchmark auditing what LLM agents acquire into their context (not just what they disclose) across 1,182 cases, 7 acquisition behaviors, and 16 domains. It highlights over-acquisition of sensitive data as a precursor to leakage.

entry.title: InfoAtlas: A Foundation Model for Zero-Shot Statistical Dependence Estimate

author.name: Zhengyang Hu, Yanzhi Chen, Hanxiang Ren, Qunsong Zeng, Youyi Zheng, Adrian Weller, Kaibin Huang, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces InfoAtlas, a foundation-model architecture for zero-shot mutual information estimation that infers statistical dependence in a single forward pass after pretraining on large-scale synthetic data. It eliminates the costly per-dataset iterative optimization of neural MI estimators.

entry.title: PR2: Predictive Routing Replay for MoE-Based LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daize Dong, Junlin Chen, Haolong Jia, Jiawei Wu, Huanwei Di, Jiang Liu, Jialian Wu, Zhengzhong Liu, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Hongyi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Predictive Routing Replay (PR2) to stabilize RL training of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs by addressing router drift and staleness that cause rollout-training mismatch. It predicts how the router evolves under off-policy updates rather than simply freezing the replay route.

entry.title: GeoSAM-3D: Geodesic Prompt Propagation for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Segmentation from Monocular Video

author.name: Arun Sharma

entry.summary: GeoSAM-3D enables open-vocabulary 3D scene segmentation from a single monocular video by propagating user prompts via heat-kernel geodesic distance over a Gaussian-splat scene graph. The geodesic propagation preserves continuity on curved surfaces and reduces leakage across disconnected regions.

entry.title: Skill or Skip? Learning Selective Skill Invocation in Agentic Tasks via Dual-Granularity Preference Learning

author.name: Chishui Chen, Jiaye Lin, Te Sun, Junxi Wang, Yi Yang, Cong Qin, Yangen Hu, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng

entry.summary: SelSkill is a dual-granularity preference-learning framework that teaches agents whether a relevant skill should actually be invoked at a given decision point, not just which skill is relevant. It uses predictive uncertainty to prioritize decision points and builds invoke-skip preference pairs.

entry.title: On the Difficulty of Learning a Meta-network for Training Data Selection

author.name: Zilin Du, Junqi Zhao, Boyang Albert Li

entry.summary: This work analyzes why meta-learning for training-data selection often underperforms, identifying poor gradient signal-to-noise ratio and lack of quality-correlated features as core obstacles. It provides mathematical analysis of normalized data-weight dynamics.

entry.title: Pause and Think: A Dataset and Benchmark for Video-Grounded Assistive Action Suggestion

author.name: Shivam Singh, Saptarshi Majumdar, Pratik Prabhanjan, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: This work introduces a reasoning-centric video dataset and benchmark for assistive action suggestion that encourages models to pause and reason over visual evidence before answering. A fine-tuned 4B model matches much larger models like Qwen3-VL-235B and GPT-5.2 on certain tasks.

entry.title: EPIC: Efficient and Parallel Inference under CFG Constraints for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Hyundong Jin, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: EPIC is an efficient framework for context-free grammar constrained decoding in diffusion language models that preserves parallel decoding, overcoming prior methods that were up to four times slower and sacrificed parallelism. It avoids sequential validity-check overhead.

entry.title: WaveFilter: Enhancing the Long-Context Capability of Diffusion LLMs via Wavelet-Guided KV Cache Filtering

author.name: Jinnan Yang, Yan Wang, Zhen Bi, Kehao Wu, Xiaojie Li, Jungang Lou, Zechao Li, Jing Liu

entry.summary: WaveFilter is a training-free KV-cache filtering framework for diffusion LLMs that uses wavelet transforms to precisely identify critical tokens in ultra-long contexts, addressing quality degradation in long-context generation. It mitigates the computational bottleneck of multi-step diffusion inference.

entry.title: Quantum Tunneling-Aware Machine Learning: Physics-Derived Noise Models for Robust Deployment

author.name: Uiwon Hwang, Jaeho Hwang

entry.summary: QTAML derives a physics-based weight-error distribution from the WKB quantum tunneling approximation for transistors, revealing structure that generic Gaussian noise models miss, such as affine mean drift and per-bit variance hierarchy. It packages these for robust ML deployment as scaling nears quantum limits.

entry.title: Behavior-Invariant Task Representation Learning with Transformer-based World Models for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fuyuan Qian, Menglong Zhang, Song Wang, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes behavior-invariant task representation learning combined with a Transformer-based stochastic world model for offline meta-reinforcement learning, extracting task latents invariant to behavior policy. It addresses context and policy distribution shifts under sparse rewards.

entry.title: Beyond Independent Manipulation: Individual Fairness-aware Strategic Classification with Peer Imitation

author.name: Xinpeng Lv, Chunyuan Zheng, Yunxin Mao, Renzhe Xu, Jinxuan Yang, Yuanlong Chen, Wangrong Huang, Shaowu Yang, Wenjing Yang, Xinwang Liu, Peng Cui, Haotian Wang

entry.summary: This work extends strategic classification to individual fairness settings where agents' feature manipulations are interdependent through peer imitation, unlike prior assumptions of independent responses. It reformulates fairness-aware strategic classification under these coupled dynamics.

entry.title: FVSpec: Real-World Property-Based Tests as Lean Challenges

author.name: Quinn Dougherty, Max von Hippel, Hazel Shackleton, Mike Dodds

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark for formal software verification by scraping 11K Python property-based tests and translating thousands into Lean 4 specifications with placeholders. Uses a three-agent LLM pipeline to transpile imperative tests into dependently-typed Lean specs.

entry.title: PolySpeech-100: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Speech Understanding Across 100+ Languages and Dialects

author.name: Sicheng Yang, Shulan Ruan, Shiwei Wu, Yu Liu, Lu Fan, Zhi Li, You He

entry.summary: Introduces a large-scale speech understanding benchmark covering 110+ languages and dialects, including 19 Chinese dialects and 80+ low-resource languages, with focus on semantic reasoning beyond ASR. Uses a hybrid pipeline of human recordings and synthetic speech.

entry.title: MENTIS: What Belief Changes Under Alignment? Measuring Multi-Scale Latent Torsion in Language Models

author.name: Partha Pratim Saha, Samarth Raina, Mayur Parvatikar, Amit Dhanda, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Amitava Das

entry.summary: Introduces MENTIS, a geometry-first framework measuring internal representational reorganization when an instruction-tuned model becomes preference-aligned. Aims to characterize where and how selectively alignment changes internal computation across concepts and model families.

entry.title: DiscourseFlip: An Oblique Discourse-Level Opinion Manipulation Attack against Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yuyang Gong, Miaokun Chen, Jiawei Liu, Zhuo Chen, Guoxiu He, Wei Lu, XiaoFeng Wang, Xiaozhong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DiscourseFlip, a black-box opinion-manipulation attack against RAG systems that coordinates poisoning across a semantic query network to induce opinion shifts over a multi-topic query space. Formalizes discourse-level manipulation as a new threat model.

entry.title: TukaBench: A Culturally Grounded Jailbreak Benchmark for African Languages

author.name: Victor Akinode, Senyu Li, Wassim Hamidouche, Waqas Zamir, Inbal Becker-Reshef, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

entry.summary: Introduces TukaBench, a culturally-grounded jailbreak benchmark for seven African languages extending JailbreakBench beyond direct translation with code-switched and culturally-adapted prompts. Finds prompting in African languages reduces model refusal rates.

entry.title: Dr. DocBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Expert-Level and Difficult Document Parsing

author.name: Minglai Yang, Xinyan Velocity Yu, Pengyuan Li, Xinyu Guo, Zhenting Qi, Konwoo Kim, Longtian Ye, Xiaolong Luo, Jinhe Bi, Henry Zhang, Haris Riaz, Xuan Zhang, Yunze Xiao, Bangya Liu, Tom Tang, Yunfei Zhao, Qunshu Lin, Zihan Wang, Minghao Liu, Michael Lingzhi Li, Yilun Du, Jesse Thomason, Rogerio Feris, Alex Pentland, Zexue He

entry.summary: Introduces Dr. DocBench, a difficulty-aware multilingual benchmark for expert-level document parsing covering 52 subject domains and challenging structures like chemical formulas, music notation, complex tables, and cross-page layouts. Targets gaps in OCR and document-parsing evaluation.

entry.title: ClawHub Security Signals: When VirusTotal, Static Analysis, and SkillSpector Disagree

author.name: Vincent Koc, Patrick Erichsen, Jacob Tomlinson, Agustin Rivera, Michael Appel, Nir Paz

entry.summary: ClawHub Security Signals releases a sanitized dataset of 67,453 public agent-skill versions and studies disagreement among three security scanners (VirusTotal, static analysis, SkillSpector). It reveals scanners rarely flag the same skills, highlighting gaps in agent-skill security detection.

entry.title: TimeSage-MT: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Evaluating Agentic Time Series Reasoning

author.name: Yaxuan Kong, Qingren Yao, Yuqi Nie, Yichen Li, Yilei Shao, Stefan Zohren, Anna Vettoruzzo, Joaquin Vanschoren, Ming Jin, Qingsong Wen

entry.summary: TimeSage-MT is a multi-turn benchmark for agentic time series reasoning with 240 tasks and 2,680 dialogue turns across 8 domains, moving beyond single-step forecasting tasks. It evaluates whether LLM agents can sustain reliable analysis as user goals evolve.

entry.title: Demystifying Multimodal Biomolecular Co-design With Intrinsic Geodesic Coupling

author.name: Keyue Qiu, Xintong Wang, Zhilong Zhang, Hao Zhou, Wei-Ying Ma

entry.summary: This work introduces intrinsic geodesic coupling for multimodal biomolecular co-design, arguing that temporal coupling between sequence and structure generative processes is an overlooked degree of freedom. It addresses high-variance supervision from fixed synchronous coupling.

entry.title: MINTS: Minimalist Thompson Sampling

author.name: Kaizheng Wang

entry.summary: MINTS introduces a minimalist Bayesian framework placing a prior only on the optimum's location and eliminating nuisance parameters via profile likelihood, instantiated as Minimalist Thompson Sampling. It establishes near-optimal regret guarantees for constrained multi-armed bandits.

entry.title: DOT-MoE: Differentiable Optimal Transport for MoEfication

author.name: Udbhav Bamba, Arnav Chavan, Aryamaan Thakur, Steve Teig, Deepak Gupta

entry.summary: DOT-MoE formulates the conversion of dense models into sparse MoEs as a differentiable optimal transport problem, replacing heuristic neuron clustering or random splitting. It aims for stable, efficient MoEfication of pretrained dense LLMs.

entry.title: Off-the-Shelf LLMs as Process Scorers: Training-Free Alternative to PRMs for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Atoosa Chegini, Soheil Feizi

entry.summary: This work proposes Chunk-Level Guided Generation, a training-free alternative to process reward models that uses an off-the-shelf large LLM to score candidate chunks via likelihoods without generating text. It steers small-model math reasoning before errors propagate.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Pretrained Models for Instance Segmentation Tasks

author.name: Nermeen Abou Baker, David Rohrschneider, Uwe Handmann

entry.summary: Adaptive Auto-Harness extends auto-harness systems (which optimize agent prompts, skills, tools, and memory) from fixed offline benchmarks to open-ended task streams with shifting distributions. It enables sustained self-improvement with task-wise adaptation to prevent performance degradation.

entry.title: MMG2Skill: Can Agents Distill In-the-Wild Guides into Self-Evolving Skills?

author.name: Xinyu Che, Junqi Xiong, Yunfei Ge, Xinping Lei, Shihao Li, Hang Yan, Han Li, Yuanxing Zhang, Zhiqi Bai, Jinhua Hao, Ming Sun, Han Li, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: MMG2Skill formalizes guide-to-skill learning, converting noisy multimodal in-the-wild web guides into agent-executable, self-evolving skills, and introduces MMG2Skill-Bench. It proposes a closed-loop framework that compiles and continuously improves skills from agent trajectories.

entry.title: PlanarBench: Evaluating LLM Spatial Reasoning via Planar Graph Drawing

author.name: Oleksandr Nikitin

entry.summary: This work proposes a render-free framework for 3D-aware human motion control in video diffusion models, conditioning on compressed 3D human mesh tokens rather than rendered 2D guidance videos. It investigates whether diffusion models truly understand 3D structure versus reproducing 2D projections.

entry.title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models using Multi-Clip Video

author.name: Choongwon Kang, Seungjong Sun, Hyunmin Jun, Jang Hyun Kim

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Clip Video SafetyBench, a 2,920-video dataset showing that multimodal LLMs become more vulnerable to jailbreaks as video inputs contain more diverse clips related to a harmful query. Identifies clip diversity as a key driver of safety alignment failures in video MLLMs.

entry.title: Faster Synchronous On-Policy RL via Straggler-Aware Group Sizing

author.name: Azal Ahmad Khan, Ammar Ahmed, Zeshan Fayyaz, Sheng Di, Mingyi Hong, Ali Anwar

entry.summary: Proposes SAGC, a straggler-aware dynamic group-size controller for synchronous on-policy RL methods like GRPO, framing group sizing as online constrained optimization to reduce wall-clock stalls from slow rollouts. Targets the tension between larger groups and synchronization cost.

entry.title: SeClaw: Spec-Driven Security Task Synthesis for Evaluating Autonomous Agents

author.name: Hao Cheng, Changtao Miao, Tianle Song, Yin Wu, He Liu, Erjia Xiao, Junchi Chen, Xiaoyu Shi, Yichi Wang, Jing Yang, Taowen Wang, Jinhao Duan, Mengshu Sun, Peiyan Dong, Xuan Shen, Yang Cao, Renjing Xu, Kaidi Xu, Jindong Gu, Bo Zhang, Jize Zhang, Chenhao Lin, Philip Torr, Chao Shen

entry.summary: Introduces SeClaw, a framework combining specification-driven security task synthesis with execution-based evaluation for autonomous LLM agents in stateful environments. Enables scalable construction of security scenarios and assesses unsafe execution processes, not just final outcomes.

entry.title: A Pre-Training Analogue of Grokking in Language Models: Tracing Delayed Grammatical Generalization

author.name: Sherin Muckatira, Namrata Shivagunde, Vijeta Deshpande, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Proposes an exposure-based framework to study grokking-like delayed generalization during LLM pre-training, grounding evaluation in BLiMP minimal pairs and tracking when grammatical generalization emerges relative to exposure. Adapts grokking analysis from supervised epochs to next-token pre-training.

entry.title: Adaptive Order Policies for Masked Diffusion

author.name: Jama Hussein Mohamud, Mohsin Hasan, Mirco Ravanelli, Yoshua Bengio

entry.summary: Proposes learning the token-unmasking order in masked diffusion models via a lightweight policy network that reweights diffusion loss terms toward positions where the denoiser is likely correct. Studies training the policy alone and jointly with the diffusion model.

entry.title: Auditing Near-Optimal Policies Can Be Exponentially Hard: Conditional Query Lower Bounds via Occupancy Rashomon Capacity

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Sanjeda Akter, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical framework formalizing how hard it is to audit near-optimal RL policies, introducing an occupancy-measure version of Rashomon capacity and proving conditional exponential query lower bounds. It matters for AI safety and policy verification under the reality that many distinct behaviors achieve similar returns.

entry.title: EST-PRM: Stress-Testing Process Reward Models Before They Become Load-Bearing

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Fariya Afrin, Sanjeda Akter, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces EST-PRM, a stress-testing framework that probes whether process reward models give stable scores under label-preserving transformations like step inflation and reordering. Reveals that PRM scores may not be robust proxies for step correctness.

entry.title: GNMR: Runtime Stability Control for Low-Precision Large Language Model Training

author.name: Boao Kong, Weichen Jia, Engao Zhang, Guohong Li, Yonghan Dong, Yao Wang, Yaoyuan Wang, Yunke Peng, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes GNMR, a lightweight runtime controller for low-precision LLM training that monitors gradient-norm-to-mean ratios to detect and recover from numerical instabilities without changing formats or kernels. Tested on DeepSeek-style recipes and LLaMA-2 fine-tuning.

entry.title: On the Recoverability of Causal Relations from Bulk Gene Expression Data

author.name: Gongxu Luo, Boyang Sun, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Studies whether causal relations among genes are recoverable from bulk (aggregated) gene expression data, formalizing recoverability via functional-form and conditional-independence consistency. From Kun Zhang's causal-inference group.

entry.title: How Neural Losses Shape VAE Latents

author.name: Giorgio Strano, Luca Cerovaz, Michele Mancusi, Tommaso Mencattini, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: Shows that perceptual and adversarial reconstruction losses in VAEs reshape the rate-distortion problem, reducing latent information content and altering latent geometry in ways invisible from reconstructions. Provides theory and empirical verification.

entry.title: Task Structure Reverses Layerwise State Encoding in Sequence Models

author.name: Yuhang Jiang

entry.summary: Shows that the same sequence model architecture reverses its layerwise state-encoding profile depending on task structure, comparing Transformers, Mamba, Mamba-2, LSTMs, and GRUs on Parity and Dyck-k. Disentangles algebraic versus computational structure as drivers.

entry.title: Non-Vacuous Certification of Transport MCMC via Oscillation-Controlled Normalizing Flows

author.name: Jun Hu

entry.summary: Establishes the first numerically non-vacuous, rigorous spectral-gap bounds for transport MCMC samplers that use normalizing flows to precondition Metropolis-Hastings, via oscillation-controlled flows with spectral normalization. Provides certified mixing guarantees on benchmark posteriors.

entry.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xingrun Xing, Haoqing Wang, Boyan Gao, Ziheng Li, Yehui Tang

entry.summary: Proposes Trust Region On-Policy Distillation (TrOPD), which applies on-policy distillation only in regions where the teacher gives reliable supervision, stabilizing training when teacher and student distributions diverge. Improves credit assignment for LLM post-training, compression, and agent learning.

entry.title: Truthful AI Advisors: A Pre-Specified Benchmark for Large Language Model Honesty Under Preference Misalignment

author.name: Hamidreza Hasani Balyani, Seyed Pouyan Mousavi Davoudi, Alireza Amiri-Margavi, Amin Gholami Davodi, Arshia Gharagozlou

entry.summary: This paper turns the Crawford-Sobel cheap-talk economic model into a pre-specified benchmark for LLM honesty when advisor incentives misalign with users. It tests whether LLMs reveal information or strategically partition, an important alignment-evaluation question.

entry.title: OmniOPD: Logit-Free On-Policy Distillation via Speculative Verification

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Lizhu Zhang, Yifan Wu, Mingyi Wang, Peng Bo, Jiayi Liu, Xiangjun Fan, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: OmniOPD enables on-policy distillation without access to teacher logits by using speculative verification, allowing proprietary models to serve as teachers. It addresses the brittleness of token-level logit signals and degenerate repetition patterns.

entry.title: ContinuousBench: Can Differentially Private Synthetic Text Improve Capabilities?

author.name: Peihan Liu, Lucas Rosenblatt, Weiwei Kong, Natalia Ponomareva, Gautam Kamath, Rachel Cummings, Roxana Geambasu, Yu Gan, Lillian Tsai, Alex Bie

entry.summary: ContinuousBench is a continuously regenerated benchmark measuring whether differentially private synthetic text transmits genuinely new knowledge, with quarterly never-before-seen corpora paired with derived QA sets. It is designed to be unsolvable without the corpus yet learnable under DP.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimal Policy Regret in Partially Observable Markov Games

author.name: Raman Arora

entry.summary: Provides theoretical regret bounds for sequential decision-making in partially observable Markov games against adaptive adversaries, proving near-optimal policy regret with an epoch-based optimistic maximum-likelihood algorithm. Important for theoretical foundations of multi-agent learning under partial observability.

entry.title: Drifting Preference Optimization for One-Step Generative Models

author.name: Zhou Jiang, Yandong Wen, Zhen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Drifting Preference Optimization for aligning deterministic one-step text-to-image generators using a non-parametric preference field and reference drift, avoiding reliance on policy likelihoods or trajectories. Addresses a real gap in finetuning fast single-pass generators.

entry.title: Parameter-Free and Group Conditional Online Conformal Prediction

author.name: Beepul Bharti, Ambar Pal, Jacopo Teneggi, Jeremias Sulam

entry.summary: Proposes a parameter-free algorithm for group-conditional online conformal prediction, achieving group-wise coverage guarantees robust to distribution shift without learning-rate tuning. Improves fairness and uncertainty quantification under non-exchangeable data.

entry.title: ViBE: Co-Optimizing Workload Skew and Hardware Variability for MoE Serving

author.name: Seokjin Go, Marko Scrbak, Ephrem Wu, Srilatha Manne, Divya Mahajan

entry.summary: Presents ViBE, a system co-optimizing workload skew and hardware variability for distributed Mixture-of-Experts inference, addressing stragglers caused by interaction of uneven expert loads and GPU performance variation. Targets serving latency in MoE deployments.

entry.title: Quality-Diversity Evolution for Discovering Diverse Vulnerabilities in LLM Safety

author.name: Subhadip Mitra

entry.summary: Introduces a quality-diversity evolutionary red-teaming framework using MAP-Elites to discover diverse interpretable LLM attack strategies at the semantic level, avoiding mode collapse and gibberish outputs. Reveals distinct vulnerability profiles across GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5, Gemini 2.0, and an open coding model.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Compositional Diffusion for Long-Horizon Planning

author.name: Byoungwoo Park, Utkarsh A. Mishra, Jaemoo Choi, Juho Lee, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes coarse-to-fine compositional diffusion for long-horizon planning, composing short-horizon priors into globally coherent long-horizon outputs beyond enforcing only local neighbor consistency. Addresses implausible global structure in standard compositional generation.

entry.title: Don't Read Everything: A Curvature-Conditioned Query for Linear Attention

author.name: Dong Le, Thong Nguyen, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: Introduces a curvature-conditioned query mechanism for linear attention, borrowing a second-order Taylor expansion of softmax's log-partition to contract queries at read time. It aims to fix linear attention's weakness on in-context retrieval and long-context tasks.

entry.title: Don't Let a Few Network Failures Slow the Entire AllReduce

author.name: Peiqing Chen, Jiedong Jiang, Nengneng Yu, Yuefeng Wang, Sixian Xiong, Wei Wang, Zaoxing Liu

entry.summary: Provides the first information-theoretic lower bound on AllReduce completion time under asymmetric network bandwidth from NIC failures, showing overhead is only O(1/p) when stragglers retain half bandwidth. It addresses how network failures slow distributed GPU training.

entry.title: Investigating and Alleviating Harm Amplification in LLM Interactions

author.name: Ruohao Guo, Wei Xu, Alan Ritter

entry.summary: Introduces HarmAmp, a benchmark for multi-turn harm amplification across twelve risk categories, studying how LLMs compound harm over extended interactions by democratizing expertise and scaling operations. It investigates and proposes mitigations for harm amplification missed by single-turn evaluations.

entry.title: How Far Do Auto-Interpretation Labels Generalize: A Controlled Study Across Languages, Scripts, and Rewordings

author.name: Sripad Karne
