entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating VLM agents on procedural 3D modeling via code generation, testing 12 VLMs on translating text and image references into procedural code for 3D software. Includes human evaluation since automated metrics fall short.

entry.title: Topological Ignorability for Structural Causal Effects Beyond Means

author.name: Usef Faghihi

entry.summary: Introduces topological-geometrical causal metrics (Betti summaries, Euler signatures, persistent homology) to capture structural causal effects beyond means, where interventions reshape outcome distributions without changing averages. Studies ignorability assumptions for these structural estimands.

entry.title: Implicit Geographic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Language-Driven Disparities in Emergency Recommendations

author.name: Qi Han Wong

entry.summary: Investigates whether an LLM gives different medical triage recommendations for identical symptoms based solely on prompt language, finding ER recommendation rates ranging from 0% to 30% across six languages despite identical severity scores. Adding US location specification dramatically shifts recommendations.

entry.title: Needles at Scale: LLM-Assisted Target Selection for Windows Vulnerability Research

author.name: Michael J. Bommarito II

entry.summary: Presents Symbolicate-Enrich-Sample, a low-cost pipeline that turns whole-OS Windows binary corpora into a priority-ranked vulnerability research queue by recovering function symbols and attaching structural features. Argues target selection, not analysis, is the binding constraint at OS scale.

entry.title: Computation-Aware Kalman Filtering with Model Selection for Neural Dynamics

author.name: JR Huml, Jonathan Wenger, John P. Cunningham

entry.summary: This paper extends computation-aware Kalman filtering to include model selection with a novel training loss for inferring neural dynamics from single-cell recordings. It bridges Bayesian uncertainty quantification with scalable inference in large state spaces, addressing approximation errors in posterior estimation.

entry.title: MURMUR: An Efficient Inference System for Long-Form ASR

author.name: Wei-Tzu Lee, Keisuke Kamahori, Baris Kasikci

entry.summary: MURMUR is an inference system for long-form ASR that resolves the accuracy-latency trade-off by operating at both inter-chunk and intra-chunk levels, treating chunk size as a tunable parameter. It targets modern long-context ASR models for efficient deployment.

entry.title: Fair Finetuning Mitigates Distribution Inference Attacks

author.name: Rakshit Naidu

entry.summary: This work proposes Fair Fine-tuning under an Equalized Odds constraint to mitigate distribution inference attacks that leak population-level training information. It provides theoretical characterization linking fairness constraints to reduced distributional leakage.

entry.title: Multilingual Idioms in Sentences and Conversations Across High-, Medium-, and Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Saeed Almheiri, Bilal Elbouardi, Salsabila Zahirah Pranida, Irina Nikishina, Ashwath Rao B, Parameswari Krishnamurthy, Muhammad Cendekia Airlangga, Rifo Ahmad Genadi, Nguyen Phan Gia Bao, Amir Hossein Yari, Hawau Olamide Toyin, Nurdaulet Mukhituly, Mena Attia, Besher Hassan, Ahmad Fathan Hidayatullah, Tatsuki Kuribayashi, Haonan Li, Suma Bhat, Fajri Koto

entry.summary: Introduces MIDI, a multilingual idiom dataset spanning high-, medium-, and low-resource languages with idioms embedded in both sentence and conversational contexts. Benchmarks show idiom comprehension degrades substantially in low-resource languages.

entry.title: Not All Errors Are Equal: A Systematic Study of Error Propagation in Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Yafan Huang, Sheng Di, Guanpeng Li

entry.summary: Presents a systematic study of soft-error propagation in LLM inference using LLMFI, a configurable deterministic fault-injection framework, across three open models and thirteen tasks. Reveals that not all errors are equal in their impact on reasoning, math, coding, and multilingual outputs.

entry.title: Inner Product Aware Quantization: Provably Fast, Accurate, and Adaptive Algorithms

author.name: Nathan White, Krish Singal

entry.summary: Develops inner-product-aware quantization schemes that approximately preserve inner products with unseen vectors rather than just minimizing mean-squared error, with provably fast, accurate, and adaptive algorithms. Connects to adaptive stochastic quantization theory.

entry.title: Large-scale Uncertainty Quantification for Latent Variable Models Using Subsampling Markov Chain Monte Carlo

author.name: Xiaoyu Wang, Jonathan H. Huggins

entry.summary: Develops statistical scaling-limit theory for SGLD-Gibbs to provide principled hyperparameter tuning for scalable Bayesian inference in latent variable models. Derives joint asymptotics showing global parameters converge to a diffusion limit and latent variables to jump processes.

entry.title: Balancing Learning Rates Across Layers: Exact Two-Step Dynamics and Optimal Scaling in Linear Neural Networks

author.name: Tianyu Pang, Vignesh Kothapalli, Shenyang Deng, Haohui Wang, Dawei Zhou, Yaoqing Yang

entry.summary: Derives exact closed-form gradients and test loss after one and two gradient-descent steps in two- and three-layer linear networks learning linear targets, characterizing optimal layer-wise learning-rate scaling. Reveals an early-training regime where unequal learning rates minimize test loss.

entry.title: Dynamic Proxy-Mixing: Transferring Replay Controllers from Small to Large Models for Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Fariya Afrin, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Proposes PROX-YMIX, a framework that learns a dynamic replay controller on a small proxy model and transfers it frozen to a larger target model for continual instruction tuning, mitigating catastrophic forgetting. The controller adapts replay mixtures based on validation-loss dynamics rather than fixed ratios.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Learning with Noisy Proxy Covariates: Generalization Bounds and Distribution Regression

author.name: Kwangho Kim, Jisu Kim

entry.summary: Studies semi-supervised regression where pretrained representations act as noisy proxy covariates, proposing a two-stage kernel-eigenfeature plus ridge estimator with finite-sample generalization bounds. Connects to distribution regression as a special case.

entry.title: Graph Transfer Learning via Shared Latent Geometry: Theory and Applications

author.name: Tong Wu, Andrew Campbell, Anna Scaglione

entry.summary: Proposes an asymmetric two-pathway teacher-student architecture for graph transfer learning that uses a privileged-information teacher encoder with operator-polynomial features to provide quantitative transfer guarantees for physics-informed learning. Targets inference and control in physical systems.

entry.title: Confidence-Adaptive SwiGLU for Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Shaohua Li, Xiuchao Sui, Xiaobing Sun, Yuhang Wu, Liangli Zhen, Yong Liu, Rick Siow Mong Goh

entry.summary: Proposes kappa-SwiGLU for Mixture-of-Experts, which makes the SwiGLU gate sharpness a learnable function of router confidence, letting expert gates interpolate between smooth and selective gating. Evaluated on FineWeb-Edu across MoE depths.

entry.title: Latent Diffusion Pretraining for Crystal Property Prediction

author.name: Shrimon Mukherjee, Kishalay Das, Partha Basuchowdhuri, Pawan Goyal, Niloy Ganguly

entry.summary: Introduces CrysLDNet, a latent diffusion pretraining framework combining a VAE with a diffusion model to mitigate label scarcity in crystal property prediction. Provides a pretraining-finetuning strategy for materials design.

entry.title: Partial Fairness Awareness: Belief-Guided Strategic Mechanism for Strategic Agents

author.name: Xinpeng Lv, Chunyuan Zheng, Yunxin Mao, Renzhe Xu, Hao Zou, Shanzhi Gu, Liyang Xu, Huan Chen, Yuanlong Chen, Wenjing Yang, Haotian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Partial Fairness Awareness for strategic classification, releasing a candidate set of fairness constraints to balance the dilemma between public constraints enabling manipulation and hidden constraints reducing welfare. Provides theoretical analysis of fairness exposure.

entry.title: Online Packet Scheduling with Deadlines and Learning

author.name: Gianmarco Genalti, Achraf Azize, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: Frames QoS packet scheduling as an Online Packet Scheduling with Deadlines problem under bandit feedback, connecting it to sleeping bandits and providing algorithms with alpha-regret guarantees. Bridges scheduling and online learning.

entry.title: CryoProt: A Protein Pretraining Framework with Cross-Box Interactions on Cryo-EM Density Maps

author.name: Dan Luo, Xuan Lin, Peng Zhou, Junwen Zhu, Tengfei Ma, Xiangxiang Zeng, Yiping Liu

entry.summary: Proposes CryoProt, a protein pretraining framework that models cross-box interactions in cryo-EM density maps using multi-head latent attention, addressing the lack of cryo-EM-tailored pretraining and the neglect of inter-box context. Targets protein property prediction.

entry.title: Data Enrichment for Symbolic Regression Using Diffusion Models

author.name: Simon De Reuver, Tamas Kristof Toth, Teddy Lazebnik

entry.summary: Introduces a physics-guided latent diffusion framework for data enrichment in symbolic regression, generating additional samples that preserve physical structure to improve equation discovery under sparse or noisy data. Aims to remove the need for narrow domain expertise.

entry.title: Fairness in two-player zero-sum games with bandit feedback

author.name: S Akash, Pratik Gajane

entry.summary: Studies two-player zero-sum games with bandit feedback under fairness constraints requiring minimum play probability per action, using a reparametrization that maps fair strategies to an equivalent fair payoff matrix. Targets the harder mixed-equilibrium learning problem fairness induces.

entry.title: DAGGER: Gradient-Free Construction of Transiently Amplifying Networks under Hard Connectivity Constraints

author.name: James C. Ferguson

entry.summary: Introduces DAGGER, a gradient-free single-pass algorithm for constructing transiently amplifying (non-normal) networks under hard sign, sparsity, and diagonal constraints, avoiding expensive iterative eigendecomposition or basis-breaking Schur construction. Relevant to biological connectomes and structured RNN initialization.

entry.title: GLIDE: Graph-guided Leap Inference for Diffusion Estimation of Spatio-Temporal Point Processes

author.name: Guanyu Zhou, Yao Liu, Yanglei Gan, Yuxiang Cai, Peng He, Run Lin, Yuxiang Liu, Qiao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes GLIDE, a conditional diffusion framework for next-event prediction in spatio-temporal point processes that organizes history into a multi-scale graph and uses graph-guided leap inference to reduce costly reverse sampling and improve spatial localization. Addresses weak structural constraints in sparse spatial domains.

entry.title: Structure and Scale in Simplicial Sequence Modelling

author.name: Matthew Farrugia-Roberts

entry.summary: This paper hypothesizes that behavioral scaling laws and emergent internal mechanisms are connected, presenting preliminary evidence using small transformers trained on hidden Markov model outputs. It links predictable performance scaling to predictable changes in internal representation structure.

entry.title: Everywhere Learning: Artificial Intelligence with Pointwise Constraints

author.name: Ignacio Boero, Ignacio Hounie, Luiz Chamon, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: Everywhere learning proposes training AI to satisfy loss constraints with probability one over the data distribution rather than minimizing average loss. The authors develop approximate duality theory and generalization analysis for this paradigm.

entry.title: MomentKV: Closing the Directional Gap in KV Cache Eviction for Long-Context Inference

author.name: Yu Li, Binxu Li, Tian Lan

entry.summary: MomentKV improves KV cache eviction for long-context inference by addressing directional mismatch between retained and evicted tokens, which are often near-orthogonal. This directional gap, rather than residual attention mass, is identified as the main source of degradation.

entry.title: Coherent Off-Policy Improvement of Large Behavior Models with Learned Rewards

author.name: Christian Scherer, Joe Watson, Theo Gruner, Daniel Palenicek, Ingmar Posner, Jan Peters

entry.summary: This work explores inverse reinforcement learning to fine-tune large pretrained behavior models for dexterous robotic manipulation, learning rewards for coherent off-policy improvement rather than relying on sparse rewards. It addresses sample efficiency versus collecting more human demonstrations.

entry.title: Local Preferential Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Johanna Menn, Miriam Kober, Paul Brunzema, David Stenger, Sebastian Trimpe

entry.summary: Introduces local preferential Bayesian optimization methods that adapt trust-region and derivative-informed search to pairwise human feedback, enabling scaling to higher-dimensional problems. Matters for human-in-the-loop tuning where explicit objectives are unavailable.

entry.title: Out-of-Distribution generalization of quantile regression with heavy tailed inputs: an SVM approach

author.name: Baptiste Leroux, Cl\'ement Dombry, Anne Sabourin

entry.summary: Proposes an SVM framework using reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces for extreme quantile regression in the tail extrapolation regime, leveraging regular variation and angular components of extreme observations. Provides out-of-distribution generalization for heavy-tailed covariates.

entry.title: Flow Matching for Convective-Scale Precipitation Downscaling

author.name: Tom Wetherell

entry.summary: Applies flow matching to downscale daily precipitation from 8km to 2km over a convective-scale domain, benchmarking against a score-based diffusion baseline and achieving better spatial skill. Advances generative ML for climate downscaling.

entry.title: Cortex and subcortex play distinct roles over learning when cortical memory is limited

author.name: Matthew Farrell, Taro Toyoizumi

entry.summary: Extends model-based plus model-free learning frameworks by explicitly constraining the memory of the cortical model-based module, exploring how memory constraints induce resource-allocation strategies in decision-making. Provides theoretical grounding for cortex-subcortex division of labor.

entry.title: Benchmark Dataset for Catalysis on 2D MXenes

author.name: Pavlo Melnyk, Anmar Karmush, M{\aa}rten Wadenb\"ack, Ania Beatriz Rodr\'iguez-Barrera, Johanna Rosen, Michael Felsberg, Jonas Bj\"ork

entry.summary: Provides a benchmark dataset of 60,000 DFT calculations for catalysis on 2D Ti2CTy MXenes plus an out-of-distribution test set of larger systems, merging first-principles methods with ML to accelerate catalyst discovery. Supports ML force-field and property prediction research.

entry.title: KG-FairDiff: Knowledge Graph-Guided Prompt Refinement for Demographically Fair Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Farbod Davoodi, Seyed Reza Tavakoli Shiyadeh, Pooria Safaei, Sana Harighi, Parsa Gholami, Amirali Amini, Kimia Vanaei, Emad Firoozi, Parham Abed Azad, Babak Khalaj, Siavash Ahmadi, Amir Hossein Payberah, Mohammad Hossein Rohban, Soheil Kolouri, Ali Diba

entry.summary: Presents KG-FairDiff, a model-agnostic inference-time framework using knowledge-graph-guided prompt refinement to reduce demographic and cultural stereotypes in text-to-image generation. It formalizes fairness-aware prompt editing as constrained optimization without retraining closed-source models.

entry.title: PaCX-MAE: Physiology-Augmented Chest X-Ray Masked Autoencoder

author.name: Yancheng Liu, Kenichi Maeda, Manan Pancholy

entry.summary: Introduces PaCX-MAE, a cross-modal distillation framework injecting ECG and lab physiological priors into chest X-ray encoders during pretraining while remaining unimodal at inference. It shows consistent gains on physiology-dependent tasks and strong label efficiency.

entry.title: Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization with a Polyak-type Step size: A Theory-Grounded Scheduler

author.name: Dimitris Oikonomou, Nicolas Loizou

entry.summary: Derives Polyak-type adaptive step-size schedulers tailored to Sharpness-Aware Minimization, yielding theory-grounded adaptive SAM variants in deterministic and stochastic settings. It reduces SAM's sensitivity to learning-rate tuning.

entry.title: Identifiable Markov Switching Models with Instantaneous Effects and Exponential Families

author.name: Roel Hulsman, Carles Balsells-Rodas, Sara Magliacane

entry.summary: Establishes identifiability of latent regimes and regime-dependent parameters in Markov Switching Models with instantaneous effects and exponential-family dynamics, even under frequent switches and nonlinear non-Gaussian dynamics. It advances identifiable modeling of non-stationary temporal systems.

entry.title: Auditing Asset-Specific Preferences in Financial Large Language Models: Evidence from Bitcoin Representations and Portfolio Allocation

author.name: Wenbin Wu

entry.summary: Develops a three-level audit protocol to test whether financial LLMs carry asset-specific biases, applied to Bitcoin, finding frame-dependent rankings and an internal representation with causal leverage over preferences that affects portfolio allocation. It surfaces hidden biases in LLM-powered robo-advisors.

entry.title: BOUTEF: A Multilingual Corpus for FakeNews in North Africa -- Language as a Weapon

author.name: Kamel Smaili, Yassine Toughrai, Amina Laggoun, David Langlois

entry.summary: BOUTEF is a large-scale multilingual corpus for studying fake news in North Africa, covering MSA, Algerian and Tunisian dialects, Arabizi, French, English, and code-switching. It fills an under-resourced gap with fake/genuine narratives, user comments, and debunking information.

entry.title: Chunking Methods on Retrieval-Augmented Generation - Effectiveness Evaluation Against Computational Cost and Limitations

author.name: Mateusz \'Smigielski (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland), Micha{\l} Rajkowski (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland), Mateusz Zbrocki (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland), Micha{\l} Bernacki-Janson (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland), Karol Kunicki (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland), Julianna Godziszewska (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland), Maciej Piasecki (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland), Konrad Wojtasik (Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Information and Communication Technology, Wroc{\l}aw University of Science and Technology, Wroc{\l}aw 50-370, Poland)

entry.summary: This study empirically compares chunking methods for retrieval-augmented generation, evaluating effectiveness against computational cost and limitations across diverse scenarios. It seeks to enable direct comparison of fixed-size, semantic, and newer chunking strategies that often claim superiority.

entry.title: DFlare: Scaling Up Draft Capacity for Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jiebin Zhang, Zhenghan Yu, Song Liu, Eugene J. Yu, Zheng Li, Dawei Zhu, Jiangshan Duo, Weimin Xiong, Yifan Song, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Sujian Li

entry.summary: DFlare improves block diffusion speculative decoding by replacing a shared fused representation bottleneck with layer-wise fusion, allowing each draft layer to attend to its own learnable combination of target layers. This scales draft model capacity for faster LLM inference.

entry.title: Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes

author.name: Zihang Fu, Fanxiao Li, Jianyang Gu, Haonan Wang, Preslav Nakov, Bryan Hooi, Min-Yen Kan, Jiaying Wu

entry.summary: EvoNote is a self-evolving agentic framework for generating evidence-grounded health community notes that accumulates and reuses correction experience via fine-grained credit assignment into action-level memory. It is evaluated on a 1.2K multimodal health misinformation benchmark.

entry.title: TVIR: Building Deep Research Agents Towards Text--Visual Interleaved Report Generation

author.name: Xinkai Ma, Zhiqi Bai, Dingling Zhang, Pei Liu, Yishuo Yuan, He Zhu, Jiakai Wang, Qianqian Xie, Yifan Zhao, Xinlong Yang, Hao Cong, Zhiheng Yao, Fengxia Xie, Zihao Xu, Haoran Xu, Zhaohui Wang, Minghao Liu, Shirong Lin, Yingshui Tan, Yuchi Xu, Wenbo Su, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Bo Zheng, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: TVIR introduces a benchmark and hierarchical multi-agent framework for text-visual interleaved deep research report generation, where charts and images must serve analytical sub-goals with traceable sources. It addresses the text-centric gap in current deep research agents.

entry.title: Not What, But How: A Communicative Audit of LLM Response Framing

author.name: Siddhesh Milind Pawar, Sarah Masud, Haneul Yoo, Alice Oh, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: FRANZ audits LLM response framing (not just correctness) along cultural positioning, generalizing language, anthropomorphic cues, and conversational maxims for subjective queries. It contributes SQUARE, a 376k-question corpus from subreddits mapped to countries.

entry.title: HiGS: A Hierarchical Rendering Architecture for Real-Time 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Dawid Paj\k{a}k, Martin Bisson, Rodolfo Lima

entry.summary: HiGS proposes a hierarchical rendering architecture for 3D Gaussian Splatting that decouples tile sizes, running partitioning over coarse macro-tiles while rasterization runs over fine render tiles within them. This resolves the opposing scale preferences of partitioning and rasterization for real-time rendering.

entry.title: ETC: Extreme Token Compression via Task-aware Visual Information Distillation in VLMs

author.name: Yiling Gao, Hongchen Wei, Zhenzhong Chen

entry.summary: ETC proposes an extreme token compression framework for VLMs grounded in variational information distillation, preserving the instruction-aware sufficient statistic of task-relevant visual information. It uses text-to-image cross-attention to weight visual features and minimize task loss when drastically reducing tokens.

entry.title: T-CLIP: Enabling Thermal Perception for Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining

author.name: Tayeba Qazi, Ayush Maheshwari, Prerana Mukherjee, Brejesh Lall

entry.summary: T-CLIP extends CLIP-style vision-language pretraining to thermal imagery, introducing a physics-aware thermal captioning pipeline and dataset (IR-Cap) to bridge the gap where standard models fail to align thermal images with text. It addresses the conflict between global scene context and object-level heat signatures in a shared embedding space.

entry.title: RoboStressBench: Benchmarking VLM Robustness to Physical Visual Stress in Embodied Scenes

author.name: Leyi Wu, Yifan Zhao, Jinjie Zhang, Suzeyu Chen, Wosong Chen, Zhifei Chen, Tianshuo Xu, Qingchun He, Hongxin Hu, Haojian Huang, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen

entry.summary: RoboStressBench benchmarks VLM robustness to physical visual stress in embodied scenes, formulating visual perception from an inverse-graphics perspective to capture realistic scene-formation stresses rather than isolated perturbations. It targets reliable perception for embodied AI.

entry.title: MotionDreamer: Universal Skeletal Motion Generation for 3D Rigged Shapes

author.name: Ye Tao, Yuxin Yao, Kendong Liu, Dapeng Wu, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: MotionDreamer is a diffusion-based, category-agnostic framework for generating skeletal animation for rigged 3D shapes from 2D video guidance, supported by a curated dataset of ~20,000 textured, rigged, animated 3D models. It overcomes template-based methods' topology limits and per-case optimization costs.

entry.title: Pave-GRPO: Beyond Instantaneous Guidance through Principled Average Velocity Decomposition

author.name: Pengyang Ling, Jiazi Bu, Yujie Zhou, Yibin Wang, Zhenyu Hu, Zihan Zhang, Yi Jin, Huaian Chen, Yuhang Zang

entry.summary: Pave-GRPO reformulates Group Relative Policy Optimization for flow-based generative models through principled average velocity decomposition, addressing temporal sparsity where reward feedback reaches only a few denoising stages. It improves preference-optimization alignment granularity for flow models.

entry.title: Conditional Collapse in Sign Language Production: A Diagnostic and a Scaling Argument

author.name: Rui Hong, Jana Ko\v{s}eck\'a

entry.summary: Proposes a three-level diagnostic framework (initial-pose conditioning, output diversity, target faithfulness) to better evaluate Sign Language Production models, revealing that standard FID and BLEU metrics can improve while generation quality degrades. Uses latent representations from a frozen motion autoencoder to measure pairwise-distance ratios across 14 SLP checkpoints.

entry.title: Normality-Preserving Continual Industrial Anomaly Detection via Orthogonal LoRA Banks

author.name: Weibai Fang, Haijun Che, Feiyang Ren, Qiancheng Lao

entry.summary: Proposes a normality-preserving continual industrial anomaly detection framework using History Frozen Orthogonal LoRA Banks to isolate category-specific normality priors and prevent catastrophic forgetting in diffusion models. Addresses normality prior drift during sequential adaptation.

entry.title: Equilibrated Diffusion: Frequency-aware Textual Embedding for Equilibrated Image Customization

author.name: Liyuan Ma, Xueji Fang, Guo-Jun Qi

entry.summary: Proposes Equilibrated Diffusion, a frequency-aware approach to image customization that disentangles concept features by exploiting the link between image frequency components and semantics (low frequency for structure, high for detail). Aims for balanced customization and consistent text-visual matching.

entry.title: Neural Acquisition & Representation of Subsurface Scattering

author.name: Arjun Majumdar, Raphael Braun, Hendrik Lensch

entry.summary: Presents a method to acquire and represent subsurface scattering properties by learning per-pixel footprint responses using a U-Net with phase-shifted profilometry capture from a stereo projector-camera setup. Enables relighting with arbitrary high-resolution projector patterns.

entry.title: LL-Bench: Rethinking Low-Level Vision Evaluation in the Era of Large-Scale Generative Models

author.name: Lu Liu, Huiyu Duan, Chenxin Zhu, Jintong Lu, Haoyun Jiang, Liu Yang, Qiang Hu, Guangtao Zhai, Xiaoyun Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a mask-conditioned latent diffusion model for generative data augmentation of TEM images, synthesizing realistic transmission electron microscopy images with automatically labeled multi-class defect masks to address scarce labeled data in irradiated metal alloys. Augments small datasets to improve combined defect detection and classification.

entry.title: Directed Distance Fields for Constant-Time Ray Queries on Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Subhankar MIshra

entry.summary: Distills a Directed Distance Function from trained 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes to answer secondary ray queries (shadows, occlusion, global illumination) in constant time with a compact 52MB neural field. Enables ray tracing effects on rasterizer-only 3DGS.

entry.title: Invascal: Inverse-Vacuity Self-Calibration for Uncertainty-Aware LiDAR Range-View Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Kerim Turacan, Hannes Reichert, Andrei Bolandut, Konrad Doll

entry.summary: Invascal introduces an architecture-agnostic uncertainty-aware adapter head that decomposes LiDAR segmentation into class ranking and uncertainty strength using evidential Dirichlet representations. Improves calibration over softmax confidence for safe autonomy.

entry.title: Balancing Accuracy and Efficiency: Adaptive Dynamics Orchestration for Model Predictive Control

author.name: Francesco Cancelliere, Aniket Datar, Giovanni Muscato, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: Adaptive Dynamics Orchestration dynamically selects between high-fidelity and lightweight dynamics models in MPC for autonomous navigation, balancing accuracy against real-time efficiency based on navigation context. Avoids catastrophic failures from oversimplified models.

entry.title: RocketSmith: An Agentic System for High-Powered Rocket Design and Manufacturing

author.name: Peter Pak, Jesse Barkley, Rumi Loghmani, Derek Baich, Ananya Pamal, Amir Barati Farimani

entry.summary: RocketSmith is an agentic system that automates the design, manufacturing, and optimization of high-powered rockets, coordinating subagents to validate flight stability and generate parametric components for additive manufacturing. Built four physical rockets.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Modal Trajectory Policies for Data-Efficient Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zijia Chen, Yuenan Hou, Xinhua Jiang, Yu Li, Weijie Li, Li Liu

entry.summary: MATE uses Mixture-of-Experts with improved routing to handle heterogeneous modalities (vision, language, trajectory) in data-efficient robotic manipulation, avoiding modality interference and expert collapse common in conventional routing. Improves data-scarce performance.

entry.title: Set-Supervised Diffusion Policy: Learning Action-Chunking Diffusion through Corrections

author.name: Zhaoting Li, Gang Chen, Javier Alonso-Mora, Cosimo Della Santina, Jens Kober

entry.summary: Set-Supervised Diffusion Policy learns action-chunking diffusion policies that exploit corrective human interventions, using the negative signal of undesired actions that standard behavior cloning ignores. This reduces overfitting to teacher demonstrations and reliance on costly expert data.

entry.title: FATE-VLA:Failue-aware test generation for vision-language-action models

author.name: Arusa Kanwal, Pablo Valle, Shaukat Ali, Aitor Arrieta

entry.summary: FATE-VLA reframes VLA model evaluation as active failure discovery, combining diversity-driven exploration with surrogate models to steer testing toward high-risk scene regions. It uncovers substantially more failures than static benchmarks, improving robustness assessment.

entry.title: Weighted Conformal Clustering

author.name: Anirban Nath, YoonHaeng Hur, Genevera I. Allen

entry.summary: Weighted Conformal Clustering constructs valid confidence sets for cluster labels by correcting the mismatch between algorithm-produced synthetic labels and latent ground-truth labels, framing it as a conditional label-distribution shift. It provides rigorous uncertainty quantification for cluster assignments.

entry.title: Can LLMs even teach? Exploring the Teacher Axis

author.name: Vidya Ganga

entry.summary: This post extracts a Teacher Axis from Gemma-2-2B using MathDial conversations and finds that RLHF does not suppress pedagogical (Socratic) ability but optimizes orthogonally to it. It explores steering across layers and how student pressure affects the model's pedagogical projection.

entry.title: ForeSci: Evaluating LLM Agents for Forward-Looking AI Research Judgment

author.name: Qiuyu Tian, Zequn Liu, Yingce Xia, Haojie Yin, Youyong Kong

entry.summary: ForeSci is a temporally controlled benchmark of 500 tasks evaluating whether LLM agents can make forward-looking AI research judgments from historical evidence, with post-cutoff papers hidden during generation and used only for validation. It tests decisions like which bottleneck to attack before future evidence exists.

entry.title: Towards Understanding Modality Interaction in Multimodal Language Models via Partial Information Decomposition

author.name: Wanlong Fang, Tianle Zhang, Wen Tao, Alvin Chan

entry.summary: This paper applies Partial Information Decomposition as a decision-level framework to separate unique, redundant, and synergistic contributions of sensory and linguistic inputs in multimodal LLMs. It reveals recurring modality-use profiles—high synergy for reasoning tasks, language-unique reliance for knowledge tasks—that generalize across model families.

entry.title: Self-Revising Discovery Systems for Science: A Categorical Framework for Agentic Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Fiona Y. Wang, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: This paper develops a category-theoretic account of agentic scientific discovery for materials science, modeling system states as copresheaves and discovery as verified regime transitions using left Kan extensions to transport artifacts. It formalizes the revision of representational schemas rather than mere answer generation.

entry.title: Revisiting Ripple Effects in Knowledge Editing through Pressure-Aware Joint Neighborhood Optimization

author.name: Haoben Huang, Shuxin Liu, Ou Wu, Di Gao

entry.summary: This work revisits ripple effects in knowledge editing by jointly modeling the coupling between desirable propagation to related facts and unintended perturbation of preserved ones, identifying editable-side coordination and preserved-side leakage as coupled design pressures. It proposes Joint Neighborhood Optimization with pressure-aware coordination.

entry.title: Evidence-Gated LLM Priors for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Jiangyu Chen, Banyi

entry.summary: This work proposes an objective-wise reputation-market mechanism for using LLM-generated expert priors in discrete multi-objective Bayesian optimization without blindly trusting them, treating each expert-objective pair as a falsifiable source whose weight updates online from observed outcomes. It addresses miscalibration of LLM advice across objectives.

entry.title: Understanding Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation: A Paired Comparison of Ambient AI Drafts and Clinician Finalized Notes

author.name: Yiliang Zhou, Yawen Guo, Sairam Sutari, Jasmine Dhillon, Alexandra L. Beck, Emilie Chow, Steven Tam, Danielle Perret, Deepti Pandita, Gelareh Sadigh, Archana J. McEligot, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: Analyzes stigmatizing language in ambient AI clinical note drafts versus clinician-finalized notes across 66,297 paired sections using lexicon-based NLP, finding 21.4% of AI drafts contained stigmatizing language and quantifying removal/introduction rates. Probes bias implications of documentation tools.

entry.title: SENSE: Semantic Embedding Navigation with Soft-gated Evaluation for Retrieval-based Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shaowen Chen, Zhicheng Liao, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: SENSE improves retrieval-based speculative decoding by anchoring retrieval on target-model hidden states for semantic alignment and using soft-gated evaluation to validate semantic equivalence, overcoming brittle lexical dependencies. Accelerates LLM inference without quality loss.

entry.title: Beyond Categories of Caste: Examining Caste Bias and Morality in Text-to-Image AI Models

author.name: Divyanshu Kumar Singh, Dipto Das, Deepika Rama Subramanian, Koustuv Saha, Stephen Voida, Bryan Semaan

entry.summary: Audits caste bias in text-to-image models by shifting focus from caste as an identity category to its relational aspects, combining algorithmic audit with critical discourse analysis to understand mechanics of caste discrimination in GenAI. Reveals nuanced perpetuation of caste stereotypes.

entry.title: Planktonzilla: Multimodal dataset and models for understanding plankton ecosystems

author.name: Alan Gerson Contreras Montanares, Luis Valenzuela, Luis Mart\'i, Nayat Sanchez-Pi

entry.summary: Introduces Planktonzilla-17M, a unified plankton dataset consolidating thirteen imaging systems into 17.4 million images with standardized taxonomy and geo-environmental metadata, plus models, to overcome poor cross-instrument generalization. Supports ocean-health and climate research.

entry.title: Bridging the 2D-3D Gap: A Hierarchical Semantic-Geometric Map for Vision Language Navigation

author.name: Kailing Li, Tianwen Qian, Lijin Yang, Yuqian Fu, Jingyu Gong, Xiaoling Wang, Liang He

entry.summary: Proposes a Hierarchical Semantic-Geometric Map that transforms 3D geometric information into a structured representation compatible with VLMs to bridge the semantic-geometric gap in Vision-Language Navigation, improving zero-shot 3D spatial reasoning and action-transition modeling. Links VLMs to the physical world.

entry.title: CoilDrop-MRI: Self-supervised physics-guided MRI reconstruction with coil dropout

author.name: Tongxi Song, Ziyu Li, Zihan Li, Wen Zhong, Congyu Liao, Yang Yang, Hua Guo, Wenchuan Wu, Qiyuan Tian

entry.summary: CoilDrop-MRI is a self-supervised physics-guided MRI reconstruction method that applies coil-wise dropout, using dropped coil data as training targets to exploit signal correlation across receiver coils, extending self-supervised partitioning beyond the k-space domain. Achieves high-quality reconstruction without fully sampled data.

entry.title: Visual-Noise Guided In-Context Distillation for Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning

author.name: Junkai Chen, Yuhao He, Junxiang You, Ruiqi Liu, Chenyu Wang, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Presents a visual-noise guided in-context distillation method for unlearning targeted knowledge from multimodal LLMs while preserving utility. It aims to combine the utility-preservation of training-free methods with the actual knowledge removal of training-based approaches.

entry.title: RAFT: Data Refinement and Adaptive Distillation for Domain Fine-Tuning with Alleviated Forgetting

author.name: Yuduo Li, Xiaofeng Shi, Qian Kou, Longbin Yu, Hua Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes RAFT, a two-stage data refinement and adaptive distillation framework for domain fine-tuning that mitigates degradation of general capabilities. It addresses supervision-compatibility and trajectory-preservation gaps in standard supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: (HB-ARFM) History-Bootstrapped Flow Matching for Inverse Boiling Reconstruction

author.name: Xianwei Zou, Sheikh Md Shakeel Hassan, Arthur Feeney, Aparna Chandramowlishwaran

entry.summary: Proposes history-bootstrapped autoregressive flow matching (HB-ARFM) for spatiotemporal inverse reconstruction under partial observability, where partial observation operators induce non-Markovian posteriors unresolvable from a single timestep. Observation history bootstraps initial reconstruction via conditional flow matching to reduce ambiguity.

entry.title: Authenticity Debt and the Synthetic Content Threat Landscape: A Layered Framework for Trust, Provenance, and IP Governance in the Generative AI Era

author.name: Shubhashis Sengupta, Benjamin McCarty, Milind Savagaonkar, Rhine Andotra

entry.summary: This paper introduces authenticity debt, the cumulative institutional liability from deploying AI-generated content without verifiable provenance, and proposes a layered framework spanning authenticity, provenance, integrity, and accountability. It addresses IP governance and trust in the generative AI era.

entry.title: Dive into Waves: Morlet Spectral Transformer for Cross-Subject Emotion Decoding from EEG

author.name: Jiaxin Qing, Lexin Li

entry.summary: The Morlet Spectral Transformer addresses cross-subject EEG emotion decoding, where signals are weak, noisy, and encoded in spectral power, by integrating Morlet wavelet spectral representations with band-specific spatial modeling. It targets limitations of foundation-model and frequency-domain encoder approaches.

entry.title: MViewRouter: Internalizing Geometric Equivariance via Multi-view Alternating Attention for Combinatorial Routing

author.name: Shiyan Liu, Bohan Tan, Yaoxin Wu, Yan Jin

entry.summary: Proposes MViewRouter, a multi-view attention framework that internalizes geometric equivariance as a structural inductive bias for combinatorial routing problems like TSP and CVRP. Replaces data-augmentation symmetry handling with built-in equivariance.

entry.title: BRo-JEPA: Learning Modular Arithmetic in Latent Space

author.name: Divyansh Jha, Yuanfang Xie, Varan Mehra, Brennen Yu

entry.summary: Investigates whether neural networks learn abstract algebraic rules or memorize, using MNIST digits and modular arithmetic in a JEPA-style latent world model. Shows a block-rotation predictor imposing modulo-10 circular structure enables strong zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Consistent and Distinctive: LLM Benchmark Efficiency via Maximum Independent Set Prompt Selection on Similarity Graphs

author.name: Denica Kjorvezir, Marko Djukanovi\'c, Ana Gjorgjevikj, Gjorgjina Cenikj, Tome Eftimov

entry.summary: Proposes a graph-based prompt selection framework modeling benchmarks as similarity graphs and applying Maximum Independent Set algorithms to select diverse non-redundant prompt subsets for efficient LLM evaluation. Tests consistency of resulting rankings across many solvers and benchmarks.

entry.title: CEAR: Certified Ensemble Adversarial Robustness in DNNs

author.name: Daniel Sadig, Mohammadreza Maleki, Hamed Karimi, Reza Samavi

entry.summary: Proposes CEAR, an ensemble adversarial robustness method combining empirical and certified defenses, training ensemble members with varying perturbation levels to provide provable robustness guarantees. Aims to resist adaptive white-box attacks.

entry.title: E4GEN: Event-level Explainable Extreme-Enhanced Time-series Generation

author.name: Lin Jiang, Dahai Yu, Ximiao Li, Guang Wang

entry.summary: E4GEN is an explainable diffusion framework for extreme-event-aware time series generation, with components determining when, what, and how to control extreme events during denoising. It addresses methods that emphasize distributional fidelity but miss extreme events.

entry.title: Multilinguality of Large Language Models From a Structural Perspective

author.name: Haruki Sakajo, Yusuke Sakai, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Taro Watanabe

entry.summary: This study analyzes LLM multilinguality from a structural perspective, finding that low-resource languages are structurally more divergent from English than high/mid-resource ones, and that language-specific post-training alters structures while preserving inter-language relationships. It goes beyond token-representation analyses.

entry.title: Suppressing Forgery-Specific Shortcuts for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

author.name: Yihui Wang, Yonghui Yang, Jilong Liu, Fengbin Zhu, Le Wu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This work proposes Shortcut Subspace Suppression for generalizable deepfake detection, explicitly characterizing and suppressing method-specific shortcuts via subspace modeling. It treats variations distinguishing forgery methods as a proxy for spurious shortcuts.

entry.title: FOAM: Frequency and Operator Error-Based Adaptive Damping Method for Reducing Staleness-Oriented Error for Shampoo

author.name: Kyunghun Nam, Sumyeong Ahn

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of staleness in preconditioner updates for the Shampoo optimizer through convergence and stability lenses, then proposes FOAM, a frequency and operator-error-based adaptive damping method to suppress staleness-induced instability. Aims to reduce matrix-inversion overhead without losing fidelity.

entry.title: CRMA: A Spectrally-Bounded Backbone for Modular Continual Fine-Tuning of LLMs

author.name: Kiran Nayudu, Aswini Nutakki, Sai Vinay Naidu, Ashwin Shanmugasundaram

entry.summary: Introduces CRMA, a residual adapter whose internal mixing matrix is doubly-stochastic via Sinkhorn normalization, structurally bounding its spectral norm by construction (Birkhoff's theorem). Provides a continuously trainable shared substrate for modular continual fine-tuning while preserving forgetting guarantees.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Reference-Aligned Machine Unlearning

author.name: Rasa Khosrowshahli, Stephen Asobiela, Beatrice Ombuki-Berman, Shahryar Rahnamayan

entry.summary: Proposes RAUL, a multi-objective unlearning framework that replaces unbounded loss maximization with bounded KL alignment of forgotten-sample predictions toward a reference distribution representing unseen data. Jointly optimizes forgetting and retention to avoid catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Topology-Aware State Abstraction with Tangle Cores for Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Sanjeda Akter, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces tangle-core abstraction, an overlapping state-abstraction framework for MDPs based on graph tangles that allows interface states like doors and hubs to belong to multiple regions. Provides value-preservation guarantees for the induced overlapping abstract MDP.

entry.title: Safe-Subspace Pseudo-Label Refinement for Source-Free Graph Domain Adaptation

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Xinwang Liu, Siyang Gao, Nan Yin

entry.summary: Proposes a selective pseudo-labeling approach for source-free graph domain adaptation that identifies a confidence-consistent safe subspace where pseudo-label noise is controllable, with a target-risk decomposition. Avoids amplifying errors through message passing.

entry.title: RDA: Reward Design Agent for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hojoon Lee, Ajay Subramanian, Ben Abbatematteo, Vijay Veerabadran, Pedro Matias, Karl Ridgeway, Nitin Kamra

entry.summary: RDA is a VLM-based agentic framework that injects semantic understanding into RL reward design by decomposing tasks and analyzing visual behavior, improving on Eureka's reliance on coarse success-rate feedback. It produces policies better aligned with task instructions.

entry.title: Measurement Geometry and Design for Trustworthy Generative Inverse Problems

author.name: Pengfei Jin, Na Li, Quanzheng Li

entry.summary: This work studies generative inverse problems from a measurement-geometry perspective, asking whether a fixed measurement operator can distinguish nearby images plausible under a generative prior. It introduces a local measurement-manifold analysis to guide better measurement design, especially for medical imaging.

entry.title: 21cmEMUv3: a hybrid diffusion-LSTM emulator of 21cmFAST summary observables

author.name: Daniela Breitman, Andrei Mesinger, Steven G. Murray, Ivan Nikolic, Roberto Trotta

entry.summary: Presents 21cmEMUv3, a hybrid diffusion-LSTM emulator of 21cm cosmological summary observables trained on simulations, producing fast accurate predictions across redshift for cosmic dawn and reionization inference. Accelerates astrophysical inference pipelines.

entry.title: Data-Driven Spectral Prediction for Accelerating Large-Scale Electronic Structure Calculations

author.name: Abhiram Badrinarayanan, Davor Davidovic, Edoardo Di Napoli, Jurica Novak, Luigi Genovese, Gustavo Ramirez-Hidalgo, Xinzhe Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a data-driven framework to accelerate large-scale electronic structure calculations by predicting Chebyshev polynomial coefficients rather than discrete eigenvalues, comparing all-atom and fragment-based representations. Targets the eigenproblem bottleneck in DFT on exascale systems.

entry.title: Sympatheia: Emotionally Adaptive Voice Assistant with Continuous Affect Conditioning

author.name: Sukru Samet Dindar, Riki Shimizu, Xilin Jiang, Nima Mesgarani

entry.summary: Introduces Sympatheia, a speech-to-speech dialogue framework conditioned on continuous valence-arousal affect signals, plus Sympatheia-18k, an emotion-conditioned synthetic spoken dialogue corpus with 12 emotion anchors. Aims to build empathetic voice assistants robust to weak affective cues.

entry.title: Differentially Private Datastore Generation for Retrieval-Augmented Inference

author.name: Abdelrahman Abouelenein, Marwan Torki

entry.summary: Introduces a hashing-based framework using locality-sensitive hashing plus calibrated DP noise to generate differentially private datastores for retrieval-augmented inference. It enables on-device RAG datastore sharing with formal privacy guarantees.

entry.title: MPMWorlds: Material-Point-Method Simulations for Inferring and Extrapolating Physical Dynamics

author.name: \v{Z}iga Kova\v{c}i\v{c}, Kevin Ellis

entry.summary: Assembles MPMWorlds, a dataset of 2D Material Point Method simulations covering deformables, fluids, and emitters, to study inferring and extrapolating physical dynamics from video. It compares code generation versus video diffusion approaches, finding tradeoffs in physical stability and parameter inference.

entry.title: Self-Improving Small Object Grounding in LVLMs

author.name: Tianze Yang, Yucheng Shi, Ruitong Sun, Ninghao Liu, Jin Sun

entry.summary: Demonstrates that attention patterns in large vision-language models encode object-grounding quality, training a lightweight IoU regressor on attention maps to select reliable small-object boxes without fine-tuning. It also derives a fully training-free attention-based candidate selector.

entry.title: ShaplEIG: Bayesian Experimental Design for Shapley Value Estimation

author.name: David Rundel, Fabian Fumagalli, Maximilian Muschalik, Bernd Bischl, Matthias Feurer

entry.summary: Proposes ShaplEIG, a Bayesian experimental design approach that adaptively selects coalitions for Shapley value estimation by maximizing expected information gain, targeting settings where value-function evaluations are costly. It improves attribution accuracy under severe evaluation budgets.

entry.title: DeSQ: Decomposition-based SPARQL Query Generation

author.name: Papa Abdou Karim Karou Diallo, Aditya Sharma, Neshat Elhami Fard, Amal Zouaq

entry.summary: DeSQ is a KB-agnostic framework for knowledge base question answering that decomposes complex questions into atomic constraints, then maps them to SPARQL components for improved robustness and explainability. It aims to combine the strengths of formal query generation and direct retrieval.

entry.title: A Registry-Bound LLM Pipeline for Evidence-Grounded Trait Extraction across Tropical Plants, Aquatic Species, and Exotic Pets

author.name: Jeff Wang

entry.summary: This paper describes a registry-bound LLM pipeline producing auditable, evidence-grounded structured trait records for tropical plants, aquatic species, and pets at large scale. Four mechanisms (closed-vocabulary schema, verbatim evidence quotes, confidence labels, multi-version preservation) make extracted rows verifiable.

entry.title: When Knowledge Is Not Free: Cost-Aware Evidence Selection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Mingyan Wu, Han Yang, Omer Ben-Porat, Yftah Ziser

entry.summary: This paper introduces cost-aware retrieval-augmented generation, where evidence sources carry access-cost tiers and systems must answer within a budget. It augments MS MARCO with cost tiers and shows static selectors are brittle, motivating agentic cost-aware strategies.

entry.title: Unified Context Evolution for LLM Agents

author.name: Zixuan Zhu, Yitong Hu, Yong Dai, Junfeng Fang, Chunyang Jiang, Senkang Hu, Yuzhi Zhao

entry.summary: Unified Context Evolution (UCE) is a gradient-free framework that externalizes agent experience into an evolving library of typed Evolvable Context Units across Memory, Strategy, Workflow, and Skill types. It tracks quality through use to retain useful strategies across tasks.

entry.title: HERO'S JOURNEY: Testing Complex Rule Induction with Text Games

author.name: Anshun Asher Zheng, Kanishka Misra, David I. Beaver, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: HERO'S JOURNEY is a benchmark for rule induction in goal-directed text games, requiring agents to infer hidden rules from demonstrations and execute them over multiple steps. It finds LLMs show limited, uneven rule induction with execution itself forming a separate bottleneck.

entry.title: APE: Agentic Prompt Enhancer for Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Zijian Huang, Jay Zhangjie Wu, Zian Wang, Tianshi Cao, Jiasi Chen, Sanja Fidler, Huan Ling, Xuanchi Ren

entry.summary: APE is a lightweight framework that post-trains small language models as prompt-enhancement agents for image generation and editing, supporting single- and multi-agent rewriting without relying on large proprietary LLMs. It reduces cost, latency, and external dependence in visual generation pipelines.

entry.title: UniVerse: A Unified Modulation Framework for Segmentation-Free,Disentangled Multi-Concept Personalization

author.name: Quynh Phung, Sandesh Ghimire, Minsi Hu, Chung-Chi Tsai, Jia-Bin Huang

entry.summary: UniVerse is a unified modulation framework for segmentation-free, disentangled multi-concept personalization in diffusion transformers, enabling composable and decomposable concept extraction without explicit segmentation masks. It localizes and manipulates individual concepts from multi-object images.

entry.title: ASAP: Advancing Medical Volumetric Representation Learning with Anatomy-aware Semantically-adaptive Pre-training

author.name: Rongsheng Wang, Fenghe Tang, Zihang Jiang, Yingtai Li, Xu Zhang, Haoran Lai, Wenxin Ma, Wei Wei, Zhiyang He, Xiaodong Tao, Rui Yan, Qingsong Yao, Shaohua Kevin Zhou

entry.summary: ASAP is a vision-language pre-training framework for fine-grained medical volumetric representation from chest CT and radiology reports, integrating anatomy-aware knowledge injection with organ-level priors and semantically-adaptive selective alignment. It targets transferable, interpretable representations from weak heterogeneous supervision.

entry.title: FlowNar: Scalable Streaming Narration for Long-Form Videos

author.name: Zeyun Zhong, Manuel Martin, Chengzhi Wu, David Schneider, Frederik Diederichs, Juergen Gall, Juergen Beyerer

entry.summary: FlowNar is a framework for scalable streaming narration of long-form videos that uses dynamic context management for historical visual context removal combined with a Cross Linear Attentive Memory module to retain streaming visual history. It ensures bounded memory and computational complexity independent of video duration.

entry.title: FlowOVD: Learning Generative Latent Flows for Zero-shot Open-vocabulary Detection

author.name: Yao Wei, Andrea Cavallaro, Changjae Oh

entry.summary: FlowOVD introduces a generative perspective to open-vocabulary detection by modeling decoder query generation as a rectified-flow transport process that transforms text-agnostic queries into text-guided ones. It aims to improve query diversity and flexibility over discriminative approaches.

entry.title: ChartArena: Benchmarking Chart Parsing across Languages, Scenarios, and Formats

author.name: Shangpin Peng, Gengluo Li, Xingyu Wan, Chengquan Zhang, Hao Feng, Binghong Wu, Huawen Shen, Weinong Wang, Ziyi Cai, Zhuotao Tian, Han Hu, Can Ma, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: ChartArena is a comprehensive bilingual chart-parsing benchmark covering eight chart families (including flowcharts and mind maps) across digital, printed, and hand-drawn visual scenarios, built via human-agent collaboration. It addresses narrow chart-type coverage and incompatible output formats in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Agent Skills Should Go Beyond Text: The Case for Visual Skills

author.name: Binxiao Xu, Ruichuan An, Bocheng Zou, Hang Hua

entry.summary: This position paper argues that agent skills should extend beyond text to include visual skills, proposing a multimodal skill paradigm combining declarative textual logic with explicit visual support (static priors, visual grounding, localized state changes). It targets the bottleneck of text-only skill storage for visual-centric tasks.

entry.title: Goal2Pixel: Grounding Goals to Pixels for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Muyi Bao, Yuxin Cai, Hang Xu, Zongtai Li, Jinxi He, Jingfan Tang, Chen Lv, Ji Zhang, Yaqi Xie, Wenshan Wang

entry.summary: Goal2Pixel reformulates vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments as navigable pixel grounding, predicting a visible navigable pixel that is back-projected into a 3D waypoint rather than low-level actions. This reduces ambiguity and inefficient repeated VLM querying.

entry.title: What to Test Next: Interpretable Coverage Gap Discovery in Driving VLMs

author.name: Abhishek Aich, Sparsh Garg, Vijay Kumar BG, Turgun Yusuf Kashgari, Manmohan Chandraker

entry.summary: SliceScorer is a deterministic, interpretable scoring rule for recommending missing test slices in driving VLMs, combining an exposure-based coverage prior with a neighbor-failure prior, embedded in an LLM-orchestrated verification framework (SliceNav). It targets reliable safety validation across operational design domains. Authors include NEC and UCSD (Chandraker).

entry.title: Quality-Guided Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Kumar Abhishek, Ghassan Hamarneh

entry.summary: Proposes a quality-guided semi-supervised learning framework for medical image segmentation that trains a dedicated network to estimate segmentation quality from image-mask pairs, replacing self-referential confidence/uncertainty measures. Uses synthetic corruptions to train the quality predictor.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks on Robot Localization Systems via Deep Feature Perturbation

author.name: Zhenyu Li, Tianyi Shang

entry.summary: Investigates adversarial vulnerability of deep-learning robot localization systems by targeting Product Quantization in visual localization, using a lightweight network to perturb query features and mislead retrieval. Demonstrates safety risks for autonomous navigation.

entry.title: Pool-Select-Refine: Allocation-Aware Generative Dataset Distillation with Soft-Label-Guided Latent Refinement

author.name: Wenmin Li, Shunsuke Sakai, Zhongkai Zhao, Tatsuhito Hasegawa

entry.summary: Introduces Pool-Select-Refine, an allocation-aware generative dataset distillation method that decouples candidate generation from budget allocation, using soft-label-guided latent refinement instead of a rigid generate-and-use strategy. Improves use of limited images-per-class budgets.

entry.title: Multi-modal Video Representation Alignment for Robust Self-supervised Driver Distraction Detection

author.name: David J. Lerch, Livien Majer, Zeyun Zhong, Manuel Martin, Frederik Diederichs, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-modal video representation alignment framework for self-supervised driver distraction detection that handles faulty negatives and unreliable positives in contrastive learning using soft targets from cycle-consistency scores. Addresses violations of standard InfoNCE assumptions in noisy multi-modal data.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Linearized ADMM and Its Unrolling

author.name: Satoshi Takabe, Shunta Arai, Tadashi Wadayama

entry.summary: Proposes PA-LADMM, a physics-aware linearized ADMM algorithm for PDE-based inverse problems with convergence guarantees, plus a deep-unfolding variant. Reduces cost to one PDE solver and gradient call per iteration.

entry.title: Spiking and Event-driven Neuromorphic Mamba Models for Efficient Speech Recognition

author.name: Tauseef Ahmed, Tao Sun, Jeronimo Castrillon, Kanishkan Vadivel, Guangzhi Tang

entry.summary: Explores spiking and event-driven neuromorphic Mamba models for energy-efficient automatic speech recognition on edge devices, evaluating hardware benefits of different neuromorphic strategies. Converts dense operations into sparse computations.

entry.title: Generative Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Diffusion Modeling with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Guidance

author.name: Suk Ki Lee, Venkata Sai Deepak Mutta, Hyunwoong Ko

entry.summary: Combines decentralized diffusion-based single-agent trajectory generation with multi-agent reinforcement learning coordination for scalable multi-robot motion planning. Balances scalability with inter-agent interaction handling.

entry.title: Robust Integrated Planning and Control for Quadrotors in Dynamic Environments via NMPC with CBF Penalties

author.name: Zeinab Shayan, Mohammadreza Izadi, Reza Faieghi

entry.summary: Presents a robust integrated planning and control strategy for quadrotors using NMPC with control barrier functions embedded as exponential penalties, plus a high-gain disturbance observer and Kalman filter for moving-obstacle prediction. Improves feasibility and smooth obstacle avoidance under tight input bounds.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Reconnection for Multi-Robot Networks using Adaptive Prescribed-Time CBFs

author.name: Hao Liu, Yupeng Yang, Yanze Zhang, Wenhao Luo

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive prescribed-time control barrier function framework allowing multi-robot networks to temporarily disconnect and reconnect within an adjustable, feasible prescribed time, with a reconnection triggering mechanism balancing task execution and reconnection urgency. Relaxes overly restrictive persistent connectivity.

entry.title: FlipItRight: Stable Pose-Targeted Throw-Flip Across Diverse Objects

author.name: Axel Dawne, Shinkyu Park

entry.summary: FlipItRight is a framework for stable planar pose-targeted throw-flip with a high-DoF manipulator, decomposing the task into object-level release-state planning and robot-level swing motion construction with near-constant end-effector velocity for robustness to release-timing uncertainty. Validated on real hardware across diverse objects.

entry.title: A Simulation Platform for Flapping-Wing Vehicles

author.name: Haichuan Li, Tomi Westerlund

entry.summary: This work proposes an outcome-centric approach to robot policy adaptation, letting policies learn how dynamics affect interaction outcomes rather than encoding explicit physical parameters, grounded in a Lipschitz-regret relationship. It enables zero-shot policy adaptation under unmodeled or compound dynamics shifts.

entry.title: Constructive interpolation and generalization rates for neural ODEs: a control perspective

author.name: Antonio \'Alvarez-L\'opez, Lorenzo Liverani, Enrique Zuazua

entry.summary: This paper studies neural ODEs from a control-theoretic perspective, proving that semi-autonomous NODEs can exactly interpolate finite datasets and satisfy simultaneous cell controllability. It derives explicit population-risk and generalization bounds linking interpolation to nonparametric estimation.

entry.title: Decision-calibrated prediction sets for robust power system operations

author.name: Akylas Stratigakos, Honglin Wen, Elina Spyrou, Pierre Pinson

entry.summary: This paper introduces decision-calibrated prediction sets that calibrate uncertainty by the reliability of downstream decisions rather than predictive coverage, embedding them as uncertainty sets in robust power-system optimization. This avoids overly conservative, costly operating decisions under renewable uncertainty.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Neural Activation Control in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Abhijith Babu, Ramneet Kaur, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Olivera Kotevska, Susmit Jha, Yanzhao Wu, Sumit Kumar Jha, Anirban Roy

entry.summary: CTRL-STEER introduces closed-loop, time-varying activation steering for Vision-Language-Action models, replacing fixed steering coefficients that cause overcorrection and oscillation in embodied control. It decouples representation from regulation to steer along motion-aware directions adaptively.

entry.title: VESTA: Visual Exploration with Statistical Tool Agents

author.name: William Rudman, Abhishek Divekar, Kanishk Jain, Sebastian Joseph, Stella S. R. Offner, Matthew Lease, Kyle Mahowald, Greg Durrett, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: VESTA equips vision-language models with a dynamically growing exploration toolkit of data transformations, hypothesis-driven visualizations, and statistical tests to guide automated statistical model fitting. Unlike prior critique-only agents, it actively explores data before and during refinement.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory Risk-Aware Compression for Long-Horizon Agent Safety

author.name: Zhepei Hong, Lin Wang, Liting Li, Haokai Ma, Junfeng Fang, Fei Shen, Dan Zhang, Xiang Wang

entry.summary: TRACE reframes long-horizon agent safety detection as trajectory-level evidence compression using a Compressor-Reader design, where the Compressor encodes a full trajectory into a compact latent evidence state and the Reader judges safety with it. It aggregates sparse, delayed, compositional risk signals that escape turn-level detectors.

entry.title: Latent Reward Steering: An Adaptive Inference-Time Framework that Implicitly Promotes Cognitive Behaviors in Reasoning LLMs

author.name: Jiakang Li, Guanyu Zhu, Can Jin, Chenxi Huang, Dexu Yu, Ronghao Chen, Yang Zhou, Hongwu Peng, Xuanqi Lan, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Youhua Li

entry.summary: Latent Reward Steering is an adaptive inference-time framework that promotes cognitive behaviors in reasoning LLMs by optimizing sparse-autoencoder latent states that implicitly carry those behaviors, guided by a latent reward model trained on final-answer correctness. It avoids predefined behavior-level control or fixed steering directions.

entry.title: FALAT: Tracing Failures in LLM Agent Trajectories via Dependency-Guided Search

author.name: Md Nakhla Rafi, Md Ahasanuzzaman, Dong Jae Kim, Zhijie Wang, Tse-Hsun Chen

entry.summary: FALAT is a diagnostic framework for failure attribution in LLM agent trajectories that frames attribution as dependency-guided search rather than independent step classification, accounting for how earlier corrupted states propagate to later steps. It constructs an expectation model to identify the decisive error.

entry.title: Prospect-Theory Behavior from Bellman Optimality in MDPs with Catastrophic States

author.name: Yujiao Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that prospect-theory-like behaviors—S-shaped value profiles, endogenous loss sensitivity above one, and reflection-effect policy reversals—emerge from standard risk-neutral Bellman optimality in MDPs with an absorbing catastrophic state, without utility curvature or probability weighting. It demonstrates this across 495 configurations.

entry.title: Diagnosing LLM Arbitration Behavior over Pre-evidence Epistemic States in RAG-based Fact-Checking

author.name: Yuxi Sun, Wenbo Shang, Wei Gao, Xin Huang, Jing Ma

entry.summary: PAVE is a diagnostic testbed that stratifies an LLM verifier in RAG-based fact-checking into four epistemic states based on correctness and confidence of its pre-evidence prior, evaluating how it arbitrates between parametric and contextual signals under misleading evidence. It characterizes prior-context discrepancy that prior frameworks ignore.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Sustain Long-Horizon Organizational Dynamics?

author.name: Xuancheng Zhu, Yang Yue, Shuaibing Wan, Zihan Dou, Xiaohan Zhang, Yongrui Liu, Guoshun Nan

entry.summary: TaskWeave formulates long-horizon organizational simulation as a memory-centered coordination problem, using a Formulate-Partition-Diagnose-Align cycle and dependency-aware trace memory to sustain coherent multi-agent behavior. It is evaluated on a year-long IT company simulation.

entry.title: Transferring Information Across Interventions in Causal Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Mohammad Ali Javidian

entry.summary: This work proposes graph-coupled causal Bayesian optimization that shares information across interventions by exploiting common underlying mechanisms in a causal system, rather than learning each intervention's effect in isolation. It improves sample efficiency in costly experimental optimization.

entry.title: MobEvolve: An Agentic Self-Evolving Heuristic System for Interpretable Human Mobility Generation

author.name: Junlin He, Yihong Tang, Tong Nie, Ao Qu, Yuebing Liang, Hamzeh Alizadeh, Bang Liu, Wei Ma, Lijun Sun

entry.summary: MobEvolve is an agentic self-evolving heuristic framework for interpretable human mobility generation, initializing a behavior-inspired heuristic system that an LLM agent iteratively evolves by diagnosing empirical misalignments on a validation set. It seeks interpretability, behavioral plausibility, distributional alignment, and efficiency simultaneously.

entry.title: VET: A Framework for Analyzing AI Discourse

author.name: Meredith Ringel Morris

entry.summary: The VET Framework categorizes AI discourse along valence, effectiveness, and trajectory dimensions to identify and critique narratives of AI Hype, Doom, Denial, and Normalcy. Authored by Meredith Ringel Morris, it serves as an AI literacy tool for vetting polarized public discourse.

entry.title: S3TS: Stochastic Scenario-Structured Tree Search for Advanced Planning Under Uncertainty

author.name: Fabio Pavirani, Bert Claessens, Pierre Pinson, Chris Develder

entry.summary: S3TS is a stochastic scenario-structured tree search method for planning under uncertainty in energy scheduling, simultaneously handling non-linear system models and uncertainty from renewables, which existing methods address only one at a time. It bridges Monte Carlo tree search and stochastic optimization.

entry.title: Tracking the Behavioral Trajectories of Adapting Agents

author.name: Jonah Leshin, Manish Shah, Ian Timmis

entry.summary: Presents a method for measuring agent traits as directions in text-embedding space, training a linear model on before/after skill-file diffs to score behavioral edits (e.g., propensity to seek sensitive data). Achieves 91% sign-classification accuracy on a small labeled set.

entry.title: Examine Clinicians' Modification of Hedging Language in Ambient AI Documentation: A Comparative Study of AI Drafts and Final Notes

author.name: Yiliang Zhou, Yawen Guo, Di Hu, Sairam Sutari, Emilie Chow, Steven Tam, Danielle Perret, Deepti Pandita, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: Conducts paired analysis of clinician edits to ambient AI clinical note drafts to examine how edits change hedging language, finding hedging is more often introduced than removed across 62,811 paired sections. Reveals systematic certainty/uncertainty shifts varying by vendor and specialty.

entry.title: Hoeffding Concept Bottleneck Models with Applications to Overhead Images

author.name: Cl\'ement B\'enard, Manon Arfib, Christophe Labreuche, Victor Qu\'etu

entry.summary: Hoeffding Concept Bottleneck Models replace the linear aggregation of concept scores with a Hoeffding functional decomposition to capture nonlinear concept-output relations, improving explainability and reducing information leakage, applied to overhead image classification. Addresses leakage from large numbers of concepts.

entry.title: Automatically Differentiable Nonlinear Tensor Networks (ADNTNs) for Exponential Compression of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Andrzej Cichocki, Michal Wietczak

entry.summary: Studies Automatically Differentiable Nonlinear Tensor Networks (TTN, augmented TTN, MERA) as structured weight generators trained end-to-end for exponential compression of deep neural networks. Extends low-rank adaptation and tensor factorization with nonlinear activations and lateral mixing.

entry.title: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs on Code Generation for Complex Interactive Webpages

author.name: Fan Wu, Lishuai Dong, Cuiyun Gao, Yujia Chen, Yiming Huang, Yang Xiao, Qing Liao

entry.summary: Benchmarks MLLMs on generating code for complex interactive webpages, moving beyond static-page evaluations to assess interaction consistency between generated and reference behaviors. It exposes gaps in evaluating dynamic, user-interactive front-end code generation.

entry.title: ARCA: Adapter-Residual Credit Assignment When Token Signals Degenerate

author.name: Rodney Lafuente-Mercado

entry.summary: Proposes ARCA, an adapter-residual credit assignment method addressing how token-level credit signals (surprisal, entropy reduction, divergence) become degenerate under LoRA's low-rank constraint in LLM RL. It formalizes and directly measures this failure mode.

entry.title: Detector-Evasive LLM Paraphrasing via Constrained Policy Optimization

author.name: Mingyi Wang, Zhuoer Shen, Yuheng Bu, Shaofeng Zou

entry.summary: Formulates detector-evasive LLM paraphrasing as a Constrained Markov Decision Process where evasion is the objective and semantic preservation is an explicit constraint, proposing DEPO, a Lagrangian primal-dual RL algorithm. It provides precise control over the evasion-semantics trade-off lacking in scalarized reward designs.

entry.title: Pre-Deployment Robustness Stress Testing for CT Segmentation Systems Using Clinically Motivated Multi-Corruption Augmentation

author.name: CholMin Kang, Jonghyun Chung, Amanpreet Kaurb, Nagesh Gulkotwarb, Arthi Sivasankaranb

entry.summary: RAMP is a robustness-oriented augmentation framework for CT segmentation that injects clinically plausible corruptions (noise, contrast shifts, artifacts) during training to improve deployment stability. It provides pre-deployment stress testing across CT segmentation settings.

entry.title: Logit Distillation on Manifolds: Mapping by Learning

author.name: Yiru Yang, Junling Wang, Nishant Kumar Singh, Luohong Wu, Haoran Yan

entry.summary: This work proposes manifold-based logit distillation that maps student and teacher representations into an aligned high-dimensional embedding space, combined with LoRA injection to reduce ensemble deployment cost. It targets transferring ensemble benefits into single deployable models.

entry.title: MoEIoU: Rethinking Bounding-Box Regression as a Mixture of Experts

author.name: Vinay Edula, Priyanka Bagade

entry.summary: MoEIoU recasts bounding-box regression as a mixture of experts that jointly models overlap, center alignment, and shape, adapting penalty emphasis to optimization dynamics rather than using fixed geometric penalties. This addresses the changing nature of box errors across training stages.

entry.title: Test-Time Training for Zero-Resource Dense Retrieval Reranking

author.name: Shiyan Liu, Yichen Li

entry.summary: Proposes DART, a test-time adaptation method for dense retrieval reranking in zero-resource settings, using top/bottom-ranked documents as pseudo-positive/negative supervision to adapt a bilinear scoring matrix per query. Avoids costly cross-encoder training.

entry.title: pcbGPT: Automatic PCB Schematic Synthesis from Natural Language Requirements

author.name: Tobias King, Steven Kehrberg, Michael Beigl, Tobias R\"oddiger

entry.summary: Presents pcbGPT, a grounded system generating editable KiCad PCB schematics from natural-language specifications using a Python DSL, component-library search, datasheet-grounded knowledge, and execution-based checking. Targets embedded, IoT, and wearable hardware design.

entry.title: PALTO: Physics-Informed Active Learning for Tri-Gate FinFET Design Optimization for Vertical Power Delivery

author.name: Ayoub Sadeghi, Leonid Popryho, Inna Partin-Vaisband

entry.summary: Introduces IndoBias, a culturally-grounded bias benchmark for Indonesian and three local languages (Javanese, Sundanese, Makasar), with dual depth-oriented and breadth-oriented evaluation tracks grounded in social-science frameworks. Reveals localized stereotypes in LLMs.

entry.title: ChronosAD: Leveraging Time Series Foundation Models for Accurate Anomaly Detection

author.name: Uzair Khan, Luigi Capogrosso, Francesco Biondani, Michele Magno, Franco Fummi, Francesco Setti, Marco Cristani

entry.summary: Introduces ChronosAD, a time-series anomaly detection architecture using a time-series foundation model as a zero-shot feature extractor refined by a temporal block of BiLSTM and multi-head attention. Aims to generalize across datasets where anomalies are subtle or context-dependent.

entry.title: Estimating Mutual Information between Time Series and Temporal Event Sequences Across Diverse Analysis Tasks

author.name: Haoji Hu, Huaqing Mao, Yijun Lin, Xiaowei Jia, Jinwei Zhou, Minoh Jeong, Yao-Yi Chiang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a nonparametric mutual information estimator measuring dependence between continuous time series and discrete temporal event sequences without ad hoc discretization. It addresses instability of existing estimators under quantization and event redundancy.

entry.title: JenBridge: Adaptive Long-Form Video Soundtracking across Scene Transitions

author.name: Jiashuo Yu, Yao Yao, Boyu Chen, Alex Wang

entry.summary: JenBridge is a modular framework for adaptive long-form video soundtracking that maintains coherence across scene transitions using a flow-matching Transformer with dual text-visual conditioning. It targets narrative continuity that short-clip music systems lack.

entry.title: Dynamic Trust-Aware Sparse Communication Topology for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Consensus

author.name: Wanshuang Gou, Zihan Liu

entry.summary: DySCo introduces dynamic trust-aware sparse communication topologies for LLM multi-agent consensus, reducing the quadratic message and token costs of fully connected debate. It adapts communication relationships to task instances and reasoning states.

entry.title: RA-LWLM: Retrieval-Augmented In-Context Localization with Wireless Foundation Models

author.name: Guangjin Pan, Hui Chen, Hei Victor Cheng, Henk Wymeersch

entry.summary: RA-LWLM is a retrieval-augmented in-context localization framework for 6G that externalizes scene-specific information into per-scene fingerprint databases instead of model weights, enabling training-free cross-scene adaptation. It uses a frozen wireless foundation model.

entry.title: Monitoring Agentic Systems Before They're Reliable

author.name: Marisa Ferrara Boston, Glen Hanson, Effi Georgala, JD Hudgens, Heather Frase

entry.summary: Presents a monitoring and triage methodology for agentic systems before they are reliable, where structural defects dominate over task-level errors. Decomposes evaluation into quality/suitability/efficiency across three scopes using variance signals and FMEA-style severity routing.

entry.title: KG-Guard: Graph-Based Hallucination Detection for Knowledge Base Question Answering

author.name: Albert Sawczyn, Piotr Bielak, Tomasz Kajdanowicz

entry.summary: Formulates hallucination detection in knowledge-base QA as answer-node classification and proposes a lightweight graph-based framework treating the answering LLM as a component within a question-specific subgraph. Targets cases where LLMs ignore graph evidence or perform invalid reasoning.

entry.title: The role of class encoding in neural collapse

author.name: Bastien Massion, Roy Makhlouf, Estelle Massart

entry.summary: Investigates how label encoding affects neural collapse using the unrestricted feature model with MSE loss, showing one-hot encoded balanced data transitions from a simplex equiangular tight frame to an orthogonal frame as bias regularization increases. Extends analysis to arbitrary encodings.

entry.title: Torus Graphs for Large Scale Neural Phase Analysis

author.name: Jack Goffinet, Casey Hanks, David E. Carlson
