entry.summary: Develops a stochastic score-matching procedure for Torus Graph models that scales neural phase analysis to hundreds of EEG/LFP channels, overcoming the prior O(d^6) bottleneck. Enables principled study of phase relationships across brain regions.

entry.title: Distributed GNEP Algorithms without Multiplier Sharing and Applications to Multi-Robot Coordination and Contextual Bandit-Based Active Learning

author.name: Shao-An Yin

entry.summary: Introduces fully distributed continuous-time algorithms for Generalized Nash Equilibrium Problems that converge without sharing Lagrange multipliers, improving privacy and reducing communication. Applies to multi-robot coordination and contextual bandit active learning.

entry.title: LeAP: Learnable Adaptive Permutation for Feature Selection in Heterogeneous and Sparse Recommender Systems

author.name: Yihong Huang, Chen Chu, Fei Chen, Yu Lin, Ruiduan Li, Zhihao Li

entry.summary: Proposes LeAP, a learnable adaptive permutation method for feature selection in industrial recommender systems that handles heterogeneous feature dimensions, extreme sparsity, and the computational cost of permutation-based importance. Targets large-scale efficient feature selection.

entry.title: A Per-Component Diagnostic Protocol for Neural HJB-PIDE Solvers under Control-Dependent L\'evy Jumps

author.name: R. Drissi

entry.summary: Proposes a five-step diagnostic protocol for residual-trained neural HJB-PIDE solvers under control-dependent Levy jumps, decomposing the Hamiltonian into components and comparing against independent references to catch operator errors hidden by good scalar metrics. Detects a missing mixture factor in a Merton-Variance-Gamma benchmark.

entry.title: IMWM: Intuition Models Complement World Models for Latent Planning

author.name: Baoqi Gao, Ruize Han, Miao Wang, Song Wang

entry.summary: IMWM pairs a learned latent world model with an intuition model trained from demonstrations to recognize promising actions, addressing the finding that even a perfect world model can fail due to search bottlenecks. The two models collaborate through retrieval initialization and other lightweight components.

entry.title: Decentralized Instruction Tuning: Conflict-Aware Splitting and Weight Merging

author.name: Minsik Choi, Geewook Kim

entry.summary: MERIT enables decentralized instruction tuning by training mixture parts independently and merging in parameter space, supported by a local quadratic theory showing weight merging yields curvature-weighted variance reduction. It addresses gradient interference and bandwidth bottlenecks jointly.

entry.title: Why Are DMD Students Lazy? Understanding the Copying Behavior in Few-Step Distillation

author.name: Shucheng Li, Iolo Jones, Alexander Tong, Michael M. Bronstein

entry.summary: This work investigates why DMD-distilled few-step generators in high dimensions spontaneously reproduce the teacher's noise-data pairings (copying), despite distribution-level supervision being agnostic to pairings. It shows copying is not from adversarial objectives or memorization.

entry.title: Positional Encodings Anchor Spatial Structure in Vision Transformers: A Geometric Perspective on Robustness

author.name: Mahmoud Mannes

entry.summary: Investigates how positional encodings shape spatial representation geometry in vision transformers and their relation to robustness, introducing a Spatial Similarity Distance Correlation metric. Finds PEs anchor stable spatial structure that content-driven structure lacks under permutation.

entry.title: Riemannian Stochastic Optimization for Sufficient Dimension Reduction

author.name: Thibault Pautrel, Fran\c{c}ois Portier

entry.summary: Develops SMAVE, a Riemannian stochastic optimization algorithm for sufficient dimension reduction that recasts the MAVE criterion as smooth maximization on the Stiefel manifold with closed-form gradients. Avoids both curse of dimensionality and quadratic per-iteration cost.

entry.title: Annotation-Informed Block-Sparse Bayesian Modeling for cis-Expression Prediction

author.name: Lei Huang, Hui Shen, Kuan-Jui Su, Chuan Qiu, Martha Isabel Gonzalez-Ramirez, Anqi Liu, Zhe Luo, Yun Gong, Yipu Zhang, Dawei Li, Chaoyang Zhang, Hong-Wen Deng

entry.summary: Introduces bsBSLMM, a block-sparse Bayesian model incorporating LD-block spike-and-slab sparsity and a TSS-informed prior for cis-expression prediction from genotypes. Outperforms standard methods across 23,098 genes in held-out prediction.

entry.title: Reason, Retrieve, Re-rank: A Zero-Shot Reasoning-Aware Framework for Composed Video Retrieval

author.name: Ali Alavi

entry.summary: Introduces R3-CoVR, a training-free zero-shot pipeline for reasoning-aware composed video retrieval that uses an MLLM to verbalize the after-effects of an edit, embeds with a contrastive video-text encoder, and re-ranks under constraints. Targets the CVPR 2026 VidLLMs workshop challenge.

entry.title: Towards Optimal Robustness in Learning-Augmented Paging

author.name: Peng Chen, Hailiang Zhao, Xueyan Tang, Yixuan Wang, Shuiguang Deng

entry.summary: Studies learning-augmented paging, working to close the robustness gap between existing bounds (2H_k+O(1)) and the optimal competitive ratio H_k in the randomized setting. It introduces a unifying primitive and new properties of optimal algorithms.

entry.title: Learning Chaotic Dynamics through Second-Order Geometric Supervision

author.name: Shinhoo Kang, Hai V. Nguyen, Tan Bui-Thanh

entry.summary: Shows that enforcing second-order (curvature) consistency, beyond trajectory and Jacobian matching, helps neural models learn chaotic dynamics that preserve attractor geometry and invariant statistics. It uses model-constrained Hessian approximations to make this tractable in high dimensions.

entry.title: Density-Aware Translation of Spurious Correlations in Zero-Shot VLMs

author.name: Afsaneh Hasanebrahimi, Hanxun Huang, Christopher Leckie, Sarah Erfani

entry.summary: Proposes Density-Aware Translation (DAT) to refine CLIP image-text similarity using a local geometric density term from group reference sets, mitigating spurious correlations in zero-shot classification without fine-tuning. It leverages the modality gap and anisotropic embedding geometry.

entry.title: CORE-MTL: Rethinking Gradient Balancing via Causal Orthogonal Representations

author.name: Chengfeng Wu, Tao Zou, Yanru Wu, Jingge Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CORE-MTL, a causally motivated representation-centric multi-task learning framework that factorizes the shared representation into orthogonal semantic and residual components to disentangle task-relevant structure from spurious context. It aims to reduce negative transfer beyond gradient-balancing methods.

entry.title: ART: Attention Run-time Termination for Efficient Large Language Model Decoding

author.name: Chen Qiu, Guozhong Li, Panos Kalnis

entry.summary: Proposes ProtoAda, a prototype-guided framework for multimodal continual instruction tuning that adaptively expands LoRA adapters and consolidates geometry, addressing wrong routing when tasks share visual-linguistic semantics but differ in response structure. It improves over image-text-similarity-only routing in mixture-of-LoRA-experts setups.

entry.title: TalkTag: Fine-Grained Morphosyntactic Error Annotation for Transcribed Speech

author.name: Shamira Venturini (Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences), Oliver Hennh\"ofer (Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences), Steffen Kinkel (Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences), Jannik Str\"otgen (Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: TalkTag is an LLM-based tool fine-tuned to automate CHAT-style morphosyntactic error annotation in spoken-language transcripts under extreme data scarcity using children's narrative data. It provides a scalable alternative to labor-intensive manual annotation in clinical and developmental research.

entry.title: General Covariant Action Modeling: Constructing Generalized Manifolds via Spatio-Temporal Decoupling

author.name: Huaihai Lyu, Chaofan Chen, Mingyu Cao, Yuheng Ji, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: The Generalized Action Manifold framework enforces general covariance in embodied policies through structural disentanglement, using an arc-length parameterizer to separate spatial path geometry from temporal dynamics. It aims for robust generalization from limited demonstration data.

entry.title: {\alpha}Depth: Learning Single-Pass Soft Boundary Decomposition for Stereo Conversion

author.name: Xiang Zhang, Yang Zhang, Lukas Mehl, Karlis Martins Briedis, Markus Gross, Christopher Schroers

entry.summary: AlphaDepth introduces a layered representation that decomposes soft boundaries (hair, defocus blur) for high-fidelity stereo conversion by estimating layered color and depth values at ambiguous regions. It resolves single-layer depth ambiguity in a single pass without user intervention.

entry.title: Images as Tables: In-Context Learning with TabPFN for Low-Data Detection of AI-Generated Images

author.name: Jan Philip Walter, Shashank Agnihotri, Margret Keuper

entry.summary: This work detects AI-generated images in low-data regimes by encoding images via frozen DINOv3, reducing CLS features to structured rows with PCA, and applying TabPFN for in-context tabular classification without gradient fine-tuning. It treats fake-image detection as low-data structured prediction.

entry.title: Decoupled Residual Denoising Diffusion Models for Unified and Data Efficient Image-to-Image Translation

author.name: Ziyue Lin, Jiahe Hou, Hongyu Xia, Xinrui Xie, Feifei Wang, Yuyin Zhou, Wei Wang, Jiawei Liu, Liangqiong Qu

entry.summary: DRDD decouples residual and noise removal in diffusion models for unified, data-efficient image-to-image translation, leveraging the finding that Gaussian noise implicitly harmonizes feature distributions across domains. It avoids prematurely eroding this harmonization that coupled diffusion processes cause.

entry.title: Training-free image inversion for one-step diffusion models

author.name: Tao Wu, Senmao Li, Yaxing Wang, Shiqi Yang, Kai Wang, Joost van de Weijer

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free inversion framework for one-step diffusion models, identifying initial latent editability and caption-gap as key obstacles and introducing iterative noise alignment and suffix learning to address them. It enables real image inversion and editing for fast one-step models.

entry.title: Splatshot: 3D Face Avatar Generation from a Single Unconstrained Photo

author.name: Hao Liang, Zhixuan Ge, Soumendu Majee, Joanna Li, Ashok Veeraraghavan, Guha Balakrishnan

entry.summary: Splatshot reconstructs photorealistic 3D face avatars from a single unconstrained photo by coupling explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting (for geometric consistency) with 2D diffusion priors (for photorealism) in a training-free per-step 3D feedback denoising loop. It exploits the complementary strengths of the two paradigms.

entry.title: Unsupervised Collaborative Domain Adaptation for Driving Scene Parsing

author.name: Jiahe Fan, Shaolong Shu, Mingjian Sun, Tiehua Zhang, Bohong Xiao, Hanli Wang, Rui Fan

entry.summary: Presents an unsupervised collaborative domain adaptation method for driving scene parsing that uses multiple pre-trained source models to mitigate source-specific biases without accessing source data. Improves robustness across diverse road, weather, and traffic conditions.

entry.title: Beyond Low-Rank: Low-Rank Sparse Prompting via Spiking Neural Network and Prompt Factorization

author.name: Yumiao Zhao, Bo Jiang, Beibei Wang, Xixi Wan, Xiao Wang, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Proposes LoRSP, integrating brain-inspired spiking neural networks with low-rank prompt factorization for efficient visual prompting that avoids dense pixel-level prompts. Aims for sparse, energy-efficient adaptation of large pretrained vision models.

entry.title: PINNOCHIO: Physics-Informed Neural Network for Coupled Hyperelastic Interface-Volume Simulation in Orthognathic Surgery

author.name: Jungwook Lee, Daeseung Kim, Kevin Gu, Zhangfeng Hu, Tianshu Kuang, Finn Hopeman, Michael A. K. Liebschner, Jaime Gateno, Pingkun Yan

entry.summary: PINNOCHIO is a physics-informed neural network for predicting facial soft-tissue deformation in orthognathic surgery planning, coupling hyperelastic interface-volume simulation with partial clinical supervision. Balances FEM accuracy with deep learning efficiency.

entry.title: A Sonar-Visual Dataset for Cross-Modal Underwater Robot Perception

author.name: Weitung Chen, Phil Tinn, Per Gunnar Auran, Martin Ludvigsen, Peter Halland Haro

entry.summary: SOVIS is a sonar-visual dataset with over 76,000 paired frames from 17 dives at six fjord sites, supported by a synchronization pipeline and interactive annotation tool, enabling cross-modal underwater perception research. Demonstrates proof-of-concept cross-modal prediction.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Modeling and Control of Emergent Behaviors in Robot Swarms

author.name: Zixuan Jin, Wenzhuo Zhang, Shuxian Quan, Zirui Dong, Fangwen Ye, Yuchen Shi, Cheng Xu

entry.summary: PhySwarm is a physics-informed micro-macro framework modeling multi-stage swarm emergence as physically constrained density-field evolution via a multi-phase advection-diffusion-reaction model coupled to executable robot motion. Bridges macroscopic field dynamics with microscopic robot control.

entry.title: Predicted-Flow Control Barrier Functions for Real-Time Safe Optimal Control

author.name: Amirsaeid Safari, Jesse B. Hoagg

entry.summary: Predicted-Flow Control Barrier Functions generalize CBFs from current-state functions to functionals of a predicted flow over a finite horizon, certifying safety along the whole trajectory and reducing myopia. The paper addresses validity guarantees under control constraints.

entry.title: Empirical Likelihood with Generative AI

author.name: Jiguang Li, Sid Kankanala, Veronika Rockova

entry.summary: This work proposes a nonparametric Bayesian framework based on exponentially tilted empirical likelihood, particularly suited when prior information is specified on observables, such as with auxiliary or generative-AI-synthesized data. It enables moment-condition-based inference incorporating synthetic data sources.

entry.title: CAST: Non-Privileged Clipped Asymmetric Self-Teaching with Advantage Flipping for GRPO

author.name: Yang Li, Gongle Xue, Yijia Guo, Yuheng Yuan, Liwen Hu, Lei Ma

entry.summary: CAST proposes a non-privileged clipped asymmetric self-teaching method with advantage flipping to improve GRPO when group-relative advantages vanish because all sampled trajectories share the same correctness. It addresses noisy token-level guidance from on-policy self-distillation.

entry.title: Probe Before You Edit: Probing-Guided Molecular Optimization for LLM Agents in Structure-Based Drug Design

author.name: Zaifei Yang, Weiyu Chen, Yaqing Wang, James Kwok

entry.summary: This paper introduces probing-guided molecular optimization for LLM agents in structure-based drug design, using diagnostic metrics to expose that agents edit ligands without knowing how the pocket-ligand complex responds, rarely improving binding and druggability jointly. Probing before editing addresses this failure mode.

entry.title: Ryze: Evidence-Enriched Data Synthesis from Biomedical Papers

author.name: Yeqi Huang, Yue Chen, Yanwei Ye, Guanhao Su, Luo Mai

entry.summary: Ryze is a fully automated system that converts raw biomedical papers into evidence-enriched training sets and a domain-specialized VLM, synthesizing QA pairs with complete supporting evidence across figures, tables, captions, and text. It reduces reliance on costly expert annotation while preserving evidence structure.

entry.title: TriLens: Per-Layer Logit-Lens Entropy for White-Box Hallucination Detection

author.name: Bohan Yang, Yijun Gong, Zhi Zhang, Ge Zhang, Wenpeng Xing, Meng Han

entry.summary: TriLens is a white-box hallucination detector that reads the multi-head attention output, feed-forward output, and residual stream through the model's logit lens at every layer, recording only the entropy of each readout to form a compact trajectory of how certainty forms across depth. It avoids storing high-dimensional states or multiple samples.

entry.title: MindClaw: Closed-Loop Embodied Mental-State Reasoning for Precision Intervention

author.name: Ruoxuan Zhang, Qiaoqiao Wan, Zhengguang Wang, Chenghao Yu, Hongxia Xie, Jianlong Fu, Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: MindClaw extends robot-centric Theory of Mind reasoning to a real-time closed-loop setting for embodied mental-state reasoning with precision intervention, deciding when reasoning is needed and intervening only when help is useful. It connects multi-source perception to maintain and update actor-specific beliefs in a changing environment.

entry.title: SIRIUS-SQL: Anchoring Multi-Candidate Text-to-SQL in Execution Feedback

author.name: Leo Luo, Haining Xie, Siqi Shen, Zhipeng Ma, Rui Ling, Hang Xu, Hefeng Jiang, Dingwei Chen, Yang Li, Peng Chen, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: SIRIUS-SQL improves multi-candidate text-to-SQL by addressing redundant sampling, error-type-specific correction (runtime errors, timeouts, empty results), and single-angle selection limitations through execution feedback anchoring. It combines difficulty-aware sampling with multi-angle selection.

entry.title: Early Diagnosis of Wasted Computation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Failure-Aware Observability

author.name: Xianyou Li, Weiran Yan, Yichao Wu, Penghao Liang, Mengwei Yuan, Jianan Liu, Jing Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a failure-aware observability framework for diagnosing wasted computation in tool-using multi-agent LLM traces, mapping recurring failure modes to online trace signals like tool reliability, orchestration loops, and budget pressure. It is evaluated on a three-agent QA system over GAIA validation tasks.

entry.title: EvoBrain: Continual Learning of EEG Foundation Models Across Heterogeneous BCI Tasks

author.name: Yangxuan Zhou, Sha Zhao, Jiquan Wang, Shijian Li, Gang Pan

entry.summary: EvoBrain formulates EEG foundation model adaptation as a cross-task continual learning problem, proposing a dynamic task-aware framework to enable knowledge transfer across heterogeneous BCI tasks without task-isolated fine-tuning. It addresses scalability and overhead that otherwise scale linearly with task count.

entry.title: OctoT2I: A Self-Evolving Agentic Text-to-Image Router

author.name: Xu Jiang, Bin Chen, Gehui Li, Yule Duan, Ronggang Wang, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: OctoT2I is a self-evolving agentic text-to-image router that reformulates T2I as joint optimization of generation quality and inference efficiency, using a stateful multi-round routing strategy to adaptively select among diverse models. It avoids reliance on handcrafted priors and rigid single-path decisions.

entry.title: COMAP: Co-Evolving World Models and Agent Policies for LLM Agents

author.name: Youwei Liu, Jian Wang, Hanlin Wang, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: COMAP co-evolves textual world models and agent policies through closed-loop interaction so the world model adapts to the evolving agent's state-action distribution, avoiding fixed world models or external reward dependence. The agent uses future-aware reflection on predicted feedback.

entry.title: BenHalluEval: A Multi-Task Hallucination Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models on Bengali

author.name: Shefayat E Shams Adib, Ahmed Alfey Sani, Ekramul Alam Esham, Ajwad Abrar, Ishmam Tashdeed, Md Taukir Azam Chowdhury

entry.summary: BenHalluEval is the first fine-grained hallucination evaluation framework for Bengali, covering QA, code-mixed QA, summarization, and reasoning with 12,000 hallucinated candidates and a dual-track protocol measuring false positives and hallucination detection across seven LLMs. Fills a gap for the sixth most-spoken language.

entry.title: Rare Events, Real Signals: Functional Ensembles as Units of Computation in Deep Spiking Networks

author.name: Aditi Aravind, Konstantinos Ladakis, Mario Alexios Savaglio, Stelios M. Smirnakis, Maria Papadopouli

entry.summary: Introduces a neuroscience-inspired functional connectivity framework to analyze deep spiking neural networks, defining first-order functionally-connected neuron groups via significant pairwise correlations and tracking their response properties. Finds biological cortex principles preserved in spiking ResNets.

entry.title: Multi-Contrast MRI Motion Correction via Parameter-Informed Disentanglement and Adaptive Experts

author.name: Honglin Xiong, Yuxian Tang, Feng Li, Yulin Wang, Lei Xiang, Dinggang Shen, Qian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified MRI motion correction framework using ScanCLIP for parameter-informed contrast disentanglement plus a severity-aware Mixture-of-Experts correction network. It generalizes across diverse MRI contrasts and artifact severities unlike contrast-specific methods.

entry.title: LLMs Need Encoders for Semantic IDs Too

author.name: Xiangyi Chen, Zelun Wang, Xinyi Li, Yi-Ping Hsu, Jaewon Yang, Jiajing Xu

entry.summary: Argues Semantic IDs in generative recommendation constitute a distinct modality requiring dedicated encoders, since a SID token's meaning depends on its prefix context. Proposes PrefixMem, a lightweight prefix n-gram memory encoder providing prefix-conditioned representations, analogous to vision encoders in multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: CodeCytos: AI-assisted spatial molecular imaging analysis via code-augmented agent action space

author.name: Hung Q. Vo, Huy Q. Vo, Son T. Ly, Zhihao Wan, Anh-Vu Nguyen, Hong Zhao, Jianting Sheng, Stephen T. C. Wong, Hien V. Nguyen

entry.summary: CodeCytos is a code-augmented reasoning agent for spatial molecular imaging analysis, enabling programmable, dynamic interaction with tissue imaging data beyond fixed pre-implemented features. It aims to automate and customize complex spatial cellular analyses.

entry.title: An Open-Source Benchmark and Baseline for Multi-temporal Referring Segmentation

author.name: Bingyu Li, Da Zhang, Tao Huo, Zhiyuan Zhao, Junyu Gao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Introduces a new task and 21K-sample benchmark for multi-temporal referring segmentation, where models segment language-described temporal changes across image sequences. Provides an automated data construction pipeline and baseline agent.

entry.title: ThinkSwitch: Context Distillation with LoRA and Weight Interpolation for Specific-Purpose Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Dhruv Saini, Rohan Pandey

entry.summary: Introduces ThinkSwitch, a low-compute procedure co-training paired instruct and thinking checkpoints by distilling answer-only outputs into the instruct model via QLoRA and reconstructing thinking checkpoints via spherical weight interpolation. Aims to reduce reasoning-trace latency.

entry.title: FreqLite: A Lightweight Frequency-Decomposed Linear Model with Adaptive Reversible Normalization for Robust Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Mirza Samad Ahmed Baiga, Syeda Anshrah Gillani

entry.summary: Presents FreqLite, an ultra-lightweight channel-independent frequency-decomposed linear forecaster using a learnable lossless spectral filter and adaptive reversible normalization for long-term time-series forecasting. Addresses limitations of fixed decomposition filters and single-statistic de-normalization.

entry.title: Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory

author.name: Ruiyin Li, Yiran Zhang, Xiyu Zhou, Yangxiao Cai, Peng Liang, Weisong Sun, Jifeng Xuan, Zhi Jin, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes MAAD, a knowledge-driven multi-agent framework for software architecture design that orchestrates agents with external knowledge and hierarchical memory to bridge requirements and architecture. Aims to broaden exploration of architectural alternatives under agile pressures.

entry.title: Identifying High-Confidence Social Biases in LLMs for Trustworthy Conversational Tutoring Agents

author.name: Aitor Arronte Alvarez, Naiyi Xie Fincham

entry.summary: This study evaluates high-confidence social biases in LLMs used as conversational tutoring agents, identifying cases where models fail to recognize biased judgments while remaining confident. It introduces a dataset generation method for bias evaluation in educational settings.

entry.title: HAIM: Human-AI Music Datasets for AI Music Production Tracking Benchmark

author.name: Seonghyeon Go, Yumin Kim

entry.summary: HAIM introduces human-AI music datasets and a benchmark for tracking AI involvement across the music production workflow, moving beyond binary AI-or-human detection. It reflects realistic workflows where AI refines human tracks and humans post-process AI material.

entry.title: Unveiling the Limits of Large Language Models in Inferring Pragmatic Meaning from Non-Verbal Responses

author.name: Sugyeong Eo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of LLMs' ability to infer pragmatic meaning from dialogue consisting solely of non-verbal responses. It examines whether models recognize indirect intent and how to improve their non-verbal interpretation.

entry.title: Rethinking Evaluation Paradigms in IBP-based Certified Training

author.name: Konstantin Kaulen, Hadar Shavit, Holger H. Hoos

entry.summary: Critiques evaluation practices in IBP-based certified training, arguing that reporting single configurations is misleading given the natural-vs-certified accuracy tradeoff. Proposes evaluating across configurations for fairer comparison of certified robustness methods.

entry.title: Modeling Spectral Energy Shifts in Spatio-Temporal Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yilin Liu, Hongchao Zhang, Taylor T. Johnson, Ahmad F. Taha, Meiyi Ma

entry.summary: Identifies camouflaged graph anomalies that decrease spectral energy variation and evade existing spectral methods, and proposes a node-level spectral energy formulation compatible with message passing. Builds an energy-aware graph learning framework for static and dynamic graphs.

entry.title: Canonicalized Stable-List Replay for Private Federated Continual Learning over Language-Model Embeddings

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Abu Sa-Adat Mohamed Moon-Im Al Ahsan, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces CSLR, a method for private federated continual learning over language-model embeddings that aligns unordered, noisy replay candidate lists across clients using public anchor sentences. Provides identifiability guarantees under differential privacy constraints.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Noise Adaptation: Transferring Knowledge from Noise Domain

author.name: Yuan Yao, Jin Song, Huixia Li, Tongtong Yuan, Jiaqi Wu, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Formalizes Semi-Supervised Noise Adaptation, using a synthetic Gaussian noise domain as a surrogate source for transfer learning in the semi-supervised setting. Builds on the surprising observation that noise domains can aid target generalization.

entry.title: When Hard Negatives Hurt: Bridging the Generative-Discriminative Gap in Hard Negative Synthesis for Retrieval

author.name: Zhicheng Zhang, Jiwei Tang, Kuicai Dong, Xiaopeng Li, Jieming Zhu, Jingyu Li, Qianhui Zhu, Fengyuan Lu, Wang Jiaheng, Gang Wang, Hai-Tao Zheng, Zhaocheng Du

entry.summary: This work identifies a generative-discriminative gap when using LLM-synthesized hard negatives for retriever training, showing naive use degrades performance. It formalizes why fluent generation conflicts with the strategic relevance violations needed for contrastive learning.

entry.title: All Models are Wrong, Knowing Where is Useful: On Model Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bernd Frauenknecht, Devdutt Subhasish, Artur Eisele, Friedrich Solowjow, Sebastian Trimpe

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework for handling probabilistic model inaccuracies in model-based RL through targeted uncertainty handling, mitigating model exploitation. It reports successes in hardware learning and safe exploration for robotics.

entry.title: Private and Stable Test-Time Adaptation with Differential Privacy

author.name: Zefeng Li, Qiaoyue Tang, Mathias Lecuyer, Evan Shelhamer

entry.summary: This work casts several test-time adaptation methods (Tent, EATA, SAR, DeYO, COME) into differentially private forms with per-sample gradient clipping and noise. On ImageNet-C, DP-TTA provides privacy at small accuracy cost, and clipping can even improve stability.

entry.title: Low-Pass Flow Matching

author.name: Francesco M. Ruscio, T. Konstantin Rusch

entry.summary: Low-Pass Flow Matching introduces an operator-modulated interpolant that induces a time-varying spectral bias transitioning from source spectrum to a frequency-decaying bias as the path approaches data, better matching natural data spectra. It improves sample quality and reduces sampling cost with adaptive ODE solvers.

entry.title: Per-Group Error, Not Total MSE: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models for 11-DoF Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Pau Montagut Bofi, Mario Garc\'ia Blasco, Tessa Pulli, Markus Vincze

entry.summary: Argues that aggregate MSE misleads model selection when fine-tuning VLA models for heterogeneous mobile manipulators, since easy joints mask failing ones, and advocates per-group error analysis. Demonstrates on an 11-DoF robot comparing SmolVLA and pi-0.5.

entry.title: Feature Alignment Determines Fusion Strategy: A Comparative Study of Cross-Attention and Concatenation in Multimodal Learning

author.name: Zhiqiang Zhou, Xuezhen Xie

entry.summary: A controlled comparative study showing that feature alignment quality, not data scale, determines whether concatenation or cross-attention works better for multimodal fusion. It provides a sample-complexity theory explaining when concatenation outperforms cross-attention on pre-aligned features.

entry.title: Site4Drug: Predicting Drug-Binding Target Sites with an AI Agent

author.name: Taehan Kim, Sarrah Rose Mikhail Leung, Bharat Mekala, Jeongbin Park

entry.summary: Presents Site4Drug, a modality-aware AI agent that ranks druggable target sites on proteins with explicit constraints, evidence summaries, risk flags, and decision logs, and can recommend binding modality from the same evidence. It targets the ambiguous bottleneck of choosing where to intervene, especially for membrane proteins.

entry.title: Benchmarking Local LLMs for Natural-Language-to-SQL Querying in Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing: An Empirical Benchmark on Consumer-Grade Hardware

author.name: Sagar Bhetwal, Rajan Bastakoti, Nirajan Acharya, Gaurav Kumar Gupta

entry.summary: This study benchmarks four open-source LLMs for natural-language-to-SQL in biopharmaceutical manufacturing on consumer-grade hardware, motivated by regulatory restrictions on cloud AI. It evaluates locally deployed models via a FastAPI platform on a synthetic manufacturing database.

entry.title: Do Gender Cues Affect LLM Value Trade-offs? Evidence from a Controlled Decision Benchmark

author.name: Yangyang Liu, Dong Yu, Pengyuan Liu

entry.summary: This paper builds a controlled benchmark (RVDB) to test whether gender cues in prompts alter LLM value trade-off decisions while holding all other variables fixed. It finds explicit gender cues induce systematic decision flips, exposing fairness concerns in value-sensitive settings.

entry.title: Segmentation-Guided Spatial Indexing for Generalizable and Explainable Deepfake Detection

author.name: Izaldein Al-Zyoud, Abdulmotaleb El Saddik

entry.summary: This work introduces segmentation-guided spatial indexing for deepfake detection that first selects semantically meaningful facial patch tokens (via a FaRL parser on DINOv3 features) and pools only those before classification. It improves generalization and provides structural region attribution for explainability.

entry.title: An Attribute-Based Measure of Video Complexity

author.name: Aditya Sarkar, Yi Li, Zihao Wang, Jiacheng Cheng, Sai Vidyaranya Nuthalapati, Aashu Singh, Shlok Kumar Mishra, David Jacobs, Nuno Vasconcelos

entry.summary: VideoABC proposes a non-parametric framework for estimating the complexity that video-question pairs pose to video-LLMs, defining complexity as the probability of model failure. It projects videos into a quantized space of complexity-informative attributes and computes expected complexity per cell.

entry.title: Cohort-Scale Neural Atlases of Ultrasound Video

author.name: Zhuorui Zhang, Roger Pallar\`es-L\'opez, Xuan Wu, Praneeth Namburi, Brian W. Anthony

entry.summary: This work introduces cohort-scale neural atlases for ultrasound video, registering observations across a population to a shared canonical coordinate system to amortize costly per-frame annotation. It extends neural atlas methods beyond single videos or small image sets.

entry.title: MMDG-Bench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Domain Generalization

author.name: Qianshan Zhan, Qian Wang, Da Li, Xiao-Jun Zeng, Xiatian Zhu

entry.summary: MMDG-Bench is a benchmark for multimodal domain generalization, integrating multi-modal learning and domain generalization with two frameworks (DG-then-MML and MML-then-DG) across tasks like video-audio-flow action recognition and RGB-Depth-IR face anti-spoofing. It standardizes evaluation in an under-explored intersection.

entry.title: Ask4VG: Risk-Aware Question Selection for Reducing Prior-Driven Answers in Medical VQA

author.name: Xiaorong Zhu, Qiang Li, Zibo Xu, Weijie Wang, Weizhi Nie

entry.summary: Ask4VG is a label-free framework for risk-aware question selection in medical VQA, estimating hallucination risk via counterfactual visual probing (original, perturbed, blank, mismatched images) to reduce prior-driven, visually unsupported answers. It targets grounding of medical responses in image evidence.

entry.title: HakushoBench: A Japanese Chart and Table VQA Benchmark from Governmental White Papers

author.name: Issa Sugiura, Shuhei Kurita, Yusuke Oda, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: HakushoBench is a Japanese chart and table VQA benchmark built from governmental white papers, addressing the scarcity of non-English document-understanding benchmarks by leveraging freely available naturally occurring charts. It tests whether English-centric progress generalizes across languages.

entry.title: HOLA: Holistic Multi-Modal Alignment for Open-Set 3D Recognition

author.name: Koby Aharonov, Oren Shrout, Ayellet Tal

entry.summary: HOLA is a holistic multimodal alignment method for open-set 3D recognition that aligns each point cloud with multiple images and texts (rather than a single view) via a decoupled loss separating positive aggregation from negative competition. It captures a more complete understanding of 3D objects.

entry.title: ROGLE: Robust Global-Local Alignment with Automated Region Supervision for Text-Based Person Search

author.name: Zequn Xie, Xibei Jia, Sihang Cai, Shulei Wang, Tao Jin

entry.summary: Presents ROGLE, a global-local alignment framework for text-based person search that automatically mines pseudo region-sentence pairs to overcome reliance on costly manual region annotations. Improves fine-grained alignment in CLIP-based retrieval.

entry.title: Distortion-Aware Fusion of Statistical and Vision-Language Features for Blind Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Bishr Omer Abdelrahman Adam, Xu Li

entry.summary: Proposes a distortion-aware fusion framework for blind image quality assessment that combines natural scene statistics with SigLIP and CLIP-H vision-language embeddings via a multiplicative gating mechanism learning per-input stream weights. Explores complementarity of classical and modern features.

entry.title: Training-Free Composed Video Retrieval via Visual Representation-Guided Video-LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yang Liu, Qianqian Xu, Peisong Wen, Siran Dai, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Develops a training-free composed video retrieval framework for the CVPR 2026 challenge that uses frozen DINOv3 to obtain visually relevant candidates then applies video-LLMs to evaluate whether each satisfies a modification instruction. Combines visual filtering with reasoning-based reranking.

entry.title: Hierarchical Semantic-Augmented Navigation: Optimal Transport and Graph-Driven Reasoning for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Changshuo Wang

entry.summary: HSAN combines hierarchical semantic scene graphs, optimal transport, and graph reasoning for vision-language navigation in continuous environments. Targets long-horizon navigation with multi-level environmental representations.

entry.title: Linear Motility Maps in Nonlinear Viscous Fluids

author.name: Yishun Zhou, Shai Revzen

entry.summary: Shows that linear-in-velocity motility maps extend to power-law (Ostwald-de Waele) viscous fluids, extending Purcell's Scallop Theorem, while Carreau-Yasuda fluids can violate this property to enable net displacement. Theoretical result for low-Reynolds-number locomotion.

entry.title: PHASOR: Phase-Anchored Universal Action Representations for Humanoid Embodiments

author.name: Kihyun Kim, Chaeyun Kim, Jongho Shin, Taeyoun Kwon, Junghyun Kim, Mijin Koo, Haon Park

entry.summary: PHASOR proposes treating the action embedding space as a first-class design target for humanoid robot policies, factorizing motion into a phase manifold capturing cyclic structure via FFT coefficients plus a pose branch. The aim is more interpretable, transferable action representations across embodiments.

entry.title: Towards Precise Intent-Aligned VLA Aerial Navigation via Expert-Guided GRPO

author.name: Tianyang Chen, Wenjun Li, Xin zhou, Yuze Wu, Fei Gao

entry.summary: This work applies expert-guided GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning to VLA-based UAV aerial navigation, addressing inefficient exploration in large continuous spaces and weak supervision of human intent. It aims for precise intent-aligned navigation beyond standard supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: A Machine-to-Machine Knowledge-Guided LLM Agent for Generalizable Radiotherapy Treatment Planning

author.name: Md Mainul Abrar, Xun Jia, Yujie Chi

entry.summary: This work proposes a machine-to-machine knowledge-guided LLM framework for automated radiotherapy treatment planning, transferring deep RL-derived parameter distribution knowledge to an LLM agent via in-context learning. The DRL guidance constrains the LLM to physically valid plans, enabling autonomous iterative planning.

entry.title: FlowSDR: Sufficient Dimension Reduction via Conditional Normalizing Flows

author.name: Yuexiao Dong, Kenichiro Mcalinn, Edoardo Airoldi, Lei Li

entry.summary: FlowSDR proposes a likelihood-based sufficient dimension reduction framework that jointly learns the projection and conditional density using monotone rational-quadratic spline normalizing flows. It is Fisher consistent and admits a mutual-information interpretation.

entry.title: NYT: Senator Sanders Proposes Gov't Take 50% Ownership of AI Labs

author.name: Julian Bradshaw

entry.summary: A news post summarizing Senator Bernie Sanders's NYT op-ed proposing the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, which would impose a one-time 50 percent stock tax to give the public ownership and board representation in major AI labs. It covers a significant AI policy proposal.

entry.title: Evaluating Bivariate Causal Statements Based on Mutual Compatibility

author.name: Erik Jahn, Dominik Janzing

entry.summary: This work develops methods to evaluate collections of bivariate causal statements for mutual compatibility, introducing a compatibility score that flags implausible induced models requiring excessive confounding, without relying on the faithfulness assumption. It also defines an incompatibility score for purely graphical statements.

entry.title: From "Weak" Signals to Strong Models: Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA Merging

author.name: Qi Sun, Siyue Zhang, Yulin Chen, Yuxiang Xue, Ru Peng, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: Preference Delta Aggregation derives a preference delta from each weak-weaker model pair, instantiates it as a LoRA adapter via preference optimization, and merges adapters to improve stronger models. It explores whether multiple weak supervision signals can be constructively aggregated.

entry.title: SDR: Set-Distance Rewards for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Halil Ibrahim Gulluk, Max Van Puyvelde, Wim Van Criekinge, Olivier Gevaert

entry.summary: SDR introduces set-to-set distance rewards for radiology report generation, embedding report sentences as unordered sets and using permutation-invariant distances as continuous RLVR rewards. This fits the unordered, orthogonal nature of radiology findings better than exact-match or step-level rewards.

entry.title: Certificate-Guided Evaluation of Reinforcement Learning Generalization

author.name: Vignesh Subramanian, {\DJ}or{\dj}e \v{Z}ikeli\'c, Suguman Bansal

entry.summary: This work presents a logic-driven framework to evaluate RL generalization on families of inductive reach-avoid tasks, introducing a neural certificate function that validates generated trajectories by enforcing key conditions. The certification rate serves as a litmus test for generalization across continuous environments.

entry.title: Dive into Ambiguity: A*-Inspired Multi-Agents Commonsense Obfuscation Attack on LLM Prompts

author.name: Boxuan Wang, Zhuoyun Li, Xiaowei Huang, Yi Dong

entry.summary: This work proposes an A*-inspired multi-agent factual error induction framework that generates semantically aligned yet obfuscated prompts to trigger commonsense hallucinations in LLMs, using a hierarchical rewrite strategy with a dynamic semantic dispersion coefficient. It targets adversarial robustness in safety-critical settings.

entry.title: Physically-Constrained Mamba-SDE for Remaining Useful Life Prediction under Irregular Observations

author.name: Deyu Zhuang, Peiliang Gong, Yang Shao, Liyuan Shu, Qi Zhu, Xiaoli Li, Daoqiang Zhang

entry.summary: PC-MambaSDE is a physically-constrained continuous-time framework for remaining useful life prediction under irregular sensor observations, combining a mask-aware continuous Mamba encoder with stochastic differential equations to enforce irreversible degradation. It handles asynchronous sampling, burst missingness, and temporal jitter.

entry.title: Algorithmic algorithm development with LLMs: A Case Study on LLM-Usage for Contraction Order Optimization in Tensor Networks

author.name: Fabian Hoppe, Melven R\"ohrig-Z\"ollner, Philipp Knechtges

entry.summary: This case study examines LLM-based algorithm development for tensor-network contraction-order optimization using the OpenEvolve verifier-guided evolutionary coding agent, focusing on LLM choice, evaluation metrics, and test instances. It highlights both the promise of such agents and the continuing need for human evaluation and interpretation.

entry.title: Bridging the Last Mile of Time Series Forecasting with LLM Agents

author.name: Yuhua Liao, Zetian Wang, Qiangqiang Nie, Zhenhua Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates the last-mile forecasting problem of revising statistical forecasts using weakly structured business context (holidays, campaigns, expert feedback) and presents an LLM-agent framework sitting atop a forecasting backbone. Addresses an underexplored but practically critical stage.

entry.title: Business Utility of Large Language Models as Exploratory Data Analysis Agents

author.name: Rafa{\l} {\L}ab\k{e}dzki, Patryk Miziu{\l}a, Hubert Rutkowski, Szymon Betlewski, Cezary Depta, Szymon Janowski, Jaros{\l}aw Kochanowicz, Jan Kanty Milczek

entry.summary: Evaluates LLMs as exploratory data analysis agents in business settings via an agent-based supply chain simulation benchmark, assessing not just average performance but repeatability across fifteen model-variant configurations. Emphasizes that deployable EDA agents need trustworthy repeatability.

entry.title: CLSP-REQA: A Real-Time Quality-Aware Closed-Loop Seizure Prediction Framework with Mamba-BiLSTM and Confidence-Gated Intervention

author.name: Mufeng Chen, Qi Wu, Bingchao Huang, Xiwen Lai, Zekai Chen, Xinge Ouyang, Quansheng Ren

entry.summary: CLSP-REQA is a closed-loop seizure prediction framework embedding a lightweight real-time EEG quality estimator alongside a Mamba-BiLSTM backbone, modulating output confidence via tiered fusion to account for signal quality variability and using strict evaluation protocols. Targets reliable closed-loop neurostimulation.

entry.title: Structured Visual Evidence Decomposition for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Screening of Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome

author.name: Chen Zhan, Yingchen Wei, Xiaoyu Tan, Jingjing Huang, Xihe Qiu

entry.summary: EviOSAHS is an evidence-grounded multimodal framework for pre-polysomnography obstructive sleep apnea screening that decomposes facial images into seven fixed anatomical queries, converting visual responses into structured evidence cards before clinical adjudication. Separates evidence acquisition from final decision to improve calibration.

entry.title: A Protocol-Language Model for Network Intrusion (Without Deep Packet Inspection)

author.name: Vivek Kumar Sharma

entry.summary: Presents PLM-NIDS, treating network flows as a language whose grammar lives in L3/L4 packet metadata (length, timing, TTL, flags, ports), avoiding deep packet inspection on encrypted TLS 1.3/QUIC traffic. A RWKV-4 state-space model learns the flow grammar with low validation loss.

entry.title: Hyperbolic and Evidence-Prioritized Experts for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zijie Zhou, Dandan Zhu, Hangxiangpan Wang, Heng Zhang, Huishen Jiao, Yi Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes hyperbolic and evidence-prioritized experts for large vision-language models, arguing existing Mixture-of-Experts approaches wrongly treat vision and language symmetrically. It uses hyperbolic expert space to encode hierarchical containment relationships between text queries and visual scenes.

entry.title: CAFOSat: A Strongly Annotated Dataset for Infrastructure-Aware CAFO Mapping Using High-Resolution Imagery

author.name: Oishee Bintey Hoque, Nibir Chandra Mandal, Mandy L Wilson, Samarth Swarup, Madhav Marathe, Abhijin Adiga

entry.summary: CAFOSat is a strongly annotated, infrastructure-aware dataset for mapping concentrated animal feeding operations across the US, combining high-resolution NAIP imagery with multi-source inventories refined via human-in-the-loop annotation. It supports environmental and public health surveillance.

entry.title: A Fiber Criterion for Representation Identifiability in Supervised Learning

author.name: Vasileios Sevetlidis

entry.summary: Formalizes representation-level identifiability in supervised learning, characterizing when a representation property is identifiable from the predictor as exactly when it is constant on fibers of the head-composition projection. Provides theoretical conditions and augmentation-based obstructions.

entry.title: GC-MoE: Genomics-Guided Cell-Type-Specific Mixture of Experts for Histology-Based Single-Cell Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Kaito Shiku, Ahtisham Fazeel Abbasi, Ryoma Bise, Yuichiro Iwashita, Kazuya Nishimura, Andreas Dengel, Muhammad Nabeel Asim

entry.summary: Proposes GC-MoE, a genomics-guided cell-type-specific mixture-of-experts model that predicts single-cell gene expression from histopathology images by routing to cell-type-specific experts. Targets cell-to-cell expression variability beyond spot-level prediction.

entry.title: UME: A Unified Meta-Generalization Framework for Cross-Domain ETA

author.name: Duo Wang, Qiong Wu, Jianguo Wu, Ruiyu Xu, Jinhui Yi, Zhonggen Sun, Zhentao Zhang, Yu Zhang, Ke Xing, Yongjun Yin, Zishuo Li, Jianwen Huang

entry.summary: Presents UME, a unified meta-generalization framework for cross-domain estimated-time-of-arrival prediction that handles zero-shot prediction to unseen domains and inconsistent feature spaces in international delivery platforms. Addresses cold-start and feature-space mismatch.

entry.title: Task-Induced Representational Invariances Depend on Learning Objective in Deep RL

author.name: Manu Srinath Halvagal, Sebastian Lee, SueYeon Chung

entry.summary: This work analyzes deep RL representations through MDP reduction theory, finding value-based DQN learns invariances different from those of other objectives even at comparable performance. It connects learned representations to neuroscience models of goal-directed behavior.

entry.title: A combination of noise and bilateral filters achieve supralinear and scalable adversarial robustness in CNNs

author.name: Nicolas Stalder, Benjamin F. Grewe, Matteo Saponati, Pau Vilimelis Aceituno

entry.summary: This work theoretically shows that gaussian noise and bilateral filtering enhance CNN adversarial robustness through complementary mechanisms, yielding supralinear robustness when combined. It offers a scalable alternative to computationally intensive adversarial training.

entry.title: Query-Limited Community Recovery in Stochastic Block Models

author.name: Sabyasachi Basu, Manuj Mukherjee, Lutz Oettershagen, Suhas Thejaswi

entry.summary: Studies exact two-community recovery in stochastic block models under limited, noisy neighborhood-oracle queries with finite budgets, giving sharp non-adaptive benchmarks for balanced querying. It also considers combined oracle-plus-subsampled-graph access.

entry.title: Disentanglement-Based Equivariant Learning for Compositional VQA

author.name: Zhou Du, Zhaoquan Yuan, Xiao Wu, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: Introduces DEAL, a disentanglement-based equivariant learning framework for compositional visual question answering, guided only by ground-truth answers using causality-inspired interventions to capture compositional variation. It avoids additional training clues required by prior state-of-the-art.

entry.title: Towards Automated Discovery: A Review of Generative Models, Multimodal Learning and Closed-Loop Workflows in Inverse Materials Design

author.name: Anand Babu, Rog\'erio Almeida Gouv\^ea, Gian-Marco Rignanese

entry.summary: A review surveying generative crystal-structure models (VAEs, flows, autoregressive, diffusion), multimodal learning, and closed-loop pipelines for inverse materials design, emphasizing how physical constraints and feasibility are enforced. It maps the state of automated materials discovery.

entry.title: Where to Refine, When to Stop: Rethinking Redundancy via Latent Discrepancy for Efficient Visual Autoregressive Generation

author.name: Changwang Mei, Peisong Wang, Zekun Li, Changsheng Li, Shuang Qiu, Qinghao Hu, Gang Li, Yifan Zhang, Zhihui Wei, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: This work introduces Latent Discrepancy, a unified metric for identifying redundant computation in visual autoregressive models by measuring token contribution to pixel-space generation rather than relying on heuristic layer features. It accelerates high-resolution VAR inference with better redundancy identification.

entry.title: FiSeR: Fine-Grained Source Representations for Cross-Domain AI Image Detection

author.name: Shan Zhang, Yongxin He, Mingming Zhang, Huiwen Tian, Lei Ma

entry.summary: FiSeR proposes a hierarchical contrastive learning framework for cross-domain AI-generated image detection that improves natural-versus-synthetic separability while preserving generator identity information. It is motivated by the finding that classification heads overfit to training-domain artifacts despite features remaining partially separable.

entry.title: One Channel to Rule Them All: Rethinking Input Representation for Visual Place Recognition

author.name: Timur Ismagilov, Shakaiba Majeed, Michael Milford, Tan Viet Tuyen Nguyen, Sarvapali D. Ramchurn, Shoaib Ehsan

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that RGB color is necessary for visual place recognition, finding that grayscale matches or outperforms RGB under severe appearance shifts while color helps only with persistent discriminative chromatic cues. A gray-trained MixVPR model achieves strong recall.

entry.title: Flexible Control of 3D CT Generation via Text and Semantically-Defined Segmentation Prompts

author.name: Weicheng Dai, Chenyu Wang, Andy Li, Shantanu Ghosh, Kayhan Batmanghelich

entry.summary: This work proposes flexible multimodal control for 3D CT generation, combining text prompts with semantically-defined partial segmentation prompts to provide spatial control without requiring full-organ annotations. It balances flexibility and spatial precision for volumetric medical synthesis.

entry.title: PAI-Studio: Cinematic Video Background Replacement with Camera-Aware Motion

author.name: Heyuan Gao, Bangxun Tang, Yiren Song, Guian Fang, Zijian He, Jie Yang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: PAI-Studio introduces a reference-conditioned cinematic video background replacement task that generates dynamic backgrounds aligned with foreground motion while preserving foreground identity and achieving consistent illumination with realistic relighting. It builds on a Diffusion Transformer video backbone.

entry.title: PathAR: Structure-First Autoregressive Synthesis of Multimodal Pathology Images

author.name: Yuan Zhang, Jiahao Xia, Junzhang Huang, Meng Wang, Feng Chen, Guanyu Yang, Huazhu Fu

entry.summary: PathAR is a structure-first autoregressive framework for synthesizing multimodal pathology images that explicitly factorizes morphological structure from modality-specific appearance, improving structural controllability under modality shifts. It addresses data scarcity in multimodal pathology.

entry.title: Turing Patterns for Multimedia: Reaction-Diffusion Multi-Modal Fusion for Language-Guided Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Wei Ji, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: RDMF reimagines language-guided video moment retrieval as a Turing-inspired reaction-diffusion process, where video features diffuse across time and react with textual semantics to model dynamic, non-linear cross-modal interactions. It departs from static cross-attention or prompt-tuning.

entry.title: 3rd Place at CVPR 2026 CASTLE Challenge: Agentic Multi-View Long-Context Video Understanding via Hierarchical Knowledge Graph Retrieval

author.name: Raghad Albusayes, Munirah Alyahya

entry.summary: Describes a third-place CVPR 2026 CASTLE Challenge solution for multi-view long-context video understanding using a training-free agentic framework with hierarchical knowledge graph retrieval. Handles 600+ hours of synchronized ego/exo footage for complex spatiotemporal questions.

entry.title: Vision-language Models for Driver Monitoring Systems: A Driver Activity Description Dataset

author.name: David J. Lerch, Sarath Mulugurthi, Manuel Martin, Frederik Diederichs, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: Creates a detailed natural-language description version of the Drive&Act dataset and benchmarks three VLMs on fine-grained driver activity description, showing current VLMs fail at subtle distinctions. Trains VLMs on the new description dataset with cross-dataset evaluation.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Dead Tree Detection via Knowledge Distillation in Aerial Imagery

author.name: Anis Ur Rahman, Mete Ahishali, Einari Heinaro, Samuli Junttila

entry.summary: Advances dead-tree detection in aerial imagery via knowledge distillation, adapting a model trained on Finnish data to Polish, German, and Estonian forest domains. Evaluates four KD variants against a fine-tuning baseline using tree-level IoU and F1 metrics.

entry.title: Question-Aware Evidence Ledgers for Video Relational Reasoning

author.name: Yilin Ou, Mengshi Qi, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: Presents a test-time reasoning pipeline for video relational reasoning (VRR-QA challenge) built around a GPT-5.5 video QA solver augmented with question-aware evidence ledgers that make targets, counts, reference frames, and temporal/spatial scope explicit. Uses external tools like detection and depth only when needed.

entry.title: NDPP-Grasp: Non-Differentiable Physical Plausibility Constraint-Guided Task-Oriented Dexterous Grasp Generation

author.name: Qiuchi Xiang, Haoxuan Qu, Hossein Rahmani, Jun Liu

entry.summary: NDPP-Grasp generates task-oriented dexterous grasps by injecting non-differentiable physical plausibility constraints directly into the diffusion generation trajectory, rather than relying on after-the-fact refinement. This produces grasps that are both functionally suitable and physically valid.

entry.title: Continuous Data Assimilation with Learned Surrogate Dynamics

author.name: Wenwen Li, Daniel Sanz-Alonso

entry.summary: This paper develops a finite-dimensional analysis of nudging-based continuous data assimilation that uses learned surrogate models of unknown dynamics. It establishes conditions guaranteeing accurate state tracking under model error in both noise-free and noisy settings.

entry.title: Agents on a Tree: Pathwise Coordination for Multi-Objective Molecular Optimization

author.name: Jia Zhang, Tengfei Ma, Tianle Li, Daojian Zeng, Xieping Gao, Xiangxiang Zeng

entry.summary: ATOM formulates multi-objective molecular optimization as a tree-structured multi-agent search where each node hosts an agent specialized for an objective and agents coordinate along paths rather than enforcing global consensus. This preserves diverse trade-off trajectories in vast chemical spaces.

entry.title: TIGER: Traceable Inference with Graph-Based Evidence Routing for Mitigating Hallucinations in Multimodal Generation

author.name: Kaixiang Zhao, Tianrun Yu, Shawn Huang, Porter Jenkins, Yushun Dong, Amanda Hughes

entry.summary: TIGER is an inference-time framework that mitigates hallucination in multimodal generation by independently extracting an observation graph from the input and a claim graph from the output, then assigning each claim a graph-conditioned risk score for localized fact-level repair. It avoids hallucinated claims biasing input interpretation.

entry.title: TAPS: Target-Aware Prefix Tree Selection for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding

author.name: Zhuoyu Wang, Junnan Huang, Xinyu Chen

entry.summary: TAPS proposes target-aware prefix-tree selection for diffusion-drafted speculative decoding, addressing that existing methods rank draft-tree nodes by marginal probability and waste verification on unreachable descendants of rejected prefixes. It conditions ranking on prefix reachability to improve acceptance per latency.

entry.title: Efficient Test-time Inference for Generative Planning Models

author.name: Robert Gieselmann, Mihai Samson, Federico Pecora, Jeremy L. Wyatt

entry.summary: This paper shows that a modified classical Open-Closed List search provides an efficient inference procedure for generative planning models, synergizing a learned generative rollout model with a learned heuristic for path prioritization. It offers a more efficient alternative to brute-force test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: Regularized Offline Policy Optimization with Posterior Hybrid Bayesian Belief

author.name: Hongqiang Lin, Pengfei Wang, Nenggan Zheng

entry.summary: This paper presents a regularized offline RL method using a posterior hybrid Bayesian belief over dynamics to unify sample-level and model-level epistemic uncertainty quantification. It addresses the computational intractability of policy optimization in Bayesian offline RL.

entry.title: Decoupled Behavioral Cloning for Scalable Inductive Generalization in RL from Specifications

author.name: Vignesh Subramanian, Subhajit Roy, Suguman Bansal

entry.summary: DIBS proposes a decoupled behavioral cloning approach for inductive generalization in RL from specifications, separating learning task-specific teacher policies from learning the policy-evolution function via behavioral cloning. It addresses poor training scalability when aggregated reward feedback becomes noisy across many tasks.

entry.title: AnyEdit++: Adaptive Long-Form Knowledge Editing via Bayesian Surprise

author.name: Bowen Tian, Caixue He, Jiemin Wu, Jingying Wang, Wenshuo Chen, Zexi Li, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: AnyEdit++ is a structure-aware long-form knowledge editing framework with Bayes-Chunk, an adaptive segmentation mechanism that identifies semantic boundaries via Bayesian surprise rather than fixed-window chunking. It is backed by theory on structural independence requiring orthogonal anchor keys to minimize cross-segment interference.

entry.title: "Skill issues'': data-centric optimization of lakehouse agents

author.name: Nicole Rose Schneider, Davide Ghilardi, Giacomo Piccinini, Jacopo Tagliabue

entry.summary: This work studies data-centric optimization of skill and environment files for coding agents operating on a branching lakehouse, reframing data-agent evaluation as a state-verification rather than output-matching problem. It presents a pipeline generating task-verifier pairs through executable lakehouse changes.

entry.title: Brain-Atlas-Guided Generative Counterfactual Attention for Explainable Cognitive Decline Diagnosis Using Multimodal Connectomes

author.name: Xiongri Shen, Jiaqi Wang, Zhenxi Song, Yi Zhong, Leilei Zhao, Xin He, Baiying Lei, Zhiguo Zhang

entry.summary: GCAN is an atlas-knowledge-guided generative counterfactual attention network for explainable diagnosis of cognitive decline using multimodal brain connectomes, framing diagnosis as source-to-target counterfactual generation. It aims to improve both classification and interpretability of connectivity changes.

entry.title: FlowTime: Towards Continuous Generative Watch Time Prediction via Flow-based Personalized Priors

author.name: Hongxu Ma, Han Zhou, Chenghou Jin, Jie Zhang, Xiaoyu Yang, Chunjie Chen, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: FlowTime introduces a flow-based generative approach with personalized priors for continuous watch-time prediction in short-video recommenders, addressing mean-collapse, quantization, and latency limitations of existing paradigms. It revisits the problem from a causal perspective to capture multimodal interaction patterns.

entry.title: TERRA: Task-Embedded Reasoning and Representation Architecture for Cross-Domain Applications

author.name: Shayan Shokri

entry.summary: TERRA studies transfer of action-conditioned latent predictive representations across structurally analogous but unrelated domains such as driving scenes, robot workspaces, and financial order books. It gives a formal treatment of when representations or predictors learned in one structured-state domain carry over to another.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Adaptive Propagation for Protein-Protein Interaction Site Prediction

author.name: Enqiang Zhu, Yizi Liu, Yilong Luo, Yao Chen, Yu Zhang, Baoshan Ma

entry.summary: SGAP-PPIS is a structure-guided adaptive propagation model for protein-protein interaction site prediction that adapts information diffusion to local geometric environments rather than using fixed propagation schemes. It aims to distinguish true interaction sites from structurally similar non-interacting neighbors.

entry.title: Bayesian Spectral Emotion Transition Discovery from Multi-Annotator Disagreement

author.name: Keito Inoshita, Takato Ueno

entry.summary: BSETD is a two-stage Bayesian framework that discovers emotion-transition structure from multi-rater soft labels, using a hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial posterior built from outer products of soft labels to retain annotator-disagreement uncertainty. It avoids discarding the uncertainty lost by majority-vote hard labels.

entry.title: BADGER: Bridging Agentic and Deterministic Evaluation for Generative Enterprise Reasoning

author.name: Shannon Serrao, Soumitra Chatterjee, Dorina Strori, Abhishek Sharma, Nathan Miller

entry.summary: BADGER is a unified evaluation framework from Merkle integrating text-to-SQL assessment with agentic behavior evaluation into a production-grade pipeline calibrated against human expert judgment. It bridges execution-accuracy protocols and LLM-based assessment for enterprise reasoning.

entry.title: An Abstract Worlds Semantic Framework for Belief Change Operators

author.name: Daniel Grimaldi, M. Vanina Martinez, Ricardo O. Rodriguez

entry.summary: This paper proposes Abstract Worlds Semantics, a syntax-free set-theoretic framework for belief change inspired by Grove, treating worlds as primitive elements with world contraction and revision operators. It unifies classical and non-prioritized belief change models including AGM, KM, and Multiple Change.

entry.title: CSRP: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Chinese Text Correction via Reinforcement Learning with Efficiency-Aware Rewards

author.name: Wei Tian, Yuhao Zhou, Man Lan

entry.summary: CSRP is a three-stage framework for Chinese grammatical error correction combining continual pretraining, chain-of-thought SFT with explicit error reasoning, and GRPO with an efficiency-aware reward that penalizes unnecessary edits to reduce over-correction. Builds correction capability progressively.

entry.title: Update Opacity: Epistemic Accessibility and Governance Under AI System Change

author.name: Andrea Ferrario, Joshua Hatherley

entry.summary: Frames update opacity (users unable to understand why the same input now yields different outputs after model updates) as a diachronic failure of epistemic accessibility and a governance problem requiring selective disclosure. Argues against disclosing every update due to overload.

entry.title: Can Predicted Dynamics Exist in the Physical World?

author.name: Barak Or

entry.summary: Formulates physical admissibility as a prediction-control interface, arguing low RMSE does not guarantee physical executability, and evaluates decoded proposals against kinematic, dynamic, and horizon conditions to flag violations with component-level reasons. Demonstrated on the LeRobot PushT task.

entry.title: PEACE: A Planner-Executor Agent with Constraint Enforcement for UAVs

author.name: Erdem Uysal, Timo Kehrer, Sebastiano Panichella

entry.summary: Proposes PEACE, a planner-executor agent for PX4 drones that uses an LLM for single-pass mission planning while delegating low-level control to a structured ROS 2 tool-calling interface, reducing latency and hallucination risk. It builds a world model from modular detectors and depth projection for constrained UAV autonomy.

entry.title: Versatile Framework with Semantic and Structural guidance for Image Reconstruction from Brain Activity

author.name: Yizhuo Lu, Changde Du, Qiongyi Zhou, Liuyun Jiang, Huiguang He

entry.summary: Presents a framework for reconstructing visual stimuli from brain activity with both semantic and structural guidance, addressing prior methods' failure to preserve fine-grained spatial details like position and orientation. It improves controllability and interpretability of brain decoding.

entry.title: MyoSem: Aligning Electromyography to Natural-Language Action Semantics for Hand Action Understanding

author.name: Chiyue Wang, Dong She, Yang Gao, Zhanpeng Jin

entry.summary: Presents MyoSem, an EMG-to-action semantic alignment framework mapping low-level EMG signals into a shared semantic space built from multi-view action descriptions, enabling bidirectional EMG-text retrieval. It moves beyond fixed-label classification toward generalizable hand action understanding.

entry.title: Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems

author.name: Xiangyu Wang, Yawen He, Shivendra Pratap Singh, Han Huang, Mengtong Hu, Sharath Ciddu, Yi-Hsuan Hsieh, Erik Groving, Yi Ding, Jieming Di, Tony Wang, Min Yun, Xiaoyu Chen, Ling Leng, Rob Malkin

entry.summary: Introduces SCALR, a framework generating synthetic cross-domain user-item interaction events for large-scale recommendation, inspired by LLM synthetic data success. It decomposes cross-domain learning into translating source-domain events into a target domain to address sparsity and noisy feedback.

entry.title: Isolating LLM Lexical Bias: A Curation-Free Triangulated Metric for Preference-Stage Learning

author.name: Xiaoyang Ming, Jose Hernandez, Thomas Stephan Juzek

entry.summary: Proposes a curation-free triangulated metric to isolate LLM lexical bias introduced during preference-learning stages like RLHF, such as overuse of words like delve and furthermore. It addresses the reliance of prior research on manual curation to study preference-induced lexical misalignment.

entry.title: Short-form Text Rewriting with Phi Silica

author.name: Divya Tadimeti, Shawn Pan, Sameera Lanka, Chenghui Zhou, Sadid Hasan

entry.summary: This empirical study adapts the small Phi Silica model for short-form text rewriting via dataset curation, prompt distillation, and PEFT, using GPT-5-chat for supervision and judging. It shows fine-tuning improves semantic fidelity and hallucination robustness in this constrained setting.

entry.title: Dynamic Coordination Strategy Selection for Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Thanh Luong Tuan

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether enterprise multi-agent coordination strategy (consensus, debate, synthesis, or single-agent) should be selected dynamically by problem class, running a frozen matrix of enterprise tasks across multiple model arms. It finds a bounded but operationally useful result rather than the strong original hypothesis.

entry.title: RefDiffNet: Learning to Expose Subtle PCB Defects Before Detection

author.name: Vinay Edula, Nilesh Badwe, Priyanka Bagade

entry.summary: RefDiffNet is a lightweight plug-and-play input enhancement block that uses an aligned defect-free reference image to expose subtle PCB defects before detection, reviving a classical inspection idea in the deep learning era. It enhances images prior to the detector backbone.

entry.title: Temporally-Aligned Evaluation for Audio-Driven Talking Head Generation

author.name: Zhicheng Zhang, Lei Wang, Yu Zhang, Yongsheng Gao

entry.summary: Argues that audio-driven talking-head generation should be evaluated as a sequence-alignment problem rather than frame-wise comparison, since speech-driven motion has natural timing variations. Introduces a temporally-aligned evaluation reformulation.

entry.title: DiffuSent: Towards a Unified Diffusion Framework for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Shu Long, Yanglei Gan, Xuchuan Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes DiffuSent, a non-autoregressive diffusion framework that unifies all seven aspect-based sentiment analysis subtasks as boundary denoising diffusion processes with contrastive denoising training. Addresses boundary insensitivity in multi-word aspect and opinion terms.

entry.title: GJDNet: Robust Graph Neural Networks via Joint Disentangled Learning Against Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Canyixing Cui, Tao Wu, Xingping Xian, Xiao-Ke Xu, Mao Wang, Weina Niu

entry.summary: GJDNet defends graph neural networks against adversarial attacks by jointly disentangling node representations and decision spaces, targeting structure-feature mismatches caused by adversarial edge perturbations. It moves beyond fixed assortativity assumptions in prior defenses.

entry.title: Time-Aware Diffusion based on Preference Disentanglement for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Bangguo Zhu, Peng Huo, Yuanbo Zhao, Zhicheng Du, Jun Yin, Senzhang Wang

entry.summary: TDPM proposes time-aware diffusion with preference disentanglement for generative recommendation, addressing the limitation that diffusion processes apply uniformly across historical interactions. It models non-stationary, time-evolving user preferences over semantic indices.

entry.title: Breaking the Information Silo: Semantic Personas for Cross-Domain Recommendation

author.name: Jonathan Mayo, Moshe Unger, Konstantin Bauman

entry.summary: SPHERE enables cross-domain recommendation across strictly disjoint domains with no shared users or items by using semantic personas rather than identity or graph structure alignment. It overcomes the information-silo limitation of platforms.

entry.title: Boosting Multimodal Federated Learning via Chained Modality Optimization

author.name: Zixin Zhang, Fan Qi, Shuai Li, Xiaoshan Yang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: FedMChain restructures multimodal federated learning as a chain of modality-wise phases to mitigate modality competition where dominant modalities suppress weaker ones. Each modality gets a dedicated optimization window with cross-modal error compensation.

entry.title: RadioMaster: Multi-Agent System for Autonomous Radio Signal Generation

author.name: Jiazhen Lei, Tianze Cao, Yuxin Sha, Sihan Wang, Bingbing Wang, Fengyuan Zhu, Zeming Yang, Xiaohua Tian

entry.summary: RadioMaster is a multi-agent system for autonomous radio signal generation, translating user intents into physical-layer signals. It addresses LLMs' domain ignorance and insensitivity to hardware constraints in wireless prototyping.

entry.title: Echo: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Speaker Diarization and Speech Recognition in a Shared Latent Space

author.name: Louis Mouchon

entry.summary: Echo is a proof-of-concept audio system built around a single 25M-parameter ViT encoder pretrained with a JEPA objective, carrying speaker identity, phonetic content, and source routing in one shared latent space. It handles diarization and source separation with light heads and no per-task fine-tuning.

entry.title: Repurposing Adversarial Perturbations for Continual Learning: From Defense to Active Alignment

author.name: Ran Liu, Min Yu, Mingqi Liu, Jianguo Jiang, Gang Li, Rongsheng Li, Ning Li, Zhen Xu, Weiqing Huang, Ming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AdvCL, which repurposes adversarial perturbations as a geometric control signal for stable continual learning in LLMs via three plug-in modules promoting local smoothness, preventing over-alignment, and aligning toward prior-task prototypes. Reports gains in both performance and robustness.

entry.title: ODTQA-FoRe: An Open-Domain Tabular Question Answering Dataset for Future Data Forecasting and Reasoning

author.name: Zhensheng Wang, Xiaole Liu, Wenmian Yang, Kun Zhou, Yiquan Zhang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: Introduces a new open-domain tabular QA task for future data forecasting and reasoning, with a real-estate dataset, plus TimeFore, an LLM-agent framework with Retriever, Forecaster, and reasoning roles. Targets future-oriented numerical prediction beyond retrieval-style table QA.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Multi-Task Graph Transformer for Trip-Level Transit Prediction

author.name: Oluwaleke Yusuf, Adil Rasheed, Frank Lindseth

entry.summary: Proposes SMT-GraphFormer, a spatiotemporal multi-task graph transformer that frames trip-level transit prediction as sequence-to-sequence boarding/alighting forecasting with delay and dwell as auxiliary tasks. Aims to capture within-trip evolution and network context.

entry.title: Conditioned free-energy density of proteins using unbalanced solutions to constraint satisfaction problems

author.name: Pratik Worah, Subhash Khot, Srinivasa Varadhan

entry.summary: This paper reduces the computation of free-energy for conditioned Curie-Weiss spin Hamiltonians to an unbalanced norm computation, designing a polynomial-time SDP algorithm with bounds. Applied to Ubiquitin, it explores backbone conformations and identifies flexible protein regions.

entry.title: Genotype-Conditioned Molecular Generation via Evidence-Grounded Multi-Objective Latent Perturbation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Brenda Nogueira, Gisela A. Gonzalez-Montiel, Nitesh V. Chawla, Nuno Moniz

entry.summary: This work optimizes a pretrained genotype-to-drug diffusion model via learnable latent perturbations to maximize a composite reward combining drug sensitivity, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility. It targets personalized anticancer drug generation conditioned on cancer genotypes.

entry.title: Fast Generalization after Interpolation via Critically Damped Momentum Optimization

author.name: Luca Muscarnera, Silas Ruhrberg Est\'evez, Yuanzhang Xiao, Mihaela Van der Schaar

entry.summary: GROKtimizer is a biphasic optimization schedule combining rapid convergence to interpolation with subsequent complexity minimization, motivated by two-regime risk minimization theory. It targets fast generalization in high-dimensional low-sample regimes.

entry.title: When Tabular Foundation Models Transfer Across Modalities: A Systematic Evaluation Across 95 Datasets, 7 Modalities, and Two Regimes

author.name: Julien Lafrance

entry.summary: This work systematically evaluates a single classification pipeline combining ETF preprocessing with a tabular foundation model for in-context inference across 95 datasets, 7 modalities, and two regimes. It carefully fixes the comparison against strong lightweight tuned baselines on the same frozen features.

entry.title: BlockGen: Flexible Blockwise Sequence Modeling with Hybrid Samplers

author.name: Justin Deschenaux, Caglar Gulcehre

entry.summary: BlockGen explores blockwise sequence modeling with hybrid samplers, investigating whether uniform-state diffusion models outperform masked diffusion when tokens are generated blockwise rather than full-sequence, with informed correctors targeting likely-wrong tokens. It addresses open questions about discrete diffusion paradigms.

entry.title: Entropy Minimization without Model Collapse: Mitigating Prediction Bias in Medical Imaging

author.name: Tim Nielen, Sameer Ambekar, Johannes Kiechle, Daniel M. Lang, Julia A. Schnabel

entry.summary: This work explains entropy minimization's model-collapse failure in test-time adaptation as distribution shifts merging class feature clusters while the decision boundary stays fixed, creating prediction bias. It shows EM amplifies this bias and proposes a mitigation for medical imaging.

entry.title: Guidance for Low-Level Perceptual Editing in Unconditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Shreyansh Modi, Akshat Tomar, Aarush Aggarwal

entry.summary: Presents a training-free framework for global low-level perceptual and aesthetic editing in unconditional diffusion models, using degradation concept vectors and bottleneck patching with classifier-free guidance. Addresses failure of standard h-space patching for global transformations.

entry.title: Statistical Testing on Directed Graphs by Surrogate Data Generation

author.name: Chun Hei Michael Chan, Alexandre Cionca, Dimitri Van De Ville

entry.summary: Extends surrogate-data-based non-parametric hypothesis testing from undirected to directed graphs by revisiting stationary graph signals via eigendecomposition of the directed graph shift operator. Enables statistical testing on directed graph signals.

entry.title: Efficient Approximation for Encoder--Decoder Neural Operators via Variation Spaces

author.name: Jia-Qi Yang, Lei Shi

entry.summary: Develops a variation-space function theory for encoder-decoder neural operators, establishing approximation bounds in Bochner L^q norm with constants independent of encoding dimension. It decomposes error into encoding and finite-width terms of order N^{-1/2}.

entry.title: On the Uncertainty Quantification Ability of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Tyler R. Johnson, Kian Ben-Jacob, Nima Negarandeh, Oriol Vendrell-Gallart, Ramin Bostanabad
